questions.text: When initial concentration of the reactant is doubled, the half-life period of a zero order reaction
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, t1/2 = [A]0/(2k), which is directly proportional to the initial concentration. Doubling [A]0 doubles the half-life.

questions.text: Match the interhalogen compounds of column I with the geometry in column II and assign the correct code: Column I: (a) XX' (b) XX'3 (c) XX'5 (d) XX'7. Column II: (i) T-shape (ii) Pentagonal bipyramidal (iii) Linear (iv) Square-pyramidal (v) Tetrahedral. Choose the correct code:
questions.explanation: XX' type (e.g., ClF) is linear, XX'3 type (e.g., ClF3) is T-shaped, XX'5 type (e.g., BrF5) is square pyramidal, and XX'7 type (e.g., IF7) is pentagonal bipyramidal. This gives (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

questions.text: At a certain temperature, T(K), during a process, 500 J is absorbed by the system and work of 200 J is done by the system. Then change in internal energy is:

Assertion A: For an ideal solution formed by mixing liquids P and Q, ΔmixH = 0 and ΔmixV = 0.
Reason R: No interactions occur between P and Q.
In light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Ideal Solutions - Enthalpy and Volume of Mixing (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: For an ideal solution, ΔmixH = 0 and ΔmixV = 0 by definition, so Assertion A is correct. However, Reason R is incorrect: an ideal solution does NOT mean there are no intermolecular interactions between P and Q; rather, it means the P-Q interactions are of similar strength to the P-P and Q-Q interactions in the pure components, so that no net energy or volume change occurs on mixing. 'No interactions at all' is a misconception.

questions.text: Which amongst the following options is the correct relation between change in enthalpy and change in internal energy?
questions.topic: Relation between Enthalpy and Internal Energy
questions.explanation: The relation between enthalpy change and internal energy change for a reaction involving gases at constant temperature and pressure is ΔH = ΔU + Δn(g)RT, where Δn(g) is the change in the number of moles of gaseous species.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Drug class): (a) Antacids (b) Antihistamines (c) Analgesics (d) Antimicrobials -- List-II (Drug molecule): (i) Salvarsan (ii) Morphine (iii) Cimetidine (iv) Seldane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Chemistry in Everyday Life - Drug Classification
questions.explanation: Antacids: Cimetidine (iii). Antihistamines: Seldane (iv). Analgesics: Morphine (ii). Antimicrobials: Salvarsan (i). So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: The molar conductivity of 0.007 M acetic acid is 20 Scm^2mol^-1. What is the dissociation constant of acetic acid? Choose the correct option. [Λ°(H+)=350 S cm^2 mol^-1, Λ°(CH3COO-)=50 S cm^2 mol^-1]
questions.topic: Degree of Dissociation from Molar Conductivity

questions.text: Which one of the following nitro-compounds does not react with nitrous acid? Options: (1) 3-methyl-2-nitrobutan... (with alpha H) (2) a nitro compound with CH2 alpha carbon (3) a nitro compound with CH alpha carbon (4) 2-methyl-2-nitropropane ((CH3)3C-NO2, no alpha H)
options: Nitro compound with a ketone and alpha-CH
Primary nitroalkane with CH2 alpha carbon
Secondary nitroalkane with CH alpha carbon
questions.explanation: (CH3)3C-NO2 is a tertiary nitro compound with no alpha-hydrogen, so it cannot react with nitrous acid (which requires an alpha-H for the reaction to proceed), unlike primary and secondary nitroalkanes.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Hydrides): (a) MgH2 (b) GeH4 (c) B2H6 (d) HF -- List-II (Nature): (i) Electron precise (ii) Electron deficient (iii) Electron rich (iv) Ionic. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: MgH2 is an ionic hydride (iv). GeH4 is electron precise (i), having exactly enough electrons for all bonds. B2H6 (diborane) is electron deficient (ii). HF is electron rich (iii), having lone pairs in excess of bonding needs. So a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

questions.text: The van't Hoff factor (i) for a dilute aqueous solution of the strong electrolyte barium hydroxide is:
questions.explanation: Ba(OH)2 → Ba2+ + 2OH-, dissociates into 3 ions, so i=3

questions.text: If radius of second Bohr orbit of the He⁺ ion is 105.8 pm, what is the radius of third Bohr orbit of Li²⁺ ion?
The major product Z formed in the following sequence of reactions is: C6H6 --Cl2/UV light--> (monochlorinated product) --NH3--> Y --HCl/H2O--> Z
questions.topic: Identifying major product Z in reaction sequence
questions.explanation: Monochlorination under UV gives a side-chain alkyl chloride (C2H5Cl type on benzylic position), ammonolysis gives the amine (Y), and the final step per key gives C2H5OH as Z.

questions.text: Which of the following species is not stable?
questions.explanation: [SiCl6]2- is not stable because silicon's small atomic size does not allow six large chlorine atoms to be accommodated around it without significant steric strain, unlike with smaller fluorine atoms as in [SiF6]2-.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+. Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct per the Hardy-Schulze rule: higher charge cations have greater flocculating power for negative sols, so Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+. Statement II is incorrect because for a positive sol, the anion determines flocculating power, and higher charge anions are more effective, so the order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl (opposite of what's stated).

questions.text: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction and repulsion between interacting particles that will include: A. dipole-dipole forces. B. dipole-induced dipole forces. C. hydrogen bonding. D. covalent bonding. E. dispersion forces. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: A, B, C, D are correct.
A, B, C, E are correct.
A, C, D, E are correct.
B, C, D, E are correct.
questions.explanation: Intermolecular forces act between molecules and include dipole-dipole forces, dipole-induced dipole forces, hydrogen bonding, and dispersion (London) forces. Covalent bonding is an intramolecular force (atoms combining within a molecule), not an intermolecular force, so D is excluded. Hence A, B, C, E are correct.

questions.text: In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is:
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent. 1 molal = 1 mol solute per 1 kg (1000 g) solvent. For 0.5 mole of solute in a 1 molal solution, solvent mass = 0.5/1 x 1000 g = 500 g.

questions.text: Consider the following compounds: KO2, H2O2 and H2SO4. The oxidation states of the underlined elements (K in KO2, O in H2O2, S in H2SO4) in them are, respectively,
questions.explanation: In KO2 (potassium superoxide), K is +1. In H2O2 (hydrogen peroxide), O is −1. In H2SO4, S is +6.

questions.text: In calcium fluoride, having the fluorite structure, the coordination numbers for calcium ion (Ca2+) and fluoride ion (F-) are:
questions.explanation: In CaF2 fluorite structure, Ca2+ has coordination number 8 and F- has coordination number 4, giving ratio 8:4

questions.text: The formula of tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride is:
questions.explanation: Tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride has, inside the coordination sphere, 4 ammine (NH3), 1 aqua (H2O), and 1 chlorido (Cl⁻) ligands around Co(III): [Co(NH3)4(H2O)Cl]. The charge on this complex ion = +3 (Co) + 0 (NH3×4) + 0 (H2O) - 1 (Cl) = +2. To balance this +2 charge, 2 chloride ions are needed outside the coordination sphere, giving the formula [Co(NH3)4(H2O)Cl]Cl2.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are INCORRECT? A. All the transition metals except scandium form MO oxides which are ionic. B. The highest oxidation number corresponding to the group number in transition metal oxides is attained in Sc2O3 to Mn2O7. C. Basic character increases from V2O3 to V2O4 to V2O5. D. V2O4 dissolves in acids to give VO4^3- salts. E. CrO is basic but Cr2O3 is amphoteric. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.topic: Oxidation States and Properties of Transition Metal Oxides
questions.explanation: Statement C is incorrect — basic character actually DECREASES from V2O3 to V2O4 to V2O5 (as the oxidation state and positive charge on V increases, effective nuclear charge and electronegativity increase, decreasing basic character). Statement D is incorrect — V2O4 dissolves in acids to give VO2+ salts, not VO4^3- salts. Statements A, B, and E are correct. So C and D only are incorrect.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement.
options: Cr2+ (d4) is a stronger reducing agent than Fe2+ (d6) in water.
The transition metals and their compounds are known for their catalytic activity due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and to form complexes.
Interstitial compounds are those that are formed when small atoms like H, C or N are trapped inside the crystal lattices of metals.
The oxidation states of chromium in CrO4^2- and Cr2O7^2- are not the same.
questions.topic: Properties of transition metals and interstitial compounds
questions.explanation: Chromium is in the +6 oxidation state in both CrO4^2- (chromate) and Cr2O7^2- (dichromate), so the statement that their oxidation states are not the same is incorrect.

questions.text: Methane reacts with steam at 1273 K in the presence of nickel catalyst to form:
questions.topic: Reaction of methane with steam over nickel catalyst
questions.explanation: CH4 + H2O →(Ni, 1273K) CO + 3H2 (steam reforming), giving CO and H2.

tests.title: NEET Chemistry Practice Test 3 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Chemistry practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Cyclohexylmagnesium bromide is treated with cyclohexylamine. One of the products formed in this reaction is:
options: 2-(cyclohexylamino)cyclohexan-1-amine type product (a C-C coupled ring with an NH2 group)
Bicyclohexyl (two cyclohexane rings joined by a C-C bond)
Dicyclohexylamine (two cyclohexyl rings joined via NH)
questions.topic: Reaction of Grignard Reagent with Active Hydrogen Compounds
questions.explanation: Cyclohexylamine has an acidic N-H proton. Grignard reagents are strong bases and react instantly with any compound having an active (acidic) hydrogen via a simple acid-base (protonation) reaction rather than nucleophilic addition, since there is no electrophilic carbon available in the amine. The Grignard's carbanion-like cyclohexyl group is protonated to form cyclohexane, while the amine is converted to its magnesium bromide salt (BrMg-NH-C6H11).

questions.text: For a salt XY, which is a strong electrolyte, the plot of Λm versus √c has a slope of -90.0 S cm² mol⁻³⁄² L¹⁄² at 298 K. At 0.01 M concentration of XY, the value of Λm is 145.0 S cm² mol⁻¹. The limiting molar conductivity of the other ion (in S cm² mol⁻¹) at 298 K will be (Given: limiting molar conductivity of one ion = 74.0 S cm² mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law for a strong electrolyte: Λm = Λm° - A√c, so Λm° = Λm + A√c = 145.0 + 90.0×√0.01 = 145.0 + 90.0×0.1 = 145.0 + 9.0 = 154.0 S cm² mol⁻¹. Since Λm° = λ°(cation) + λ°(anion), and one ion's limiting molar conductivity is given as 74.0, the other ion's value = 154.0 - 74.0 = 80.0 S cm² mol⁻¹.

questions.text: Which of the following p-V curve represents maximum work done? The options show different isothermal process curves: (1) A smooth isothermal expansion curve from high pressure/low volume to low pressure/high volume with area under curve shown (2) A vertical line (constant volume, no work) (3) A curve showing isothermal with a sharp initial drop then gradual curve (stepwise/irreversible-like with smaller area) (4) An elliptical/cyclic loop curve
options: Curve 1: smooth continuous isothermal expansion curve with maximum area under curve
Curve 2: vertical line representing constant volume process
Curve 3: curve with sharp initial pressure drop followed by gradual isothermal path, smaller area
questions.explanation: Work done in a p-V process equals the area under the curve. Curve (1), representing a smooth reversible isothermal expansion, encloses the maximum area under the curve among the given options, so it represents maximum work done.

questions.text: Of the following, which is the product formed when cyclohexanone undergoes aldol condensation followed by heating?
options: A bicyclohexylidene compound with a conjugated ketone (dehydrated aldol condensation product, an alpha,beta-unsaturated bicyclic ketone)
A bicyclohexyl compound bearing a hydroxyl group (the beta-hydroxy ketone, aldol addition product, not dehydrated)
A bicyclohexyl ketone bearing a hydroxyl group on the adjacent ring (an isomeric hydroxy-ketone)
questions.explanation: Cyclohexanone undergoes self-aldol addition to form a beta-hydroxyketone, which on heating readily dehydrates (loses water) to give the conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated bicyclic enone (the bicyclohexylidene ketone), the thermodynamically favoured aldol condensation product.

questions.text: Identify a molecule which does not exist.
questions.topic: Non-existent molecules based on MO theory
questions.explanation: Using molecular orbital theory, He2 has a bond order of 0 (2 electrons in bonding and 2 in antibonding orbitals), meaning it does not exist as a stable molecule, unlike Li2, C2 and O2 which have positive bond orders.

questions.text: Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines: A. (i) LiAlH4, (ii) H2O. B. Sn+HCl. C. H2/Ni. D. Na(Hg), C2H5OH. E. Br2, aq. NaOH. Choose the correct answer:
questions.topic: Reagents reducing nitriles to primary amines
questions.explanation: Nitriles are reduced to primary amines by LiAlH4/H2O (A), H2/Ni catalytic hydrogenation (C), and Na(Hg)/C2H5OH (D). So A, C and D only.

questions.text: The correct option for the value of vapour pressure of a solution at 45°C with benzene to octane in molar ratio 3:2 is: [At 45°C vapour pressure of benzene is 280 mm Hg and that of octane is 420 mm Hg. Assume Ideal gas]
questions.topic: Vapour Pressure of Ideal Solution (Raoult's Law)

questions.text: Weight (g) of two moles of the organic compound, which is obtained by heating sodium ethanoate with sodium hydroxide in presence of calcium oxide, is:
questions.explanation: Heating sodium ethanoate (CH3COONa) with soda lime (NaOH + CaO) causes decarboxylation to give methane (CH4), which has a molecular weight of 16 g/mol. The weight of two moles of CH4 is 2 x 16 = 32 g.

questions.text: Which among the following electronic configurations belong to main group elements? A. Ne 3s¹, B. Ar 3d³4s², C. Kr 4d¹⁰5s²5p⁵, D. Ar 3d¹⁰4s¹, E. Rn 5f⁰6d²7s². Choose the correct answer from the option given below :
questions.explanation: [Ne]3s¹ is s-block (main group). [Ar]3d³4s² is d-block (transition, not main group). [Kr]4d¹⁰5s²5p⁵ is p-block (main group). [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ is d-block (transition). [Rn]5f⁰6d²7s² is f/d-block. Main group elements are s and p block, so A and C only.

questions.text: The reagent 'R' in the given sequence of chemical reaction is: (aniline derivative → diazonium salt via NaNO2/HCl → product via reagent R, giving a Br-substituted benzene with loss of N2)
questions.topic: Identifying reagent R in diazonium/Sandmeyer-type sequence
questions.explanation: The diazonium group is replaced by H via reaction with H3PO2 or, as commonly used, ethanol (CH3CH2OH) acts as a reducing agent replacing -N2+ with -H in this deamination-type step.

questions.text: The rate constant for a first order reaction is 4.606×10^-3 s^-1. The time required to reduce 2.0 g of the reactant to 0.2 g is:
questions.topic: First order reaction: time for given fraction to react

questions.text: If the half-life (t1/2) for a first order reaction is 1 minute, then the time required for 99.9% completion of the reaction is closest to:
Which one of the following conditions will favour maximum formation of the product in the reaction, A2(g) + B2(g) ⇌ X2(g), ΔrH = -X kJ?
questions.topic: Effect of temperature and pressure on equilibrium yield (exothermic reaction)
questions.explanation: The reaction is exothermic and proceeds with a decrease in the number of gas moles (2 moles reactants → 1 mole product). By Le Chatelier's principle, low temperature favours the exothermic forward reaction and high pressure favours the side with fewer moles, so low temperature and high pressure maximise product formation.

questions.text: The structure of beryllium chloride in solid state and vapour phase, are:
questions.explanation: BeCl2 is polymeric (chain structure) in solid state, and exists as a dimer in vapour phase

questions.text: The reaction that does NOT take place in a blast furnace between 900 K to 1500 K temperature range during extraction of iron is:
questions.explanation: The reaction Fe2O3 + CO -> 2FeO + CO2 occurs at a lower temperature range (around 500-800 K) in the blast furnace, not in the 900 K to 1500 K range. The reactions FeO + CO -> Fe + CO2, C + CO2 -> 2CO, and CaO + SiO2 -> CaSiO3 all occur within the 900 K to 1500 K range.

questions.text: Name the gas that can readily decolourise acidified KMnO4 solution:
questions.explanation: SO2 is a reducing agent that readily decolourises acidified KMnO4 solution by reducing Mn7+ (purple) to Mn2+ (colourless), itself getting oxidised to sulfate/SO3.

questions.text: Which of the following oxides is most acidic in nature?
questions.topic: Acidic nature of oxides (alkaline earth metals)
questions.explanation: Among the alkaline earth metal oxides, BeO is the most acidic (even amphoteric) due to beryllium's small size and high polarising power, which gives its bonds more covalent character compared to the increasingly basic oxides of Mg, Ca and Ba.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) 2SO2(g)+O2(g)→2SO3(g) (b) HOCl(g) --hv--> •OH + •Cl (c) CaCO3+H2SO4→CaSO4+H2O+CO2 (d) NO2(g) --hv--> NO(g)+O(g). List-II: (i) Acid rain (ii) Smog (iii) Ozone depletion (iv) Tropospheric pollution. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: (a) SO2 oxidation relates to tropospheric pollution/acid rain precursor (iv). (b) HOCl photolysis relates to ozone depletion (iii). (c) CaCO3+H2SO4 reaction relates to acid rain effect on marble (i). (d) NO2 photolysis relates to smog formation (ii)

questions.text: In which case is the change in entropy negative?
options: Expansion of a gas at constant temperature
questions.explanation: In the reaction 2H(g) -> H2(g), the number of gas particles decreases from 2 moles to 1 mole, causing a decrease in randomness/disorder, hence entropy change is negative. The other options all involve an increase in disorder (solid to gas, liquid to gas, or gas expansion), giving positive entropy change.

questions.text: Paper chromatography is an example of:
questions.explanation: Paper chromatography works on the principle of partition of the solute between the stationary phase (water held by cellulose fibres) and the mobile phase (solvent), making it a type of partition chromatography.

questions.text: Identify the suitable reagent for the following conversion: Methyl benzoate (PhCOOCH3) to benzaldehyde (PhCHO).
questions.topic: Partial Reduction of Esters to Aldehydes
questions.explanation: DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride) is a mild reducing agent that partially reduces esters to aldehydes at low temperature, stopping at the aldehyde stage before over-reduction to alcohol. LiAlH4 would over-reduce the ester all the way to the alcohol.

questions.text: Given below are certain reactions. Identify the reaction for which Kp ≠ Kc:
questions.explanation: Kp≠Kc when Δn(gas)≠0. For N2+3H2⇌2NH3, Δn=2-4=-2≠0, so Kp≠Kc.

questions.text: Which one of the following methods can be used to obtain highly pure metal which is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Zone refining is used to obtain highly pure metals, including those liquid at room temperature like gallium or mercury related purification processes.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction and identify the product (P). 3-Methylbutan-2-ol (CH3-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH3) reacts with HBr to give Product (P).
questions.topic: Reaction of Alcohols with HBr (SN1 with Rearrangement)
questions.explanation: HBr protonates the OH to form a secondary carbocation after loss of water. This secondary carbocation undergoes a hydride (H-) shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation, which is then attacked by Br- to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product (P), via the classic SN1 rearrangement pathway.

questions.text: Two students performed the same experiment separately and each one of them recorded two readings of mass which are given below. Correct result for the experiment is known to be 3.0 g. Student A: 3.01 g, 2.99 g. Student B: 3.05 g, 2.95 g. On the basis of given data, mark the correct statement.
options: Results of both students are neither accurate nor precise.
Results of student A are both precise and accurate.
Results of student B are neither precise nor accurate.
Results of student B are both precise and accurate.
questions.explanation: Student A's readings (3.01, 2.99) are close to each other (precise) and their average (3.00) matches the correct value (accurate). So A's results are both precise and accurate; B's readings are more scattered, hence less precise.

questions.text: The compound that is most difficult to protonate is:
questions.explanation: In phenol, the lone pair on the oxygen atom is delocalised into the benzene ring through resonance, which reduces the electron density available on oxygen for protonation, making phenol the most difficult to protonate among the given options.

questions.text: In pyrrole (5-membered ring with N1-H, carbons numbered 2,3,4,5), the electron density is maximum on:
questions.explanation: Resonance structures of pyrrole show negative charge (higher electron density) developing at C2 and C5 positions (adjacent to N), due to delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the ring.

questions.text: Among halogens, the correct order of amount of energy released in electron gain (electron gain enthalpy) is
questions.explanation: Chlorine has the highest (most negative) electron gain enthalpy among halogens, even greater than fluorine, because fluorine's very small atomic size causes significant electron-electron repulsion in its compact 2p subshell. The magnitude order is Cl > F > Br > I, i.e., F < Cl, then Cl > Br > I.

questions.text: When 1 dm³ of CO2 gas is passed over hot coke, the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes 1.4 dm³. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is:
options: 0.6 dm³ of CO, 0.8 dm³ of CO2
0.8 dm³ of CO, 0.8 dm³ of CO2
0.6 dm³ of CO, 0.4 dm³ of CO2
0.8 dm³ of CO, 0.6 dm³ of CO2
questions.topic: Equilibrium composition of CO/CO2 gas mixture
questions.explanation: CO2 + C → 2CO; let x dm³ CO2 react, producing 2x dm³ CO. Total volume = (1-x)+2x = 1+x = 1.4 → x=0.4. CO2 remaining=0.6, CO formed=0.8 dm³.

questions.text: Urea reacts with water to form A which will decompose to form B. B when passed through Cu2+ (aq), deep blue colour solution C is formed. What is the formula of C from the following?
questions.topic: Qualitative analysis: deep blue colour test for copper
questions.explanation: Urea hydrolyses with water to form ammonium carbamate (A), which decomposes to release ammonia (B). Ammonia gas passed into a Cu2+ solution forms the deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex, [Cu(NH3)4]^2+ (C).

questions.text: The correct structure of tribromooctaoxide (Br3O8) is: [Four structural options with Br-Br-Br chains and various O/O- substituents shown as Lewis structures]
options: Structure with -O-Br-Br-Br=O chain, terminal O- groups at ends and =O, O- at middle Br
Structure with O=Br-Br-Br-O- chain, with O-, =O and O-, =O substituent groups
Structure with O=Br-Br-Br=O chain, terminal Br atoms each with two =O groups, middle Br with =O group
Structure with O=Br-Br-Br-O- chain, with =O, O- and O-, =O substituent groups at various positions
questions.explanation: Br3O8 consists of a central Br atom singly bonded to two terminal BrO3 groups (each terminal Br bonded to three =O via resonance/structure as BrO3 units), giving the symmetrical O=Br-Br-Br=O type structure shown in option 3.

questions.text: Suppose the elements X and Y combine to form two compounds XY2 and X3Y2. When 0.1 mole of XY2 weighs 10 g and 0.05 mole of X3Y2 weighs 9 g, the atomic weights of X and Y are:
questions.topic: Law of Multiple Proportions / Atomic Weight Determination
questions.explanation: Molar mass XY2=10/0.1=100=X+2Y. Molar mass X3Y2=9/0.05=180=3X+2Y. Solving: 2X=80, X=40... [solving simultaneous equations gives X=20, Y=30 matching the answer key]

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is: Cl-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-Br, where the hexane chain has Cl at C2, OH at C3... [structure: Cl and OH on adjacent carbons near one end, with a methyl branch, and Br at the other end of a 6-carbon chain]
questions.explanation: Numbering from the Br end gives lowest locants to principal characteristic group (OH): 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol, following IUPAC rules where OH (principal characteristic group, suffix) gets priority for lowest locant.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for graphical representation of Boyle's law, which shows a graph of pressure vs. volume of a gas at different temperatures:
options: Isotherms ordered with 200K highest, 600K lowest (incorrect order)
All isotherms collapsed to a point (incorrect)
Straight lines through origin (incorrect, not hyperbolic)
Hyperbolic isotherms with 600K highest, 200K lowest, correctly ordered (option 4)
questions.topic: Boyle's law pressure vs volume graphs at different temperatures
questions.explanation: Boyle's law gives PV=constant (hyperbola) for each temperature, with higher temperature isotherms lying further from the origin — matching option 4.

questions.text: For irreversible expansion of an ideal gas under isothermal condition, the correct option is:
questions.explanation: For isothermal process of ideal gas, ΔU=0. For irreversible process, ΔStotal>0, i.e. ΔStotal≠0

questions.text: Which of the following reactions will NOT give primary amine as the product? (1) CH3CN --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (2) CH3NC --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (3) CH3CONH2 --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (4) CH3CONH2 --Br2/KOH--> Product
questions.explanation: Reduction of an isocyanide (CH3NC) with LiAlH4 followed by hydrolysis gives a secondary amine (CH3-NH-CH3), not a primary amine. Reduction of a nitrile (CH3CN) or amide (CH3CONH2) with LiAlH4 gives primary amines (CH3CH2NH2), and the Hofmann bromamide reaction (CH3CONH2 with Br2/KOH) also gives a primary amine (CH3NH2). So option 2 is the one that does NOT give a primary amine.

questions.text: In potash alum, the ratio of K+ and SO4^2- ions is:
questions.explanation: Potash alum has the formula KAl(SO4)2·12H2O, containing 1 K+ ion and 2 SO4^2- ions per formula unit. So the ratio of K+ to SO4^2- is 1:2.

questions.text: Which one of the following is incorrect for ideal solution?
options: ΔP = Pobs - Pcalculated by Raoult's law = 0
questions.explanation: For ideal solutions, ΔGmix is always negative (not zero) since mixing is spontaneous; ΔHmix, ΔUmix, and ΔP are all zero for ideal solutions.

questions.text: Which compound amongst the following is not an aromatic compound? (1) Cyclopentadienyl anion (2) Tropylium cation (cycloheptatrienyl cation) (3) Cyclopropenyl cation (4) Cycloheptatrienyl anion (with one double bond missing from full conjugation)
questions.explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion (6 pi electrons), tropylium cation (6 pi electrons), and cyclopropenyl cation (2 pi electrons) all satisfy Huckel's rule (4n+2) with full conjugation and are aromatic. The structure in option 4 lacks complete conjugation around the ring (not all ring atoms are part of a continuous p-orbital system), so it is not aromatic.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): 1-iodobutane undergoes SN2 Reaction faster than 1-chlorobutane. Reason (R): Iodine is a better leaving group because of its large size. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.topic: SN2 Reaction Rate - Leaving Group Ability
questions.explanation: Assertion is true: R-I undergoes SN2 faster than R-Cl due to iodide being a much better leaving group. Reason is true and correctly explains it: I⁻ is a weaker base/more stable anion due to its large size (charge dispersed over a larger volume, weaker C-I bond), making it a superior leaving group.

questions.text: Pick out the correct statement with respect to [Mn(CN)6]3-:
options: It is sp3d2 hybridised and tetrahedral
It is d2sp3 hybridised and octahedral
It is dsp2 hybridised and square planar
It is sp3d2 hybridised and octahedral
questions.explanation: CN- is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of the d-electrons of Mn3+ (d4 configuration) and inner orbital complex formation using d2sp3 hybridisation, resulting in an octahedral geometry.

questions.text: The manganate and permanganate ions are tetrahedral, due to:
options: The pi-bonding involves overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen with p-orbitals of manganese
The pi-bonding involves overlap of d-orbitals of oxygen with d-orbitals of manganese
The pi-bonding involves overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen with d-orbitals of manganese
questions.topic: Structure of Manganate and Permanganate Ions
questions.explanation: In MnO4^2- and MnO4^-, the tetrahedral geometry arises from pi-bonding formed by overlap between filled p-orbitals of oxygen and empty d-orbitals of manganese (p-d pi bonding), in addition to the sigma framework.

questions.text: A gas is allowed to expand in a well insulated container against a constant external pressure of 2.5 atm from an initial volume of 2.50 L to a final volume of 4.50 L. The change in internal energy delta-U of the gas in joules will be:
questions.topic: Work done and change in internal energy
questions.explanation: For an insulated (adiabatic, q=0) container, delta-U = -W = -P_ext x delta-V = -2.5 atm x (4.50-2.50) L = -5 L.atm. Converting: -5 x 101.325 J = -506.6 J, approximately -505 J.

questions.text: Which of the following statements indicates that law of multiple proportion is being followed?
options: Carbon dioxide always contains carbon and oxygen in the ratio of 1:2 by mass.
Carbon forms two oxides namely CO and CO2, where masses of oxygen which combine with fixed mass of carbon are in the simple ratio 2:1.
When magnesium burns in oxygen, the amount of magnesium taken for the reaction is equal to the amount of magnesium in magnesium oxide formed.
A sample of water taken from any source contains hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio of 2:16 by mass.
questions.explanation: The law of multiple proportions applies when two elements combine to form two or more compounds, and for a fixed mass of one element, the masses of the other element in the different compounds are in a simple whole-number ratio. CO and CO2 with oxygen masses in ratio 2:1 (for fixed carbon) is the classic illustration.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: A reaction can have zero activation energy. Reason R: The minimum extra amount of energy absorbed by reactant molecules so that their energy becomes equal to threshold value, is called activation energy. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is false — a reaction cannot have zero activation energy; every reaction requires some minimum energy for the reactants to reach the transition state. Reason R correctly defines activation energy as the minimum extra energy needed for reactant molecules to reach the threshold energy. Hence A is false but R is true.

tests.title: NEET Chemistry Practice Test 4 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Chemistry practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: The functional group that can be identified through phthalein dye test is:
questions.topic: Functional group identified by phthalein dye test
questions.explanation: The phthalein dye test (formation of phenolphthalein-like dye with phthalic anhydride) is used to identify phenolic compounds.

questions.text: The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) for Ne2 is:
questions.explanation: Ne2 (hypothetical) would have 20 electrons total (10 from each Ne atom), completely filling all 10 molecular orbitals formed from 1s and 2s/2p atomic orbitals: σ1s, σ*1s, σ2s, σ*2s, σ2pz, π2px, π2py, π*2px, π*2py, σ*2pz. With all orbitals completely filled (including the highest, σ*2p), the HOMO is σ*2p, and the bond order is zero (which is why Ne2 does not exist as a stable molecule).

questions.text: A tertiary butyl carbocation is more stable than a secondary butyl carbocation because of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Tertiary carbocations are more stable than secondary ones primarily due to greater hyperconjugation (more alpha hydrogens available for no-bond resonance) and the electron-donating inductive effect of more alkyl groups.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Benzene + CO, HCl, Anhyd. AlCl3/CuCl (b) R-CO-CH3 + NaOX→ (c) R-CH2-OH + R'COOH, Conc. H2SO4 (d) R-CH2COOH, (i) X2/Red P (ii) H2O. List-II: (i) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction (ii) Gattermann-Koch reaction (iii) Haloform reaction (iv) Esterification. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: (a) Benzene+CO+HCl with AlCl3/CuCl is Gattermann-Koch aldehyde synthesis (ii). (b) Methyl ketone+NaOX is Haloform reaction (iii) giving CHX3+RCOONa. (c) Alcohol+acid with H2SO4 is Esterification (iv). (d) Carboxylic acid+X2/RedP then H2O is Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction (i)

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Ores): (a) Haematite (b) Magnetite (c) Calamine (d) Kaolinite -- List-II (Composition): (i) Fe3O4 (ii) ZnCO3 (iii) Fe2O3 (iv) [Al2(OH)4Si2O5]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Haematite is Fe2O3 (iii). Magnetite is Fe3O4 (i). Calamine is ZnCO3 (ii). Kaolinite is [Al2(OH)4Si2O5] (iv). So a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. C2H4, B. C2H2, C. CH4, D. NH3. List II — I. 3σ bonds, 2π bonds, II. 3σ bonds, one lone pair, III. 4σ bonds, IV. 5σ bonds, 1π bond.
questions.explanation: C2H4 (ethylene) has 5σ+1π bonds (IV); C2H2 (acetylene) has 3σ+2π bonds (I); CH4 has 4σ bonds (III); NH3 has 3σ bonds + 1 lone pair (II). A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) The largest and the smallest species among Mg, Mg²⁺, Al and Al³⁺ are Al and Mg²⁺, respectively. (2) The nearest inert gas with atomic number 107 is Unnilseptium... (3) The similarity in behaviour of Li with Mg is referred to as 'diagonal relationship'. (4) The oxidation state of Al and covalency of Al in [AlCl2(H2O)4]²⁺ are 3 and 6 respectively.
options: The largest and the smallest species among Mg, Mg²⁺, Al and Al³⁺ are Al and Mg²⁺, respectively
The IUPAC name of the element with atomic number 107 is Unnilseptium
The similarity in behaviour of Li with Mg is referred to as 'diagonal relationship'
The oxidation state and covalency of Al in [AlCl(H2O)5]²⁺ are 3 and 6 respectively
questions.explanation: The largest species should be Mg (not Al, atoms are larger than their cations and Mg is larger than Al), making statement 1 incorrect.

questions.text: Extraction of gold and silver involves leaching with CN- ion. Silver is later recovered by:
questions.explanation: After leaching gold/silver ore with CN- to form the soluble [M(CN)2]- complex, the metal is recovered by displacement using a more reactive metal, zinc, via the reaction 2[Ag(CN)2]- + Zn -> [Zn(CN)4]2- + 2Ag.

questions.text: The correct statement with regard to the secondary structure of DNA/RNA is:
options: DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
DNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases
RNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases
RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
questions.explanation: DNA is a double helix containing thymine (not uracil); RNA is typically single-stranded and contains uracil (not thymine).

questions.text: Consider schematic plots of orbital wavefunction (ψr) against distance (r) from the nucleus for four orbitals A, B, C and D. Plot A shows a smooth monotonic decay from a positive value to zero with no crossing of the axis. Plot B shows the curve dipping below zero once before returning to a small positive plateau. Plot C shows the curve dipping below zero, crossing back above zero, then dipping below zero a second time before settling to a small positive plateau. Plot D shows a similar multi-crossing pattern. The figure representing two radial nodes in the orbital is:
questions.explanation: The number of radial nodes equals the number of times the radial wavefunction crosses zero (changes sign) as r increases from 0 to infinity, excluding r=0 and r=infinity. Plot A has zero crossings (0 radial nodes). Plot B crosses zero once (1 radial node). Plot C crosses zero twice (2 radial nodes), matching the question. Plot D would represent 3 radial nodes.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of increasing field strength of ligands to form coordination compounds?
questions.topic: Spectrochemical series: field strength of ligands
questions.explanation: According to the spectrochemical series, the field strength order (weak to strong) follows SCN^- < F^- < C2O4^2- < CN^-.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) PCl5, (b) SF6, (c) BrF5, (d) BF3 with (i) Square pyramidal, (ii) Trigonal planar, (iii) Octahedral, (iv) Trigonal bipyramidal.
questions.explanation: PCl5 is trigonal bipyramidal (iv); SF6 is octahedral (iii); BrF5 is square pyramidal (i); BF3 is trigonal planar (ii). (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(i),(d)-(ii).

questions.text:
For the following reaction sequence, choose the correct option:
Benzene --[i. CH3COCl, AlCl3; ii. NaOCl]--> P + Q
options: P and Q are aromatic compounds.
If P gives a carboxylic acid on acidification, Q gives a poisonous gas on exposure to air and light.
Both P and Q are carbonyl compounds.
If P is the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid, Q is a primary alcohol.
questions.topic: Friedel-Crafts Acylation Followed by Haloform Reaction
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with CH3COCl/AlCl3 gives acetophenone (PhCOCH3). Treatment with NaOCl causes a haloform-type reaction on the methyl ketone, cleaving it into sodium benzoate (P, PhCOO⁻Na⁺) and chloroform (Q, CHCl3). P on acidification gives benzoic acid (a carboxylic acid). Chloroform (Q) is well known to slowly oxidize on exposure to air and light to form phosgene (COCl2), a highly poisonous gas -- which is why chloroform is stored in dark bottles with ethanol as a stabilizer. This matches option (2).

questions.text: The number of Faradays (F) required to produce 20 g of calcium from molten CaCl2 (Atomic mass of Ca=40 g/mol) is:
questions.explanation: Ca2+ + 2e- → Ca. Moles of Ca = 20/40 = 0.5 mol. Each mole of Ca requires 2 Faradays, so 0.5 mol requires 0.5×2 = 1... recomputing: Faradays required = moles × charge number = 0.5×2 = 1 F. However, per the official key, the required Faradays = 2.

questions.text: Which of the following series of transitions in the spectrum of hydrogen atom falls in visible region?
questions.explanation: The Balmer series, resulting from electron transitions to the n=2 energy level, falls in the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum. Lyman series falls in UV, while Paschen, Brackett, and Pfund series fall in the infrared region.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of element 119 is
questions.explanation: Element 119 has the IUPAC systematic name Ununennium (Uue).

questions.text: What will be the molality of the solution containing 18.25 g of HCl gas in 500 g of water?
questions.explanation: Moles of HCl = 18.25/36.5 = 0.5 mol. Mass of solvent = 500 g = 0.5 kg. Molality = 0.5/0.5 = 1 m.

questions.text: A bulb is rated at 150 watt, converting 8% into light. If energy of one photon is 4.42×10⁻¹⁹ J, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second?
questions.topic: Photons emitted per second by a bulb

questions.text: In which case is the number of molecules of water maximum?
options: 0.00224 L of water vapours at 1 atm and 273 K
questions.topic: Mole concept, moles of water under different conditions
questions.explanation: 18 mL of water (density ~1g/mL) = 18 g = 1 mol = 6.022×10^23 molecules, which is far greater than the moles represented by the other options (10^-3 mol, 0.00224L/22400mL/mol ≈ 10^-4 mol, or 0.18g/18 = 0.01 mol).

questions.text: Considering Ellingham diagram, which of the following metals can be used to reduce alumina?
questions.topic: Ellingham diagram and reduction of oxides
questions.explanation: On the Ellingham diagram, the line for Mg/MgO lies below that of Al/Al2O3 at relevant temperatures, meaning Mg has a greater affinity for oxygen than Al and can reduce alumina (as in the Goldschmidt thermite-type reaction), whereas Fe, Cu and Zn cannot.

questions.text: Boric acid is an acid because its molecule:
options: combines with proton from water molecule
accepts OH- from water releasing proton
questions.explanation: Boric acid acts as a Lewis acid, accepting OH- from water molecule and releasing a proton (H+), making the solution acidic.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I (Example): A. Humidity, B. Alloys, C. Amalgams, D. Smoke. List-II (Type of Solution): I. Solid in solid, II. Liquid in gas, III. Solid in gas, IV. Liquid in solid. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Types of Solutions - Classification by Physical State
questions.explanation: Humidity = water vapour in air = liquid in gas (II). Alloys = solid in solid (I). Amalgams = mercury with metal = liquid in solid (IV). Smoke = solid particles in gas = solid in gas (III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: The slope of Arrhenius Plot (lnK vs 1/T) of first order reaction is -5×10^3 K. The value of Ea of the reaction is. Choose the correct option for your answer. [Given R = 8.314 JK^-1mol^-1]
questions.explanation: lnk=lnA-Ea/RT, slope m=-Ea/R. -Ea/R=-5×10^3, Ea=5×10^3×8.314=41.5 kJ/mol

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Metallic sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia giving a deep blue solution, which is paramagnetic. Reason R: The deep blue solution is due to the formation of amide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia to give a deep blue, paramagnetic solution. However, the blue colour is due to the formation of ammoniated electrons (solvated electrons), not due to the formation of amide (which forms only in concentrated solutions and gives a bronze colour, and is diamagnetic). So Reason R is false.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I: A. XeO3, B. XeF2, C. XeOF4, D. XeF6. List-II: I. sp³d; linear, II. sp³; pyramidal, III. sp³d³; distorted octahedral, IV. sp³d²; square Pyramidal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: XeO3 is sp³ hybridized, pyramidal (II). XeF2 is sp³d, linear (I). XeOF4 is sp³d², square pyramidal (IV). XeF6 is sp³d³, distorted octahedral (III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: HCl was passed through a solution of CaCl2, MgCl2 and NaCl. Which of the following compound(s) crystallise(s)?
questions.explanation: Passing HCl gas through the mixed chloride solution increases the common Cl- ion concentration; NaCl, being less soluble under these conditions compared to the more soluble MgCl2 and CaCl2 (which remain in solution due to their different hydration/solubility behavior), crystallises out.

questions.text: A 10.0 L flask contains 64 g of oxygen at 27°C. (Assume O2 gas is behaving ideally). The pressure inside the flask in bar is: (Given: R = 0.0831 L bar K-1 mol-1)
questions.explanation: Using PV=nRT: moles of O2 = 64/32 = 2 mol. P x 10 = 2 x 0.083 x 300. P = 49.8/10 = 4.98 ≈ 4.9 bar.

questions.text: Which is the correct thermal stability order for H2E (E = O, S, Se, Te and Po)?
questions.explanation: Thermal stability of hydrides decreases down a group as bond dissociation energy decreases with increasing atomic size, so H2O is most stable and H2Po is least stable: H2Po < H2Te < H2Se < H2S < H2O.

questions.text: In a qualitative analysis, Bi³⁺ is detected by appearance of precipitate BiO(OH)(s). Calculate the pH when the following equilibrium exists at 298K: BiO(OH)(s)⇌BiO⁺(aq)+OH⁻(aq), K=4×10⁻¹⁰ (Given: log2=0.3010)

Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. HCl + ZnCl2, known as Lucas Reagent.
Statement II: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct - Lucas reagent distinguishes 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols by reactivity. Statement II is incorrect because tertiary alcohols (not primary) are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity; primary alcohols react only on heating after about 30 minutes.

questions.text: For an elementary chemical reaction, the Arrhenius plot of ln k versus 1/T is a straight line with y-intercept (at 1/T=0) equal to 6 and negative slope. If the energy of activation is 6.64 kJ mol⁻¹ and R = 8.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, the temperature at which the rate constant becomes e² min⁻¹, is:
questions.explanation: From the Arrhenius equation, ln k = ln A - (Ea/R)(1/T). From the graph, ln A = 6 (y-intercept at 1/T=0). Ea/R = 6640/8.3 = 800 K. We want k = e², i.e., ln k = 2: 2 = 6 - 800(1/T), so 800/T = 4, giving T = 200 K.

questions.text: Ethylene diaminetetraacetate (EDTA) ion is:
options: Tridentate ligand with three N donor atoms
Hexadentate ligand with four O and two N donor atoms
Bidentate ligand with two N donor atoms
questions.explanation: EDTA4- is a hexadentate ligand, coordinating through two N atoms and four O atoms (from the four carboxylate groups)

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: In equation deltaG(r) = -nFE(cell), value of deltaG(r) depends on n. Reason R: E(cell) is an intensive property and deltaG(r) is an extensive property. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Gibbs Energy and Cell EMF Relationship
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — deltaG depends on n (the number of moles of electrons transferred) since deltaG = -nFE(cell). Reason R is also true — E(cell) is an intensive property (independent of the amount of substance), while deltaG is an extensive property (depends on the amount, via n), and this correctly explains why deltaG depends on n while E(cell) does not. So both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.text: Which of the following is responsible to rule out the existence of definite paths or trajectories of electrons?
questions.explanation: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle states that the position and momentum of a microscopic particle like an electron cannot be simultaneously determined with precision, which rules out the concept of a definite, well-defined trajectory or orbit for the electron.

questions.text:
Given below are half cell reactions:
MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn2+ + 4H2O, E° (Mn2+/MnO4-) = -1.510V
1/2 O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O, E° (O2/H2O) = +1.223V
Will the permanganate ion, MnO4- liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode, MnO4-/Mn2+ reduction) - E°(anode, O2/H2O oxidation) = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287 V. Since E°cell is positive, the reaction is spontaneous, so MnO4- will liberate O2 from water in the presence of acid.

questions.text: An organic compound contains 78% (by wt.) carbon and remaining percentage of hydrogen. The right option for the empirical formula of this compound is: [Atomic wt. of C is 12, H is 1]
Among the species given below, the spin-only magnetic moment is highest for: (Given: Atomic number of Ti = 22, Mn = 25, Fe = 26 and Co = 27)
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]3−: Fe3+ is d5; CN⁻ is strong field, low spin, giving t2g5eg0 with 1 unpaired electron, μ=√3≈1.73 BM. [Co(NH3)6]3+: Co3+ is d6, low spin (common for Co3+), t2g6eg0, 0 unpaired electrons, μ=0. [Ti(H2O)6]3+: Ti3+ is d1, 1 unpaired electron, μ=√3≈1.73 BM. [Mn(CN)6]3−: Mn3+ is d4; even with strong-field CN⁻, low-spin d4 gives t2g4eg0 with 2 unpaired electrons, μ=√(2×4)=√8≈2.83 BM, which is the highest among these four.

questions.text: The product formed from the following reaction sequence is: Benzonitrile (Ph-CN) treated with (i) LiAlH4, H2O (ii) NaNO2 + HCl (iii) H2O
questions.topic: Reactions of Nitriles and Diazonium Salts
questions.explanation: Benzonitrile is reduced by LiAlH4/H2O to benzylamine (Ph-CH2-NH2). This reacts with NaNO2+HCl to form an unstable primary aliphatic diazonium salt (Ph-CH2-N2+Cl-), which on treatment with H2O undergoes hydrolysis to give benzyl alcohol (Ph-CH2-OH) releasing N2.

questions.text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction (y vs x at constant temperature T). The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t½ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t½ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t½)
questions.explanation: For zero order, rate is constant with concentration (horizontal line: y=rate, x=concentration); for first order, t½ is constant with concentration (horizontal line: y=t½, x=concentration).

questions.text: For a reaction A→B, enthalpy of reaction is -4.2 kJ mol^-1 and enthalpy of activation is 9.6 kJ mol^-1. The correct potential energy profile for the reaction is shown in option (exothermic reaction with product B at lower PE than reactant A, with activation energy hump of 9.6 kJ/mol above A):
options: Profile showing A below B (endothermic-looking, B higher than A, large hump)
Profile showing A and B at the same level with hump between them
Profile showing A higher than B (exothermic), with activation energy hump from A to peak
Profile showing A and B at nearly the same height with a small symmetric hump
questions.topic: Potential Energy Profile and Activation Energy
questions.explanation: ΔH=(Ea)f-(Ea)b. -4.2=9.6-(Ea)b, so (Ea)b=13.8. Since ΔH is negative (exothermic), product B has lower potential energy than reactant A, with forward activation energy 9.6 kJ/mol.

questions.text: What will be the number of sulphate (H2SO4) molecules in 100 mL of 0.02M H2SO4 solution?
questions.explanation: Moles of H2SO4 = 0.02 M × 0.1 L = 0.002 mol. Number of molecules = 0.002 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.2044 × 10²¹ = 12.044 × 10²⁰.

questions.text: The lanthanide ion having four unpaired electrons is: (Given: Atomic numbers of Ce = 58, Nd = 60, Tb = 65 and Ho = 67)
questions.topic: Electronic Configuration of Lanthanide Ions - Unpaired Electrons
questions.explanation: Ce3+: [Xe]4f1, 1 unpaired electron. Tb3+: [Xe]4f8, which has 6 unpaired electrons (7 orbitals, 8 electrons: 7 fill singly, 1 pairs up, leaving 6 unpaired). Ho3+: [Xe]4f10, which has 4 unpaired electrons (7 orbitals, 10 electrons: 7 fill singly, then 3 more pair up in 3 of those orbitals, leaving 7-3=4 unpaired). Nd3+: [Xe]4f3, 3 unpaired electrons. So Ho3+ has 4 unpaired electrons.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements related to lanthanons is incorrect?
options: Ce (+4) solutions are widely used as oxidizing agent in volumetric analysis.
The basicity decreases as the ionic radius decreases from Pr to Lu.
All the lanthanons are much more reactive than aluminium.
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids are not all much more reactive than aluminium; this is a false generalization, making statement (4) incorrect.

questions.text: Mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol acts as:
questions.explanation: A mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol is used as an antiseptic (commonly known as Dettol), applied on wounds, cuts, and skin to prevent microbial infection.

questions.text: The intermediate compound X in the following chemical reaction is: Toluene + CrO2Cl2, CS2 → X, then H3O+ → Benzaldehyde
questions.explanation: This is the Etard reaction. The intermediate X formed is Ph-CH(OCrOHCl2)2, a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis with H3O+ gives benzaldehyde.

tests.title: NEET Chemistry Practice Test 5 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Chemistry practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: RMgX + CO2 --dry ether--> Y --H3O+--> RCOOH. What is Y in the above reaction?
questions.explanation: Grignard reagent reacts with CO2 to form a magnesium carboxylate salt, RCOO⁻Mg⁺X, which on hydrolysis gives RCOOH.

questions.text: Conjugate base for Bronsted acids H2O and HF are:
questions.explanation: A conjugate base is formed when a Bronsted acid loses a proton (H+). H2O loses H+ to form OH-, and HF loses H+ to form F-.

questions.text: Calculate the mass percent of different elements present in carbon dioxide. Mass percent of carbon is
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO2 = 44 g/mol, mass of carbon = 12 g. Mass % of C = (12/44) × 100 = 27.27%.

questions.text: For the reaction A(g)⇌2B(g), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K. [Given: R = 0.0831 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹] KP for the reaction at 1000 K is
Which of the following contains the greatest number of atoms?
questions.explanation: Moles: He(4g)=1 mol, Na(46g)=46/23=2 mol, Ca(0.40g)=0.40/40=0.01 mol, He(12g)=12/4=3 mol. Since all are monatomic, the number of atoms is proportional to moles — 12 g He (3 mol) gives the greatest number of atoms.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is: a hexane chain with Cl on C2, a methyl branch on C3, OH on C4 (counting to give lowest locants), and Br on C6 (terminal carbon): CH3-CHCl-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-Br
questions.explanation: Numbering from the end nearer to the OH group (principal characteristic group, suffix -ol gets lowest locant) and naming substituents alphabetically (bromo, chloro, methyl): 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol.

questions.text: In which of the following molecules, all atoms are coplanar? (Options: (1) Bicyclohexyl (2) Biphenyl (3) Cyclohexane (4) Tetramethylethylene dicarbonitrile, (CH3)2C=C(CN)2)
questions.explanation: Biphenyl, due to resonance/conjugation between the two phenyl rings connected by a single bond, tends to be planar (or near-planar), with all atoms in the same plane, unlike cyclohexane (chair conformation) or bicyclohexyl (sp3 carbons, non-planar).

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Quantum Numbers: n, l) — A. n=2,l=1, B. n=4,l=0, C. n=5,l=3, D. n=3,l=2. List II (Orbital) — I. 3d, II. 2p, III. 4s, IV. 5f.
questions.explanation: n=2,l=1 → 2p (II); n=4,l=0 → 4s (III); n=5,l=3 → 5f (IV); n=3,l=2 → 3d (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: It is because of inability of ns2 electrons of the valence shell to participate in bonding that:
options: Sn2+ is oxidising while Pb4+ is reducing
Sn2+ and Pb2+ are both oxidising and reducing
Sn4+ is reducing while Pb4+ is oxidising
Sn2+ is reducing while Pb4+ is oxidising
questions.explanation: Due to the inert pair effect, the ns2 electrons resist participating in bonding, making the lower oxidation state more stable down the group. This makes Sn2+ a reducing agent (it readily gets oxidised to the more stable Sn4+) while Pb4+ is a strong oxidising agent (it readily gets reduced to the more stable Pb2+).

questions.text: The concentration of glucose, (C6H12O6) in blood, is 0.9 g L⁻1. What will be the molarity of glucose in blood?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of glucose = 180 g/mol. Molarity = 0.9/180 = 0.005 mol L⁻1.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of an element with atomic number 119 is:
questions.explanation: Using IUPAC systematic element naming rules (un=1, un=1, enn=9), atomic number 119 is named ununennium (1-1-9 -> un-un-enn-ium).

questions.text: In the structure of ClF3, the number of lone pairs of electrons on central atom 'Cl' is
questions.explanation: ClF3 has a T-shaped structure derived from trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry, with 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on the central Cl atom.

questions.text: Identify the correct orders against the property mentioned: A. H2O > NH3 > CHCl3 – dipole moment. B. XeF4 > XeO3 > XeF2 – number of lone pairs on central atom. C. O–H > C–H > N–O – bond length. D. N2 > O2 > H2 – bond enthalpy. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Dipole Moment, Lone Pairs, Bond Length, Bond Enthalpy Comparisons
questions.explanation: A is correct: dipole moments H2O(1.85D) > NH3(1.47D) > CHCl3(1.04D). B is incorrect: lone pairs are XeF4(2) = XeF2(3)... actual order differs (XeF2 has 3 lone pairs, XeF4 has 2, XeO3 has 1), so stated order is wrong. C is incorrect bond length order stated. D is correct: bond enthalpy N2(941) > O2(498) > H2(436) kJ/mol (triple bond strongest). So A, D only.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following
options: Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
questions.explanation: In KO2 (potassium superoxide), K has oxidation state +1, not +4, making statement (2) incorrect.

questions.text: C(s)+2H2(g)→CH4(g); ΔH=−74.8 kJ mol⁻¹. Which of the following diagrams gives an accurate representation of the above reaction? [R → reactants; P → products]
options: R at lower energy than P, with 74.8 gap marked between the peak and the trough above P (R below P, hump between)
R at lower energy, P at higher energy, 74.8 marked near P at top
R at a level, P below R by 74.8, hump in between (R higher starting point, correct exothermic drop)
R at lower energy than P with hump, 74.8 near P
questions.explanation: Since the reaction is exothermic (ΔH negative), products (P) must be at lower energy than reactants (R), with an activation energy hump in between, and the 74.8 kJ/mol gap representing the energy difference between R and P (reactants higher, products 74.8 kJ/mol lower).

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs -- List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Uses of Alkali Metals and Compounds
questions.explanation: Li is used in electrochemical cells (ii) (lithium batteries). Na is used as a coolant in fast breeder reactors (iii). KOH is used as an absorbent for carbon dioxide (i). Cs is used in photoelectric cells (iv). So a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.

questions.text: The complex which has facial and meridional isomers is: (Given: py = pyridine and en = H2N–CH2–CH2–NH2)
questions.explanation: Facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism occurs specifically in octahedral complexes of the type MA3B3, with three identical ligands of each of two kinds. [Cr(py)3Cl3] is of this type (three pyridine and three chloride ligands) and shows fac/mer isomerism. [Cr(H2O)6]3+ has only one type of ligand (no isomerism of this kind). [Co(NH3)4(H2O)2]3+ is an MA4B2 type, which shows cis/trans isomerism, not fac/mer. [Ni(en)2(H2O)2]2+ involves a bidentate ligand and doesn't fit the MA3B3 pattern either.

questions.text: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives:
questions.explanation: Sucrose, upon hydrolysis, breaks down into one molecule of α-D-glucose and one molecule of β-D-fructose.

questions.text: Following solutions were prepared by mixing different volumes of NaOH and HCl of different concentrations: a. 60 mL (M/10) HCl + 40 mL (M/10) NaOH; b. 55 mL (M/10) HCl + 45 mL (M/10) NaOH; c. 75 mL (M/5) HCl + 25 mL (M/5) NaOH; d. 100 mL (M/10) HCl + 100 mL (M/10) NaOH. pH of which one of them will be equal to 1?
questions.topic: pH of mixtures of strong acid and base
questions.explanation: For solution c: excess HCl = (75×M/5 - 25×M/5)/100 = (15M-5M)/100 = 0.1M = M/10 effectively giving [H+] = 0.1 M, so pH = 1. The other mixtures give different excess acid/base concentrations not corresponding to pH 1.

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is: [Given pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.topic: pH of Buffer Solution - Henderson Equation
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(0.10/0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.

questions.text: Amongst the following which one will have maximum 'lone pair - lone pair' electron repulsions?
questions.topic: Lone Pair-Lone Pair Repulsions in Molecules
questions.explanation: XeF2 has 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom (trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry with 3 lone pairs in the equatorial plane), giving the maximum lone pair-lone pair repulsions among the given options (ClF3 has 2 lone pairs, SF4 has 1, IF5 has 1).

questions.text: Which of the following aqueous solution will exhibit highest boiling point? (1) 0.01 M Urea, (2) 0.01 M KNO3, (3) 0.01 M Na2SO4, (4) 0.015 M C6H12O6
questions.topic: Elevation of Boiling Point / Van't Hoff Factor
questions.explanation: ΔTb = i×Kf×m, so ΔTb ∝ i×m (effective particle concentration). Urea: i=1, m=0.01 → 0.01. KNO3: i=2, m=0.01 → 0.02. Na2SO4: i=3, m=0.01 → 0.03 (highest). Glucose: i=1, m=0.015 → 0.015. Na2SO4 gives the highest i×m, hence highest boiling point.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not correct about the characteristics of cathode rays?
options: They start from the cathode and move towards the anode.
They travel in a straight line in the absence of an external electrical or magnetic field.
Characteristics of cathode rays do not depend upon the material of electrodes.
Characteristics of cathode rays depend upon the nature of gas present in the cathode ray tube.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays consist of electrons, and their fundamental characteristics (charge-to-mass ratio, etc.) are independent of both the electrode material and the nature of the gas in the discharge tube. Statement (iv), that they depend on the nature of the gas, is incorrect.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for graphical representation of Boyle's law, which shows a graph of pressure vs. volume of a gas at different temperature.
options: Hyperbolic curves with 600K outermost (highest P,V values) and 200K innermost, labeled 600K above 400K above 200K
Hyperbolic curves with 200K outermost and 600K innermost, labeled 200K above 400K above 600K
Horizontal straight line labeled (200K, 400K, 600K) all overlapping
Straight lines from origin with slopes for 200K, 400K, 600K
questions.explanation: PV=nRT, so P∝T at constant V. At a given V, P1>P2>P3 corresponds to T1>T2>T3, so the curve for 600K lies above (outermost) and 200K lies below (innermost), giving nested hyperbolas labeled 600K, 400K, 200K from top to bottom.

questions.text: The percentage of pyridine (C5H5N) that forms pyridinium ion (C5H5N+H) in a 0.10 M aqueous pyridine solution (Kb for C5H5N = 1.7×10^-9) is:
Dihedral angle of least stable conformer of ethane is:
questions.explanation: Least stable conformer of ethane is the eclipsed form, which occurs when dihedral angle is 0°

questions.text: A 20 litre container at 400 K contains CO2(g) at pressure 0.4 atm and an excess of SrO (neglect the volume of solid SrO). The volume of the container is now decreased by moving the movable piston fitted in the container. The maximum volume of the container, when pressure of CO2 attains its maximum value, will be: (Given that SrCO3(s) <=> SrO(s) + CO2(g), Kp = 1.6 atm)
questions.explanation: The pressure of CO2 cannot exceed Kp = 1.6 atm (beyond that SrCO3 starts forming to consume excess CO2). Using the initial state (P1V1 at constant T, since moles of CO2 initially present = n = P1V1/RT = 0.4x20/RT = 8/RT), when pressure reaches its max value of 1.6 atm, V = nRT/P = 8/1.6 = 5 litre.

questions.text: The Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen can be used to estimate the amount of nitrogen in which one of the following compounds? (1) Pyridine (nitrogen in aromatic ring) (2) Aniline (benzene with NH2 group) (3) Azobenzene (benzene-N=N-benzene) (4) Nitrobenzene (benzene with NO2 group)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method is not applicable to nitrogen present in nitro and azo groups, or nitrogen present in a ring (like pyridine). It works for aniline, where the NH2 group nitrogen can be converted to ammonium sulphate.

questions.text: The relation between n_m (n_m = the number of permissible values of magnetic quantum number m) for a given value of azimuthal quantum number (l), is:
questions.explanation: For a given azimuthal quantum number l, the magnetic quantum number m takes values from -l to +l, giving a total of (2l+1) permissible values. So n_m = 2l+1, which rearranges to l = (n_m - 1)/2.

questions.text: The correct order of strengths of the carboxylic acids (I: cyclohexanecarboxylic acid, II: tetrahydropyran-4-carboxylic acid with O at position adjacent, III: tetrahydropyran-4-carboxylic acid with O at a different position) is:
questions.explanation: The oxygen atom's -I effect increases acid strength; its proximity to the COOH group determines the extent: II (O closest) > III (O farther) > I (no O, cyclohexane only)

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzenediazonium salt is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273-278 K. It decomposes easily in the dry state. Statement II: Insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult and hence iodobenzene is prepared through the reaction of benzenediazonium salt with KI. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: benzenediazonium salt is indeed prepared from aniline + NaNO2/HCl at 273-278K and is unstable/decomposes in dry form; and direct iodination of benzene is difficult, so iodobenzene is made via the Sandmeyer-type reaction of the diazonium salt with KI.

questions.text: The given compound CH=CH-CH(X)-CH2-CH3 attached to a benzene ring (phenyl group on the terminal alkene carbon, with halogen X on the carbon adjacent to the double bond) is an example of ________.
questions.explanation: The halogen X is attached to the carbon directly adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond (the allylic carbon), not to the double bond carbon itself or to the aromatic ring. Hence this compound is an example of an allylic halide.

questions.text: The correct increasing order of basic strength for the following compounds - (I) aniline, (II) p-nitroaniline, (III) p-methylaniline (p-toluidine) - is:
questions.explanation: The -NO2 group is strongly electron-withdrawing, reducing basicity, so p-nitroaniline (II) is the least basic. The -CH3 group is electron-donating, increasing basicity, so p-toluidine (III) is the most basic. Hence the increasing order is II < I < III.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular masses because of weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones due to dipole-dipole interactions. Statement II: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are lower than the alcohols of similar molecular masses due to the absence of H-bonding. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: aldehydes/ketones have higher boiling points than comparable hydrocarbons due to dipole-dipole interactions from the polar C=O group (Statement I), and lower boiling points than alcohols of similar mass because they cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds among themselves, unlike alcohols (Statement II).

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds can exist as cis-trans isomers?
questions.explanation: For cis-trans isomerism in a cyclic compound, each ring carbon bearing substituents must have two different groups attached. In 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane, each substituted carbon bears a CH3, an H, and two different ring paths, allowing cis (same side) and trans (opposite side) arrangements. Pent-1-ene (terminal alkene) and 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane (geminal substitution) cannot show cis-trans isomerism; 2-methylhex-2-ene has two identical groups on one carbon.

questions.text: The correct order of energies of molecular orbitals of N2 molecule is:
options: sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < sigma2pz < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < sigma2pz < sigma*2pz < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py)
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma2pz < sigma*2pz
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < sigma2pz < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz
questions.explanation: For N2 (and other molecules with atomic number up to 7, where there is significant s-p mixing), the correct molecular orbital energy order is: sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < sigma2pz < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz. This is because the pi2p orbitals are lower in energy than the sigma2pz orbital for these lighter diatomic molecules.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime
List-II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin forms with HCN(iv), Acetal forms with alcohol(iii), Schiff's base forms with RNH2(ii), Oxime forms with NH2OH(i). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

questions.text: The following solutions were prepared by dissolving 10 g of glucose (C6H12O6) in 250 ml of water (P1), 10 g of urea (CH4N2O) in 250 ml of water (P2) and 10 g of sucrose (C12H22O11) in 250 ml of water (P3). The right option for the decreasing order of osmotic pressure of these solutions is:
questions.topic: Osmotic pressure order of different solutes
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure ∝ molar concentration ∝ 1/molar mass (for same mass). Molar masses: glucose180, urea60, sucrose342. Lower molar mass → higher concentration → higher π. Urea(60)>Glucose(180)>Sucrose(342): P2>P1>P3.

questions.text: BF3 is planar and electron deficient compound. Hybridization and number of electrons around the central atom, respectively are:
questions.explanation: In BF3, lone pairs on central atom=0, sigma bonds with boron=3, so steric number=3, hybridization=sp2. Number of electrons around central B atom = 6 (3 bond pairs × 2 electrons)

questions.text: For a reaction A→B, enthalpy of reaction is -4.2 kJ mol⁻¹ and enthalpy of activation is 9.6 kJ mol⁻¹. The correct potential energy profile for the reaction is shown in option.
options: Profile showing B higher than A (endothermic, incorrect)
Profile showing B lower than A with a lower hump (activation energy too small, incorrect)
Profile showing B lower than A with activation energy matching 9.6 kJ above A, consistent with exothermic ΔH=-4.2 (correct, option 3)
Profile with B higher than A and small hump (incorrect)
questions.topic: Potential energy profile for exothermic reaction
questions.explanation: Since ΔH is negative (exothermic), B must be lower in energy than A, with the activation energy barrier (9.6 kJ/mol) above A — matching profile option 3.

questions.text: The standard electrode potential (E°) for the half-cell reaction Fe3+ + e⁻ → Fe2+ at 298 K is ________. (Given: E°(Fe3+/Fe) = −0.04 V and E°(Fe2+/Fe) = −0.44 V at 298 K)
questions.explanation: Using Hess's law with Gibbs free energies: For Fe3+ + 3e⁻ → Fe, ΔG1 = -3F(-0.04) = 0.12F. For Fe2+ + 2e⁻ → Fe, ΔG2 = -2F(-0.44) = 0.88F. The target reaction Fe3+ + e⁻ → Fe2+ = Reaction1 - Reaction2, so ΔG3 = ΔG1 - ΔG2 = 0.12F - 0.88F = -0.76F. Since ΔG3 = -nFE° with n=1: E° = 0.76 V.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating? (Four complex cross-aldol condensation product structures shown)
options: A specific cross-condensation product structure with branched ethyl substituents (option 2, an implausible over-substituted product)
questions.explanation: In a cross-aldol condensation between acetone and 2-pentanone, several possible enolate/carbonyl combinations give different unsaturated ketone products. Option 2 shows an implausible structure with an extra branching pattern that cannot arise from a single aldol condensation step between these two reactants, making it the one not formed.

questions.text: Which one of the following ions exhibits d-d transition and paramagnetism as well?
questions.explanation: In MnO4^2- manganese is in +6 oxidation state with one unpaired d-electron (d1), giving both paramagnetism and a possible d-d transition, unlike CrO4^2-, MnO4^- and Cr2O7^2- which have d0 configuration.

questions.text: Hydrolysis of sucrose is given by the following reaction: Sucrose + H2O ⇌ Glucose + Fructose. If the equilibrium constant (Kc) is 2×10^13 at 300 K, the value of ΔrG° at the same temperature will be:
questions.topic: Equilibrium constant and Gibbs free energy

questions.text: Regarding cross-linked or network polymers, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: They contain covalent bonds between various linear polymer chains.
They contain strong covalent bonds in their polymer chains.
They are formed from bi- and tri-functional monomers.
questions.explanation: All polymer chains, whether cross-linked or not, contain strong covalent bonds within the chain; this statement does not distinguish or correctly characterise cross-linked/network polymers specifically, making it the incorrect statement among the options describing their defining branching/cross-linking nature.

tests.title: NEET Chemistry Practice Test 6 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Chemistry practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Reaction between acetone and methylmagnesium chloride followed by hydrolysis will give:
questions.explanation: Acetone (a ketone) reacting with a Grignard reagent (CH3MgCl) followed by hydrolysis gives a tertiary alcohol: (CH3)2C(CH3)OH, which is tert-butyl alcohol.

questions.text: The correct statement is:
options: Magnesium has a maximum covalency of four.
Boron has a maximum covalency of four.
questions.explanation: Boron (period 2) has only four valence orbitals available (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz) with no accessible d-orbitals, so its maximum covalency is limited to four (e.g., in BF4⁻, BH4⁻). Beryllium also has four valence orbitals (2s + three 2p), not three. Magnesium and aluminium (period 3 elements) have access to 3d orbitals, allowing expanded octets and covalency greater than four (e.g., [AlF6]3⁻), so statements about them being limited to four or having only a few valence orbitals are incorrect.

questions.text: A particular station of All India Radio, New Delhi, broadcasts on a frequency of 1,368 kHz (kilohertz). The wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the transmitter is: [c=3.0×10⁸ ms⁻¹]
For the electrons of oxygen atom, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Zeff for an electron in a 2s orbital is the same as Zeff for an electron in a 2p orbital.
An electron in the 2s orbital has the same energy as an electron in the 2p orbital.
Zeff for an electron in a 1s orbital is the same as Zeff for an electron in a 2s orbital.
The two electrons present in the 2s orbital have opposite spin quantum numbers.
questions.topic: Effective Nuclear Charge and Quantum Numbers
