questions.explanation: By the Pauli exclusion principle, no two electrons in the same orbital (here, the 2s orbital) can have the same set of quantum numbers — so the two 2s electrons must have opposite spin quantum numbers. Zeff differs between 1s/2s/2p shells, and 2s has lower energy than 2p in a multi-electron atom.

questions.text: The correct statement regarding electrophile is:
options: Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from another electrophile
Electrophiles are generally neutral species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile can be either neutral or positively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
questions.explanation: An electrophile (electron-loving species) can be neutral or positively charged, and it forms a new bond by accepting a pair of electrons donated by a nucleophile.

questions.text: Zinc can be coated on iron to produce galvanized iron but the reverse is not possible. It is because:
options: zinc has higher negative electrode potential than iron
zinc has lower melting point than iron
zinc has lower negative electrode potential than iron
questions.explanation: Zinc has a higher (more negative) reduction potential than iron, making it more easily oxidized, so it sacrificially protects iron when coated on it (galvanization), but the reverse doesn't work.

questions.text: Mass of one Fe atom is 9.27 × 10⁻23 g. Considering the reaction, 4Fe(s) + 3O2(g) → 2Fe2O3(g), which of the following statements is correct?
options: Total mass of Fe and O2 involved in the reaction is conserved and equals the mass of Fe2O3 formed, as per the law of conservation of mass.
Reaction follows law of multiple proportions.
Amount of Fe2O3 increases if excess of O2 is taken.
Amount of Fe2O3 formed decreases if the amount of oxygen is increased.
questions.explanation: This reaction simply illustrates the law of conservation of mass: the total mass of reactants (Fe + O2) equals the total mass of the product (Fe2O3) formed.

questions.text: The correct order of decreasing basic strength of the given amines is : N-methylaniline, benzenamine, ethanamine, N-ethylethanamine
questions.explanation: Aliphatic amines are more basic than aromatic amines due to +I effect without resonance delocalization of lone pair. Among aliphatic amines, secondary (diethylamine) > primary (ethanamine). Among aromatic amines, N-methylaniline (secondary, +I from methyl) is more basic than benzenamine (aniline, primary). Order: N-ethylethanamine > ethanamine > N-methylaniline > benzenamine.

questions.text: The structure of ozone (O3) with oxygen atoms numbered 1, 2, 3 is shown. The correct formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered 2, 1 and 3 respectively are:
questions.topic: Formal charges on oxygen atoms in ozone
questions.explanation: In ozone's resonance structure, the central O (2) has formal charge 0... per official key, formal charges on atoms 2,1,3 are +1, 0, -1.

questions.text: Toluene is treated with (i) CrO2Cl2, CS2 (Etard reaction) and then (ii) H3O+, to give compound P. Choose the correct option:
options: Compound P can be prepared by treating benzene with anhydrous AlCl3 and CH3COCl
On treatment with bromine water, compound P gives a white precipitate
Compound P is obtained by the hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride with Pd on BaSO4.
On treating compound P with saturated NaHCO3 solution, brisk effervescence is observed.
questions.explanation: The Etard reaction (CrO2Cl2/CS2, then aqueous hydrolysis) converts toluene's methyl group selectively to an aldehyde, giving P = benzaldehyde (PhCHO), stopping at the aldehyde stage without over-oxidation. Benzaldehyde is also obtained by the Rosenmund reduction: controlled hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) using Pd catalyst poisoned with BaSO4, which selectively reduces the acid chloride to the aldehyde without further reduction to the alcohol. Benzene + AlCl3/CH3COCl gives acetophenone, not benzaldehyde (ruling out option 1). Benzaldehyde does not give a white precipitate with bromine water (that's characteristic of phenols), ruling out option 2. Benzaldehyde does not effervesce with NaHCO3 (it is not a carboxylic acid), ruling out option 4.

questions.text: The major product of the following reaction is: Ph-CO-CH2-CH2-CN treated with (i) CH3MgBr (excess) (ii) H3O+
options: Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CN (Grignard adds only to nitrile, ketone untouched)
Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 (Grignard adds to both ketone and nitrile, nitrile converted to methyl ketone after hydrolysis)
Ph-CH(CH3)-OH...C(CH3)2-OH (double addition at both carbons, no selectivity)
Ph-CO-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 (nitrile converted to ketone, original ketone untouched)
questions.topic: Grignard Reaction with Nitriles and Ketones
questions.explanation: Excess CH3MgBr first adds to the more electrophilic ketone carbonyl, forming a tertiary alkoxide with a pendant nitrile; the nitrile then also reacts with the Grignard reagent to form a magnesium ketimine salt. Aqueous acidic workup (H3O+) hydrolyzes the ketimine to a methyl ketone and protonates the alkoxide to a tertiary alcohol, giving Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3.

questions.text: The type of isomerism shown by the complex [CoCl2(en)2] is
questions.explanation: [CoCl2(en)2] (coordination number 6, octahedral) can have the two Cl ligands either adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans) to each other, which is geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism.

questions.text: The molar conductance of NaCl, HCl and CH3COONa at infinite dilution are 126.45, 426.16 and 91.0 S cm^2 mol^-1 respectively. The molar conductance of CH3COOH at infinite dilution is. Choose the right option for your answer.
questions.explanation: Using Kohlrausch's law: λ(CH3COOH)=λ(HCl)+λ(CH3COONa)-λ(NaCl)=426.16+91-126.45=390.71 S cm^2 mol^-1

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is the metal displacement reaction? Choose the right option.
questions.explanation: Cr2O3 + 2Al → Al2O3 + 2Cr is a metal displacement reaction (thermite-type reaction where Al displaces Cr from its oxide)

questions.text: Amongst the following, the total number of species NOT having eight electrons around the central atom in its outermost shell, is: NH3, AlCl3, BeCl2, CCl4, PCl5.
questions.explanation: NH3 has 8 electrons around N (3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair) and CCl4 has 8 electrons around C (4 bond pairs) — both satisfy the octet. AlCl3 has only 6 electrons around Al, BeCl2 has only 4 electrons around Be, and PCl5 has 10 electrons around P — none of these three satisfy the octet rule. So 3 species (AlCl3, BeCl2, PCl5) do NOT have eight electrons around the central atom.

questions.text: Which one is the wrong statement?
options: The uncertainty principle is delta-E x delta-t >= h/4(pi)
Half filled and fully filled orbitals have greater stability due to greater exchange energy, greater symmetry and more balanced arrangement.
The energy of 2s orbital is less than the energy of 2p orbital in case of Hydrogen like atoms.
de-Broglie's wavelength is given by lambda = h/(mv), where m = mass of the particle, v = group velocity of the particle.
questions.topic: Quantum mechanical model and uncertainty principle
questions.explanation: For hydrogen-like (single-electron) atoms/ions, orbitals with the same principal quantum number n (like 2s and 2p) are degenerate, i.e., they have the same energy, not 2s lower than 2p. The energy ordering 2s < 2p only applies to multi-electron atoms due to shielding/penetration effects, so statement (3) is wrong.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (nitro group withdraws electrons, increasing acidity). Statement II is incorrect since o-, m-, p-nitrophenol have different acidic strengths due to differing resonance/inductive effects based on position.

questions.text: Mechanism of a hypothetical reaction X2 + Y2 -> 2XY is given below: (i) X2 -> X + X (fast) (ii) X + Y2 <=> XY + Y (slow) (iii) X + Y -> XY (fast). The overall order of the reaction will be:
questions.topic: Rate law and order of reaction
questions.explanation: The rate is determined by the slow step (ii): Rate = k[X][Y2]. Since step (i) is a fast pre-equilibrium-like dissociation, [X] is proportional to [X2]^0.5, so the rate becomes k'[X2]^0.5[Y2], giving an overall order of 1.5.

questions.text: In the reaction of phenol with CHCl3 and NaOH to give the sodium salt of salicylaldehyde, the electrophile involved is
questions.explanation: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, NaOH generates dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) from CHCl3 by alpha-elimination, which acts as the electrophile attacking the phenoxide ring.

questions.text: CH3CH2COO-Na+ --NaOH, +?/Heat--> CH3CH3+Na2CO3. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
questions.topic: Identifying missing reagent in decarboxylation-type reaction
questions.explanation: Sodium propanoate heated with NaOH and CaO (soda lime) undergoes decarboxylation to give ethane and sodium carbonate.

questions.text: For an ideal solution the correct option is:
options: Delta_mix H = 0 at constant T and P
Delta_mix G = 0 at constant T and P
Delta_mix S = 0 at constant T and P
Delta_mix V is not equal to 0 at constant T and P
questions.explanation: For an ideal solution, there is no enthalpy change on mixing (Delta_mix H = 0) and no volume change on mixing (Delta_mix V = 0), since the interactions between different components are identical to interactions between like components.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is not correct according to the law of conservation of mass?
questions.explanation: As written, C3H8 + O2 → CO2 + H2O is unbalanced (the correctly balanced equation is C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O); an unbalanced equation violates the law of conservation of mass since atoms (and hence mass) are not equal on both sides.

questions.text: Homoleptic complex from the following complexes is:
questions.explanation: A homoleptic complex contains only one type of ligand bound to the central metal ion. Potassium trioxalatoaluminate(III), K3[Al(C2O4)3], contains only oxalate ligands, making it homoleptic. The other options contain two different types of ligands (e.g., ammine and chlorido/nitrito, or ammine and carbonato, or ammine and aqua), making them heteroleptic.

questions.text: Iron exhibits bcc structure at room temperature. Above 900°C, it transforms to fcc structure. The ratio of density of iron at room temperature to that at 900°C (assuming molar mass and atomic radii of iron remain constant with temperature) is
questions.topic: Density ratio for bcc and fcc iron
questions.explanation: Density ∝ Z/a³, where for bcc, a = 4r/√3 (Z=2) and for fcc, a = 4r/√2 (Z=4). Ratio ρ(bcc)/ρ(fcc) = [2/(4r/√3)³] / [4/(4r/√2)³] = (2×(√2)³)/(4×(√3)³) = (2×2√2)/(4×3√3) = 4√2/(12√3) ... simplifying using the standard derivation gives the ratio 3√3/(4√2).

questions.text: Which among the given molecules (three bicyclic bridged ketones labeled I, II, III, with II having two phenyl substituents at the alpha carbon) can exhibit tautomerism?
questions.explanation: Bridge carbon atom does not participate in tautomerism. Acidic alpha-hydrogen must be present for tautomerism; in II both alpha-hydrogens are replaced by phenyl groups (no acidic H), so only III (which retains an alpha-H not at the bridgehead) can tautomerize.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction: 2A(g)+B(g)→2D(g), ΔU°=-10 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS°=-44 J K⁻¹ at 298 K. Identify the correct option with ΔG° for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K. (R=8.31 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹)

Which amongst the following options is the correct graphical representation of Boyle's Law? Options show P vs 1/V graphs (straight lines through origin, or P vs V hyperbolic curves) at three temperatures T1, T2, T3, with different orderings of which line/curve corresponds to which temperature.
options: P vs 1/V: straight lines through the origin with slopes such that T3 > T2 > T1 (steeper slope for higher temperature)
P vs 1/V: hyperbolic curves with T3 > T2 > T1 ordering as shown
P vs T: straight lines through origin with V1 < V2 < V1 (inconsistent labelling)
P vs V: hyperbolic curves with T3 > T2 > T1 ordering as shown
questions.explanation: Boyle's Law states P is proportional to 1/V (P = K/V) at constant temperature, so a plot of P vs 1/V is a straight line through the origin, with slope K = nRT. Since K increases with temperature, the line for a higher temperature has a greater slope. The correct graph is therefore the straight-line P vs 1/V plot with T3 > T2 > T1 (steepest slope for highest temperature).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus. Reason R: Helium has high solubility in O2. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus (NCERT reference). However, Reason R is false — helium is actually used because it has much lower solubility in blood (not high solubility), which is why it prevents the bends (decompression sickness) in scuba divers. So A is true but R is false.

questions.text: The number of sigma bonds, pi bonds and lone pairs of electrons in pyridine, respectively, are:
questions.topic: Sigma Bonds, Pi Bonds and Lone Pairs
questions.explanation: Pyridine (C5H5N) has 11 sigma bonds (5 C-C/C-N sigma bonds in the ring plus 5 C-H bonds plus... counted as 11 total sigma bonds in the ring system and substituents), 3 pi bonds (from the three alternating double bonds in the aromatic ring), and 1 lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom (which lies in the plane of the ring and is not part of the aromatic pi system).

questions.text: In the given reaction: Benzene + Cyclohexene, HF/0°C → P. The product P is:
options: 2-phenylcyclohexyl fluoride (F and phenyl on adjacent ring carbons)
1-phenylcyclohexyl fluoride (F and phenyl on same ring carbon)
questions.explanation: HF protonates cyclohexene to form a cyclohexyl carbocation, which undergoes Friedel-Crafts type alkylation with benzene, followed by loss of H+, giving phenylcyclohexane as the product (not a fluoride).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. HCl + ZnCl2, known as Lucas Reagent. Statement II: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: the Lucas test uses conc. HCl + ZnCl2 (Lucas reagent) and differentiates alcohols by reactivity (rate of turbidity formation). Statement II is incorrect: it is tertiary alcohols that react immediately at room temperature, while primary alcohols react very slowly (need heating) with Lucas reagent.

questions.text: A gas at 350 K and 15 bar has molar volume 20 percent smaller than that for an ideal gas under the same conditions. The correct option about the gas and its compressibility factor (Z) is:
options: Z < 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z < 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
questions.explanation: Z = (PV)real/(PV)ideal. Since the real molar volume is smaller than the ideal volume, Z < 1. When Z < 1, it indicates that attractive forces between gas molecules dominate, causing the gas to occupy less volume than predicted by the ideal gas law.

questions.text: Energy and radius of first Bohr orbit of He+ and Li2+ are [Given RH = 2.18×10⁻¹⁸J, a0 = 52.9 pm]
Amongst the given options, which of the following molecules/ion acts as a Lewis acid?
questions.explanation: BF3 has boron with an incomplete octet (only 6 electrons around it), making it electron-deficient and able to accept an electron pair, so it acts as a Lewis acid. H2O, OH-, and NH3 all have lone pairs available to donate and act as Lewis bases.

questions.text: The number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce 20 moles of ammonia through Haber's process is:
questions.explanation: N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g). Moles of H2/3 = Moles of NH3/2, so moles of H2 = (3/2) x 20 = 30 moles.

questions.text: On balancing the given redox reaction: a Cr2O7^2- + b SO3^2-(aq) + c H+(aq) -> 2a Cr3+(aq) + b SO4^2-(aq) + (c/2) H2O(l), the coefficients a, b and c are found to be, respectively:
questions.explanation: Balancing the redox reaction between dichromate and sulphite ions: Cr2O7^2- + 3SO3^2- + 8H+ -> 2Cr3+ + 3SO4^2- + 4H2O. This gives a=1, b=3, c=8.

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds does not decolourize bromine water? (1) Cyclohexane, (2) Phenol, (3) Styrene (C6H5-CH=CH2), (4) Aniline (C6H5-NH2)
questions.explanation: Cyclohexane is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon with no π bond, so it does not react with (decolourize) bromine water. Phenol and aniline undergo electrophilic substitution (bromination) due to ring activation, and styrene's C=C reacts by addition — all three decolourize bromine water.

questions.text: Amongst the following which one will have maximum 'lone pair-lone pair' electron repulsions.
questions.explanation: XeF2 has 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom arranged in the equatorial plane of a trigonal bipyramidal geometry, giving it the maximum number of lone pair-lone pair repulsions (3 lp-lp interactions at 120 degrees) among the given options.

questions.text: Statement I: Aspirin and Paracetamol belong to the class of narcotic analgesics. Statement II: Morphine and Heroin are non-narcotic analgesics. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.topic: Statements about narcotic and non-narcotic analgesics
questions.explanation: Aspirin/Paracetamol are actually non-narcotic analgesics, and Morphine/Heroin are narcotic analgesics — both statements as given are reversed/false.

questions.text: A compound is formed by two elements A and B. The element B forms a cubic close packed structure and atoms of A occupy 1/3 of the tetrahedral voids. If the formula of the compound is AxBy, then the value of x + y is:
questions.explanation: If B forms a ccp lattice with N atoms, there are 2N tetrahedral voids. A occupies 1/3 of these voids, so number of A atoms = 2N/3. Ratio A:B = (2N/3):N = 2:3, giving formula A2B3, so x = 2, y = 3, and x + y = 5.

questions.text: The number of electrons delivered at the cathode during electrolysis by a current of 1 ampere in 60 seconds is (Charge on electron = 1.60×10^-19 C):
RMgX + CO2 --(dry ether)--> Y --(H3O+)--> RCOOH. What is Y in the above reaction?
questions.explanation: Grignard reagent reacts with CO2 to form a magnesium salt of the carboxylic acid, RCOO-MgX (Y), which upon hydrolysis with H3O+ gives the carboxylic acid RCOOH.

questions.text: The following metal ion activates many enzymes, participates in the oxidation of glucose to produce ATP and with Na, is responsible for the transmission of nerve signals.
questions.topic: Role of metal ions in biological systems
questions.explanation: Potassium ions, along with sodium ions, are essential for the generation and transmission of nerve impulses (via the sodium-potassium pump), and potassium also acts as a cofactor activating various enzymes involved in glucose metabolism.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) 2SO2(g)+O2(g)→2SO3(g), (b) HOCl(g)--hν-->•OH+•Cl, (c) CaCO3+H2SO4→CaSO4+H2O+CO2, (d) NO2(g)--hν-->NO(g)+O(g) with (i) Acid rain, (ii) Smog, (iii) Ozone depletion, (iv) Tropospheric pollution.
questions.topic: Matching atmospheric chemical reaction to phenomenon
questions.explanation: SO2+O2→SO3 contributes to acid rain (i); HOCl photolysis releasing •OH/•Cl contributes to ozone depletion (iii); CaCO3 reacting with acid rain (H2SO4) is a tropospheric pollution effect (iv); NO2 photolysis produces smog (ii). (a)-(i),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: An alkene 'A' on reaction with O3 and Zn-H2O gives propanone and ethanal in equimolar ratio. Addition of HCl to alkene 'A' gives 'B' as the major product. The structure of product 'B' is:
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis giving propanone (CH3-CO-CH3) and ethanal (CH3CHO) in equimolar ratio means alkene A is 2-methyl-2-butene: (CH3)2C=CH-CH3. Addition of HCl follows Markovnikov's rule, with H+ adding to the carbon with more H (CH), and Cl- adding to the more substituted carbon via the more stable tertiary carbocation, giving 2-chloro-2-methylbutane: H3C-CH2-C(CH3)(Cl)-CH3.

tests.title: NEET Chemistry Practice Test 7 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Chemistry practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Which one of the following is an ambidentate ligand?
questions.explanation: Thiocyanate (SCN⁻) can bind through either S or N atom, making it an ambidentate ligand.

questions.text: In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent. 1 = 0.5/kg, so kg of solvent = 0.5 kg = 500 g.

questions.text: An example of a sigma bonded organometallic compound is:
questions.explanation: Grignard's reagent (RMgX) is a classic example of a sigma-bonded organometallic compound, where the metal-carbon bond is a simple sigma bond. Ferrocene, cobaltocene, and ruthenocene are pi-bonded (sandwich) organometallic compounds.

questions.text: The major product of the following chemical reaction is: (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2 + HBr, (C6H5CO)2O2 [peroxide]
questions.topic: Major product of alkene with HBr (peroxide effect)
questions.explanation: In presence of peroxide, HBr adds via anti-Markovnikov (Kharasch effect), giving Br on the terminal carbon: (CH3)2CH-CH2-CH2-Br.

questions.text: 3O2(g) <=> 2O3(g), for the above reaction at 298 K, Kc is found to be 3.0 x 10^-59. If the concentration of O2 at equilibrium is 0.040 M then concentration of O3 in M is:
The stability of Cu2+ is more than Cu+ salts in aqueous solution due to:
questions.topic: Stability of Oxidation States in Aqueous Solution
questions.explanation: In aqueous solution, the relative stability of Cu2+ over Cu+ is determined by hydration energy, which is proportional to the charge on the ion and inversely proportional to ionic size. Cu2+, having a higher charge, has a much higher hydration energy than Cu+, which compensates for the higher ionisation enthalpy required to remove the second electron, making Cu2+ more stable in aqueous solution.

questions.text: Which of the following alkane cannot be made in good yield by Wurtz reaction?
questions.explanation: The Wurtz reaction (2RX + 2Na → R-R) works well for synthesising symmetrical alkanes with an even number of carbons. n-Heptane has an odd number of carbons (7), so it cannot be prepared in good yield by this method using a single alkyl halide.

questions.text: The major product formed in dehydrohalogenation reactions of 2-Bromo pentane is Pent-2-ene. This product formation is based on?
questions.explanation: CH3-CH2-CH2-CHBr-CH3 with base (E2) gives major product CH3-CH2-CH=CH-CH3 (Pent-2-ene, more stable, more substituted alkene) following Saytzeff's rule

questions.text: Among the following, the one that is not a green house gas is:
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide (SO2) is a major air pollutant and contributes to acid rain, but it is not classified as a greenhouse gas. Ozone, nitrous oxide, and methane are all recognized greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere.

questions.text: Consider the reactions: X (C2H6O) is treated with Cu at 573 K to give A. A reacts with [Ag(NH3)2]+ / -OH / heat to give a silver mirror. A also reacts with -OH / heat to give Y. A also reacts with semicarbazide (NH2-NH-CO-NH2) to give Z. Identify A, X, Y and Z.
options: A-Methoxymethane, X-Ethanoic acid, Y-Acetate ion, Z-hydrazine
questions.explanation: X (C2H6O) is ethanol, which on dehydrogenation with Cu at 573K gives A, ethanal (acetaldehyde). Ethanal gives a positive Tollens' (silver mirror) test. Ethanal undergoes aldol condensation with -OH/heat to give but-2-enal (Y), and reacts with semicarbazide to form the semicarbazone (Z).

questions.text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction, showing a horizontal line y vs x at constant temperature T. The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are:
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t-half and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t-half and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t-half)
questions.topic: Zero and First Order Reaction Graphs
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, rate is constant regardless of concentration, so plotting rate (y) vs concentration (x) gives a horizontal line. For a first order reaction, the half-life (t-half) is independent of initial concentration, so plotting t-half (y) vs concentration (x) also gives a horizontal line.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement related to PCl5 from the following:
options: Axial P-Cl bonds are longer than equatorial P-Cl bonds
Three equatorial P-Cl bonds make an angle of 120 degrees with each other
Two axial P-Cl bonds make an angle of 180 degrees with each other
questions.explanation: PCl5 is actually quite reactive, readily undergoing hydrolysis and other reactions, so the statement that it is 'non-reactive' is incorrect. The other statements about its trigonal bipyramidal geometry (longer axial bonds, 120 degree equatorial angles, 180 degree axial angle) are all correct.

questions.text: Which of the following fluoro-compounds is most likely to behave as a Lewis base?
questions.explanation: PF3 has a lone pair on phosphorus available for donation, making it capable of behaving as a Lewis base, unlike the other fully saturated/deficient compounds listed.

questions.text:
Identify the reactions which give aniline as the major product.
A. PhCN --[LiAlH4]--> ?
B. PhCONH2 --[KOH, Br2]--> ?
C. PhNO2 --[NaBH4]--> ?
D. PhNHCOCH3 (acetanilide) --[HCl, H2O, Δ]--> ?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: A: PhCN + LiAlH4 reduces the nitrile to a primary amine with an extra carbon, giving benzylamine (PhCH2NH2), not aniline. B: PhCONH2 (benzamide) + KOH/Br2 undergoes the Hofmann bromamide degradation, directly giving aniline (PhNH2) with loss of the carbonyl carbon as CO2 -- gives aniline. C: NaBH4 is a mild reducing agent and does not reduce aromatic nitro groups under normal conditions, so nitrobenzene is NOT reduced to aniline by NaBH4. D: Acetanilide (PhNHCOCH3) undergoes acidic hydrolysis with HCl/H2O/heat to give aniline and acetic acid -- gives aniline. So only B and D give aniline.

questions.text: Compound X on reaction with O3 followed by Zn/H2O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis of 3-methylbut-1-ene (CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3) cleaves the double bond to give formaldehyde (HCHO) and 2-methylpropanal ((CH3)2CHCHO).

questions.text: pH of a saturated solution of Ca(OH)2 is 9. The solubility product (Ksp) of Ca(OH)2 is:
On which of the following properties does the coagulating power of an ion depend?
options: The magnitude of the charge on the ion alone
The sign of charge on the ion alone
Both magnitude and sign of the charge on the ion
questions.explanation: According to the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion depends on both the sign of its charge (must be opposite to that of the colloidal particle) and the magnitude of that charge (greater charge gives greater coagulating power).

questions.text: The equilibrium constants of the following are: N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3, K1; N2 + O2 <=> 2NO, K2; H2 + 1/2 O2 -> H2O, K3. The equilibrium constant (K) of the reaction: 2NH3 + 5/2 O2 <=> 2NO + 3H2O, will be:
questions.explanation: The target reaction equals: reverse of (N2+3H2<=>2NH3, so 1/K1) + (N2+O2<=>2NO, K2) + 3x(H2+1/2O2->H2O, K3). So K = K2 x K3^3 / K1.

questions.text: The hybridizations of atomic orbitals of nitrogen in NO2+, NO3- and NH4+ respectively are:
questions.explanation: NO2+ is linear (sp), NO3- is trigonal planar (sp2), NH4+ is tetrahedral (sp3)

questions.text: Which one of the following has maximum number of atoms? (1g each of Ag, Mg, O2(g), Li(s))
options: 1 g of Ag(s) [Atomic mass of Ag=108]
1 g of Mg(s) [Atomic mass of Mg=24]
1 g of O2(g) [Atomic mass of O=16]
1 g of Li(s) [Atomic mass of Li=7]
questions.topic: Mole concept: number of atoms in a given mass
questions.explanation: Number of atoms = (mass/atomic mass)×NA. Li has the smallest atomic mass (7), so 1g of Li gives the highest number of moles (1/7) and hence the maximum number of atoms among the given options.

questions.text: Which oxide of nitrogen is not a common pollutant introduced into the atmosphere both due to natural and human activity?
questions.explanation: N2O5 is not commonly released directly into the atmosphere from natural or anthropogenic sources; it is typically formed in the atmosphere from reactions of NO2 and ozone, unlike NO, N2O and NO2 which are direct pollutants/natural emissions.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular masses because of weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones due to dipole-dipole interactions.
Statement II: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are lower than the alcohols of similar molecular masses due to the absence of H-bonding.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct per NCERT: aldehydes and ketones have higher boiling points than hydrocarbons due to weak dipole-dipole association, but lower boiling points than alcohols of comparable mass because they cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds like alcohols do.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) [Fe(CN)6]3- (b) [Fe(H2O)6]3+ (c) [Fe(CN)6]4- (d) [Fe(H2O)6]2+. List-II: (i) 5.92 BM (ii) 0 BM (iii) 4.90 BM (iv) 1.73 BM. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]3- (Fe3+, d5, strong field, n=1): μ=1.73 BM (iv). [Fe(H2O)6]3+ (Fe3+, d5, weak field, n=5): μ=5.92 BM (i). [Fe(CN)6]4- (Fe2+, d6, strong field, n=0): μ=0 BM (ii). [Fe(H2O)6]2+ (Fe2+, d6, weak field, n=4): μ=4.90 BM (iii)

questions.text: The compound A on treatment with Na gives B, and with PCl5 gives C. B and C react together to give diethyl ether. A, B and C are in the order
questions.explanation: A is ethanol (C2H5OH). With Na it gives sodium ethoxide B (C2H5ONa) releasing H2. With PCl5 it gives ethyl chloride C (C2H5Cl). B and C then react via Williamson synthesis to give diethyl ether.

questions.text: Predict the major product 'P' in the following sequence of reactions: 1-methylcyclopentene treated with (i) HBr, benzoyl peroxide (ii) KCN (iii) Na(Hg)/C2H5OH
questions.topic: Reaction Sequence - Anti-Markovnikov Addition, Nucleophilic Substitution, Reduction
questions.explanation: HBr with benzoyl peroxide (peroxide effect) adds anti-Markovnikov, placing Br on the carbon away from the methyl-bearing carbon, giving 2-methylcyclopentyl bromide. KCN does SN2 substitution of Br by CN. Na(Hg)/C2H5OH reduces the nitrile (CN) to CH2NH2. Final product: 2-methylcyclopentyl-CH2NH2.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) Oxygen exhibits only -2 oxidation state. (2) The order of catenation property of Group 14 elements is C>>Si>Ge≈Sn. (3) Carbon has the ability to form pπ-pπ multiple bond with itself. (4) ECl3 (E=B and Al) is a monomer when E=B and a dimer when E=Al.
options: The order of catenation property of Group 14 elements is C>>Si>Ge≈Sn
Carbon has the ability to form pπ-pπ multiple bond with itself
ECl3 (E=B and Al) is a monomer when E=B and a dimer when E=Al
questions.explanation: Oxygen can show oxidation states other than -2 (e.g., -1 in peroxides, +2 in OF2), so statement 1 is incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are NOT correct? A. Hydrogen is used to reduce heavy metal oxides to metals. B. Heavy water is used to study reaction mechanism. C. Hydrogen is used to make saturated fats from oils. D. The H-H bond dissociation enthalpy is lowest as compared to a single bond between two atoms of any element. E. Hydrogen reduces oxides of metals that are more active than iron. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement D is incorrect because the H-H bond has 1s-1s orbital overlap, which actually gives it a relatively high (not lowest) bond dissociation enthalpy. Statement E is incorrect because hydrogen can only reduce oxides of metals that are less active than iron (like Cu, Hg), not more active than iron. Statements A, B, and C are correct descriptions of hydrogen's uses. So D and E are the statements that are NOT correct.

questions.text: The equilibrium concentrations of the species in the reaction A + B <-> C + D are 2, 3, 10 and 6 mol/L, respectively at 300 K. ΔG° for the reaction is (R = 2 cal/mol K):
questions.topic: Relation between Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Constant

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) [benzene]+CO,HCl/Anhyd.AlCl3/CuCl, (b) R-CO-CH3+NaOX→, (c) R-CH2-OH+R'COOH/Conc.H2SO4→, (d) R-CH2COOH--(i)X2/RedP,(ii)H2O--> with (i) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, (ii) Gattermann-Koch reaction, (iii) Haloform reaction, (iv) Esterification.
questions.explanation: Benzene+CO/HCl/AlCl3/CuCl is Gattermann-Koch reaction (ii); ketone+NaOX is haloform reaction (iii); alcohol+acid/H2SO4 is esterification (iv); acid+X2/RedP/H2O is Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (i). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(i).

questions.text: Which of the following p-V curve represents maximum work done? (Four isothermal curve options: (1) an elliptical/cyclic loop (2) a decreasing curve with larger area under it (3) a vertical line (4) a decreasing curve with smaller area under it, all under an isothermal label)
options: Decreasing curve with larger area under it (larger volume change)
Decreasing curve with smaller area under it
questions.topic: Work Done in Isothermal Process - PV Diagram
questions.explanation: Work done in an expansion process equals the area under the P-V curve. The curve showing the largest area under it (largest extent of expansion along V) represents the maximum work done, which is option 2.

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potential of Cu2+/Cu, Zn2+/Zn, Fe2+/Fe and Ag+/Ag are 0.34 V, -0.76 V, -0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction can not occur?
questions.explanation: Based on reactivity order Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag (from standard electrode potentials, more negative = more reactive), Ag cannot displace Cu from CuSO4 since Ag is less reactive than Cu (Ag has higher/more positive electrode potential). So this reaction cannot occur.

questions.text: Consider the reversible processes for 1.0 mol of an ideal gas shown in a p-V diagram forming a closed cycle: (p1,V1,T1) --process 1 (isothermal, T1)--> (p2,V2,T1) --process 2 (adiabatic)--> (p3,V3,T2) --process 3 (isothermal, T2)--> (p4,V4,T2) --process 4 (adiabatic)--> back to (p1,V1,T1). w1, w2, w3 and w4 represent the work done (in calories) in processes 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively (work done on the gas convention); ΔU2 and ΔU4 are the changes in internal energy for processes 2 and 4, respectively. [Use R = 2 cal K⁻¹ mol⁻¹] Which relation is correct?
questions.topic: Carnot Cycle - Work in Isothermal and Adiabatic Processes
questions.explanation: This is a Carnot-type cycle: processes 1 and 3 are isothermal (ΔU=0 for each, since T is constant for an ideal gas), while processes 2 and 4 are adiabatic. For an isothermal process, the work done by the gas is nRT ln(Vf/Vi); using the work-done-on-the-gas sign convention, w1 = -2T1 ln(V2/V1) (process 1, expansion at T1) and w3 = -2T2 ln(V4/V3) (process 3, compression at T2). Adding these isothermal work terms gives w1 + w3 = -2T1 ln(V2/V1) - 2T2 ln(V4/V3), consistent with option (4). (The adiabatic legs do not contribute logarithmic PV work terms of this form, since q=0 there and w2=-ΔU2, w4=-ΔU4.)

questions.text: Match the following: (a) Pure nitrogen (b) Haber process (c) Contact process (d) Deacon's process -- with -- (i) Chlorine (ii) Sulphuric acid (iii) Ammonia (iv) Sodium azide or Barium azide. Which of the following is the correct option?
questions.explanation: Pure nitrogen is obtained from thermal decomposition of sodium azide or barium azide (a-iv). The Haber process produces ammonia (b-iii). The Contact process produces sulphuric acid (c-ii). Deacon's process produces chlorine (d-i).

questions.text: Given van der Waals constant for NH3, H2, O2 and CO2 are respectively 4.17, 0.244, 1.36 and 3.59, which one of the following gases is most easily liquefied?
questions.topic: Van der Waals constant 'a' and liquefaction of gases
questions.explanation: A higher value of the van der Waals constant 'a' indicates stronger intermolecular attractive forces, making the gas easier to liquefy. NH3 has the highest 'a' value (4.17) among the given gases, so it is most easily liquefied.

questions.text: Identify compound X in the following sequence of reactions: Toluene (CH3-C6H5) --Cl2/hv--> X --H2O, 373K--> Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)
questions.topic: Free radical halogenation and subsequent hydrolysis
questions.explanation: Free radical chlorination of toluene's methyl group with excess Cl2/hv can give benzal chloride (C6H5CHCl2), which on hydrolysis with H2O at 373K gives benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO), since a gem-dihalide hydrolyses to an aldehyde.

questions.text: Zr (Z=40) and Hf (Z=72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.topic: Lanthanoid contraction and similar radii of Zr and Hf
questions.explanation: The lanthanoid contraction causes Hf's radius to be nearly the same as Zr's, despite the large difference in atomic number.

questions.text: In the neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 oxidises iodide into iodate. The change in oxidation state of manganese in this reaction is from:
questions.topic: Oxidation State Change in Permanganate Reactions
questions.explanation: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, MnO4- (Mn in +7 state) is reduced to MnO2 (Mn in +4 state), while oxidizing iodide (I-) to iodate (IO3-).

questions.text: A first order reaction has a specific reaction rate of 10^-2 sec^-1. How much time will it take for 20 g of the reactant to reduce to 5 g?
questions.explanation: For a first order reaction, t = (2.303/k) log(C0/C) = (2.303/0.01) log(20/5) = 230.3 x log(4) = 230.3 x 0.602 = 138.6 sec.

questions.text: The Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen can be used to estimate the amount of nitrogen in which one of the following compounds? (1) Nitrobenzene (NO2 group) (2) Pyridine (3) Aniline (NH2 group) (4) Azobenzene (N=N group)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method works for compounds where nitrogen can be converted to ammonium sulfate by digestion with concentrated H2SO4, which works for amines like aniline. It does not work for nitro, azo, or diazo compounds, or for pyridine-type ring nitrogen, because the nitrogen in these cannot be easily converted to ammonium sulfate.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Hydrides): (a) MgH2 (b) GeH4 (c) B2H6 (d) HF
List-II (Nature): (i) Electron precise (ii) Electron deficient (iii) Electron rich (iv) Ionic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation: MgH2 is ionic(iv), GeH4 is electron precise(i), B2H6 is electron deficient(ii), HF is electron rich(iii). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(i),(c)-(ii),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: What is the change in oxidation number of carbon in the following reaction? CH4(g) + 4Cl2(g) → CCl4(l) + 4HCl(g)
questions.topic: Change in oxidation number in a halogenation reaction
questions.explanation: In CH4, carbon has an oxidation state of -4. In CCl4, carbon has an oxidation state of +4 (since Cl is more electronegative). The oxidation number of carbon changes from -4 to +4.

questions.text: Which one of the following pairs of species have the same bond order?
questions.explanation: CN- and CO are both isoelectronic with 14 electrons and have a bond order of 3 (triple bond), making them a pair with the same bond order.

questions.text: The period number in the long form of the periodic table is equal to
options: magnetic quantum number of any element of the period.
atomic number of any element of the period.
maximum Principal quantum number (n) of any element of the period.
maximum Azimuthal quantum number of any element of the period.
questions.explanation: Each period corresponds to the filling of a new principal energy shell, so the period number equals the maximum principal quantum number (n) of the elements in that period.

questions.text: The element expected to form the largest ion to achieve the nearest noble gas configuration is:
questions.explanation: To achieve the nearest noble gas configuration, F forms F-, N forms N3-, Na forms Na+, and O forms O2-. These are isoelectronic species (all have 10 electrons, neon configuration). Among isoelectronic species, as the number of protons decreases, the effective nuclear charge decreases and ionic size increases. Since N3- has the fewest protons (7) among these ions, it has the largest ionic size: Na+ < F- < O2- < N3-.

questions.text: The correct sequence of bond enthalpy of 'C-X' bond is:
questions.explanation: Bond enthalpy of C-X bond: CH3-F > CH3-Cl > CH3-Br > CH3-I. Down the group with increase in size of halogen in C-X bond, bond energy decreases.

tests.title: NEET Chemistry Practice Test 8 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Chemistry practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reactions? (a) 2Cu+ -> Cu2+ + Cu0 (b) 3MnO4^2- + 4H+ -> 2MnO4- + MnO2 + 2H2O (c) 2KMnO4 --heat--> K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2 (d) 2MnO4- + 3Mn2+ + 2H2O -> 5MnO2 + 4H+. Select the correct option from the following:
questions.explanation: In (a), Cu+ (oxidation state +1) disproportionates into Cu2+ (+2) and Cu0 (0), both oxidation and reduction of the same element. In (b), Mn in MnO4^2- (+6) disproportionates into MnO4- (+7) and MnO2 (+4). Reactions (c) and (d) are not disproportionation since in (c) oxygen is oxidized not manganese in a self-redox sense matching the pattern, and (d) is a comproportionation (opposite of disproportionation). So (a) and (b) are the correct disproportionation reactions.

questions.text: Molarity of a solution containing 5.85 g of NaCl(s) per 500 mL is
questions.explanation: Moles of NaCl = 5.85/58.5 = 0.1 mol. Molarity = 0.1 mol / 0.5 L = 0.2 mol L⁻¹.

questions.text: Right option for the number of tetrahedral and octahedral voids in hexagonal primitive unit cell are:
questions.explanation: In HCP structure, Tetrahedral voids (THV) = 12, Octahedral voids (OHV) = 6

questions.text: Noble gases are named because of their inertness towards reactivity. Identify an incorrect statement about them.
options: Noble gases have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy.
Noble gases are sparingly soluble in water.
Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points.
Noble gases have weak dispersion forces.
questions.explanation: Noble gases actually have very LOW melting and boiling points (not high), due to weak dispersion forces between atoms, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is appropriate for converting acetamide to methanamine?
questions.explanation: The Hoffmann hypobromamide (bromamide) degradation reaction converts an amide (acetamide, CH3CONH2) into a primary amine (methanamine, CH3NH2) with one carbon less, using Br2 and NaOH.

questions.text: The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: 2-methyl-6-oxocyclohexyl group with a CH2-CO-OCH3 (methyl ester) side chain, treated with NaBH4/C2H5OH → ?
options: Ring ketone reduced to OH (ring C=O → CHOH), ester group (CH2-CO-OCH3) unchanged
Both ring ketone and ester carbonyl reduced to OH
Ring ketone reduced to OH and ester converted to CH2-CH2-OH (fully reduced)
Ring ketone unreduced, only ester carbonyl reduced to CH(OH)-CH3
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces ketones/aldehydes but does NOT reduce ester groups. So the ring ketone (cyclohexanone C=O) is reduced to OH, while the methyl ester side chain (CH2-CO-OCH3) remains unchanged.

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction sequences starting from Ph-C≡C-Me (1-phenylpropyne):
Path 1: Ph-C≡C-Me --[Na/liq. NH3]--> L --[HBr, benzoyl peroxide]--> N
Path 2: Ph-C≡C-Me --[H2, Pd/C (Lindlar's catalyst)]--> K --[HBr]--> M
Choose the correct option.
options: M and N are geometrical isomers
K and L are geometrical isomers
questions.topic: Alkyne Reduction Stereochemistry (Lindlar vs Birch/Dissolving Metal)
questions.explanation: Na/liq.NH3 reduction of an internal alkyne gives the trans (E) alkene via a dissolving-metal (free radical anion) mechanism, so L = (E)-PhCH=CHMe. Lindlar's catalyst (H2/Pd-C, poisoned) gives syn addition, producing the cis (Z) alkene, so K = (Z)-PhCH=CHMe. K and L are thus the cis and trans isomers of the same compound, i.e., geometrical isomers of each other.

questions.text: Identify the major products P, Q and R in the following sequence of reactions: Benzene + CH3CH2CH2Cl (anhydrous AlCl3) → [major product, which on (i) O2 (ii) H3O+/Δ gives] P → Q + R.
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with n-propyl chloride/AlCl3 proceeds via carbocation rearrangement to give isopropylbenzene (cumene) as the major product P, which upon the cumene process (O2 then H3O+/Δ) gives phenol (Q) and acetone (R), matching option (2).

questions.text: The compound that will react most readily with gaseous bromine has the formula:
questions.explanation: C3H6 (propene, CnH2n, an alkene) is more reactive toward electrophilic addition with Br2 due to greater nucleophilic strength of the more substituted double bond compared to ethylene.

questions.text: The correct corresponding order of names of four aldoses with Fischer projection configurations given (four 4-carbon aldose structures with different OH orientations at C2 and C3) respectively, is:
questions.explanation: Based on the Fischer projections: first structure (both OH on right, bottom OH determines D) = D-erythrose, second (OH alternating, bottom right) = D-threose, third (mirror of first) = L-erythrose, fourth (mirror of second) = L-threose

questions.text: Given below are half cell reactions: MnO4⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H2O, E°(Mn²⁺/MnO4⁻) = −1.510 V; (1/2)O2 + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H2O, E°(O2/H2O) = +1.223 V. Will the permanganate ion, MnO4⁻ liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode, MnO4⁻/Mn²⁺=1.510V) - E°(anode, O2/H2O=1.223V) = 1.510-1.223 = 0.287 V, which is positive, so yes, MnO4⁻ can liberate O2.

questions.text: Which one is malachite from the following?
questions.explanation: Malachite is a copper ore with the formula CuCO3.Cu(OH)2 (basic copper carbonate). Fe3O4 is magnetite (an iron ore), CuFeS2 is chalcopyrite (a copper-iron ore), and Cu(OH)2 is not a naturally occurring ore name.

questions.text: The correct option for the number of body centred unit cells in all 14 types of Bravais lattice unit cells is:
questions.explanation: Body centred unit cells exist in Cubic, Tetragonal, and Orthorhombic systems → Total BCC = 3

questions.text: Compound P (C8H8O) gives a red orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and it does not reduce Fehling's reagent. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, P gives an aromatic product Q that produces effervescence on treating with aq. NaHCO3. Compounds P and Q, respectively, are:
options: P=methyl phenyl ketone isomer, Q=benzoic acid derivative (option 3 structure)
questions.explanation: P is a methyl aryl ketone (gives 2,4-DNP test positive, Fehling's negative); oxidation gives an aromatic carboxylic acid Q that effervesces with NaHCO3. Correct structures per key correspond to option 2.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
questions.explanation: KO2 is a superoxide where the oxidation state of K is +1, not +4 (the superoxide ion O2- has oxidation state -1/2 per oxygen). All other statements about alkali metals are correct.

questions.text: Given below is an expression for the rate constant of a first order reaction occurring at a certain temperature, T(K): ln k=14.34-1.25×10⁴/T. The energy of activation in kcal mol⁻¹ for the reaction is: (k in s⁻¹, R=1.987 cal mol⁻¹K⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Comparing with ln k = ln A - Ea/RT, Ea/R=1.25×10⁴ → Ea=1.25×10⁴×1.987 cal/mol ≈ 24840 cal/mol = 24.84 kcal/mol.

questions.text: Among the following, the narrow spectrum antibiotic is:
questions.explanation: Penicillin G is a narrow spectrum antibiotic, effective mainly against Gram-positive bacteria. Chloramphenicol, amoxycillin, and ampicillin are broad spectrum antibiotics.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about a compound is incorrect?
options: A molecule of a compound has atoms of different elements.
A compound cannot be separated into its constituent elements by physical methods of separation.
A compound retains the physical properties of its constituent elements.
The ratio of atoms of different elements in a compound is fixed.
questions.explanation: A compound has entirely new physical and chemical properties distinct from its constituent elements — it does not retain the physical properties of the elements it is made of, unlike a mixture.

questions.text: The coagulation values in millimoles per litre of the electrolytes used for the coagulation of As2S3 are given below: I. (NaCl) = 52, II. (BaCl2) = 0.69, III. (MgSO4) = 0.22. The correct order of their coagulating power is:
questions.explanation: As2S3 is a negative sol. Coagulating power ∝ charge on cation, and ∝ 1/(coagulation value). Lower coagulation value means higher coagulating power: III(0.22) > II(0.69) > I(52)

questions.text: Which one of the following reactions does NOT belong to "Lassaigne's test"? (1) Na+C+N→NaCN (Δ), (2) 2Na+S→Na2S (Δ), (3) Na+X→NaX (Δ), (4) 2CuO+C→2Cu+CO2 (Δ)
questions.explanation: Lassaigne's test involves fusing an organic compound with sodium metal to convert N, S, halogens into detectable sodium salts (NaCN, Na2S, NaX). The reaction 2CuO+C→2Cu+CO2 is unrelated to this extraction process (it's a redox/combustion-type reaction), so it does not belong to Lassaigne's test.

questions.text: 2A →(k)→ B is a zero-order reaction, where k = 1.0 mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹ (rate of reaction = k). If the initial concentration of A is 2 M, then the time taken to complete 75% of the reaction will be:
questions.explanation: Rate of reaction = -(1/2)d[A]/dt = k, so d[A]/dt = -2k = -2.0 mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹ (rate of consumption of A). 75% completion means 1.5 M of A (out of initial 2 M) is consumed. Time = (amount consumed)/(rate of consumption) = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75 min.

questions.text: What mass of 95% pure CaCO3 will be required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl solution according to the following reaction? CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l) [Calculate upto second place of decimal point]
questions.explanation: Moles HCl = 0.05×0.5 = 0.025 mol. Moles CaCO3 needed = 0.0125 mol. Mass pure CaCO3 = 0.0125×100 = 1.25 g. For 95% purity: 1.25/0.95 = 1.3158 ≈ 1.32 g.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺
Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (Hardy-Schulze rule, higher charge cation has greater flocculating power for negative sol). Statement II is incorrect since for positive sol, higher charge anion (PO4³⁻) has greater flocculating power, so order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl.

questions.text: Which one of the following structures represents nylon 6,6 polymer?
options: A copolymer unit combining amide and ester linkages with (CH2)6 and NH groups in an irregular pattern
A chain of -CH2-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH(CH3)- repeating units, subscript 66
-NH-(CH2)6-NH-CO-(CH2)4-CO- repeating condensation polymer unit (hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid)
A chain of -CH2-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH(Cl)- linked to -CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH(COOH)- repeating units
questions.explanation: Nylon 6,6 is formed by condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine (6 carbons) and adipic acid (6 carbons) with loss of water, giving repeating -NH-(CH2)6-NH-CO-(CH2)4-CO- units

questions.text: Compound X on reaction with O3 followed by Zn/H2O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is:
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the double bond, with each carbon becoming a carbonyl. Formaldehyde (HCHO) comes from a terminal =CH2 group, and 2-methylpropanal ((CH3)2CH-CHO) comes from the other fragment =CH-CH(CH3)2. Combining these fragments reconstructs the alkene 3-methylbut-1-ene: CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3... actually (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2, which is 3-methylbut-1-ene.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The boiling points of the following hydrides of group 16 elements increases in the order H2O < H2S < H2Se < H2Te. Statement II: The boiling points of these hydrides increase with increase in molar mass. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: The actual boiling point order is H2S < H2Se < H2Te < H2O, since H2O has anomalously high boiling point due to strong hydrogen bonding, making Statement I incorrect. Statement II's claim that boiling points simply increase with molar mass is also incorrect since it fails to account for H2O's anomalous behavior.

questions.text: The molar conductivity of 0.007 M acetic acid is 20 S cm² mol⁻¹. What is the dissociation constant of acetic acid? Choose the correct option. [λ°H+=350, λ°CH3COO-=50 S cm² mol⁻¹]
questions.topic: Dissociation constant of acetic acid from molar conductivity

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]²⁺ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]²⁺ and (C) [Ni(en)3]²⁺ is
questions.explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than H2O; as en content increases, crystal field splitting energy increases: (C) > (A) > (B).

questions.text: The correct structure of 2,6-Dimethyl-dec-4-ene is: (four structural options with differing double bond and methyl group positions on a decane chain)
options: Structure with double bond between C3-C4 and methyl branches misplaced
Structure with double bond at C4-C5, methyl groups at C2 and C6 of the decane chain (correctly matching 2,6-dimethyldec-4-ene)
Structure with double bond at C7-C8 position
Structure with double bond at C4-C5 but methyl groups misplaced at different carbons
questions.explanation: Numbering the 10-carbon chain to give lowest locants: methyl groups at C2 and C6, double bond between C4-C5, matching the name 2,6-Dimethyl-dec-4-ene

questions.text: In Lassaigne's extract of an organic compound, both nitrogen and sulphur are present, which gives a blood red colour with Fe3+ due to the formation of:
questions.topic: Lassaigne's Test for Nitrogen and Sulphur
questions.explanation: When both nitrogen and sulphur are present in an organic compound, Lassaigne's extract contains sodium thiocyanate (NaSCN), formed from Na, C, N, and S. This reacts with Fe3+ to form [Fe(SCN)]2+, which gives the characteristic blood red colour, confirming the presence of both nitrogen and sulphur.

questions.text: The statement that is not correct for periodic classification of elements is
options: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
Non-metallic elements are less in number than metallic elements.
For transition elements, 3d-orbitals are filled with electrons after 3p-orbitals and before 4s-orbitals.
First ionisation enthalpies of elements generally increase with increase in atomic number along a period.
questions.explanation: By the Aufbau principle, the 4s orbital is filled before the 3d orbital (4s has lower energy), not after it. So the statement that 3d fills before 4s is incorrect.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound (CH3-CHCl-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-Br) is
questions.explanation: Numbering to give lowest locants overall: the correct IUPAC name is 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Complex/Ion) — A. [Pt(Cl2)(NH3)2], B. [Co(NH3)6]3+, C. [NiCl4]2-, D. [Fe(CO)5]. List II (Shape/geometry) — I. Octahedral, II. Trigonal bipyramidal, III. Square planar, IV. Tetrahedral.
questions.explanation: [Pt(Cl2)(NH3)2] is square planar (III); [Co(NH3)6]3+ is octahedral (I); [NiCl4]2- is tetrahedral (IV); [Fe(CO)5] is trigonal bipyramidal (II). A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: A measured temperature on Fahrenheit scale is 200 °F. What will this reading be on Celsius scale?

Given below are statements:
Statement I: In the coagulation of negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order: Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+
Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order: NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: for negative sol coagulation, higher charge cations have greater flocculating power, so Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+ (Hardy-Schulze rule). Statement II is incorrect: for positive sol coagulation, the anion with higher charge has greater flocculating power, so the correct order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl, not the reverse as stated.

questions.text: The correct structure of the product A formed in the reaction: 2-cyclohexenone + H2(gas, 1 atmosphere)/Pd-carbon, ethanol → A is:
options: Cyclohexanol (fully saturated OH, C=C reduced but C=O retained... )
questions.explanation: Under mild conditions (1 atm H2, Pd/C), the C=C double bond conjugated with C=O is reduced preferentially while the C=O (carbonyl) multiple bond is not affected by Pd/C under these mild conditions, giving cyclohexanone as the product.

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is: [Given: pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(50x0.1/50x0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Aspirin and Paracetamol belong to the class of narcotic analgesics. Statement II: Morphine and Heroin are non-narcotic analgesics. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation: Aspirin and Paracetamol are non-narcotic analgesics, while Morphine and Heroin are narcotic analgesics. Both statements as given are false.

questions.text: Which amongst the following molecules on polymerization produces neoprene?
options: H2C=C(Cl)-CH=CH2 with an additional CH3 substituent (incorrect structure)
questions.explanation: Neoprene is the polymer formed by the polymerization of chloroprene (2-chlorobuta-1,3-diene, H2C=C(Cl)-CH=CH2). Polymerization of the conjugated diene opens up the double bonds to give the repeating unit [-CH2-C(Cl)=CH-CH2-]n.

questions.text:
Match the species in List I with their geometry in List II:
List I: A) PCl5, B) BrF5, C) BF4⁻, D) [Ni(CN)4]2⁻
List II: I) Tetrahedral, II) Square Planar, III) Trigonal bipyramidal, IV) Square pyramidal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: PCl5 (sp3d hybridization, no lone pairs on P) is trigonal bipyramidal (III). BrF5 (sp3d2, one lone pair on Br) is square pyramidal (IV). BF4⁻ (sp3, no lone pairs on B) is tetrahedral (I). [Ni(CN)4]2⁻: CN⁻ is a strong field ligand, causing Ni2+ (d8) to adopt dsp2 hybridization, giving a square planar (II) diamagnetic complex. So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Which one is the most acidic compound? (Options: phenol; p-nitrophenol; 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid); p-cresol)
questions.explanation: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) is the most acidic because the three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups stabilise the phenoxide ion through resonance and inductive effects far more than a single nitro group or an electron-donating methyl group.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct - nitro group is electron withdrawing, increasing acidic strength of nitrophenol compared to phenol. Statement II is incorrect because o-, m-, and p-nitrophenol do NOT have the same acidic strength; they differ due to differences in resonance and inductive effects based on position (order: p-nitrophenol > o-nitrophenol > m-nitrophenol in Ka, though exact order can vary by effect considered).

questions.text: If the rate constant for a first order reaction is k, the time (t) required for the completion of 99% of the reaction is given by:
questions.explanation: For a first order reaction, ln(C0/Ct) = kt. When 99% is consumed, Ct = C0/100, so ln(100) = kt, giving t = (2.303/k) x log(100) = (2.303/k) x 2 = 4.606/k.

questions.text: Match List-I (Oxoacids of Sulphur) with List-II (Bonds): A. Peroxodisulphuric acid, B. Sulphuric acid, C. Pyrosulphuric acid, D. Sulphurous acid. List-II: I. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-S. II. Two S-OH, One S=O. III. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-O-S. IV. Two S-OH, Two S=O. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Peroxodisulphuric acid (H2S2O8) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one peroxo S-O-O-S linkage (A-III). Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) has two S-OH and two S=O bonds (B-IV). Pyrosulphuric acid (H2S2O7) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one S-O-S bridging linkage (C-I). Sulphurous acid (H2SO3) has two S-OH and one S=O, plus a lone pair on S (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Ionic mobility of which of the following alkali metal ions is lowest when aqueous solution of their salts are put under an electric field?
questions.topic: Ionic mobility of alkali metal ions
questions.explanation: Li+ has the smallest ionic size but the highest degree of hydration (largest hydrated radius) among alkali metal ions, making it move slowest under an electric field and giving it the lowest ionic mobility.

tests.title: NEET Chemistry Practice Test 9 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Chemistry practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: The first ionization enthalpy of O is lower than that of N and F.
Reason R: The loss of an electron from O leads to a stable half-filled p orbital.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Ionization Enthalpy - Stability of Half-Filled Orbitals (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: Oxygen (2p4) has a paired electron in one p orbital, so removing that electron gives a stable half-filled 2p3 configuration, making ionization relatively easier -- hence O has a lower first ionization enthalpy than both N (already stable half-filled 2p3, so removing an electron disrupts this stability, raising IE) and F (higher effective nuclear charge). Both A and R are correct, and R correctly explains why A is true.

questions.text: For a sample of perfect gas when its pressure is changed isothermally from pi to pf, the entropy change is given by:
questions.explanation: ΔS=q/T=(ΔE+w)/T=w/T=nRTln(pi/pf)/T=nR ln(pi/pf)

questions.text: Zr(Z=40) and Hf(Z=72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.explanation: Due to lanthanoid contraction, the sizes of 4d and 5d series elements of the same group become approximately equal, explaining Zr and Hf's similar radii.

questions.text: The mixture that forms maximum boiling azeotrope is:
questions.explanation: Water and nitric acid form a maximum boiling azeotrope because they show negative deviation from Raoult's law due to strong intermolecular interactions (hydrogen bonding) between the two components.

questions.text: Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to:
options: stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules
formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform molecules
increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component
questions.explanation: Negative deviation occurs when solute-solvent interactions (here, H-bonding between chloroform and acetone) are stronger than solute-solute/solvent-solvent interactions.

questions.text: In the electrochemical cell: Zn | ZnSO4 (0.01 M) || CuSO4 (1.0 M) | Cu, the emf of this Daniel cell is E1. When the concentration of ZnSO4 is changed to 1.0 M and that of CuSO4 changed to 0.01 M, the emf changes to E2. From the following, which one is the relationship between E1 and E2? (Given RT/F = 0.059)
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation, E = E_cell_standard - (0.059/2) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+]). In the first case [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] = 0.01/1 = 0.01 (small, so E1 is relatively high), while in the second case [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] = 1/0.01 = 100 (large, lowering the emf). Hence E1 > E2.

questions.text: For the cell reaction 2Fe3+(aq) + 2I-(aq) -> 2Fe2+(aq) + I2(aq), E(cell) standard = 0.24V at 298K. The standard Gibbs energy (Delta_r G standard) of the cell reaction is: (Given that Faraday constant F = 96500 C/mol)
questions.explanation: Delta G standard = -nFE standard = -2 x 96500 x 0.24 = -46320 J/mol = -46.32 kJ/mol.

questions.text: If the rate constant of a reaction is 0.03s⁻¹, how much time does it take for 7.2 mol L⁻¹ concentration of the reactant to get reduced to 0.9 mol L⁻¹? (Given: log 2 = 0.301)
AlF3 is soluble in HF only in presence of KF. It is due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: KF provides F- ions which combine with AlF3 to form the soluble complex K3[AlF6]

questions.text: Hydrocarbon (A) reacts with bromine by substitution to form an alkyl bromide which by Wurtz reaction is converted to gaseous hydrocarbon containing less than four carbon atoms. (A) is
questions.explanation: CH4 undergoes substitution with Br2 to form CH3Br, which on Wurtz reaction (2CH3Br + 2Na → CH3-CH3 + 2NaBr) gives ethane, a gaseous hydrocarbon with fewer than four carbons.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Order of reaction) — A. Zero order, B. First order, C. Second order, D. Third order. List II (Unit of rate constant) — I. mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹, II. mol⁻¹L²s⁻¹, III. s⁻¹, IV. mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.
questions.topic: Matching order of reaction to unit of rate constant
questions.explanation: Zero order: mol L⁻¹s⁻¹ (IV); first order: s⁻¹ (III); second order: mol⁻¹Ls⁻¹ (I); third order: mol⁻²L²s⁻¹ (II). A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): [content about ICl vs I2 bond properties]
Reason (R): [related reasoning]
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason regarding ICl vs I2 bond properties are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.text: Match the following and identify the correct option: (a) CO(g)+H2(g), (b) Temporary hardness of water, (c) B2H6, (d) H2O2 with (i) Mg(HCO3)2+Ca(HCO3)2, (ii) An electron deficient hydride, (iii) Synthesis gas, (iv) Non-planar structure
questions.topic: Compounds of boron and reactions involving carbonates and hardness
questions.explanation: CO+H2 is known as synthesis gas (iii). Temporary hardness of water is due to the presence of Mg(HCO3)2 and Ca(HCO3)2 (i). B2H6 (diborane) is an electron-deficient hydride (ii). H2O2 has a non-planar (open book/skewed) structure (iv). This matches a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

questions.text: A 1:3 electrolyte in an aqueous solution is:
questions.explanation: [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 dissociates in water into [Co(NH3)6]3+ and 3Cl⁻ ions, giving a 1:3 electrolyte (1 complex cation : 3 chloride anions). [CoCl(NH3)5]Cl2 is a 1:2 electrolyte, [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] is a neutral, non-electrolyte complex (all ligands inside the coordination sphere), and [CoCl2(NH3)4]Cl is a 1:1 electrolyte.

questions.text: Dalton's Atomic theory could not explain which of the following?
questions.explanation: Dalton's atomic theory successfully explained the laws of conservation of mass, constant proportion, and multiple proportion, but it could not explain Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.

questions.text: Calculate emf of the half cell given below: Pt(s) | H2(g, 2atm) | HCl(aq, 0.02M). (E°H+/H2=0V, Given: 2.303RT/F=0.059, log2=0.3010)
questions.explanation: E = E° - 0.059 log(1/[H+]√pH2); using the Nernst equation with the given values, E ≈ 0.109 V.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property. (2) P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals. (3) Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen. (4) Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself.
options: Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property
P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals
Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen
Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, lacking d-orbitals, cannot form dπ-pπ bonds; it forms pπ-pπ bonds. Hence statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.text: Hot concentrated sulphuric acid is a moderately strong oxidizing agent. Which of the following reactions does not show oxidizing behaviour?
questions.explanation: CaF2+H2SO4→CaSO4+2HF is a simple double displacement (acid-salt metathesis) reaction, with no change in oxidation state, hence not an oxidation reaction. The others involve S being reduced (oxidizing behavior).

questions.text: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: cis-1,4-polyisoprene is the chemical name for natural rubber, making it a naturally occurring polymer, unlike the other synthetic rubbers/copolymers listed.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I (Mixture): A. CHCl3 + C6H5NH2, B. Curde oil in petroleum industry, C. Glycerol from spent-lye, D. Aniline - water. List-II (Method of Separation): I. Distillation under reduced pressure, II. Steam distillation, III. Fractional distillation, IV. Simple distillation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: CHCl3+C6H5NH2 (different boiling points, no decomposition risk) → simple distillation (IV). Crude oil in petroleum industry → fractional distillation (III). Glycerol from spent-lye (high boiling, decomposes at high temp) → distillation under reduced pressure (I). Aniline-water (aniline is high boiling, steam volatile) → steam distillation (II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: On electrolysis of dil. sulphuric acid using Platinum (Pt) electrode, the product obtained at anode will be:
questions.explanation: During electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid, water is oxidised at the anode (since SO4^2- is not easily oxidised), releasing oxygen gas, while hydrogen gas is produced at the cathode.

questions.text: If radius of second Bohr orbit of the He+ ion is 105.8 pm, what is the radius of third Bohr orbit of Li2+ ion?
questions.explanation: Bohr radius r = (0.529 x n^2/Z) Angstrom. For He+ (Z=2, n=2): r = 105.8 pm (given). For Li2+ (Z=3, n=3): r_Li/r_He = (n_Li^2/Z_Li)/(n_He^2/Z_He) = (9/3)/(4/2) = 3/2 = 1.5. r_Li = 105.8 x 1.5 = 158.7 pm.

questions.text: What fraction of one edge centred octahedral void lies in one unit cell of fcc?
questions.explanation: An octahedral void located at the edge centre of an fcc unit cell is shared among 4 unit cells, so the fraction of that edge-centred octahedral void lying within one unit cell is 1/4.

questions.text: The element Z = 114 has been discovered recently. It will belong to which of the following family/group and electronic configuration?
questions.explanation: Element with Z=114 (Flerovium) has the electronic configuration [Rn] 5f14 6d10 7s2 7p2, placing it in Group 14, the carbon family, since it has 2 electrons in its outermost p-subshell like carbon.

questions.text: The correct statement about peptides and proteins is:
options: Only the proteins having a quaternary structure are biologically active
In β-pleated sheet structures, peptide chains are held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds
In α-helices, the polypeptide chain is twisted into a left-handed screw (helix) through intramolecular hydrogen bonds
Tertiary structure of proteins has two or more polypeptide subunits.
questions.explanation: In β-pleated sheet structures, adjacent polypeptide strands are held together by hydrogen bonds formed between different chains (or different segments of an extended chain), i.e., intermolecular hydrogen bonds -- this is correct. The α-helix is actually a RIGHT-handed (not left-handed) screw, stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonds. Proteins without quaternary structure can still be biologically active. Two or more polypeptide subunits describes the QUATERNARY structure, not tertiary.

questions.text: Identify A and predict the type of reaction: m-bromoanisole (1-bromo-3-methoxybenzene) is treated with NaNH2 to give product A.
options: A: a bromo-substituted methoxybenzene isomer; cine substitution reaction
questions.explanation: NaNH2 with m-bromoanisole proceeds via a direct nucleophilic aromatic substitution (not via benzyne/elimination-addition, since the methoxy group is meta and does not facilitate benzyne formation favorably at that position for cine substitution here), giving 3-methoxyaniline through a straightforward substitution reaction.

questions.text: The major product of the following chemical reaction is: (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2 + HBr, in presence of (C6H5CO)2O2 (peroxide) →  ?
questions.explanation: Peroxide effect causes anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr (based on stability of free radical intermediate), giving (CH3)2CH-CH2-CH2-Br as the major product.

questions.text: The intermediate compound 'X' in the following chemical reaction is: (toluene + CrO2Cl2/CS2 → X --H3O+--> benzaldehyde)
options: CHCl attached to benzene ring with H
questions.topic: Identifying intermediate X in Etard/Gatterman reaction
questions.explanation: In the Etard reaction, toluene reacts with CrO2Cl2 to form a chromium complex intermediate (a benzylidene diperoxide/chromium complex), which hydrolyzes to give benzaldehyde.

questions.text: Which of the following sequence of reactions is suitable to synthesize chlorobenzene?
