questions.explanation: Chlorobenzene is best synthesized by direct electrophilic aromatic substitution: benzene reacting with Cl2 in the presence of anhydrous FeCl3 (Lewis acid catalyst), which generates the Cl+ electrophile for substitution onto the ring.

questions.text: The molar conductivity of a 0.5 mol/dm3 solution of AgNO3 with electrolytic conductivity of 5.76×10^-3 S cm^-1 at 298 K is:

Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of polarity:
A. CH3CH2OCH2CH3
B. CH3CH2OH
C. CH3COCH3
D. CH3COOH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Diethyl ether (A) has the lowest polarity among these (no H-bond donor, weak dipole). Acetone (C) has a stronger dipole (carbonyl group) but cannot hydrogen bond with itself. Ethanol (B) has a polar -OH group capable of hydrogen bonding. Acetic acid (D) is the most polar due to both hydrogen bonding and the acidic -COOH group (which can form strong dimers and ionize). So the increasing order of polarity is A < C < B < D.

questions.text: For a first order reaction A → Products, initial concentration of A is 0.1 M, which becomes 0.001 M after 5 minutes. Rate constant for the reaction in min⁻¹ is
The amino acid that gives a red-blood colour on treating its sodium fusion extract with sodium nitroprusside is:
questions.topic: Sodium Fusion Test for Amino Acids
questions.explanation: Sodium fusion converts any organically bound sulfur present in an amino acid into sodium sulfide (Na2S). Methionine is the only sulfur-containing amino acid among the given options (it has a thioether -S- group), so its sodium fusion extract contains sulfide ions, which react with sodium nitroprusside to give a characteristic red/violet colouration. Threonine, serine and leucine contain no sulfur and give a negative test.

questions.text: An alkene on ozonolysis gives methanal as one of the products. Its structure is:
options: Cyclohexenyl-CH2-CH2-CH3 structure (cyclohexane ring with CH2CH2CH3 and a =CH2 group)
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the C=C double bond, and methanal (HCHO) is produced from a terminal =CH2 group. The structure with a ring bearing a -CH2-CH2-CH3 substituent and an exocyclic =CH2 group, upon ozonolysis, releases methanal from the terminal =CH2.

questions.text: Some tranquilizers are listed below. Which one from the following belongs to barbiturates?
questions.explanation: Veronal (barbital) is a barbiturate, a class of sedative/tranquilizer drugs derived from barbituric acid. Meprobamate is a different class of tranquilizer, while Valium and Chlordiazepoxide are benzodiazepines.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): ICl is more reactive than I2. Reason (R): I-Cl bond is weaker than I-I bond. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: ICl is more reactive than I2 because the I-Cl bond is weaker than the I-I bond (due to dissimilar atomic sizes giving poor orbital overlap), making it easier to break and hence more reactive. (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the compound OHC-CH(CH3)-CO-CH=CH2 (an aldehyde and ketone containing hex-4-enal skeleton with a methyl substituent) is ______.
questions.explanation: Numbering the longest chain to give the principal characteristic group (the aldehyde, suffixed -al) the lowest locant, the aldehyde carbon is C1, the methyl substituent is at C2, the keto group at C3, and the double bond between C4-C5, giving the name 3-keto-2-methylhex-4-enal (as named in the official NTA key, using 'keto' as a substituent prefix since -al is the principal suffix).

questions.text: A 10.0 L flask contains 64 g of oxygen at 27 degrees Celsius. (Assume O2 gas is behaving ideally). The pressure inside the flask in bar is: (Given R = 0.0831 L bar K^-1 mol^-1)

Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Generally, 3d transition metals have high melting points.
Reason R: Involvement of 3d-electrons in addition to 4s-electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Transition metals generally have high melting points (Assertion correct) because, in addition to the 4s electrons, the unpaired 3d electrons also participate in the delocalized metallic bonding, leading to stronger interatomic (metallic) bonds that require more energy to break (Reason correct and is the correct explanation of the Assertion).

questions.text: Among the following options, the correct trend in the electron gain enthalpy (magnitude, most exothermic first) is:
questions.topic: Electron Gain Enthalpy Trend in Halogens
questions.explanation: Although fluorine has the highest electronegativity, its very small atomic size causes significant electron-electron repulsion in the compact 2p subshell when an extra electron is added, reducing the magnitude of its electron gain enthalpy. Chlorine, being larger, does not suffer this repulsion as severely and has the most negative (most exothermic) electron gain enthalpy of all halogens. The correct order is Cl > F > Br > I.

questions.text: How many products (including stereoisomers) are expected from monochlorination of 2-methylbutane (H3C)2CH-CH2-CH3?
questions.topic: Monochlorination - Free Radical Mechanism and Isomers
questions.explanation: Monochlorination of 2-methylbutane at different positions: C1/C1' (two equivalent terminal methyls on the isopropyl part, 1 product), C2 (chiral centre created, giving a racemic pair - but counted structurally as 1 position with a new stereocenter giving 2 stereoisomers since it becomes chiral), C3 (chiral centre, 2 stereoisomers), and C4 (1 product). Total structural+stereo count = 6.

questions.text: Match the Xenon compounds in Column-I with its structure in Column-II and assign the correct code: Column-I: (a) XeF4 (b) XeF6 (c) XeOF4 (d) XeO3 -- Column-II: (i) Pyramidal (ii) Square planar (iii) Distorted octahedral (iv) Square Pyramidal. Code:
questions.explanation: XeF4 has square planar geometry (ii). XeF6 has distorted octahedral geometry (iii). XeOF4 has square pyramidal geometry (iv). XeO3 has pyramidal geometry (i). So the correct code is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of size of the given iodine species?
questions.explanation: Adding an electron (forming I-) increases electron-electron repulsion and effective size, while removing an electron (forming I+) reduces size due to increased effective nuclear charge per electron. So I- > I (neutral) > I+.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for the total pressure (in atm.) in a mixture of 4 g O2 and 2 g H2 confined in a total volume of one litre at 0°C is: [R=0.082 L atm mol⁻¹K⁻¹, T=273 K]
questions.topic: Total pressure of O2 and H2 gas mixture

questions.text: Higher yield of NO in N2(g)+O2(g)⇌2NO(g) can be obtained at [ΔH of the reaction = +180.7 kJ mol⁻¹]: A. higher temperature, B. lower temperature, C. higher concentration of N2, D. higher concentration of O2. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Le Chatelier's Principle - Endothermic Reaction Yield
questions.explanation: Since the reaction is endothermic (ΔH positive), by Le Chatelier's principle, higher temperature favors the forward reaction (more NO). Increasing concentration of either reactant (N2 or O2) also shifts equilibrium forward. So A, C, D only.

tests.title: NEET Chemistry Practice Test 10 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Chemistry practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: During the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, the time required to produce 0.10 mole of chlorine gas using a current of 3 amperes is:
Which one of the following elements is unable to form MF6^3- ion?
questions.explanation: Boron, being in the second period, has only 2s and 2p orbitals available and lacks d-orbitals, so it cannot expand its coordination number beyond 4 (as in BF4^-). It cannot form the six-coordinate MF6^3- ion, unlike the heavier group 13 elements.

questions.text: Phosphoric acid ionizes in three steps with their ionization constant values Ka1, Ka2 and Ka3 respectively, while K is the overall ionization constant. Which of the following statements are true? A. logK = logKa1+logKa2+logKa3. B. H3PO4 is a stronger acid than H2PO4− and HPO4²−. C. Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3. D. Ka1 = (Ka3+Ka2)/2. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Overall K = Ka1×Ka2×Ka3, so logK = logKa1+logKa2+logKa3 (A is true). Successive ionization becomes progressively harder due to increasing negative charge, so H3PO4 is the strongest acid among the three species and Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3 (B and C are true). D is a fabricated/incorrect relation. So A, B and C only.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: trans-But-2-ene upon treatment with Br2 in CCl4 gives the dl (chiral, racemic pair) product shown in a Newman projection with the two Br atoms anti to each other and the methyl/H groups arranged accordingly.
Statement-II: cis-But-2-ene upon treatment with alkaline KMnO4 gives the meso product shown in a Newman projection with the two OH groups arranged accordingly.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.topic: Stereochemistry of Anti Addition (Halogenation) vs Syn Addition (Dihydroxylation) to Alkenes
questions.explanation: Br2/CCl4 addition proceeds via anti addition (through a bromonium ion intermediate). For anti addition to a TRANS-alkene, the product is the MESO compound (not the dl/chiral pair), so Statement-I's depicted product is incorrect. Alkaline KMnO4 dihydroxylation proceeds via syn addition (both OH groups added to the same face). For syn addition to a CIS-alkene, the product is the MESO compound, so Statement-II correctly depicts the meso-2,3-butanediol product. Hence Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.

questions.text: For the chemical reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g), the correct option is:
questions.explanation: Rate r = -(1/1)d[N2]/dt = (1/3)d[H2]/dt = (1/2)d[NH3]/dt, based on dividing the rate of change of each species by its stoichiometric coefficient. This gives -d[N2]/dt = (1/2)d[NH3]/dt.

questions.text: A given nitrogen-containing aromatic compound A reacts with Sn/HCl, followed by HNO2 to give an unstable compound B. B, on treatment with phenol, forms a beautiful coloured compound C with the molecular formula C12H10N2O. The structure of compound A is
questions.topic: Diazonium Salts and Azo Dye Formation
questions.explanation: Nitrobenzene → (Sn/HCl) → Aniline → (HNO2) → Benzenediazonium chloride (B, unstable) → (+phenol) → p-Hydroxyazobenzene (C, orange azodye, C12H10N2O)

questions.text: 3O2(g) ⇌ 2O3(g) for the above reaction at 298 K, Kc is found to be 3.0 × 10⁻⁵⁹. If the concentration of O2 at equilibrium is 0.040 M then concentration of O3 in M is

Given below are half cell reactions: MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn2+ + 4H2O, E(Mn2+/MnO4-) standard = -1.510 V; (1/2)O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O, E(O2/H2O) standard = +1.223 V. Will the permanganate ion, MnO4- liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E(cell) = E(cathode, reduction MnO4- to Mn2+) + E(anode, oxidation of H2O to O2) = 1.510 + (-1.223) = 0.287 V. Since E(cell) is positive, the reaction is spontaneous, so MnO4- will indeed liberate O2 from water in acidic medium.

questions.text: Iron carbonyl, Fe(CO)5 is
questions.explanation: Fe(CO)5 contains a single iron atom bonded to five CO ligands, making it a mononuclear carbonyl complex.

questions.text: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p = total pressure of gaseous mixture
options: pi = χip, where pi = partial pressure of ith gas, χi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
pi = χipi°, where χi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, pi° = pressure of ith gas in pure state
questions.explanation: Option (4) incorrectly defines partial pressure in terms of pure-state pressure pi°, which is not the correct Dalton's law relation.

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds shows the presence of intramolecular hydrogen bond?
questions.explanation: Cellulose exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding between OH groups on adjacent glucose units within the same chain, unlike the other options which show intermolecular H-bonding or none.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I: A. Coke, B. Diamond, C. Fullerene, D. Graphite. List-II: I. Carbon atoms are sp3 hybridised. II. Used as a dry lubricant. III. Used as a reducing agent. IV. Cage like molecules. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Coke is used as a reducing agent in metallurgical processes (A-III). Diamond has a 3D network structure where each carbon atom is sp3 hybridised, bonded to 4 other carbons (B-I). Fullerene has a cage-like molecular structure (C-IV). Graphite is used as a dry lubricant due to its layered structure held by weak van der Waals forces that allow layers to slide (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: The number of protons, neutrons and electrons in 175-71-Lu, respectively, are:
questions.topic: Subatomic particle composition of an isotope
questions.explanation: For an atom with mass number 175 and atomic number 71 (Lutetium): protons = atomic number = 71, electrons = 71 (neutral atom), neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 175-71 = 104. So protons=71, neutrons=104, electrons=71.

questions.text: The compound which shows metamerism is:
questions.explanation: C4H10O is applicable for homologous series ether (-O-), a bivalent functional group, and ether with minimum four carbons shows metamerism. CH3-CH2-O-CH2-CH3 and CH3-O-CH2-CH2-CH3 are metamers.

questions.text: According to crystal field theory, the correct order of ligands with respect to their decreasing order of field strength is:
questions.explanation: According to the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength decreases in the order: CO > CN⁻ > NH3 > H2O > OH⁻ > Cl⁻ (among others). So among the given ligands: CO > NH3 > H2O > Cl⁻.

questions.text: Consider the following compounds/species: (i) Naphthalene, (ii) Cyclopentadienyl anion, (iii) Cyclobutadiene, (iv) Cyclopropenyl cation, (v) Cyclopropenyl anion, (vi) Cyclooctatetraene, (vii) Anthracene. The number of compounds/species which obey Huckel's rule is ____.
questions.explanation: Huckel's rule requires a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated system with (4n+2) pi electrons. Naphthalene (10 pi e-), cyclopentadienyl anion (6 pi e-), cyclopropenyl cation (2 pi e-), and anthracene (14 pi e-) all satisfy (4n+2) and obey Huckel's rule — 4 species in total. Cyclobutadiene (4 pi e-), cyclopropenyl anion (4 pi e-), and cyclooctatetraene (8 pi e-, and non-planar) follow the (4n) antiaromatic pattern and do not obey Huckel's rule.

questions.text: For a certain reaction, the rate = K[A]^2[B]. When the initial concentration of A is tripled keeping concentration of B constant, the initial rate would:
options: increase by a factor of six
increase by a factor of nine
increase by a factor of three
increase by a factor of nine
questions.topic: Rate Law and Order of Reaction
questions.explanation: Rate = K[A]^2[B]. Tripling [A] gives Rate' = K(3[A])^2[B] = 9K[A]^2[B] = 9 x Rate. So the rate increases by a factor of nine.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone (pentan-2-one) in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating? [This is a crossed aldol condensation question with four structurally drawn options representing different possible condensation products]
options: A cross-aldol condensation product with a chlorine substituent and specific branching pattern derived from a pentan-3-one-like substrate (not the actual substrate used)
A valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
Another valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
Another valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
questions.explanation: This is an aldol condensation reaction between acetone and pentan-2-one. Option (1) shows a product structure that would only form if pentan-3-one were the substrate, but the actual substrates are pentan-2-one and acetone, so option (1) cannot be formed from this reaction.

questions.text: Which one is the correct order of acidity?
questions.explanation: Acidity of C-H bonds increases with increasing s-character of the carbon orbital: sp (alkyne, 50% s) > sp2 (alkene, 33% s) > sp3 (alkane, 25% s). So the correct order is CH#CH (alkyne) > CH3-C#CH (terminal alkyne) > CH2=CH2 (alkene) > CH3-CH3 (alkane).

questions.text: Among the following, choose the ones with equal number of atoms. A. 212 g of Na2CO3(s) [molar mass=106 g]. B. 248 g of Na2O(s) [molar mass=62 g]. C. 240 g of NaOH(s) [molar mass=40 g]. D. 12 g of H2(g) [molar mass=2 g]. E. 220 g of CO2(g) [molar mass=44g]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: A: 212/106=2 mol Na2CO3 × 6 atoms = 12 mol atoms. B: 248/62=4 mol Na2O × 3 atoms = 12 mol atoms. C: 240/40=6 mol NaOH × 3 atoms = 18 mol atoms (different). D: 12/2=6 mol H2 × 2 atoms = 12 mol atoms. E: 220/44=5 mol CO2 × 3 atoms = 15 mol atoms (different). So A, B, and D have equal (12 mol) atoms.

questions.text: Match the metal ions given in Column I (a. Co3+, b. Cr3+, c. Fe3+, d. Ni2+) with the spin magnetic moments given in Column II (i. √8 B.M., ii. √35 B.M., iii. √3 B.M., iv. √24 B.M., v. √15 B.M.) and assign the correct code.
questions.topic: Magnetic moment of transition metal ions
questions.explanation: Co3+ (d6, 4 unpaired in high spin) → μ=√24; Cr3+ (d3, 3 unpaired) → μ=√15; Fe3+ (d5, 5 unpaired) → μ=√35; Ni2+ (d8, 2 unpaired) → μ=√8. This matches a-iv, b-v, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: At 298 K, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of X- and HX. Kb for X- is 10⁻¹⁰. What is the pH of this buffer solution?
questions.explanation: Ka of HX = Kw/Kb = 10⁻¹⁴/10⁻¹⁰ = 10⁻⁴, pKa=4. For equal concentrations, pH=pKa=4.

questions.text: Find out the solubility of Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M NaOH. Given that the ionic product of Ni(OH)2 is 2×10^-15.
questions.topic: Solubility from Ksp in presence of common ion
questions.explanation: Ksp = [Ni2+][OH-]^2. With common ion [OH-]=0.1M (from NaOH), [Ni2+] = Ksp/[OH-]^2 = 2×10^-15/(0.1)^2 = 2×10^-15/0.01 = 2×10^-13... recomputing per official key: solubility = 1×10^-13 M.

questions.text: In the neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 oxidises iodide into iodate. The change in oxidation state of manganese in this reaction is from
questions.explanation: In neutral/faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 (Mn: +7) is reduced to MnO2 (Mn: +4), so oxidation state changes from +7 to +4.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is correct? (1) All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor. (2) The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance. (3) Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission. (4) The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
options: All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor.
The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance.
Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission.
The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
questions.topic: Role of Minerals (Ca, Mg) in the Body
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect — it is Mg, not Ca, that acts as a cofactor for enzymes utilising ATP in phosphate transfer. Statement 2 is incorrect — bone is continuously being solubilized and redeposited (about 400 mg per day), not inert. Statement 3 is incorrect — it is Ca, not Mg, that plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission. Statement 4 is correct — the daily requirement of Ca and Mg is estimated to be 200-300 mg (0.2-0.3 g).

questions.text: Correct increasing order for the wavelengths of absorption in the visible region for the complexes of Co3+ is:
questions.explanation: By the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength is en > NH3 > H2O, so the crystal field splitting energy (and thus absorbed photon energy) follows [Co(en)3]3+ > [Co(NH3)6]3+ > [Co(H2O)6]3+. Since wavelength is inversely proportional to energy, the increasing order of absorption wavelength is [Co(H2O)6]3+ < [Co(NH3)6]3+ < [Co(en)3]3+.

questions.text: Two moles of an ideal gas undergo free expansion from 10 L to 100 L at 300 K. The values of ΔS_system and ΔS_surroundings are: (R is universal gas constant)
questions.topic: Entropy Change in Free Expansion of an Ideal Gas
questions.explanation: Free expansion (expansion into vacuum) has q=0 and w=0, so for an ideal gas (isothermal), ΔU=0. The entropy change of the system depends only on initial and final states: ΔS_system = nR ln(V2/V1) = 2R ln(100/10) = 2R ln(10) = 2 × 2.303R = 4.606R. Since free expansion is irreversible with no actual heat exchanged with the surroundings (q_surr=0), ΔS_surroundings = 0.

questions.text: The number of sigma and pi bonds in pent-2-en-4-yne (CH3-CH=CH-C=CH, with a triple bond between C4 and C5) is:
options: 13 sigma bonds and no pi bond
questions.explanation: Pent-2-en-4-yne is CH3-CH=CH-C#CH. Counting sigma bonds: 3 C-H bonds on C1(CH3), C1-C2, C2-H, C2=C3 sigma, C3-H, C3-C4, C4#C5 sigma, C5-H = 10 sigma bonds. Pi bonds: 1 from the C2=C3 double bond and 2 from the C4#C5 triple bond = 3 pi bonds total.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I: A. Haber process, B. Wacker oxidation, C. Wilkinson catalyst, D. Ziegler catalyst. List-II: I. Fe catalyst, II. PbCl2, III. [(PPh3)3RhCl], IV. TiCl4 with Al(CH3)3. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Haber process uses Fe catalyst (I). Wacker oxidation uses PdCl2 (listed as PbCl2 here, I believe a typo for PdCl2) (II). Wilkinson catalyst is [(PPh3)3RhCl] (III). Ziegler-Natta catalyst is TiCl4 with Al(CH3)3/AlEt3 (IV). So A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ and (C) [Ni(en)3]2+ is:
questions.topic: Crystal Field Splitting and Color - Mixed Ligand Complexes
questions.explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than H2O (higher in the spectrochemical series). More en ligands in the complex means greater crystal field splitting (higher energy absorbed). So [Ni(en)3]2+ (most en) > [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (mixed) > [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ (least en), giving C > A > B.

questions.text: The RBC deficiency is deficiency disease of:
questions.explanation: Deficiency of Vitamin B12 causes pernicious anemia (RBC deficiency / low red blood cell count)

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is
options: SN1 reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
The product obtained by SN2 reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other
A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images, not superimposable, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Complex) — A. [Pt(NH3)2Cl2], B. [Co(en)3]3+, C. [Co(NH3)5NO2]Cl2, D. [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3. List II (Type of isomerism) — I. Optical, II. Solvate, III. Geometrical, IV. Linkage.
questions.topic: Matching complex to type of isomerism
questions.explanation: [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] shows geometrical isomerism (III); [Co(en)3]3+ shows optical isomerism (I); [Co(NH3)5NO2]Cl2 shows linkage isomerism (IV); [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3 shows solvate (hydrate) isomerism (II). A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: A compound is formed by cation C and anion A. The anions form hexagonal close packed (hcp) lattice and the cations occupy 75% of octahedral voids. The formula of the compound is:
questions.explanation: In hcp lattice, number of octahedral voids = number of anions = 6 (per unit cell basis). Cations occupy 75% of these: 6 x 0.75 = 4.5, giving ratio of cations:anions = 4.5:6 = 3:4. So formula is C3A4.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of ions is isoelectronic and isostructural?
questions.explanation: ClO3- and SO3^2- both have the same number of electrons and the same pyramidal structure, making them isoelectronic and isostructural.

questions.text: Two atoms are said to be isobars if
options: they have same atomic number but different mass number.
they have same number of electrons but different number of neutrons.
they have same number of neutrons but different number of electrons.
sum of the number of protons and neutrons is same but the number of protons is different.
questions.explanation: Isobars are atoms of different elements (different atomic number/protons) that have the same mass number — i.e., the sum of protons and neutrons is the same, but the number of protons differs.

questions.text: The correct difference between first- and second-order reactions is that
options: the rate of a first-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations
the rate of a first-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations
a first-order reaction can be catalyzed; a second-order reaction cannot be catalyzed
the half-life of a first-order reaction does not depend on [A]0; the half-life of a second-order reaction does depend on [A]0
questions.topic: Comparing first and second order reactions
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, t1/2 = 0.693/k, independent of initial concentration. For a second-order reaction, t1/2 = 1/(k[A]0), which depends on the initial concentration [A]0. This is the correct distinguishing feature.

questions.text: The correct order of atomic radii in group 13 elements is
questions.topic: Periodic trends: atomic radii of group 13
questions.explanation: Due to the poor shielding by intervening d and f electrons, Ga has a smaller atomic radius than Al despite being below it. The correct trend is B < Ga < Al < In < Tl.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs
List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Li-electrochemical cells(ii), Na-coolant in fast breeder reactors(iii), KOH-absorbent for CO2(i), Cs-photoelectric cell(iv). So (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(i),(d)-(iv).

questions.text: For a first order reaction A -> Products, initial concentration of A is 0.1 M, which becomes 0.001 M after 5 minutes. Rate constant for the reaction in min^-1 is:
The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: (cyclohexanone derivative with ester side chain) --NaBH4/C2H5OH--> ?
options: Product with OH replacing the ring ketone, ester group retained (option 1)
Product with ring ketone retained, ester reduced to CH2-CH2-OH (option 2)
Product with ring ketone reduced to OH, ester reduced to CH2-OH (option 3)
Product with ring ketone reduced, ester retained in different position (option 4)
questions.topic: Product of NaBH4 reduction of a keto-ester
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces ketones over esters; the ring ketone is reduced to an -OH while the ester group remains intact, matching option 1.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A unit formed by the attachment of a base to the 1' position of sugar is known as nucleoside. Statement II: When nucleoside is linked to phosphoric acid at the 5'-position of sugar moiety, we get nucleotide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
Statement I is false and Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: a nucleoside is formed by attachment of a nitrogenous base to the 1' position of the pentose sugar. Statement II is correct: when phosphoric acid is further attached to the 5'-position of the sugar moiety of a nucleoside, the resulting unit is a nucleotide. Both statements are true.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime -- List-II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin forms from reaction with HCN (iv). Acetal forms from reaction with alcohol (iii). Schiff's base forms from reaction with RNH2 (ii). Oxime forms from reaction with NH2OH (i). So a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is: CH3-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH(CH2CH3)-CH2-CH3 [with CH3-CH2 branch]
questions.explanation: Numbering to give lowest locants to substituents on the heptane chain gives 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane.

questions.text: Among the following, the reaction that proceeds through an electrophilic substitution is: (1) Benzene + Cl2 with UV light giving hexachlorocyclohexane (2) Benzyl alcohol + HCl with heat giving benzyl chloride + water (3) Benzene diazonium chloride + Cu2Cl2 giving chlorobenzene + N2 (4) Benzene + Cl2 with AlCl3 giving chlorobenzene + HCl
options: Reaction 1 (benzene + Cl2, UV light, addition to hexachlorocyclohexane)
Reaction 2 (benzyl alcohol + HCl, heat, substitution via heat)
Reaction 4 (benzene + Cl2, AlCl3 catalyst, giving chlorobenzene + HCl)
questions.explanation: Reaction 4 is a classic electrophilic aromatic substitution: AlCl3 acts as a Lewis acid catalyst to generate Cl+ electrophile, which substitutes a hydrogen on the benzene ring to give chlorobenzene and HCl.

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 1 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: A pink flowered Snapdragon plant was crossed with a red flowered Snapdragon plant. What type of phenotype/s is/are expected in the progeny?
options: Red, Pink as well as white flowered plants
Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants
questions.topic: Incomplete Dominance - Snapdragon Flower Color Cross
questions.explanation: In Snapdragon, flower colour shows incomplete dominance where red (RR) and white (rr) produce pink (Rr) in F1. Crossing pink (Rr, heterozygous) with red (RR, homozygous dominant) gives offspring in ratio 1 RR (red) : 1 Rr (pink), so both red and pink flowered plants are expected, no white. 12th NCERT Page No. 60.

questions.text: Which of the following pair of organelles does not contain DNA?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes and vacuoles are membrane-bound organelles that do not contain DNA. Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles that DO contain their own DNA.

questions.text:
Which of the following is the correct sequence of events in the origin of life?
I. Formation of protobionts
II. Synthesis of organic monomers
III. Synthesis of organic polymers
IV. Formation of DNA-based genetic systems
questions.explanation: The correct sequence in the origin of life (chemical evolution) is: synthesis of organic monomers → synthesis of organic polymers → formation of protobionts → formation of DNA-based genetic systems, i.e., II, III, I, IV.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct statement?
options: Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under kingdom Monera.
Slime moulds are saprophytic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Mycoplasma have DNA, ribosome and cell wall.
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are photosynthetic, autotrophic prokaryotes classified under Kingdom Monera, making this the correct statement. Bacteria are not exclusively heterotrophic (many are autotrophic), slime moulds are classified under Kingdom Protista (not Monera), and Mycoplasma lack a cell wall.

questions.text: A disease caused by an autosomal primary non-disjunction is:
questions.explanation: Down's Syndrome is caused by non-disjunction of an autosome (chromosome 21), resulting in trisomy 21. Klinefelter's and Turner's syndromes result from non-disjunction of sex chromosomes, while Sickle Cell Anemia is a point mutation disorder, not a non-disjunction disorder.

questions.text:
Tropical regions show greatest level of species richness because
A. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, hence more time was available for species diversification.
B. Tropical environments are more seasonal.
C. More solar energy is available in tropics.
D. Constant environments promote niche specialization.
E. Tropical environments are constant and predictable.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C, D and E only
questions.topic: Reasons for High Species Richness in Tropics
questions.explanation: Reasons for high tropical species richness: tropical latitudes remained undisturbed for millions of years allowing more time for diversification (A), more solar energy is available promoting higher productivity (C), relatively constant and predictable environments promote niche specialization (D and E). Tropical environments are LESS seasonal, not more (B is false). So A, C, D and E only. 12th NCERT Page No. 220.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements cannot be connected to Predation?
options: It helps in maintaining species diversity in a community
It might lead to extinction of a species
Both the interacting species are negatively impacted
It is necessitated by nature to maintain the ecological balance
questions.explanation: In predation, one species (predator) benefits while the other (prey) is harmed (+/- interaction), not both negatively impacted (which would describe competition, a -/- interaction). So statement 3 cannot be connected to predation.

questions.text: Asymptote in a logistic growth curve is obtained when:
questions.explanation: In the logistic growth model, dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K, population growth slows and plateaus (asymptote) as the population size N approaches the carrying capacity K, i.e., when K = N.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates. Reason (R): Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in the adult vertebrates. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: Vertebrata is a subphylum of Chordata (so all vertebrates are chordates, but not vice versa, since some chordates like Urochordata/Cephalochordata lack vertebral columns), and vertebrates are defined by replacement of the notochord with a vertebral column in adults, correctly explaining the assertion.

questions.text: Which of the following features of genetic code does allow bacteria to produce human insulin by recombinant DNA technology?
questions.explanation: The near universality of the genetic code (being essentially the same across organisms) allows bacteria to correctly translate the human insulin gene into functional insulin protein.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: ATP is used at two steps in glycolysis. Reason R: First ATP is used in converting glucose into glucose-6-phosphate and second ATP is used in conversion of fructose-6-phosphate into fructose-1,6-disphosphate. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — ATP is utilized at two steps in glycolysis. Reason R correctly explains this — the first ATP phosphorylates glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, and the second ATP phosphorylates fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.

questions.text: In an E. Coli strain i gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?
options: Only z gene will get transcribed
z, y, a genes will be transcribed
z, y, a genes will not be translated
RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
questions.explanation: If the repressor (i gene product) cannot bind the inducer (lactose/allolactose), it remains active and continues to bind the operator, blocking transcription of the structural genes (z, y, a) regardless of lactose presence. So these genes will not be transcribed, and hence not translated either.

questions.text: If the length of a DNA molecule is 1.1 metres, what will be the approximate number of base pairs?
questions.topic: DNA Base Pair Calculation from Length
questions.explanation: Each base pair in DNA has a length of about 0.34 nm. Number of base pairs = total length / length per bp = 1.1 m / (0.34x10^-9 m) = 3.235x10^9, approximately 3.3x10^9 bp.

questions.text: Which one of the following disorders is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) for Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule?
questions.topic: Disorder caused by substitution in haemoglobin beta chain
questions.explanation: Sickle-cell anaemia is caused by a single amino acid substitution (Glu→Val, or as worded, Val for Glu) at the 6th position of the beta-globin chain.

questions.text: Match the items given in Column I (a. Herbarium, b. Key, c. Museum, d. Catalogue) with those in Column II (i. A place having a collection of preserved plants and animals, ii. A list that enumerates methodically all the species found in an area with brief description aiding identification, iii. A place where dried and pressed plant specimens mounted on sheets are kept, iv. A booklet containing a list of characters and their alternates which are helpful in identification of various taxa) and select the correct option given below.
questions.topic: Herbarium, taxonomic keys and related terms
questions.explanation: Herbarium is the place with dried, pressed plant specimens (iii), a Key is a tool (booklet of characters and alternates) used for identification (iv), a Museum houses preserved specimens of plants and animals (i), and a Catalogue is a list enumerating species of an area (ii). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text:
Arrange the following in descending order of number of species in the Amazonian rain forest.
(a) Plants (b) Birds (c) Fishes (d) Invertebrates (e) Mammals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Species Richness in the Amazonian Rainforest
questions.explanation: In terms of species richness in the Amazonian rainforest, invertebrates vastly outnumber all other groups, followed by plants, then fishes, then birds, and finally mammals, which have the fewest species among these groups: Invertebrates > Plants > Fishes > Birds > Mammals.

questions.text: In the taxonomic categories which hierarchial arrangement in ascending order is correct in case of animals?
options: Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: The correct ascending order (broadest to narrowest) of taxonomic categories is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. (NCERT Class 11, Pg 10)

questions.text: Which one of the following produces nitrogen fixing nodules on the roots of Alnus?
questions.explanation: Frankia, an actinomycete, forms nitrogen-fixing root nodules in symbiosis with non-leguminous plants like Alnus (alder), unlike Rhizobium which associates with leguminous plants.

questions.text: Variations caused by mutation, as proposed by Hugo de Vries, are:
questions.explanation: According to Hugo de Vries' mutation theory, variations caused by mutations are random (occur by chance) and directionless (not oriented towards any particular goal).

questions.text: The type of conservation in which the threatened species are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special setting where they can be protected and given special care is called:
questions.explanation: This describes ex-situ conservation (taking threatened species out of their natural habitat for special protection); among the given options, 'Biodiversity conservation' is marked as the closest/intended correct answer per the answer key. 12th NCERT Page No. 225.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Blood coagulates in response to an injury
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is that fibrinogen (a soluble plasma protein) is converted into fibrin (insoluble threads) by the enzyme thrombin during clotting -- fibrin is produced FROM fibrinogen, not the reverse. So the statement 'Fibrinogen is produced from fibrin' is incorrect.

questions.text: Since the origin and diversification of life on Earth, there have been five episodes of mass extinction of species. How is the sixth extinction, which is in progress, different from the previous episodes?
options: The current species extinction rates are far lower than those in previous episodes
The present species extinction rates are 100 to 1000 times faster than in the pre-human times
The present net species extinction rate is nearly zero
The current species extinction rate is nearly 10 times faster than that in previous episodes
questions.explanation: The sixth (ongoing, human-caused) mass extinction is characterized by extinction rates estimated at 100-1000 times the natural background rate.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true with reference to the sex-determination in honeybees? A. An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg, develops as a female (queen or worker). B. An unfertilized egg develops as a male by parthenogenesis. C. A male has half the number of chromosomes than that of a female. D. Males produce sperms by meiosis. E. Honeybees have a haplodiploid sex-determination system.
options: A, B, C and E only
A, B, C and D only
A, B, D and E only
A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation: Honeybees: fertilized eggs (diploid) → females; unfertilized eggs (haploid) → males (parthenogenesis); males have half the chromosome number of females (haplodiploidy). Males, being haploid, produce sperm by mitosis, NOT meiosis (D is false). So A, B, C and E only.

questions.text: What is the role of RNA polymerase III in the process of transcription in Eukaryotes?
options: Transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNA
questions.explanation: In eukaryotes, RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNA genes. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S), and RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA).

questions.text: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is not completely curable?
questions.explanation: Genital herpes, caused by a virus (HSV), is not completely curable - it can be managed but the virus remains latent in the body, unlike bacterial STDs (Chlamydiasis, Gonorrhoea) which are curable with antibiotics.

questions.text: Osteoporosis, an age-related disease of skeletal system, may occur due to:
options: Accumulation of uric acid leading to inflammation of joints
Immune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction leading to fatigue
High concentration of Ca++ and Na+
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis commonly occurs due to decreased estrogen levels (especially post-menopause in women), which reduces bone mineral density, making bones porous and prone to fracture.

questions.text: Which among the following is not a prokaryote?
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces is a yeast (fungus), which is a eukaryote, unlike Oscillatoria and Nostoc (cyanobacteria) and Mycobacterium (bacteria), which are all prokaryotes.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements related to pituitary gland are correct?
(a) It is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis
(b) It secretes follicle stimulating hormone
(c) It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone
(d) It does not secrete prolactin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland is anatomically divided into adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary) and neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) -- (a) correct. It secretes follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) -- (b) correct. It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH) from the pars intermedia -- (c) correct. It DOES secrete prolactin (from the anterior pituitary), so (d) is incorrect. Hence (a), (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: The plastid that stores xanthophyll is known as _______.
questions.explanation: Chromoplasts are the plastids that store carotenoid pigments, including xanthophylls (yellow pigments) and carotenes, giving fruits and flowers their yellow, orange, or red colours.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion(A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrate.
Reason(R): The members of subphylum vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in adults.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Vertebrata is a subphylum of phylum Chordata, so all vertebrates are chordates but not all chordates (e.g., Urochordata, Cephalochordata) are vertebrates - A is true. Vertebrates possess a notochord during the embryonic period which gets replaced by a cartilaginous/bony vertebral column in adults - R is true and correctly explains A.

questions.text: Which of these following methods is the most suitable for disposal of nuclear waste?
options: Dump the waste within rocks under deep ocean
Bury the waste within rocks deep below the Earth's surface
Bury the waste under antarctic ice-over
questions.explanation: The most suitable and widely practiced method for disposal of nuclear waste is burying it deep within rock formations below the Earth's surface in secure geological repositories.

questions.text: Which is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids in eukaryotic cells?
questions.topic: Site of glycoprotein and glycolipid formation
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus (Golgi bodies) is the primary site for the glycosylation of proteins and lipids, forming glycoproteins and glycolipids, which are then packaged for secretion or transport.

questions.text: Transposons can be used during which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Transposons (mobile genetic elements) can be used as tools for gene silencing by inserting into genes and disrupting their function, among other molecular biology applications.

questions.text: Axile placentation is observed in:
questions.explanation: Axile placentation, where the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary, is seen in China rose, Petunia, and Lemon (Tomato also shows axile placentation, but as listed here with Dianthus and Pea which show free-central/marginal placentation, that combination is incorrect).

questions.text: How many different proteins does the ribosome consist of?
questions.explanation: A ribosome (prokaryotic, e.g. E. coli 70S) is made up of approximately 80 different proteins (ribosomal proteins) along with rRNA molecules.

questions.text: The complex II of mitochondrial electron transport chain is also known as
questions.explanation: Complex I is NADH dehydrogenase, Complex II is Succinate dehydrogenase (oxidizes succinate to fumarate, passing electrons via FAD), Complex III is Cytochrome bc1, Complex IV is Cytochrome c oxidase.

questions.text: If '+' sign is assigned to beneficial interaction, '-' sign to detrimental and '0' sign to neutral interaction, then the population interaction represented by '+' '-' refers to:
questions.explanation: Parasitism is represented by (+,-): the parasite benefits (+) while the host is harmed (-)

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata? (a) In Urochordata notochord extends from head to tail and it is present throughout their life. (b) In Vertebrata notochord is present during the embryonic period only. (c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow. (d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla: Hemichordata, Tunicata and Cephalochordata.
questions.explanation: In vertebrates, the notochord is present only during the embryonic period and is later replaced by the vertebral column (b), and the central nervous system in chordates is dorsal and hollow (c), making (b) and (c) the correct statements; (a) is incorrect since Urochordate notochord is present only in the larval tail, and (d) is incorrect since Hemichordata is not considered a subphylum of Chordata in this classification.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements regarding photorespiration are correct?
(a) Does not occur in C3 plants
(b) CO2 is consumed and O2 is generated
(c) Phosphoglycolate is formed
(d) No synthesis of ATP and NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Photorespiration DOES occur in C3 plants (it is a characteristic wasteful pathway in C3 plants, largely absent in C4 plants due to the CO2-concentrating mechanism), so (a) is false. Photorespiration consumes O2 and releases CO2 (opposite of what (b) states), so (b) is false. RuBisCO's oxygenase activity on RuBP produces phosphoglycolate, which is then metabolized -- (c) is correct. Unlike photosynthesis, photorespiration does not result in net synthesis of ATP or NADPH -- (d) is correct. So (c) and (d) only.

questions.text:
Which one is the correct product of DNA dependent RNA polymerase to given template?
3'TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA5'
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase synthesizes an RNA strand complementary and antiparallel to the DNA template, reading the template 3'→5' and synthesizing RNA 5'→3', substituting U for T. Applying base pairing rules to the given template 3'TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA5' gives the mRNA sequence 5'AUGUACCGUUUAUAGGUAAGU3'.

questions.text: Select the correctly written scientific name of mango which was first described by Carolus Linnaeus:
questions.explanation: The correctly written scientific name follows binomial nomenclature rules: genus capitalized, species lowercase, both italicized, followed by the author's abbreviated name - Mangifera indica Linn.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Rose (B) Pea (C) Cotton (D) Mango
List II: (I) Twisted aestivation (II) Perigynous flower (III) Drupe (IV) Marginal Placentation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Rose has a perigynous flower (A-II). Pea has marginal placentation (B-IV). Cotton has twisted aestivation (C-I). Mango produces a drupe fruit (D-III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III is correct.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. Iron, B. Zinc, C. Boron, D. Molybdenum. List II: I. Synthesis of auxin, II. Component of nitrate reductase, III. Activator of catalase, IV. Cell elongation and differentiation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Iron is an activator of catalase (A-III). Zinc is involved in the synthesis of auxin (tryptophan synthesis) (B-I). Boron is required for cell elongation and differentiation (C-IV). Molybdenum is a component of nitrate reductase (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Select the favourable conditions required for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin at the alveoli.
options: Low pO2, low pCO2, more H+, higher temperature
High pO2, low pCO2, less H+, lower temperature
Low pO2, high pCO2, more H+, higher temperature
High pO2, high pCO2, less H+, higher temperature
questions.explanation: Oxyhaemoglobin formation at alveoli is favoured by high pO2, low pCO2, less H+ concentration, and lower temperature — opposite conditions favour oxygen release at tissues (Bohr effect).

questions.text: Now a days it is possible to detect the mutated gene causing cancer by allowing radioactive probe to hybridise its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, followed by its detection using autoradiography because:
options: Mutated gene does not appear on photographic film as the probe has complementarity with it.
Mutated gene partially appears on a photographic film.
Mutated gene completely and clearly appears on a photographic film.
Mutated gene does not appear on a photographic film as the probe has no complementarity with it.
questions.explanation: The radioactive probe is designed to be complementary to the normal (non-mutated) gene sequence. Since it cannot hybridize with the mutated gene (no complementarity), the mutated gene does not appear (no signal) on the autoradiograph/photographic film.

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 2 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Movement and accumulation of ions across a membrane against their concentration gradient can be explained by:
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy (ATP) to move ions and molecules across a membrane against their concentration gradient, unlike passive transport, facilitated diffusion, or osmosis, which all move substances along their gradient.

questions.text: Bulliform cells are responsible for
options: Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
Protecting the plant from salt stress.
questions.topic: Bulliform Cells - Function in Leaf Curling
questions.explanation: Bulliform (motor) cells are large, empty cells present in the epidermis of grass (monocot) leaves. They help in inward curling of leaves during water stress to minimize water loss. 11th NCERT Page No. 77.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Lipase (B) Nuclease (C) Protease (D) Amylase
List II: (I) Peptide bond (II) Ester bond (III) Glycosidic bond (IV) Phosphodiester bond
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Lipase hydrolyzes ester bonds in lipids (A-II). Nuclease hydrolyzes phosphodiester bonds in nucleic acids (B-IV). Protease hydrolyzes peptide bonds in proteins (C-I). Amylase hydrolyzes glycosidic bonds in carbohydrates (D-III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III is correct.

questions.text: What is the name of the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart in a frog?
questions.explanation: Vena cava carries deoxygenated blood from body parts to the sinus venosus, which then passes this blood into the right atrium of the frog's heart.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement.
options: Split gene arrangement is characteristic of prokaryotes.
In capping, methyl guanosine triphosphate is added to the 3' end of hnRNA.
RNA polymerase binds with Rho factor to terminate the process of transcription in bacteria.
The coding strand in a transcription unit is copied to an mRNA.
questions.explanation: Rho factor is a protein that binds with RNA polymerase and assists in terminating transcription in bacteria (Rho-dependent termination). Split genes are characteristic of eukaryotes (not prokaryotes); capping adds methyl guanosine triphosphate to the 5' end (not 3'); and the template strand (not coding strand) is copied to make mRNA.

questions.text: Use of bioresources by multinational companies and organisations without authorisation from the concerned country and its people is called
questions.explanation: Biopiracy refers to the unauthorised use/exploitation of a country's bioresources (and associated traditional knowledge) by other nations or multinational companies without fair compensation or permission.

questions.text:
Which of the following are secondary lymphoid organs?
(a) Bone marrow (b) Tonsils (c) Spleen (d) Thymus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Bone marrow and thymus are PRIMARY lymphoid organs (where lymphocytes mature). Tonsils and spleen are SECONDARY lymphoid organs (where mature lymphocytes interact with antigens and undergo proliferation into effector cells), along with lymph nodes, Peyer's patches, and appendix. So (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: In which animal do haploid cells divide mitotically to produce gametes?
questions.topic: Animals where haploid cells divide mitotically to produce gametes
questions.explanation: In honeybees, males are haploid (from unfertilized eggs) and produce sperm via mitotic division of haploid cells, not meiosis.

questions.text: Under normal physiological conditions in human being every 100ml of oxygenated blood can deliver _____ ml of O₂ to the tissues.
questions.explanation: Under normal physiological conditions, every 100 ml of oxygenated blood delivers around 5 ml of O₂ to the tissues.

questions.text: Auxin is used by gardeners to prepare weed-free lawns. But no damage is caused to grass as auxin
options: Does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.
Can help in cell division in grasses, to produce growth
Promotes abscission of mature leaves only
questions.topic: Auxin Herbicide - Selective Action on Dicot Weeds
questions.explanation: Synthetic auxins like 2,4-D are used as selective herbicides because they do not affect mature monocotyledonous plants (grasses) but kill broad-leaved dicot weeds. 11th NCERT Page No. 176.

questions.text:
Match the hominids with their correct brain size.
(a) Homo habilis (b) Homo neanderthalensis (c) Homo erectus (d) Homo sapiens
(i) 900cc (ii) 1350cc (iii) 650-800 cc (iv) 1400 cc
Select the correct option.
questions.explanation: Homo habilis had a brain capacity of about 650-800 cc (iii); Homo erectus about 900 cc (i); Homo neanderthalensis about 1350 cc (ii); Homo sapiens about 1400 cc (iv).

questions.text: Use of an artificial kidney during hemodialysis may result in: (a) Nitrogenous waste build-up in the body (b) Non-elimination of excess potassium ions (c) Reduced absorption of calcium ions from gastro-intestinal tract (d) Reduced RBC production. Which of the following options is the most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Hemodialysis via artificial kidney does not correct the reduced absorption of calcium ions from the GI tract (normally regulated by erythropoietin and vitamin D activation functions of kidney) or the reduced RBC production (due to lack of erythropoietin secretion by diseased kidneys), since dialysis only removes wastes/excess ions but doesn't replace the kidney's hormonal functions.

questions.text: Tegmina in cockroach, arises from:
questions.explanation: The tegmina (forewings) of a cockroach arise from the mesothorax, while the hind wings arise from the metathorax.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the most abundant protein in the animals?
questions.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal kingdom, forming a major structural component of connective tissues, skin, bones and cartilage.

questions.text: Which one of the following symbols represents mating between relatives (consanguineous mating) in human pedigree analysis?
options: A double horizontal line connecting a square and a circle (indicating consanguineous mating)
A square and circle connected with a single line, with a filled square offspring below connected to another couple above
A filled square, filled circle, and filled diamond shown side by side
A square connected to a circle by a single horizontal line (normal mating symbol)
questions.explanation: In pedigree analysis, a double horizontal line connecting a square (male) and a circle (female) represents consanguineous mating (mating between relatives), as opposed to a single line which represents a normal (non-related) mating.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct? A. The Amazon rainforest being cut and cleared for cultivation of soyabeans is an example of habitat loss. B. Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon became extinct due to over-exploitation by humans. C. The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in East Africa helped in population growth of cichlid fish in the lake. D. Water hyacinth is an invasive species. E. When a species becomes extinct, the plant and animal species associated with it are not affected.
options: A, B, D and E only
questions.topic: Correct statements about habitat loss/extinction examples
questions.explanation: A is true (habitat loss example). B is true (over-exploitation led to their extinction). D is true (water hyacinth is invasive). C is false (Nile perch caused decline, not growth, of cichlid populations). E is false (co-extinction occurs). A, B and D only.

questions.text: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and calcium at a given time, is referred to as:
questions.topic: Term for nutrient amount in soil at a given time
questions.explanation: The amount of nutrients present in the soil at any given time is called the standing state (or standing state of nutrients).

questions.text: Diadelphous stamens are found in:
questions.explanation: Diadelphous stamens (filaments united into two bundles) are characteristic of pea (Fabaceae family) flowers.

questions.text: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system by the release of______.
questions.explanation: Muscle contraction is initiated when a motor neuron releases the neurotransmitter acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, which generates an action potential in the muscle fiber.

questions.text: Which of the following elements is responsible for maintaining turgor in cells?
questions.explanation: Potassium plays a key role in maintaining the turgor pressure of cells, regulating osmotic balance and stomatal movement.

questions.text: A non-proteinaceous enzyme is:
questions.explanation: Ribozymes are catalytic RNA molecules, making them non-proteinaceous enzymes, unlike the other options which are protein enzymes.

questions.text: Which of the following is present between the adjacent bones of the vertebral column?
questions.explanation: Cartilaginous intervertebral discs are present between adjacent vertebrae of the vertebral column, allowing flexibility and acting as shock absorbers.

questions.text: A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by the three regions in DNA and these are with respect to upstream and down stream end;
questions.topic: Transcription Unit - Promoter, Structural Gene, Terminator
questions.explanation: A transcription unit in DNA is defined by three regions: the promoter (upstream), the structural gene, and the terminator (downstream). 12th NCERT Page No. 92.

questions.text: Which of the following hormones released from the pituitary is actually synthesized in the hypothalamus?
questions.topic: Hypothalamic Hormones Released by Posterior Pituitary (ADH)
questions.explanation: ADH (vasopressin) and oxytocin are actually synthesized by the hypothalamus and are only stored and released from the posterior pituitary. LH, FSH and ACTH are synthesized and released by the anterior pituitary itself. 11th NCERT, Page No. - 242.

questions.text: Several hormones like hCG, hPL, estrogen, progesterone are produced by:
questions.explanation: The placenta acts as a temporary endocrine gland during pregnancy, producing hCG, human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogen, and progesterone.

questions.text: The posterior pituitary gland is not a 'true' endocrine gland because:
options: It is provided with a duct
It only stores and releases hormones
It is under the regulation of hypothalamus
questions.explanation: The posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) does not synthesize hormones itself; it only stores and releases hormones (oxytocin and vasopressin) that are synthesized by the hypothalamus, so it is not a 'true' endocrine gland.

questions.text: Choose the correct statement.
options: All Pisces have gills covered by an operculum.
All cyclostomes do not possess jaws and paired fins.
All reptiles have a three-chambered heart.
questions.explanation: All cyclostomes (like Petromyzon, Myxine) lack jaws and paired fins, which is correct. Not all Pisces have an operculum (e.g., cartilaginous fish have gill slits without an operculum), not all mammals are viviparous (e.g., Platypus, Echidna lay eggs), and crocodiles (reptiles) have a four-chambered heart.

questions.text: Match List I with List II related to muscular/skeletal system: List I — A. Tetany, B. Arthritis, C. Myasthenia gravis, D. Muscular dystrophy. List II — I. Inflammation of joints, II. Autoimmune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction, III. Wild contraction in muscle due to low Ca2+ in body fluid, IV. Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle.
questions.explanation: Tetany is caused by low Ca2+ causing wild contraction (III); Arthritis is inflammation of joints (I); Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of neuromuscular junction (II); Muscular dystrophy is progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle (IV). A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.text: The vascular cambium normally gives rise to:
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium, a lateral meristem, produces secondary xylem towards the inside and secondary phloem towards the outside during secondary growth in dicot stems and roots.

questions.text: Match the trophic levels with their correct species examples in grassland ecosystem: (a) Fourth trophic level, (b) Second trophic level, (c) First trophic level, (d) Third trophic level with (i) Crow, (ii) Vulture, (iii) Rabbit, (iv) Grass
questions.topic: Trophic levels and examples in grassland ecosystem
questions.explanation: In the grassland food chain (Grass→Rabbit→Snake/Crow→Vulture/Hawk type), grass is the first trophic level (iv), rabbit (herbivore) is the second (iii)... per official key, fourth trophic level is vulture (ii), second trophic level is rabbit (iii), first trophic level is grass (iv), third trophic level is crow (i). This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: AGGTATCGCAT is a sequence from the coding strand of a gene. What will be the corresponding sequence of the transcribed mRNA?
questions.explanation: Since the coding strand has the same sequence as the mRNA (except T is replaced by U), the mRNA sequence transcribed will be identical to the coding strand with U in place of T: AGGUAUCGCAU.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of chordates?
questions.explanation: Chordates are characterized by the presence of pharyngeal gill slits (not their absence), a dorsal hollow nerve cord, a notochord, and a post-anal tail at some stage of development. 'Absence of gills' is therefore NOT a characteristic of chordates -- the presence of gill slits is.

questions.text: Due to increasing air borne allergens and pollutants, many people in urban areas are suffering from respiratory disorder causing wheezing due to:
options: Proliferation of fibrous tissues and damage of the alveolar walls
reduction in the secretion of surfactants by pneumocytes
benign growth on mucous lining of nasal cavity
questions.explanation: Wheezing due to air borne allergens and pollutants in urban areas is caused by inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles, a characteristic feature of asthma.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. Taenia, B. Paramoecium, C. Periplaneta, D. Pheretima. List II: I. Nephridia, II. Contractile vacuole, III. Flame cells, IV. Urecose gland. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Taenia (tapeworm) excretes via flame cells (A-III). Paramoecium uses a contractile vacuole for osmoregulation/excretion (B-II). Periplaneta (cockroach) excretes via uricose glands (C-IV). Pheretima (earthworm) excretes via nephridia (D-I). So the correct match is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is not true about the universal rules of binomial nomenclature?
options: The first word in a biological name represents the specific epithet, while the second component denotes the genus
The specific epithet in the biological name starts with a small letter
Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined or printed in italics
Biological names are generally in Latin
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first word is the genus and the second is the specific epithet — the reverse of what statement 1 says, making it the incorrect statement.

questions.text: In gel electrophoresis, separated DNA fragments can be visualized with the help of:
questions.topic: Visualization of DNA in gel electrophoresis
questions.explanation: DNA fragments separated by gel electrophoresis are stained with ethidium bromide, which intercalates into the DNA and fluoresces under UV radiation, allowing the bands to be visualised.

questions.text: Alpha-helix is found in which level of protein structure?
questions.topic: Level of protein structure for alpha-helix
questions.explanation: The alpha-helix is a type of secondary structure of proteins, formed by hydrogen bonding within the polypeptide backbone.

questions.text: If a colour blind female marries a man whose mother was also colour blind, what are the chances of her progeny having colour blindness?
questions.explanation: A colour-blind man's mother being colour blind (XcXc) means the man himself must be XcY (colour blind, since he gets one Xc from his mother). Crossing a colour-blind woman (XcXc) with a colour-blind man (XcY) gives all daughters XcXc (colour blind) and all sons XcY (colour blind), so 100% of the progeny will be colour blind.

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage of inbreeding?
options: It exposes harmful recessive genes that are eliminated by selection.
Elimination of less desirable genes and accumulation of superior genes takes place due to it.
It decreases the productivity of inbred population, after continuous inbreeding.
questions.explanation: Decreased productivity of an inbred population after continuous inbreeding (inbreeding depression) is a disadvantage, not an advantage, of inbreeding. The other options describe genuine advantages of inbreeding — exposing and eliminating harmful recessive genes and accumulating superior genes (note: inbreeding actually increases, not decreases, homozygosity, but that aspect is treated as an advantage statement here).

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Protoplast fusion, (b) Plant tissue culture, (c) Meristem culture, (d) Micropropagation with (i) Totipotency, (ii) Pomato, (iii) Somaclones, (iv) Virus free plants.
questions.topic: Matching plant biotechnology term to application
questions.explanation: Protoplast fusion gives hybrids like Pomato (ii); Plant tissue culture is based on totipotency (i); Meristem culture gives virus-free plants (iv); Micropropagation produces somaclones (iii). (a)-(ii),(b)-(i),(c)-(iv),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: Good vision depends on adequate intake of carotene-rich food. Select the best option from the following statements: (a) Vitamin A derivatives are formed from carotene. (b) The photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the inner segment. (c) Retinal is a derivative of Vitamin A. (d) Retinal is a light absorbing part of all the visual photopigments.
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (c), and (d) are correct: Vitamin A derivatives form from carotene, retinal is a Vitamin A derivative, and retinal is the light-absorbing component of all visual photopigments. Statement (b) is incorrect because photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the outer segment, not the inner segment, of photoreceptor cells.

questions.text: By which method was a new breed 'Hisardale' of sheep formed by using Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams?
questions.explanation: Hisardale, a new sheep breed, was developed by cross-breeding Bikaneri ewes with Marino rams, combining desirable traits from both breeds.

questions.text: Cuboidal epithelium with brush border of microvilli is found in:
questions.topic: Location of cuboidal epithelium with brush border
questions.explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron is lined with cuboidal epithelium bearing a brush border of microvilli, which increases the surface area for reabsorption.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Exophthalmic goiter (B) Acromegaly (C) Cushing's syndrome (D) Cretinism
List II: (I) Excess secretion of cortisol, moon face & hyperglycemia (II) Hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone and stunted growth. (III) Hyper secretion of thyroid hormone & protruding eye balls. (IV) Excessive secretion of growth hormone.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Exophthalmic goiter involves hyper secretion of thyroid hormone and protruding eye balls (A-III). Acromegaly results from excessive secretion of growth hormone (B-IV). Cushing's syndrome involves excess cortisol, moon face, and hyperglycemia (C-I). Cretinism involves hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone and stunted growth (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Organ of Corti, (b) Cochlea, (c) Eustachian tube, (d) Stapes with (i) Connects middle ear and pharynx, (ii) Coiled part of the labyrinth, (iii) Attached to the oval window, (iv) Located on the basilar membrane.
questions.explanation: Organ of Corti is located on the basilar membrane (iv), Cochlea is the coiled part of the labyrinth (ii), Eustachian tube connects the middle ear and pharynx (i), and Stapes is attached to the oval window (iii). This matches a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 3 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification.
Reason (R): The ampicillin resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both the assertion (PCR amplifies DNA) and reason (ampicillin resistance gene as selectable marker) are correct statements, but they are unrelated to each other, so R does not explain A.

questions.text: Select the correct pair.
options: Loose parenchyma cells rupturing the epidermis and forming a lens shaped opening in bark — Spongy parenchyma
Large colorless empty cells in the epidermis of grass leaves — Subsidiary cells
In dicot leaves vascular bundles are surrounded by large thick-walled cells — Conjunctive tissue
Cells of medullary rays that form part of cambial ring — Interfascicular cambium
questions.topic: Correct Pair Matching - Plant Tissue Terms
questions.explanation: Cells of the medullary rays that lie between vascular bundles and become meristematic to form part of the cambial ring are called interfascicular cambium — correctly paired in option 4. (The first option describes lenticels, not spongy parenchyma; the structures in options 2 and 3 are also mismatched with their standard terms — bulliform cells and bundle sheath respectively.)

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Both species are harmed, (B) One species is harmed and the other is benefited, (C) Both species are benefited, (D) One is benefited while the other has no effect
List-II: (I) Predation, (II) Mutualism, (III) Competition, (IV) Commensalism
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: When both species are harmed, it is competition (III). When one species is harmed and the other benefited, it is predation (I) (predator benefits, prey harmed). When both species are benefited, it is mutualism (II). When one is benefited while the other has no effect, it is commensalism (IV). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.text: The number of action potentials generated by sino-arterial node (SAN) in a healthy human is ______ per minute.
questions.explanation: The sino-atrial node (SAN), the natural pacemaker of the heart, generates action potentials at a rate of approximately 70-75 per minute in a healthy resting human, setting the normal resting heart rate.

questions.text: Select the correct group/set of Australian Marsupials exhibiting adaptive radiation.
options: Mole, Flying squirrel, Tasmanian tiger cat
questions.explanation: Numbat, Spotted cuscus, and Flying phalanger are all Australian marsupials that are classic examples of adaptive radiation, having diversified from a common ancestral marsupial stock to occupy different ecological niches.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Non-Medicated IUD (B) Copper releasing IUD (C) Hormone releasing IUD (D) Implants
List II: (I) Multiload 375 (II) Progestogens (III) Lippes loop (IV) LNG-20
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Non-medicated IUDs include the Lippes loop (A-III). Copper releasing IUDs include Multiload 375 (B-I). Hormone releasing IUDs include LNG-20 (C-IV). Implants deliver progestogens (D-II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II is correct.
