questions.text: What type of ecological pyramid would be obtained with the following data? Secondary consumer: 120 g, Primary consumer: 60 g, Primary producer: 10 g
questions.explanation: Since the biomass increases from the primary producer (10g) to primary consumer (60g) to secondary consumer (120g), the pyramid of biomass is inverted (narrow base, wider top), typical of aquatic ecosystems.

questions.text: Pollen grains can be stored for several years in liquid nitrogen having a temperature of
questions.explanation: Liquid nitrogen, used for cryopreservation of pollen grains (pollen cryobanks), is maintained at a temperature of approximately -196°C.

questions.text: Which one of the following plants does not show plasticity?
questions.explanation: Maize, being a monocot with simple, generally uniform leaf morphology, does not typically show the heterophylly/plasticity seen in dicots like cotton, coriander, and buttercup, where leaf shape can vary based on environmental conditions or developmental stage.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Autoimmune disorder is a condition where body defense mechanism recognizes its own cells as foreign bodies. Statement II: Rheumatoid arthritis is a condition where body does not attack self cells. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: autoimmune disorders occur when the immune system recognizes self-cells as foreign and attacks them. Statement II is incorrect: rheumatoid arthritis is actually an autoimmune disorder where the body DOES attack its own joint tissues, not one where self cells are spared.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
options: Starch synthesis in pea : Multiple alleles
questions.topic: Linkage, sex determination and inheritance patterns
questions.explanation: Starch synthesis in pea is actually an example of incomplete dominance (not multiple alleles), making this pairing incorrect; the correct associations are T.H. Morgan with linkage, XO type sex determination with grasshoppers, and ABO blood grouping with co-dominance.

questions.text: What is the reason behind production of large holes in 'Swiss Cheese'?
options: The production of large amount of CO2 and H2 by Trichoderma polysporum
The production of large amount of CO2 and H2 by lactic acid bacteria called Lactobacillus
The production of large amount of CO2 by Propionibacterium sharmanii
The production of large amount of CO2 by Clostridium butylicum
questions.topic: Reason for large holes in Swiss cheese
questions.explanation: Swiss cheese's characteristic large holes are produced by CO2 released by the bacterium Propionibacterium sharmanii (shermanii) during fermentation.

questions.text: Among the following sets of examples for divergent evolution, select the incorrect option.
options: Forelimbs of man, bat and cheetah
Eye of octopus, bat and man
Brain of bat, man and cheetah
Heart of bat, man and cheetah
questions.explanation: The eye of the octopus (cephalopod mollusc) evolved independently from the eyes of bats and humans (vertebrates) through convergent evolution (analogous structures), not divergent evolution from a common ancestral structure, making this pairing incorrect for divergent evolution.

questions.text:
Which of the following are characteristic features of Solanaceae family?
(a) Flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic
(b) Calyx have five sepals and are united
(c) Androecium have five stamens and are epipetalous
(d) Ovary is inferior
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: In Solanaceae, flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic (regular) -- (a) correct. The calyx has five sepals, gamosepalous (united) -- (b) correct. The androecium has five stamens, epipetalous (attached to the petals) -- (c) correct. The ovary in Solanaceae is SUPERIOR, not inferior -- (d) is incorrect. So (a), (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: Pinus seed cannot germinate and establish without fungal association. This is because:
options: It has very hard seed coat
Its seeds contain inhibitors that prevent germination.
It has obligate association with mycorrhizae.
questions.explanation: Pinus has an obligate association with mycorrhizal fungi, which is necessary for seed germination and establishment of the seedling.

questions.text:
Match the following hormones with the respective disease:
(1) Insulin (2) Thyroxin (3) Corticoids (4) Growth Hormone
(i) Addison's disease (ii) Diabetes insipidus (iii) Acromegaly (iv) Goitre (v) Diabetes mellitus
Select the correct option.
questions.explanation: Insulin deficiency causes Diabetes mellitus (v); Thyroxin deficiency causes Goitre (iv); Corticoid deficiency causes Addison's disease (i); Growth Hormone excess causes Acromegaly (iii).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequence to cut DNA known as palindromic nucleotide sequence. Statement II: Restriction endonucleases cut the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindromic site. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: restriction endonucleases recognize palindromic sequences, and they typically cut the DNA at specific points slightly away from the exact center of the palindromic recognition site, generating sticky or blunt ends.

questions.text: Pollination in water hyacinth and water lily is brought about by the agency of:
questions.explanation: Despite growing in water, water hyacinth and water lily flowers emerge above the water surface and are pollinated by insects or wind, not by water (they are not hydrophilous in pollination).

questions.text: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of gymnosperms?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms (gymnos: naked, sperma: seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed/naked, both before and after fertilization. Class 11th NCERT Page No 34.

questions.text: Nitrogenous waste is excreted in the form of pellet or paste by:
questions.explanation: Pavo (peacock), being a bird, is uricotelic, excreting nitrogenous waste as semi-solid uric acid paste/pellets to conserve water, unlike mammals (ureotelic) and most aquatic animals (ammonotelic).

questions.text: Which of following organisms cannot fix nitrogen? A. Azotobacter, B. Oscillatoria, C. Anabaena, D. Volvox, E. Nostoc. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Azotobacter (bacterium), Oscillatoria, Anabaena, and Nostoc (cyanobacteria) are all nitrogen-fixing organisms. Volvox is a green alga that does not fix nitrogen.

questions.text: Identify the part of the seed from the given figure which is destined to form root when the seed germinates. [Figure: seed diagram with parts labeled A, B, C, D pointing to embryo structures - plumule, radicle region]
questions.topic: Dicot Seed Structure - Radicle Identification in Figure
questions.explanation: The radicle, labeled C in the figure, is the part of the embryo destined to develop into the root upon germination. 11th NCERT Page No. 67.

questions.text: Match the plant with the kind of life cycle it exhibits: (a) Spirogyra (b) Fern (c) Funaria (d) Cycas -- List-II: (i) Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte (ii) Dominant haploid free-living gametophyte (iii) Dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte called prothallus (iv) Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Life Cycles of Plant Groups - Matching
questions.explanation: Spirogyra (alga) has a dominant haploid free-living gametophyte (ii). Fern has a dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte prothallus (iii). Funaria (moss) has a dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent sporophyte (iv). Cycas (gymnosperm) has dominant diploid sporophyte with highly reduced gametophyte (i). So a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(a) Energy flow from producers to consumers is unidirectional
(b) Energy pyramid can never be inverted
(c) Transfer of energy follows the 1% law
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional, moving from producers to consumers (unlike nutrient cycling, which is cyclic) -- (a) is correct. Only about 1% of the solar energy incident on producers is typically captured and converted into chemical (net primary productive) energy, sometimes referred to as the 'one percent law' of energy capture efficiency by autotrophs -- (c) is correct in this sense. (Note: pyramid of energy is generally taught as always upright, but per this question's answer key, (b) is not included among the correct statements.)

questions.text:
Match the following structures with their respective location in organs:
(a) Crypts of Lieberkuhn (b) Glisson's Capsule (c) Islets of Langerhans (d) Brunner's Glands
(i) Pancreas (ii) Duodenum (iii) Small intestine (iv) Liver
Select the correct option from the following:
questions.explanation: Crypts of Lieberkuhn are found in small intestine (iii); Glisson's Capsule covers the liver (iv); Islets of Langerhans are in the pancreas (i); Brunner's Glands are in the duodenum (ii).

questions.text: The DNA fragments separated on an agarose gel can be visualised after staining with:
questions.explanation: Ethidium bromide intercalates into DNA and fluoresces under UV light, allowing DNA fragments separated on an agarose gel to be visualised.

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Pituitary gland, (b) Thyroid gland, (c) Adrenal gland, (d) Pancreas with (i) Grave's disease, (ii) Diabetes mellitus, (iii) Diabetes insipidus, (iv) Addison's disease
questions.explanation: Pituitary gland dysfunction (ADH deficiency) causes Diabetes insipidus (iii), Thyroid gland hyperactivity causes Grave's disease (i), Adrenal gland hypofunction causes Addison's disease (iv), and Pancreas dysfunction causes Diabetes mellitus (ii). This matches a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

questions.text: Which of the following restriction enzymes produces blunt ends?
questions.explanation: EcoRV is a restriction enzyme that cuts DNA to produce blunt ends, while Hind III, Sal I, and Xho I produce sticky/cohesive ends.

questions.text: Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyze the following reaction: S-G + S# → S + S#-G. Where, G → a group other than hydrogen, S → a substrate, S# → another substrate
questions.explanation: This reaction shows transfer of a group (G, other than hydrogen) from one substrate to another, which is catalyzed by transferase enzymes.

questions.text: Read the following statements on lipids and find out correct set of statements: (a) Lecithin found in the plasma membrane is a glycolipid (b) Saturated fatty acids possess one or more C=C bonds (c) Gingely oil has lower melting point, hence remains as oil in winter (d) Lipids are generally insoluble in water but soluble in some organic solvents (e) When fatty acid is esterified with glycerol, monoglycerides are formed. Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.explanation: (c) is correct: gingely (sesame) oil has a lower melting point, remaining liquid in winter. (d) is correct: lipids are insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents. (e) is correct: esterification of fatty acid with glycerol can form monoglycerides (partial esterification). (a) is incorrect as lecithin is a phospholipid, not a glycolipid. (b) is incorrect as saturated fatty acids lack C=C double bonds by definition.

questions.text: Which of the following describes the graph correctly? The graph shows potential energy vs. reaction progress, with two curves from substrate to product — a higher peak with energy difference B and a lower peak with energy difference A.
options: Exothermic reaction with energy A in absence of enzyme and B in presence of enzyme
Endothermic reaction with energy A in presence of enzyme and B in absence of enzyme
Exothermic reaction with energy A in presence of enzyme and B in absence of enzyme
Endothermic reaction with energy A in absence of enzyme and B in presence of enzyme
questions.explanation: The product is at lower potential energy than the substrate, indicating an exothermic reaction. The lower activation energy barrier (A) corresponds to the reaction in presence of enzyme (catalyzed, lower activation energy), while the higher barrier (B) is without enzyme (uncatalyzed).

questions.text: In Antirrhinum (Snapdragon), a red flower was crossed with a white flower and in F1 generation, pink flowers were obtained. When pink flowers were selfed, the F2 generation showed white, red and pink flowers. Choose the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Law of segregation does not apply in the experiment.
This experiment does not follow the principle of Dominance.
Pink colour in F1 is due to incomplete dominance.
questions.explanation: The law of segregation DOES apply in this experiment (it's a case of incomplete dominance, where alleles still segregate normally during gamete formation) - only the principle of dominance doesn't apply. So statement 2 (claiming law of segregation doesn't apply) is the incorrect statement.

questions.text: The lactose present in the growth medium of bacteria is transported to the cell by the action of:
questions.topic: Lac Operon - Permease Transport of Lactose
questions.explanation: Permease, one of the enzymes encoded by the lac operon, increases permeability of the cell to allow lactose to enter the cell. 12th NCERT Page No. 100.

questions.text: Which of the following statements wrongly represents the nature of smooth muscle?
options: These muscles are present in the wall of blood vessels
Communication among the cells is performed by intercalated discs
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs are a feature of CARDIAC muscle, not smooth muscle, making statement 4 the wrong representation of smooth muscle.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:
Assertion A: FSH acts upon ovarian follicles in female and Leydig cells in male.
Reason R: Growing ovarian follicles secrete estrogen in female while interstitial cells secrete androgen in male human being.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is false because FSH acts upon Sertoli cells (not Leydig cells) in males; LH acts upon Leydig cells. Reason R is true, as growing ovarian follicles do secrete estrogen and interstitial (Leydig) cells do secrete androgen, but this reason doesn't explain the false assertion.

questions.text: In the exponential growth equation Nt = N0e^(rt), e represents:
questions.explanation: In the exponential growth equation, e is the base of natural logarithms (≈2.71828).

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Floating Ribs, (b) Acromion, (c) Scapula, (d) Glenoid cavity with (i) Located between second and seventh ribs, (ii) Head of the Humerus, (iii) Clavicle, (iv) Do not connect with the sternum
questions.explanation: Floating ribs do not connect with the sternum (iv), Acromion articulates with the clavicle (iii), Scapula is located between the second and seventh ribs (i), and Glenoid cavity is where the head of the humerus fits (ii). This matches a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text: Which of the following plant produces non-albuminous seeds?
questions.explanation: Non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seeds are those where the endosperm is completely consumed during seed development and food is stored in the cotyledons instead. Pea is a classic example of a non-albuminous seed. Maize, barley, and wheat are all albuminous seeds (retain endosperm at maturity).

questions.text: In the following palindromic base sequences of DNA, which one can be cut easily by particular restriction enzyme? (1) 5'GATACT3'; 3'CTATGA5' (2) 5'GAATTC3'; 3'CTTAAG5' (3) 5'CTCAGT3'; 3'GAGTCA5' (4) 5'GTATTC3'; 3'CATAAG5'
questions.explanation: A true palindromic sequence reads the same 5' to 3' on both strands. GAATTC/CTTAAG (reading the complementary strand 5' to 3' as GAATTC) is a true palindrome and is the recognition sequence for the restriction enzyme EcoRI, making it easily cut.

questions.text: A dioecious flowering plant prevents both:
questions.explanation: In dioecious plants, male and female flowers are borne on separate plants entirely, which prevents both autogamy (self-pollination within the same flower) and geitonogamy (pollination between different flowers of the same plant).

questions.text: During muscular contraction which of the following events occur? (a) 'H' zone disappears. (b) 'A' band widens. (c) 'I' band reduces in width. (d) Myosine hydrolyzes ATP, releasing the ADP and Pi. (e) Z-lines attached to actins are pulled inwards. Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: During contraction: H zone disappears (a), I band reduces (c), myosin hydrolyzes ATP (d), Z-lines pulled inward (e) are all correct; A band width stays constant (b is false). (a), (c), (d), (e) only.

questions.text: Match the following sexually transmitted diseases (Column - I) with their causative agent (Column - II) and select the correct option: Column I: (a) Gonorrhea (b) Syphilis (c) Genital Warts (d) AIDS. Column II: (i) HIV (ii) Neisseria (iii) Treponema (iv) Human Papilloma Virus.
questions.explanation: Gonorrhea is caused by Neisseria (gonorrhoeae), Syphilis by Treponema (pallidum), Genital Warts by Human Papilloma Virus, and AIDS by HIV. This matches (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

questions.text: Viroids differ from viruses in having:
questions.explanation: Viroids are infectious agents consisting of free RNA molecules without any protein coat, unlike viruses, which have their nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) enclosed within a protein coat (capsid).

questions.text: Identify the cells whose secretion protects the lining of gastro-intestinal tract from various enzymes.
questions.explanation: Goblet cells secrete mucus, which protects the lining of the gastrointestinal tract from the digestive action of various enzymes.

questions.text: Match the following diseases with the causative organism and select the correct option: (a) Typhoid, (b) Pneumonia, (c) Filariasis, (d) Malaria with (i) Wuchereria, (ii) Plasmodium, (iii) Salmonella, (iv) Haemophilus
questions.explanation: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella (iii), Pneumonia by Haemophilus (iv), Filariasis by Wuchereria (i), and Malaria by Plasmodium (ii). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 4 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: If the head of cockroach is removed, it may live for few days because:
options: the supra-oesophageal ganglia of the cockroach are situated in ventral part of abdomen.
the cockroach does not have nervous system.
the head holds a small proportion of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral part of its body.
the head holds a 1/3rd of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the dorsal part of its body.
questions.explanation: The cockroach's nervous system is a ventral nerve cord with ganglia distributed along most of the body, with only a small portion of the total nervous system located in the head, allowing the body to survive for some time even after decapitation.

questions.text: Zygotic meiosis is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: In Chlamydomonas, which has a haplontic life cycle, the diploid zygote is the only diploid stage and immediately undergoes meiosis (zygotic meiosis) to restore the haploid condition.

questions.text: In the lac operon, the z gene codes for:
questions.explanation: The lacZ gene codes for beta-galactosidase, the enzyme that hydrolyses lactose.

questions.text: Which one of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
questions.explanation: Ex-situ conservation involves taking threatened animals/plants out of their natural habitat and placing them in a special protected setting. Zoological parks and botanical gardens serve this purpose. National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and protected areas are forms of in-situ conservation.

questions.text: In racemose inflorescence, ___________.
options: flowers are borne in an acropetal succession
the main axis terminates in a flower
questions.explanation: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow (unlimited growth) and flowers are borne in acropetal succession (youngest near the apex).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: The first stage of gametophyte in the life cycle of moss is protonema stage. Reason R: Protonema develops directly from spores produced in capsule. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is correct — the protonema is the first (juvenile, filamentous) stage of the gametophyte generation in mosses. Reason R is correct and explains A — the protonema develops directly by germination of spores produced inside the capsule (sporangium).

questions.text: The appearance of recombination nodules on homologous chromosomes during meiosis characterizes:
options: Sites at which crossing over occurs
questions.explanation: Recombination nodules are structures that appear on the synaptonemal complex during pachytene stage of meiosis I, marking the sites at which crossing over occurs between homologous chromosomes.

questions.text: World Ozone Day is celebrated on
questions.explanation: World Ozone Day is observed on 16th September every year, commemorating the signing of the Montreal Protocol to protect the ozone layer.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Lenticels, (b) Cork cambium, (c) Secondary cortex, (d) Cork with (i) Phellogen, (ii) Suberin deposition, (iii) Exchange of gases, (iv) Phelloderm.
questions.explanation: Lenticels allow exchange of gases (iii); Cork cambium is phellogen (i); Secondary cortex is phelloderm (iv); Cork shows suberin deposition (ii). (a)-(iii),(b)-(i),(c)-(iv),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: The cofactor of the enzyme carboxypeptidase is:
questions.explanation: Zinc is the cofactor (metal ion) required for the activity of the enzyme carboxypeptidase. 11th NCERT Page No. 118.

questions.text: Which of the following muscular disorders is inherited?
questions.explanation: Muscular dystrophy is a genetically inherited muscular disorder, unlike Myasthenia gravis (autoimmune), Botulism (bacterial toxin-caused), and Tetany (calcium deficiency-caused).

questions.text: Breeding crops with higher levels of vitamins and minerals or higher proteins and healthier fats is called:
questions.explanation: Biofortification is the breeding of crops with higher levels of vitamins, minerals, proteins, and healthier fats to improve nutritional value.

questions.text: Which of the following can be used as a biocontrol agent in the treatment of plant diseases?
questions.explanation: Trichoderma is a free-living fungus used as a biocontrol agent against several plant pathogens.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Pons (B) Hypothalamus (C) Medulla (D) Cerebellum
List II: (I) Provides additional space for Neurons. Regulates posture and balance. (II) Controls respiration and gastric secretions. (III) Connects different regions of brain. (IV) Neuro secretory cells
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Pons connects different regions of the brain (A-III). Hypothalamus contains neurosecretory cells that secrete hormones (B-IV). Medulla controls respiration and gastric secretions (C-II). Cerebellum provides additional space for neurons and regulates posture and balance (D-I). So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following is not observed during apoplastic pathway?
options: Movement of water occurs through intercellular spaces and wall of the cells
The movement does not involve crossing of cell membrane
The movement is aided by cytoplasmic streaming
Apoplast is continuous and does not provide any barrier to water movement
questions.explanation: Cytoplasmic streaming is associated with the symplastic pathway (movement through cytoplasm via plasmodesmata), not the apoplastic pathway, which involves movement through cell walls and intercellular spaces without crossing membranes or involving cytoplasm.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A protein is imagined as a line, the left end represented by first amino acid (C-terminal) and the right end represented by last amino acid (N-terminal). Statement II: Adult human haemoglobin consists of 4 subunits (two subunits of alpha type and two subunits of beta type). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.topic: Protein Structure Terminals and Haemoglobin Subunits
questions.explanation: Statement I is false — conventionally, the left end of a protein chain is the N-terminal (first amino acid) and the right end is the C-terminal (last amino acid); the statement has them reversed. Statement II is true — adult human haemoglobin consists of 4 subunits, two of alpha type and two of beta type.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In a scrubber the exhaust from the thermal plant is passed through the electric wires to charge the dust particles.
Statement II: Particulate matter (PM 2.5) can not be removed by scrubber but can be removed by an electrostatic precipitator.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect — passing exhaust through electrically charged wires to charge dust particles describes an electrostatic precipitator, not a scrubber (scrubbers use liquid/water spray to remove gaseous pollutants). Statement II is correct — fine particulate matter like PM2.5 is effectively removed by electrostatic precipitators, not scrubbers. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 271)

questions.text: What triggers activation of protoxin to active bt toxin of Bacillus thuringiensis in boll worm?
questions.explanation: The alkaline pH of the insect gut triggers the solubilization and activation of the Bt protoxin into its active toxin form, which then binds to the midgut epithelium causing cell lysis.

questions.text: What is the role of NAD+ in cellular respiration?
options: It is the final electron acceptor for anaerobic respiration.
It is a nucleotide source for ATP synthesis.
It functions as an electron carrier.
questions.topic: Role of NAD+ in cellular respiration
questions.explanation: NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) acts as an electron carrier in cellular respiration, accepting electrons and hydrogen (becoming NADH) during glycolysis and the Krebs cycle, and later donating them in the electron transport chain.

questions.text: Identify the correct description about the given figure. [Figure shows an elongated, feathery grass-like inflorescence with long exposed, hairy/plumose structures]
options: Wind pollinated plant inflorescence showing flowers with well exposed stamens.
Water pollinated flowers showing stamens with mucilaginous covering.
questions.explanation: The figure shows a grass-type inflorescence with long, feathery, well-exposed stamens and stigmas, which is characteristic of wind (anemophilous) pollination — the large surface area of feathery stigmas helps trap airborne pollen.

questions.text: Taylor conducted the experiments to prove semiconservative mode of chromosome replication on:
questions.explanation: J. Herbert Taylor demonstrated semiconservative replication of chromosomes using Vicia faba (broad bean) root tip cells with radioactive thymidine labeling, in 1958.

questions.text: The oxygenation activity of RuBisCo enzyme in photorespiration leads to the formation of:
options: 1 molecule of 4-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound
questions.explanation: In photorespiration, the oxygenase activity of RuBisCO acts on RuBP with O2 to produce one molecule of 3-phosphoglycerate (3-C compound) and one molecule of phosphoglycolate (2-C compound), with the key product counted here being 1 molecule of the 3-C compound.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements refers to Reductionist Biology?
options: Physico-chemical approach to study and understand living organisms.
Physiological approach to study and understand living organisms.
Chemical approach to study and understand living organisms.
Behavioural approach to study and understand living organisms.
questions.explanation: Reductionist Biology applies the physico-chemical approach — concepts and techniques of physics and chemistry — to study and understand the function and structure of living organisms at the molecular level.

questions.text: Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) is the primary CO2 acceptor in:
questions.explanation: In C4 plants, PEP (phosphoenolpyruvate) acts as the primary CO2 acceptor in mesophyll cells, fixing CO2 via the enzyme PEP carboxylase to form the 4-carbon compound oxaloacetate, before CO2 is released again in the bundle sheath cells for the Calvin cycle.

questions.text: Inhibition of Succinic dehydrogenase enzyme by malonate is a classical example of:
questions.explanation: Malonate closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure and competes with it for the active site of succinic dehydrogenase, making this a classic example of competitive inhibition. 11th NCERT Page No. 117.

questions.text: The balloon-shaped structures called tyloses:
options: are linked to the ascent of sap through xylem vessels
originate in the lumen of vessels
are extensions of xylem parenchyma cells into vessels
questions.explanation: Tyloses are balloon-like outgrowths of xylem parenchyma cells that extend into the vessel lumen, characteristic of heartwood (not sapwood) formation.

questions.text: In which one of the following is the ovule not enclosed by an ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization?
questions.topic: Ovules not enclosed by ovary wall
questions.explanation: Pinus (a gymnosperm) has naked ovules not enclosed within an ovary wall, unlike angiosperms.

questions.text: Which of the following is an amino acid derived hormone?
questions.explanation: Epinephrine (adrenaline) is derived from the amino acid tyrosine, making it an amino acid-derived hormone, unlike the steroid hormones estriol, estradiol and ecdysone.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct? (1) Algal blooms caused by excess of organic matter in water improve water quality and promote fisheries. (2) Water hyacinth grows abundantly in eutrophic water bodies and leads to an imbalance in the ecosystem dynamics of the water body. (3) The amount of some toxic substance of industrial waste water increases in the organisms at successive trophic levels. (4) The micro-organisms involved in biodegradation of organic matter in a sewage polluted water body consume a lot of oxygen causing the death of aquatic organisms.
options: Algal blooms caused by excess of organic matter in water improve water quality and promote fisheries.
Water hyacinth grows abundantly in eutrophic water bodies and leads to an imbalance in the ecosystem dynamics of the water body.
The amount of some toxic substance of industrial waste water increases in the organisms at successive trophic levels.
The micro-organisms involved in biodegradation of organic matter in a sewage polluted water body consume a lot of oxygen causing the death of aquatic organisms.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is NOT correct — algal blooms caused by excess organic matter (eutrophication) actually deteriorate water quality and cause large-scale fish mortality, not improve water quality or promote fisheries. The other statements correctly describe effects of water hyacinth, biomagnification, and biodegradation.

questions.text: The shorter and longer arms of a submetacentric chromosome are referred to as:
questions.explanation: The shorter arm of a chromosome is called the p-arm, and the longer arm is called the q-arm.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Down's syndrome (B) α-Thalassemia (C) β-Thalassemia (D) Klinefelter's syndrome
List II: (I) 11th chromosome (II) 'X' chromosome (III) 21st chromosome (IV) 16th chromosome
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome is caused by trisomy of the 21st chromosome (A-III). α-Thalassemia is linked to genes on the 16th chromosome (B-IV). β-Thalassemia is linked to a gene on the 11th chromosome (C-I). Klinefelter's syndrome results from an extra X chromosome (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Myelin sheath is produced by:
questions.explanation: The myelin sheath around nerve fibres is produced by Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system and by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system.

questions.text: Which of the following type of immunity is present at the time of birth and is a non-specific type of defence in the human body?
questions.topic: Innate Immunity - Non-specific Defence Present at Birth
questions.explanation: Innate immunity is non-specific and present in the body by birth, in the form of physical, physiological, cellular and cytokine barriers. Acquired immunity (antibody-based) is highly specific and develops through antigenic stimulation. Class 12th NCERT Page No. 134.

questions.text: Which kind of therapy was given in 1990 to a four-year-old girl with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency?
questions.explanation: In 1990, the first gene therapy was administered to a four-year-old girl with ADA deficiency, a landmark case in gene therapy history.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the sequence on corresponding coding strand, if the sequence on mRNA formed is as follows: 5' AUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCG AUCG 3'?
questions.topic: mRNA, Coding Strand and Template Strand Sequences
questions.explanation: The coding strand of DNA has the same sequence as the mRNA (except T replaces U) and the same 5' to 3' polarity. Since the mRNA is 5' AUCGAUCG...AUCG 3', the coding strand is 5' ATCGATCG...ATCG 3'.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Expiratory Capacity (B) Functional residual capacity (C) Vital capacity (D) Inspiratory capacity
List II: (I) Expiratory reserve volume + Tidal volume + inspiratory reserve Volume (II) Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume (III) Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume (IV) Expiratory reserve volume + residual volume
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Expiratory capacity = Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume (A-II). Functional residual capacity = Expiratory reserve volume + residual volume (B-IV). Vital capacity = Expiratory reserve volume + Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume (C-I). Inspiratory capacity = Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume (D-III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following RNAs should be most abundant in animal cell?
questions.topic: Types and abundance of cellular RNA
questions.explanation: Ribosomal RNA (r-RNA) is the most abundant type of RNA in a cell, constituting approximately 80% of total cellular RNA, as it is a major structural and functional component of the numerous ribosomes present.

questions.text:
Which of the following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells?
(a) Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits
(b) They can have plasmids
(c) They contain mesosome
(d) They have peroxisomes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, composed of 50S and 30S subunits -- (a) correct. Prokaryotes can carry extrachromosomal circular DNA called plasmids -- (b) correct. Prokaryotic cell membranes can form infoldings called mesosomes -- (c) correct. Peroxisomes are membrane-bound organelles found in eukaryotic cells, not prokaryotes -- (d) is incorrect. So (a), (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: Select the correct statement:
options: Transduction was discovered by S. Altman.
Punnett square was developed by a British scientist.
questions.topic: Key discoveries and scientists in genetics
questions.explanation: The Punnett square was developed by Reginald Punnett, a British geneticist, to predict the genotypic and phenotypic outcomes of genetic crosses.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The class name Reptilia refers to creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
Statement II: All organisms belonging to Reptilia have three chambered heart.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: The name Reptilia is derived from the Latin 'repere', meaning to creep or crawl, correctly describing their mode of locomotion -- Statement I is correct. However, not all reptiles have a three-chambered heart: crocodiles (an exception among reptiles) have a four-chambered heart, so Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following would help in prevention of diuresis?
options: More water reabsorption due to undersecretion of ADH
Reabsorption of Na+ and water from renal tubules due to aldosterone
Decrease in secretion of renin by JG cells
questions.explanation: Aldosterone promotes reabsorption of Na+ and water from the renal tubules, which helps conserve body water and prevents excessive urine output (diuresis).

questions.text: During DNA replication, Okazaki fragments are used to elongate:
options: The lagging strand towards replication fork.
The leading strand away from replication fork.
The lagging strand away from the replication fork.
The leading strand towards replication fork.
questions.explanation: Okazaki fragments are short, discontinuous segments synthesised on the lagging strand, which is replicated in a direction away from the replication fork (5' to 3' synthesis occurring discontinuously as the fork opens).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: In C3 plants, some O2 binds to RuBisCO, hence CO2 fixation is decreased.
Statement-II: In C4 plants, mesophyll cells show very little photorespiration while bundle sheath cells do not show photorespiration.
In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
questions.topic: Photorespiration in C3 and C4 Plants
questions.explanation: In C3 plants, RuBisCO's oxygenase activity causes O2 to bind instead of CO2, reducing CO2 fixation (Statement-I is true). In C4 plants, it is actually the reverse of Statement-II: mesophyll cells show no photorespiration while bundle sheath cells (which lack PSII and have high CO2 concentration) show negligible photorespiration too — the statement as given mismatches the actual biology, making Statement-II false.

questions.text: Which of the following plants is monoecious?
questions.explanation: Chara is monoecious, bearing both male (antheridia) and female (oogonia) reproductive structures on the same plant. Cycas, papaya and Marchantia are dioecious.

questions.text: The recombination frequency between the genes a & c is 5%, b & c is 15%, b & d is 9%, a & b 20%, c & d is 24% and a & d is 29%. What will be the sequence of these genes on a linear chromosome?
questions.explanation: Testing order a-c-b-d: ac=5, cb=15 ⟹ ab=5+15=20 ✓ (matches given 20); bd=9 ⟹ cd=15+9=24 ✓ (matches given 24); ad=5+15+9=29 ✓ (matches given 29). All distances are consistent with the order a, c, b, d. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 83-84)

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 5 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement related to Pollination:
options: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants
Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollination
Flowers produce foul odours to attract flies and beetles to get pollinated
Moths and butterflies are the most dominant pollinating agents among insects
questions.explanation: Bees, not moths and butterflies, are considered the most dominant and common pollinating agents among insects. The other statements about water pollination being rare, wind pollination being common abiotically, and foul-smelling flowers attracting flies/beetles are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following options best represents the enzyme composition of pancreatic juice?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic juice contains lipase (for fats), amylase (for starch), trypsinogen (inactive precursor of trypsin, for proteins), and procarboxypeptidase (inactive precursor of carboxypeptidase). Pepsin and rennin are gastric enzymes, not pancreatic.

questions.text: Identify the part of a bio-reactor which is used as a foam braker from the given figure (labelled A, B, C, D on a stirred-tank bioreactor diagram).
questions.explanation: In a stirred-tank bioreactor diagram, the foam breaker is marked as 'C' (per NCERT Class 12, Page 174 diagram).

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The primary source of energy in an ecosystem is solar energy. Statement II : The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis in an ecosystem is called net primary productivity (NPP). In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: solar energy is the primary source of energy in an ecosystem. Statement II is incorrect: the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is called Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), not Net Primary Productivity (NPP, which is GPP minus respiratory losses).

questions.text: Anaphase Promoting Complex (APC) is a protein degradation machinery necessary for proper mitosis of animal cells. If APC is defective in a human cell, which of the following is expected to occur?
options: Recombination of chromosome arms will occur
questions.explanation: APC is required to degrade securin, which releases separase to cleave cohesin holding sister chromatids together. If APC is defective, sister chromatids cannot separate, so chromosomes will not segregate during anaphase.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List – I: A. Emphysema, B. Angina Pectoris, C. Glomerulonephritis, D. Tetany. List - II: I. Rapid spasms in muscle due to low Ca++ in body fluid, II. Damaged alveolar walls and decreased respiratory surface, III. Acute chest pain when not enough oxygen is reaching to heart muscle, IV. Inflammation of glomeruli of kidney. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Emphysema: damaged alveolar walls, decreased respiratory surface (II). Angina Pectoris: acute chest pain from insufficient O2 to heart (III). Glomerulonephritis: inflammation of glomerulus of nephron (IV). Tetany: rapid muscle spasms due to low Ca++ (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: The toxin proteins isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis, coded by which of the following genes would control cotton bollworm and corn borer, respectively?
questions.topic: Bt toxin genes controlling cotton bollworm and corn borer
questions.explanation: cryIAc controls cotton bollworm and cryIAb controls corn borer.

questions.text: In frogs, the number of pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain are__________.
questions.explanation: Frogs have 10 pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain, unlike mammals (including humans) which have 12 pairs.

questions.text: Red List contains data or information on:
options: plants whose products are in international trade
questions.explanation: The IUCN Red List contains data on threatened species (plants and animals facing risk of extinction)

questions.text: Which one of the following is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis?
questions.topic: Identifying site of active rRNA synthesis
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis and ribosome assembly.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Mycoplasma can pass through less than 1 micron filter size.
Statement II: Mycoplasma are bacteria with cell wall.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are extremely small and can pass through filters of less than 1 micron (Statement I correct). However, Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall (Statement II incorrect). (NCERT Class 11, Pg 20)

questions.text: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : A typical unfertilised, angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is 8 nucleate and 7-celled. Reason (R) : The egg apparatus has 2 polar nuclei. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Assertion is correct: a typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is 8-nucleate, 7-celled (3 antipodals, 2 synergids, 1 egg cell, 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei). Reason is false: the egg apparatus consists of 2 synergids and 1 egg cell, not 2 polar nuclei (the polar nuclei are in the central cell).

questions.text: Nissl bodies are mainly composed of
questions.topic: Composition of Nissl bodies in neurons
questions.explanation: Nissl bodies (Nissl granules), found in the cell body of neurons, are composed of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) along with free ribosomes, giving them their granular, basophilic appearance.

questions.text: When the centromere is situated in the middle of two equal arms of chromosomes, the chromosome is referred to as:
questions.topic: Chromosome type based on centromere position
questions.explanation: A metacentric chromosome has the centromere in the middle, dividing it into two equal arms.

questions.text: Arrange the following events occurring in Renin-Angiotensin mechanism in the correct order: A. Increase in blood pressure and Glomerular filtration rate. B. Reabsorption of Na+ and water from distal parts of tubule due to Aldosterone. C. Fall in Glomerular filtration rate. D. Vasoconstriction by Angiotensin II and release of Aldosterone. E. Renin converts Angiotensinogen into Angiotensin I, followed by Angiotensin II.
questions.topic: Correct sequence of events in Renin-Angiotensin mechanism
questions.explanation: Sequence: fall in GFR (C) → Renin converts Angiotensinogen to Angiotensin I/II (E) → vasoconstriction and Aldosterone release (D) → Na+/water reabsorption (B) → rise in blood pressure/GFR (A): C, E, D, B, A.

questions.text: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in DNA sequence, called as:
questions.explanation: DNA fingerprinting relies on repetitive DNA sequences (satellite DNA/VNTRs) that show variation (polymorphism) between individuals.

questions.text:
Match the following:
List I: (a) Physalia, (b) Limulus, (c) Ancylostoma, (d) Pinctada
List-II: (i) Pearl oyster, (ii) Portuguese Man of War, (iii) Living fossil, (iv) Hookworm
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
(2) a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
(3) a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
(4) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
questions.explanation: Physalia = Portuguese Man of War; Limulus = Living fossil; Ancylostoma = Hookworm; Pinctada = Pearl oyster. So a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: In the represented plasmid (pBR322-like, with BamH1, Tet R, Ori, EcoR1, β-Galactosidase, and amp marked) an alien piece of DNA is inserted at EcoRI site. Which of the following strategies will be chosen to select the recombinant colonies?
options: Using ampicillin & tetracyclin containing medium plate.
Blue color colonies will be selected.
White color colonies will be selected.
Blue color colonies grown on ampicillin plates can be selected.
questions.explanation: Insertion of the alien DNA at the EcoRI site (within the β-galactosidase gene) causes insertional inactivation of β-galactosidase, so recombinant colonies appear white (no blue colour due to no enzyme activity on X-gal), while non-recombinant colonies remain blue. So white colonies are selected.

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics is incorrect with respect to cockroach?
options: 10th abdominal segment in both sexes, bears a pair of anal cerci.
A ring of gastric caeca is present at the junction of midgut and hind gut.
Hypopharynx lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouth parts.
In females, 7th-9th sterna together form a genital pouch.
questions.explanation: The ring of gastric caeca (8-100 in number) is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, not midgut and hindgut, making this statement incorrect.

questions.text: The process of translation of mRNA to proteins begins as soon as:
options: The small subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
The larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
Both the subunits join together to bind with mRNA
The tRNA is activated and the larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
questions.explanation: Translation begins when the small subunit of the ribosome binds to the mRNA first (forming the initiation complex), after which the larger subunit joins to complete the functional ribosome.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: In gymnosperms the pollen grains are released from the microsporangium and carried by air currents. Reason R: Air currents carry the pollen grains to the mouth of the archegonia where the male gametes are discharged and pollen tube is not formed. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — in gymnosperms, pollen grains are released from the microsporangium and carried by air currents to the ovule. Reason R is false — in gymnosperms, pollen tubes ARE typically formed (except in a few cases like Cycas and Ginkgo with motile sperm), and the air currents carry pollen to the micropyle, not directly to discharge male gametes at the mouth of the archegonia without a pollen tube in most gymnosperms.

questions.text: Which of the following statements with respect to Endoplasmic Reticulum is incorrect?
options: RER has ribosomes attached to ER
In prokaryotes only RER are present
SER are the sites for lipid synthesis
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound endoplasmic reticulum altogether (neither RER nor SER), so the statement that 'only RER are present in prokaryotes' is incorrect.

questions.text: Breeding crops with higher levels of vitamins and minerals or higher proteins and healthier fats is called?
questions.explanation: Breeding crops with higher nutritional value (vitamins, minerals, proteins, healthy fats) is called bio-fortification. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 166)

questions.text: Following are the statements about prostomium of earthworm. (a) It serves as a covering for mouth. (b) It helps to open cracks in the soil into which it can crawl. (c) It is one of the sensory structures. (d) It is the first body segment. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: The prostomium of earthworm covers the mouth, helps open cracks in soil for crawling, and acts as a sensory structure. It is not a true body segment (statement d is incorrect), so (a), (b) and (c) are correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Filariasis, (b) Amoebiasis, (c) Pneumonia, (d) Ringworm with (i) Haemophilus influenzae, (ii) Trichophyton, (iii) Wuchereria bancrofti, (iv) Entamoeba histolytica.
questions.explanation: Filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti (iii); Amoebiasis by Entamoeba histolytica (iv); Pneumonia by Haemophilus influenzae (i); Ringworm by Trichophyton (ii). (a)-(iii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(i),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: A temporary endocrine gland in the human body is:
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum, formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation, is a temporary endocrine gland that secretes progesterone and degenerates if pregnancy does not occur.

questions.text: Which of the following is made up of dead cells?
questions.explanation: Phellem (cork), produced by the cork cambium, is made up of dead cells with suberin deposited in their walls, making them impervious to water and gases.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Cell with active cell division capacity, (b) Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function, (c) Tissue having different types of cells, (d) Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen
List-II: (i) Vascular tissue, (ii) Meristematic tissue, (iii) Sclereids, (iv) Simple tissue
Select the correct answer from the option given below:
(1) a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
(2) a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
(3) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
(4) a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
questions.explanation: Cell with active division capacity = Meristematic tissue; tissue with all similar cells = Simple tissue; tissue with different cell types = Vascular tissue (complex); dead cells with thick walls, narrow lumen = Sclereids. So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

questions.text: Ray florets have:
questions.explanation: Ray florets, found in composite inflorescences of the Asteraceae family, have an inferior ovary, where the ovary is positioned below the point of attachment of other floral parts.

questions.text: Once the undigested and unabsorbed substances enter the caecum, their backflow is prevented by:
questions.explanation: The ileo-caecal valve, located between the ileum and caecum, prevents the backflow of undigested and unabsorbed substances from the caecum into the ileum.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Mesozoic Era (B) Proterozoic Era (C) Cenozoic Era (D) Paleozoic Era
List II: (I) Lower invertebrates (II) Fish & Amphibia (III) Birds & Reptiles (IV) Mammals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Geological Eras and Dominant Life Forms
questions.explanation: Mesozoic Era is associated with Birds & Reptiles (A-III). Proterozoic Era is associated with lower invertebrates (B-I). Cenozoic Era is associated with Mammals (C-IV). Paleozoic Era is associated with Fish & Amphibia (D-II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II is correct.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) α-1 antitrypsin (B) Cry IAb (C) Cry IAc (D) Enzyme replacement therapy
List II: (I) Cotton bollworm (II) ADA deficiency (III) Emphysema (IV) Corn borer
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Biotechnology Applications - Bt Crops and Gene Therapy
questions.explanation: α-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes emphysema (A-III). Cry IAb protein confers resistance against corn borer (B-IV). Cry IAc protein confers resistance against cotton bollworm (C-I). ADA deficiency is treated with enzyme replacement therapy/gene therapy (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: The chronological order of human evolution from early to the recent is:
options: Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Ramapithecus → Homo erectus
Australopithecus → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus
Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus
Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Australopithecus → Homo erectus
questions.explanation: The chronological order of human evolution is: Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus (followed by Homo sapiens).

questions.text: What is the genetic disorder in which an individual has an overall masculine development, gynaecomastia, and is sterile?
questions.explanation: Klinefelter's syndrome (XXY) results in overall masculine development with feminine body features like gynaecomastia (development of breasts) and sterility.

questions.text: Match the organism with its use in biotechnology: (a) Bacillus thuringiensis, (b) Thermus aquaticus, (c) Agrobacterium tumefaciens, (d) Salmonella typhimurium with (i) Cloning vector, (ii) Construction of first rDNA molecule, (iii) DNA polymerase, (iv) Cry proteins
questions.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of Cry proteins (iv), Thermus aquaticus is the source of heat-stable Taq DNA polymerase (iii), Agrobacterium tumefaciens is used as a cloning vector (i) in plant transformation, and Salmonella typhimurium was used in the construction of the first rDNA molecule (ii). This matches a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text: Which one of the following is wrong for fungi?
options: They are both unicellular and multicellular.
All fungi possess a purely cellulosic cell wall.
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls are made of chitin, not purely cellulose, making statement (3) wrong.

questions.text: Stirred-tank bioreactors have been designed for:
options: Ensuring anaerobic conditions in the culture vessel
Addition of preservatives to the product
Availability of oxygen throughout the process
questions.explanation: Stirred-tank bioreactors have a stirrer and oxygen-delivery system to ensure adequate mixing and oxygen availability throughout the culture, maintaining aerobic conditions and homogeneity.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (A) Nucleolus (B) Centriole (C) Leucoplasts (D) Golgi apparatus
List-II: (I) Site of formation of glycolipids (II) Organization like the cartwheel (III) Site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis (IV) For storing nutrients
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Cell Organelle Functions (Match List: Nucleolus, Centriole, Leucoplasts, Golgi)
questions.explanation: Nucleolus is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis (III). Centriole has an organization like the cartwheel (II). Leucoplasts are used for storing nutrients (IV). Golgi apparatus is the site of formation of glycolipids (I). So A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I. 11th NCERT Page No. 95, 99, 100.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Both wind and water pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar. Reason (R): The flowers produce enormous amount of pollen grains in wind and water pollinated flowers. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: abiotically pollinated flowers (wind/water) lack colour and nectar since these are attractants for biotic pollinators which aren't needed; and they produce enormous pollen since pollination is non-directional/random. However R does not directly explain why they lack colour/nectar (A) — the large pollen production is a separate adaptation for non-directional pollen dispersal, not the explanation for the lack of colour/nectar.

questions.text: GnRH, a hypothalamic hormone, needed in reproduction, acts on:
options: anterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of LH and FSH.
posterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of oxytocin and FSH.
posterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of LH and relaxin.
anterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of LH and oxytocin.
questions.explanation: Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone (GnRH), secreted by the hypothalamus, acts on the anterior pituitary gland to stimulate the secretion of the gonadotropins LH (Luteinising Hormone) and FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone).

questions.text: The correct order of steps in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is
questions.explanation: PCR proceeds through three repeated steps in this order: Denaturation (separating DNA strands by heat), Annealing (primer binding to the single strands), and Extension (DNA polymerase synthesizing the new strand).

questions.text: Which of the following National Parks is home to the famous musk deer or hangul?
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park in Jammu & Kashmir is famous for conserving the hangul (Kashmir stag) and is also home to musk deer.

questions.text: When cell has stalled DNA replication fork, which checkpoint should be predominantly activated?
questions.explanation: A stalled DNA replication fork primarily activates the intra-S-phase checkpoint, closely linked with the G1/S checkpoint, which prevents cells with incompletely replicated or damaged DNA from proceeding.

questions.text: Out of 'X' ribs in humans only 'Y' pairs are true ribs. Select the option that correctly represents values of X and Y and provides their explanation:
options: X=12, Y=5: True ribs are attached dorsally to vertebral column and sternum on the two ends.
X=24, Y=7: True ribs are dorsally attached to vertebral column but are free on ventral side.
X=24, Y=12: True ribs are dorsally attached to vertebral column but are free on ventral side.
X=12, Y=7: True ribs are attached dorsally to vertebral column and ventrally to the sternum.
questions.explanation: As accepted in the official NTA answer key, X=24 (total individual ribs, forming 12 pairs) and Y=7 pairs are classified as true ribs since they attach directly (dorsally to the vertebral column, and via their own costal cartilage ventrally) to the sternum, while the remaining pairs are false or floating ribs.

questions.text: The ovule of an angiosperm is technically equivalent to:
questions.explanation: The ovule is technically equivalent to the megasporangium, which is integumented and contains the megaspore mother cell that undergoes meiosis to form megaspores.

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 6 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct regarding AIDS causative agent HIV?
options: HIV does not escape but attacks the acquired immune response.
HIV is enveloped virus containing one molecule of single-stranded RNA and one molecule of reverse transcriptase.
HIV is enveloped virus that contains two identical molecules of single-stranded RNA and two molecules of reverse transcriptase.
questions.explanation: HIV is an enveloped retrovirus containing two identical copies of single-stranded RNA genome along with two molecules of reverse transcriptase enzyme.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Biological Molecules): (a) Glycogen (b) Globulin (c) Steroids (d) Thrombin
List-II (Biological functions): (i) Hormone (ii) Biocatalyst (iii) Antibody (iv) Storage product
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Glycogen is a storage product (iv); Globulin is an antibody (iii); Steroids function as hormones (i); Thrombin is an enzyme/biocatalyst (ii). (NCERT Class 11, Pg 130-131)

questions.text: The number of substrate level phosphorylations in one turn of citric acid cycle is:
questions.topic: Substrate level phosphorylation in Krebs cycle
questions.explanation: In one turn of the citric acid (Krebs) cycle, substrate level phosphorylation occurs once, at the step where succinyl-CoA is converted to succinate, generating one GTP (equivalent to ATP).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the nephron, the descending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water and permeable to electrolytes.
Statement II: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple columnar brush border epithelium and increases the surface area for reabsorption.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.explanation: The descending limb of loop of Henle is actually permeable to water and impermeable to electrolytes (the reverse of what Statement I says, so it is false). While the PCT is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium (not columnar), making Statement II also false. So both statements are false.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a criterion for classification of fungi?
questions.explanation: Fungi are classified based on mode of spore formation, fruiting body structure, and morphology of mycelium. Mode of nutrition is not a primary criterion used for fungal classification. 11th NCERT Page No. 16.

questions.text: What are the potential drawbacks in adoption of the IVF method? A. High fatality risk to mother. B. Expensive instruments and reagents. C. Husband/wife necessary for being donors. D. Less adoption of orphans. E. Not available in India. F. Possibility that the early embryo does not survive. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Drawbacks of IVF include: B (expensive instruments/reagents), D (less adoption of orphans, since couples prefer biological children via IVF), and F (early embryo may not survive). A, C, and E are not accurate drawbacks of IVF as described in NCERT (Class 12, Pg 48).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity.
Statement II: The hymen is torn during the first coitus only.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.explanation: The presence or absence of the hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity since it can be torn due to reasons other than coitus, such as physical exercise. So Statement I is true. Statement II is false because the hymen can be torn due to various non-sexual reasons, not only the first coitus.

questions.text: In angiosperms, root hairs arise from which one of the following regions of the root?
questions.explanation: Root hairs arise from the region of maturation (differentiation) of the root.

questions.text: Match List I (Cells) with List II (Secretion): A. Peptic cells, B. Goblet Cells, C. Oxyntic cells, D. Hepatic cells. List II: I. Mucus, II. Bile juice, III. Proenzyme pepsinogen, IV. HCl and intrinsic factor for absorption of vitamin B12. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.topic: Gastric Gland Cell Types and Secretions
questions.explanation: Peptic (chief) cells secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen (A-III). Goblet cells secrete mucus (B-I). Oxyntic (parietal) cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption (C-IV). Hepatic cells secrete bile juice (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: The experimental proof for semiconservative replication of DNA was first shown in a
questions.topic: Experimental proof of semiconservative DNA replication
questions.explanation: Meselson and Stahl's classic experiment demonstrating the semiconservative replication of DNA was performed using the bacterium Escherichia coli.

questions.text: The water potential of pure water is:
options: More than zero but less than one
questions.explanation: By convention, the water potential of pure water at standard temperature and pressure is taken to be zero, the maximum possible value, since any solute added lowers it below zero.

questions.text: How many turns of Calvin cycle are required for the formation of three molecules of glucose?
questions.topic: Calvin Cycle - Turns Required for Glucose Formation
questions.explanation: Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes 1 molecule of CO2. Formation of 1 molecule of glucose (6 carbons) requires 6 turns of the Calvin cycle (fixing 6 CO2 molecules). For 3 molecules of glucose, 3 × 6 = 18 turns are required.

questions.text: Find the incorrect statement(s) about photosynthesis from the following: A. The water splitting complex is associated with PS I. B. C4 plants use the C3 pathway of CO2 fixation as the main biosynthetic pathway. C. In C4 plants, photorespiration does not occur. D. C3 plants exhibit 'Kranz' anatomy. E. ATP synthesis in chloroplast occurs through chemiosmosis.
questions.explanation: A is false (water-splitting complex is with PS II, not PS I); D is false (Kranz anatomy is a feature of C4, not C3, plants). B, C, E are true. So A and D only are incorrect.

questions.text: Match Column-I with Column-II: (a) Nitrococcus, (b) Rhizobium, (c) Thiobacillus, (d) Nitrobacter with (i) Denitrification, (ii) Conversion of ammonia to nitrite, (iii) Conversion of nitrite to nitrate, (iv) Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia.
questions.explanation: Nitrococcus converts ammonia to nitrite (ii); Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia (iv); Thiobacillus (denitrifying type here) causes denitrification (i); Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate (iii). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(i),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: Assertion (A): A person goes to high altitude and experiences 'altitude sickness' with symptoms like breathing difficulty and heart palpitations. Reason (R): Due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitude, the body does not get sufficient oxygen. Choose the correct answer:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the low atmospheric pressure causing insufficient oxygen correctly explains altitude sickness symptoms.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Genetically modified organism, B. Thermostable DNA polymerase, C. Ti plasmid, D. pBR322. List II — I. Agrobacterium tumefaciens, II. Bt cotton, III. Thermus aquaticus, IV. Escherichia coli.
questions.explanation: Bt cotton is a GMO (II); Taq polymerase comes from Thermus aquaticus (III); Ti plasmid comes from Agrobacterium tumefaciens (I); pBR322 is a cloning vector from E. coli (IV). A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

questions.text: If the diploid chromosome number of a typical angiosperm is 36, what would be the chromosome number in its endosperm?
questions.explanation: If the diploid (2n) chromosome number is 36, then the haploid (n) number is 18. The endosperm in angiosperms is formed by triple fusion (one male gamete + two polar nuclei), making it triploid (3n) = 3 × 18 = 54.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of non-distilled alcoholic beverage produced by yeast?
questions.explanation: Wine and beer are produced without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) S phase, (b) G2 phase, (c) Quiescent stage, (d) G1 phase
List-II: (i) Proteins are synthesized, (ii) Inactive phase, (iii) Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication, (iv) DNA replication
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i
(2) a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv
(3) a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i
(4) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
questions.explanation: S phase = DNA replication; G2 phase = proteins synthesized (preparation for mitosis); Quiescent stage (G0) = inactive phase; G1 phase = interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. So a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

questions.text: These are regarded as major causes of biodiversity loss: A. Over exploitation B. Co-extinction C. Mutation D. Habitat loss and fragmentation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation: The major causes of biodiversity loss recognized are habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions, and co-extinction. Mutation is not listed as a major cause of biodiversity loss in this context, so A, B and D only is correct.

questions.text: Histones are enriched with -
questions.explanation: Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine, both of which carry positive charges in their side chains, allowing histones to bind the negatively charged DNA. Class 12th NCERT Page No.83.

questions.text:
With the help of given pedigree, find out the probability for the birth of a child having no disease and being a carrier (has the disease mutation in one allele of the gene) in F3 generation.
[Pedigree: F0 - unaffected male x affected female; F1 - unaffected male x carrier female, carrier female x unaffected male; F2 - carrier female, carrier female, affected male x unaffected female, unaffected female; F3 - four children marked '?' from the carrier female x affected male cross]
questions.topic: Pedigree Analysis - X-linked Recessive Inheritance Probability
questions.explanation: The pedigree pattern (disease in both sexes, carrier females, skips generations) indicates X-linked recessive inheritance. In F2, a carrier female (XᶜX) is crossed with an affected male (XᶜY). Gametes: Female gives Xᶜ or X; Male gives Xᶜ or Y. Possible F3 offspring: XᶜX (carrier female) = 1/4, XᶜXᶜ (affected female) = 1/4, XY (normal male) = 1/4, XᶜY (affected male) = 1/4. The probability of a child being unaffected AND a carrier (XᶜX) is 1/4. Class 12th NCERT Page No.73.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In a scrubber the exhaust from the thermal plant is passed through the electric wires to charge the dust particles. Statement II: Particulate matter (PM 2.5) cannot be removed by scrubber but can be removed by an electrostatic precipitator. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Passing exhaust through electric wires to charge dust particles describes the working of an electrostatic precipitator, not a scrubber, making Statement I incorrect. Statement II is correct: fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) is effectively removed by an electrostatic precipitator rather than a scrubber.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous
Statement II: Cleistogamy is disadvantageous as there is no chance for cross pollination
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct — cleistogamous flowers never open, ensuring self-pollination (autogamy), but this prevents cross-pollination, limiting genetic variation.

questions.text: Identify the wrong statement with reference to the gene 'I' that controls ABO blood groups.
options: A person will have only two of the three alleles.
When IA and IB are present together, they express same type of sugar.
Allele 'i' does not produce any sugar.
questions.topic: Multiple alleles: ABO blood group system
questions.explanation: When IA and IB alleles are present together, they are co-dominant and express both types of sugars (A and B antigens) simultaneously (AB blood group), not the 'same type' of sugar; this statement is incorrect.

questions.text: Choose the correct statements regarding cell organelles and their inclusions. A. The endomembrane system includes Golgi complex, endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria. B. Rough endoplasmic reticulum bears ribosomes on its surface. C. Both mitochondria and plastids have circular DNA. D. A network of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is called cytoskeleton. E. Mitochondrion is a single membrane-bound structure.
questions.topic: Correct statements about cell organelles and their inclusions
questions.explanation: B (RER has ribosomes), C (mitochondria/plastids have circular DNA), and D (cytoskeleton description) are correct. A is false (mitochondria are not part of the endomembrane system); E is false (mitochondrion is double membrane-bound, not single). B, C and D only.

questions.text: Calcium is important in skeletal muscle contraction because it
options: binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin.
prevents the formation of bonds between the myosin cross bridges and the actin filament.
detaches the myosin head from the actin filament.
activates the myosin ATPase by binding to it.
