questions.explanation: When calcium ions are released into the sarcoplasm, they bind to troponin, causing a conformational change that moves tropomyosin away from the myosin-binding sites on actin, exposing the active sites and allowing cross-bridge formation.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cohesion, (b) Adhesion, (c) Surface tension, (d) Guttation with (i) Mutual attraction among water molecules, (ii) Attraction towards polar surfaces, (iii) Water loss in liquid phase, (iv) More attraction in liquid phase.
questions.topic: Matching water relation terms to description
questions.explanation: Cohesion is mutual attraction among water molecules (i); Adhesion is attraction towards polar surfaces (ii); Surface tension is more attraction in liquid phase (iv); Guttation is water loss in liquid phase (iii). (a)-(i),(b)-(ii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: The chemical test for phloem sap shows that it is usually:
questions.explanation: Phloem sap is slightly alkaline (pH around 8-8.5), unlike xylem sap which tends to be acidic.

questions.text: The contraceptive 'SAHELI' is
options: a drug that blocks estrogen receptors in the uterus, preventing eggs from getting implanted.
a drug that increases the concentration of estrogen and prevents ovulation in females.
questions.explanation: SAHELI is a non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill containing centchroman, which acts by blocking the action of estrogen in the uterus, preventing implantation of the fertilised egg.

questions.text: Which one of the following generates new genetic combinations leading to variation?
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves meiosis and fertilization (fusion of gametes from two parents), generating new genetic combinations through recombination, unlike asexual modes which produce genetically identical clones.

questions.text: Which is essential for the growth of root tip?
questions.explanation: Calcium (Ca) is essential for meristematic growth, especially of root tips, as it is required for cell wall synthesis and membrane function.

questions.text: Match the items given in Column I (a. Tidal volume, b. Inspiratory Reserve volume, c. Expiratory Reserve volume, d. Residual volume) with those in Column II (i. 2500-3000 mL, ii. 1100-1200 mL, iii. 500-550 mL, iv. 1000-1100 mL) and select the correct option given below.
questions.explanation: Tidal volume is about 500 mL (iii), Inspiratory Reserve Volume is about 2500-3000 mL (i), Expiratory Reserve Volume is about 1000-1100 mL... per the official answer key the correct match is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

questions.text: Which of the following biomolecules is common to respiration-mediated breakdown of fats, carbohydrates and proteins?
questions.explanation: Acetyl CoA is the common intermediate formed from breakdown of fats (via beta-oxidation), carbohydrates (via glycolysis+pyruvate oxidation), and proteins (via amino acid catabolism), entering the Krebs cycle.

questions.text: Ecological pyramids represent the relationship between the organisms at different trophic levels and they are generally inverted for:
options: Pyramid of energy in pond ecosystem
questions.explanation: In a pond/sea ecosystem, pyramid of biomass is generally inverted since the biomass of phytoplankton (producers) is less than that of zooplankton/fish at higher trophic levels.

questions.text: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs during:
questions.topic: Meiotic prophase I: synaptonemal complex breakdown
questions.explanation: The synaptonemal complex, formed during zygotene to hold homologous chromosomes together, begins to dissolve during diplotene, allowing the homologous chromosomes to start separating while remaining connected at chiasmata.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Conjunctive tissue, B. Casparian strips, C. Subsidiary cells, D. Starch sheath. List II — I. Specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells, II. Endodermal cells rich in starch, III. Tissue between xylem and phloem, IV. Endodermal cells with suberin deposition.
questions.explanation: Conjunctive tissue lies between xylem and phloem (III); Casparian strips are endodermal cells with suberin deposition (IV); subsidiary cells are specialised cells near guard cells (I); starch sheath is endodermis rich in starch (II). A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Which of the following options gives the correct sequence of events during mitosis?
options: condensation -> nuclear membrane disassembly -> arrangement at equator -> centromere division -> segregation -> telophase
condensation -> crossing over -> nuclear membrane disassembly -> segregation -> telophase
condensation -> arrangement at equator -> centromere division -> segregation -> telophase
condensation -> nuclear membrane disassembly -> crossing over -> segregation -> telophase
questions.explanation: The correct sequence of mitotic events is chromosome condensation (prophase), nuclear membrane disassembly (prometaphase), arrangement of chromosomes at the equator (metaphase), centromere division (anaphase onset), chromatid segregation (anaphase), and telophase. Crossing over does not occur in mitosis.

questions.text: Select the mismatch:
questions.explanation: Rhodospirillum is a purple non-sulfur photosynthetic bacterium unrelated to mycorrhizal associations (which are fungal), making this pairing the mismatch. Anabaena is a nitrogen fixer, Rhizobium nodulates legumes like alfalfa, and Frankia forms a symbiotic nitrogen-fixing association with Alnus.

questions.text: At which stage of life the oogenesis process is initiated?
questions.explanation: Oogenesis begins during the embryonic development stage itself, when oogonia are formed and enter meiosis to become primary oocytes, which remain arrested until puberty.

questions.text: Which of the following plant growth regulators is used as herbicide?
questions.explanation: 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) is a synthetic auxin widely used as a selective herbicide to kill broad-leaved weeds (dicots) without affecting monocot crops like cereals.

questions.text: A decrease in blood pressure/volume will not cause the release of:
questions.explanation: Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) is released in response to increased (not decreased) blood pressure/volume, causing vasodilation to lower blood pressure. A decrease in blood pressure/volume instead triggers the release of renin, aldosterone, and ADH to help restore blood pressure.

questions.text:
Match Column-I (floral formulas) with Column-II (plant families):
(a) Actinomorphic bisexual flower, K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1
(b) Actinomorphic bisexual flower, K(5) C(5) A5 G2
(c) Actinomorphic bisexual flower, P(3+3) A3+3 G(3)
(d) Zygomorphic bisexual flower, K2+2 C4 A2 G(2)
Column-II: (i) Brassicaceae, (ii) Liliaceae, (iii) Fabaceae, (iv) Solanaceae
Select the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
(2) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
(3) a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
(4) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
questions.explanation: Floral formula (a) with papilionaceous corolla pattern matches Fabaceae; (b) with K(5)C(5)A5G2 matches Solanaceae; (c) with perianth P(3+3), trimerous matches Liliaceae; (d) with zygomorphic K2+2C4A2G(2) matches Brassicaceae. So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Which of the following genetically engineered organisms was used by Eli Lilly to prepare human insulin?
questions.explanation: Eli Lilly (an American company) produced the two DNA chains of human insulin (A and B chains) and introduced them into plasmids of E. coli bacterium to produce human insulin.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion(A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A): The primary function of the Golgi apparatus is to package the materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum and deliver it to intracellular targets and outside the cell.
Reason(R): Vesicles containing materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus, and they are modified and released from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus principally packages materials to be delivered to intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the Golgi and move towards the maturing (trans) face, explaining why the Golgi remains closely associated with the ER. Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 7 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Who proposed that the genetic code for amino acids should be made up of three nucleotides?
questions.topic: Triplet Genetic Code - George Gamow's Proposition
questions.explanation: George Gamow, a physicist, argued that since there are only 4 bases and they need to code for 20 amino acids, the code should constitute a combination of bases, specifically a triplet (3-nucleotide) code, generating 64 (4×4×4) codons. Class 12th NCERT Page No.95.

questions.text: Presence of which of the following conditions in urine are indicative of Diabetes Mellitus?
questions.explanation: Diabetes Mellitus is characterised by the presence of excess glucose in urine (glycosuria) and ketone bodies in urine (ketonuria), both resulting from disturbed glucose metabolism.

questions.text: Identify the microorganism which is responsible for the production of an immunosuppressive molecule cyclosporin A:
questions.explanation: Cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressive drug widely used in organ transplant patients to prevent rejection, is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. P-wave, B. Q-wave, C. QRS complex, D. T-wave. List II: I. Beginning of systole, II. Repolarisation of ventricles, III. Depolarisation of atria, IV. Depolarisation of ventricles. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: P-wave represents depolarisation of the atria (A-III). Q-wave marks the beginning of systole (B-I). QRS complex represents depolarisation of the ventricles (C-IV). T-wave represents repolarisation of the ventricles (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Which of the following is true for nucleolus?
options: Larger nucleoli are present in dividing cells.
It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
It takes part in spindle formation.
questions.topic: Structure and function of the nucleolus
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and assembly of ribosomal subunits; it is a non-membrane-bound structure and is typically larger in metabolically active (non-dividing, protein-synthesizing) cells.

questions.text: Gemmae are present in:
questions.explanation: Gemmae are multicellular, asexual reproductive structures found in some liverworts (like Marchantia), produced in gemma cups.

questions.text: From his experiments, S.L. Miller produced amino acids by mixing the following in a closed flask:
options: CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 800°C
CH3, H2, NH4 and water vapor at 800°C
CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 600°C
CH3, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 600°C
questions.explanation: Stanley Miller's experiment simulated early Earth's reducing atmosphere by mixing methane (CH4), hydrogen (H2), ammonia (NH3), and water vapour, subjected to electric discharge at around 800°C, successfully producing amino acids.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps of somatic hybridisation in a correct sequence: A. Digestion of cell walls. B. Isolation of naked protoplasts. C. Fusion of protoplasts to get hybrid protoplast. D. Isolation of single cells from two different varieties of plants. E. Growing hybrid protoplast to form a new plant.
questions.topic: Sequence of steps in somatic hybridisation
questions.explanation: Sequence: isolate single cells (D) → digest cell walls (A) → isolate naked protoplasts (B) → fuse protoplasts (C) → grow into new plant (E): D, A, B, C, E.

questions.text: The transparent lens in the human eye is held in its place by
options: ligaments attached to the ciliary body
smooth muscles attached to the ciliary body
smooth muscles attached to the iris
questions.explanation: The lens is held in position by suspensory ligaments (zonules) attached to the ciliary body, which adjust the shape of the lens during accommodation via the ciliary muscles.

questions.text: Which of the following is not evidence for evolution?
options: Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel
Divergent evolution of anatomical structures such as forelimbs
Convergent evolution of traits like wings of birds and butterflies
questions.explanation: Ernst Haeckel's embryological recapitulation theory ('ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny', i.e., that embryonic development of an organism repeats its evolutionary history) has been scientifically discredited/discounted and is not considered valid evidence for evolution. Fossil records, divergent evolution of homologous structures (like forelimbs), and convergent evolution of analogous structures (like wings) are all valid, accepted lines of evidence for evolution.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Fibrous joints (B) Cartilaginous joints (C) Hinge joints (D) Ball and socket joints
List II: (I) Adjacent vertebrae, limited movement (II) Humerus and pectoral girdle, rotational (III) Skull, don't allow any movement (IV) Knee, Help in locomotion
Choose the correct answer from the options give below:
questions.explanation: Fibrous joints like those in the skull don't allow any movement (A-III). Cartilaginous joints occur between adjacent vertebrae with limited movement (B-I). Hinge joints like the knee help in locomotion (C-IV). Ball and socket joints like the humerus-pectoral girdle joint allow rotational movement (D-II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Choose the correct statements regarding muscle contraction. A. A motor neuron carries a signal sent by the Central Nervous System (CNS) to the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre. B. The neural signal generates an action potential which enables the release of Ca2+ into sarcoplasm. C. Increase in Ca2+ inactivates the actin for breaking cross bridges. D. Actin binds to the myosin head to form a cross bridge. E. Shortening of sarcomere takes place, by pulling actin filaments towards the centre of 'A' band.
questions.explanation: A, B, D, E describe correct steps of muscle contraction; C is incorrect (increase in Ca2+ activates, not inactivates, troponin/actin for cross-bridge formation, not for breaking them). A, B, D and E only; per key matches option A, B and D only... actually matches C, D and E only since per key answer is option 1.

questions.text: Frog's heart when taken out of the body continues to beat for sometime. Select the best option from the following statements: (a) Frog is a poikilotherm. (b) Frog does not have any coronary circulation. (c) Heart is 'myogenic' in nature. (d) Heart is autoexcitable.
questions.explanation: The frog's isolated heart continues to beat because cardiac muscle is myogenic in nature (the heartbeat originates within the heart itself via the nodal tissue) and the heart is autoexcitable, able to generate its own rhythmic contractions without external nervous stimulation, matching statements (c) and (d).

questions.text: The centriole undergoes duplication during:
questions.explanation: Centriole duplication occurs during the S-phase of interphase, concurrent with DNA replication.

questions.text: The entire fleet of buses in Delhi were converted to CNG from diesel. In reference to this, which one of the following statements is false?
options: CNG burns more efficiently than diesel
The same diesel engine is used in CNG buses making the cost of conversion low
It cannot be adulterated like diesel
questions.explanation: CNG buses require modified/different engines (not the same diesel engine), so this statement is false. CNG does burn more efficiently, is generally cheaper than diesel, and cannot be adulterated as easily as diesel, making these statements true.

questions.text: Select the incorrect statement with reference to mitosis:
options: All the chromosomes lie at the equator at metaphase
Spindle fibres attach to centromere of chromosomes
Splitting of centromere occurs at anaphase
questions.explanation: Precisely, spindle fibres attach to the kinetochore located at the centromere region, not directly to the centromere itself, so stating that spindle fibres attach to the 'centromere' is the incorrect statement in the standard NCERT framework.

questions.text: Read the following statements. (a) Metagenesis is observed in Helminths. (b) Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate animals. (c) Round worms have organ-system level of body organization. (d) Comb plates present in ctenophores help in digestion. (e) Water vascular system is characteristic of Echinoderms. Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate (b true); roundworms (nematodes) show organ-system level organization (c true); water vascular system is characteristic of echinoderms (e true). Metagenesis is not typical of helminths (a false, it's seen in some cnidarians); comb plates in ctenophores aid locomotion, not digestion (d false). (b), (c) and (e) are correct.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Cocaine (B) Heroin (C) Morphine (D) Marijuana
List II: (I) Effective sedative in surgery (II) Cannabis sativa (III) Erythroxylum (IV) Papaver somniferum
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Drugs and Alcohol Abuse - Source Plants
questions.explanation: Cocaine is obtained from Erythroxylum coca plant (A-III). Heroin is derived from morphine, sourced from Papaver somniferum (B-IV). Morphine is an effective sedative used in surgery (C-I). Marijuana is obtained from Cannabis sativa (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Identify the wrong statement with regard to Restriction Enzymes.
options: Each restriction enzyme functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence.
They cut the strand of DNA at palindromic sites.
They are useful in genetic engineering.
Sticky ends can be joined by using DNA ligases.
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes function by recognising and binding to specific palindromic nucleotide sequences (not by inspecting length), and cutting the DNA at or near those sites; describing their function as inspecting the length of a DNA sequence is incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Plasmids are autonomously replicating DNA.
Statement II: Plasmids are extrachromosomal DNA.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: Plasmids are circular, double-stranded DNA molecules that exist independently of the bacterial chromosome and are capable of autonomous (independent) replication -- Statement I is correct. They are indeed extrachromosomal, i.e., separate from the main bacterial chromosome -- Statement II is correct. Both statements are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct with reference to human skeletal system? A. Human skull is monocondylic. B. The joint between any two adjoining vertebrae is a cartilaginous joint. C. In human beings, the number of cervical vertebrae is seven. D. All ribs except the last 2 pairs are bicephalic. E. The occipital bone of skull is articulated with atlas vertebra.
questions.explanation: C (7 cervical vertebrae), D (all except last 2 pairs of ribs are bicephalic), and E (occipital bone articulates with atlas) are correct. A is false (human skull is dicondylic, not monocondylic); B is false (vertebral joints are a type of cartilaginous but statement as broadly worded needs scrutiny). C, D and E only.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: During G0 phase of cell cycle the cell is metabolically inactive. Statement II: The centrosome undergoes duplication during S phase of interphase. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.topic: Cell Cycle - G0 Phase and Centrosome Duplication
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect — during the G0 (quiescent) phase, the cell is metabolically ACTIVE but does not proliferate/divide (it is not metabolically inactive). Statement II is correct — the centrosome duplicates during the S phase of interphase, along with DNA replication.

questions.text:
What is the fate of a piece of DNA carrying only gene of interest which is transferred into an alien organism?
A. The piece of DNA would be able to multiply itself independently in the progeny cells of the organism.
B. It may get integrated into the genome of the recipient.
C. It may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA.
D. The alien piece of DNA is not an integral part of chromosome.
E. It shows ability to replicate.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Fate of Foreign DNA Transferred into Alien Organism
questions.explanation: A foreign DNA piece (gene of interest alone, without an origin of replication) cannot multiply independently - it needs to either integrate into the host genome (B) or be part of a vector that replicates along with host DNA (C) to be inherited. So B and C only. 12th NCERT Page No. 164.

questions.text: Which one of the following organisms bears hollow and pneumatic long bones?
questions.explanation: Neophron (Egyptian vulture) is a bird, and birds have hollow, pneumatic long bones as an adaptation for flight.

questions.text: Persons with 'AB' blood group are called as "Universal recipients". This is due to:
options: Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma
Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs
Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
Presence of antibodies anti-A and anti-B on RBCs
questions.explanation: AB blood group individuals lack both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their plasma, so they can receive blood from any ABO group without agglutination reaction, making them universal recipients.

questions.text: In the following palindromic base sequences of DNA, which one can be cut easily by particular restriction enzyme?
questions.explanation: 5'GAATTC3'/3'CTTAAG5' is a true palindromic sequence (reads the same 5' to 3' on both strands), recognized by EcoRI restriction enzyme.

questions.text: Match the following: (a) Physalia, (b) Limulus, (c) Ancylostoma, (d) Pinctada with (i) Pearl oyster, (ii) Portuguese Man of War, (iii) Living fossil, (iv) Hookworm.
questions.explanation: Physalia is Portuguese Man of War (ii); Limulus is a living fossil (iii); Ancylostoma is a hookworm (iv); Pinctada is a pearl oyster (i). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(i).

questions.text: Experimental verification of the chromosomal theory of inheritance was done by:
questions.explanation: Thomas Hunt Morgan provided experimental verification of the chromosomal theory of inheritance through his studies on Drosophila, demonstrating gene linkage on chromosomes.

questions.text: Dobson units are used to measure thickness of:
questions.explanation: Dobson units (DU) are used to measure the thickness of the ozone layer.

questions.text: The process of growth is maximum during:
questions.explanation: During the log (exponential) phase, growth rate is at its maximum, as cells/organisms divide and grow rapidly under favourable conditions, unlike the lag phase (initial slow growth), senescence (decline) or dormancy (no growth).

questions.text: Which of the following glucose transporters is insulin-dependent?
questions.explanation: GLUT4 is the insulin-dependent glucose transporter, primarily found in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, which translocates to the cell membrane in response to insulin signaling.

questions.text: Graves' disease is caused due to:
questions.explanation: Graves' disease is an autoimmune disorder causing hypersecretion (hyperthyroidism) of the thyroid gland.

questions.text: You are given a tissue with its potential for differentiation in an artificial culture. Which of the following pairs of hormones would you add to the medium to secure shoots as well as roots?
questions.explanation: Auxin and cytokinin in appropriate ratios control shoot and root differentiation in tissue culture (high cytokinin:auxin → shoots, high auxin:cytokinin → roots)

questions.text: Presence of plants arranged into well defined vertical layers depending on their height can be seen best in:
questions.explanation: Tropical rain forests show the most pronounced vertical stratification (layering), with distinct emergent, canopy, understorey, shrub, and herb layers, due to their high plant diversity and dense growth competing for light.

questions.text: A population of diploid organisms is at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. If the frequency of allele A is 0.1, the frequency of AA is ____________.
questions.explanation: Under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, genotype frequencies follow p² + 2pq + q² = 1, where p is the frequency of allele A. Frequency of AA genotype = p² = (0.1)² = 0.01.

questions.text:
Match Column-I with Column-II and select the correct option using the codes given below:
Column-I: a. Mons pubis, b. Antrum, c. Trophectoderm, d. Nebenkern
Column-II: (i) Embryo formation, (ii) Sperm, (iii) Female external genitalia, (iv) Graafian follicle
Codes:
(1) a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
(2) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
(3) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
(4) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
questions.explanation: Mons pubis = female external genitalia; Antrum = Graafian follicle (fluid-filled cavity); Trophectoderm = embryo formation (outer cell layer of blastocyst); Nebenkern = sperm (mitochondrial structure in spermatid). So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a part of human central neural system?
questions.topic: Meninges of the Central Nervous System
questions.explanation: Dura mater, pia mater, and arachnoid are the three meninges (protective membranes) covering the brain and spinal cord (CNS). Pericardium is the membrane surrounding the heart, not part of the central nervous system.

questions.text: Lungs are made up of air-filled sacs, the alveoli. They do not collapse even after forceful expiration, because of:
questions.explanation: Residual Volume (RV) is the volume of air that remains in the lungs even after the most forceful expiration, preventing the alveoli from completely collapsing.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Metamerism, (b) Canal system, (c) Comb plates, (d) Cnidoblasts
List-II: (i) Coelenterata, (ii) Ctenophora, (iii) Annelida, (iv) Porifera
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
(2) a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii
(3) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
(4) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
questions.explanation: Metamerism = Annelida; Canal system = Porifera; Comb plates = Ctenophora; Cnidoblasts = Coelenterata. So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Match the following: (a) Inhibitor of catalytic activity, (b) Possess peptide bonds, (c) Cell wall material in fungi, (d) Secondary metabolite with (i) Ricin, (ii) Malonate, (iii) Chitin, (iv) Collagen
questions.explanation: Malonate is an inhibitor of catalytic activity (succinate dehydrogenase) (ii), Collagen possesses peptide bonds (iv), Chitin is the cell wall material in fungi (iii), and Ricin is a secondary metabolite (toxic protein) (i). This matches a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.

questions.text: In the given figure, which component has thin outer walls and highly thickened inner walls?
questions.explanation: In a xylem vessel cross-section, the innermost component (C, adjacent to the lumen) has thin outer walls but highly thickened inner walls due to secondary wall deposition, which provides mechanical strength while allowing lateral conduction.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Transfer RNAs and ribosomal RNA do not interact with mRNA. Statement II : RNA interference (RNAi) takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect: tRNA and rRNA DO interact with mRNA during the translation process. Statement II is correct: RNA interference occurs in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence.

questions.text: Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization. (A) Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin. (B) Heterotrophs with tissue/organ/organ system level of body organization. (C) Prokaryotes with cell wall made of polysaccharides and amino acids. (D) Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/organ level of body organization. (E) Eukaryotes with cellular body organization. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Increasing complexity: Monera (C, prokaryotes) → Protista (E, eukaryotes with cellular organization) → Fungi (A, multicellular heterotrophs, chitin cell wall) → Plantae (D, eukaryotic autotrophs, tissue/organ level) → Animalia (B, heterotrophs, tissue/organ/organ-system level). So C, E, A, D, B.

questions.text: Streptokinase produced by bacterium Streptococcus is used for
questions.explanation: Streptokinase, produced by the bacterium Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering, is used as a 'clot buster' for removing clots from the blood vessels of patients who have undergone myocardial infarction leading to heart attack.

questions.text: Which of the following is correctly matched for the product produced by them?
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's/brewer's yeast) is correctly matched with ethanol, which it produces through fermentation. Methanobacterium produces methane gas, Penicillium notatum produces the antibiotic penicillin, and Acetobacter aceti produces acetic acid (vinegar).

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 8 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: In stratosphere, which of the following elements acts as a catalyst in degradation of ozone and release of molecular oxygen?
questions.explanation: Chlorine atoms (released from CFCs) act as catalysts in the stratosphere, breaking down ozone molecules into molecular oxygen through a chain reaction, without being consumed themselves.

questions.text: The first stable product of CO2 fixation in sorghum is:
questions.explanation: Sorghum is a C4 plant; the first stable product of CO2 fixation via PEP carboxylase in C4 plants is oxaloacetic acid (OAA), a 4-carbon compound.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II with respect to methods of Contraception and their respective actions. List-I: (a) Diaphragms (b) Contraceptive Pills (c) Intra Uterine Devices (d) Lactational Amenorrhea. List-II: (i) Inhibit ovulation and Implantation (ii) Increase phagocytosis of sperm within Uterus (iii) Absence of Menstrual cycle and ovulation following parturition (iv) They cover the cervix blocking the entry of sperms. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Diaphragms cover the cervix blocking sperm entry; contraceptive pills inhibit ovulation and implantation; Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) increase phagocytosis of sperm within the uterus; and Lactational Amenorrhea is the natural absence of menstrual cycle and ovulation following parturition, matching (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).

questions.text: Which of the following is the most important cause for animals and plants being driven to extinction?
questions.explanation: Habitat loss and fragmentation is considered the most important cause of animal and plant extinctions, as per IUCN and conservation biology literature.

questions.text: Select the correct match:
options: Francois Jacob and Jacques Monod - Lac operon
Matthew Meselson and F. Stahl - Pisum sativum
Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase - TMV
questions.topic: Key experiments and discoveries in molecular biology
questions.explanation: Francois Jacob and Jacques Monod proposed the operon model (Lac operon) to explain gene regulation in bacteria, a landmark discovery in molecular biology.

questions.text: The following reaction depicts the activity of a particular class of enzymes: X-Y (Substrate) --E--> X-Y + C=C (Product, Product). Identify the enzyme class 'E' from the following options:
questions.explanation: Lyases catalyse the removal of groups to form double bonds (or addition to double bonds) without hydrolysis, matching the given reaction type.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) P wave (B) QRS complex (C) T wave (D) T-P gap
List II: (I) Heart muscles are electrically silent. (II) Depolarisation of ventricles. (III) Depolarisation of atria. (IV) Repolarisation of ventricles.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: P wave represents depolarisation of the atria (A-III). QRS complex represents depolarisation of the ventricles (B-II). T wave represents repolarisation of the ventricles (C-IV). T-P gap is when the heart muscles are electrically silent (D-I). So A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I is correct.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
options: Laminaria and Sargassum are used as food.
Algae increase the level of dissolved oxygen in the immediate environment.
Algin is obtained from red algae, and carrageenan from brown algae.
Agar-agar is obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria.
questions.explanation: Actually algin is obtained from brown algae and carrageenan from red algae - the statement has them reversed, making it wrong.

questions.text: While explaining interspecific interaction of population, (+) sign is assigned for beneficial interaction, (−) sign is assigned for detrimental interaction and (0) for neutral interaction. Which of the following interactions can be assigned (+) for one specifies and (−) for another specifies involved in the interaction?
questions.explanation: In predation, the predator benefits (+) while the prey is harmed (−), matching the (+,−) interaction pattern.

questions.text:
Consider the following:
A. The reductive division for the human female gametogenesis starts earlier than that of the male gametogenesis.
B. The gap between the first meiotic division and the second meiotic division is much shorter for males compared to females.
C. The first polar body is associated with the formation of the primary oocyte.
D. Luteinizing Hormone (LH) surge leads to disintegration of the endometrium and onset of menstrual bleeding.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: (A) Correct - female meiosis I begins during fetal life, much earlier than male meiosis which starts at puberty. (B) Correct - in males the gap between meiosis I and II is short, in females it is very long (arrested at prophase I until ovulation). (C) Incorrect - the first polar body is formed from the secondary oocyte, not associated with primary oocyte formation. (D) Incorrect - it is the fall in progesterone (not LH surge) that causes disintegration of the endometrium and menstruation. Class 12th NCERT Page No. 33.

questions.text: The final proof for DNA as the genetic material came from the experiments of:
questions.explanation: The Hershey-Chase blender experiment, using radioactively labelled bacteriophage DNA and protein, provided the final, conclusive proof that DNA (not protein) is the genetic material.

questions.text: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refers to:
questions.explanation: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refer to genes that have been expressed as RNA, identified through sequencing of cDNA, indicating active genes in a tissue.

questions.text: The hepatic portal vein drains blood to liver from:
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich, deoxygenated blood from the intestine (and other digestive organs) to the liver for processing before it enters the general circulation.

questions.text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
options: Mature sieve tube elements possess a conspicuous nucleus and usual cytoplasmic organelles
Microbodies are present both in plant and animal cells
The perinuclear space forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm
Nuclear pores act as passages for proteins and RNA molecules in both directions between nucleus and cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Mature sieve tube elements are enucleate (lack a nucleus) at maturity, so statement 1 is incorrect.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body. Statement II: Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect — endarch and exarch describe the position of PRIMARY xylem (not secondary xylem), based on the direction of protoxylem and metaxylem maturation. Statement II is correct — the exarch condition (protoxylem towards the periphery, metaxylem towards the centre) is the most common feature of root xylem.

questions.text: The pivot joint between atlas and axis is a type of:
questions.explanation: The pivot joint between the atlas and axis vertebrae, which allows rotational movement of the head, is a type of synovial joint.

questions.text: Select the incorrect statements with reference to Rh grouping. A. Erythroblastosis foetalis is a condition observed having foetus with Rh- blood and mother with Rh+ blood. B. Rh antigen is observed on RBCs in the majority of human beings. C. Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched. D. Rh incompatibility is observed when a pregnant mother is Rh- and the foetus is Rh-. E. Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the second child.
questions.explanation: A is incorrect (it's the reverse — Rh- mother with Rh+ foetus); D is incorrect (incompatibility occurs when mother is Rh- and foetus is Rh+, not Rh-); E is also inconsistent (antibodies given after first, not second, delivery) though per key, the correct selection of incorrect statements is A and D only.

questions.text: In humans, respiration occurs in the following steps. Arrange these steps in the correct order: A. Diffusion of O2 and CO2 between blood and tissues. B. Diffusion of O2 across alveolar membrane. C. Pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and CO2 rich alveolar air is released out. D. Cellular respiration. E. Transport of gases by the blood.
questions.topic: Correct sequence of steps in human respiration
questions.explanation: Sequence: pulmonary ventilation (C) → diffusion of gases across alveolar membrane (B) → transport of gases by blood (E) → diffusion between blood and tissues (A) → cellular respiration (D): C, B, E, A, D.

questions.text: In which of the following techniques, the embryos are transferred to assist those females who cannot conceive?
questions.explanation: ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves transferring the zygote/early embryo into the fallopian tube, and IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer) involves transferring the embryo into the uterus; both are embryo-transfer assisted reproductive techniques.

questions.text: Strobili or cones are found in:
questions.explanation: Equisetum (a pteridophyte, horsetail) bears strobili (cone-like reproductive structures) at the tip of its stems, unlike Salvinia, Pteris (ferns without true cones) or Marchantia (a bryophyte).

questions.text:
Which one of the following can be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance?
(A) Out of one pair of factors one is dominant and the other is recessive.
(B) Alleles do not show any expression and both the characters appear as such in F2 generation.
(C) Factors occur in pairs in normal diploid plants.
(D) The discrete unit controlling a particular character is called factor.
(E) The expression of only one of the parental characters is found in a monohybrid cross.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C, D and E
A, C, D and E only
questions.topic: Mendel's Law of Dominance - Explanatory Statements
questions.explanation: The Law of Dominance explains: one factor of a pair is dominant and other recessive (A); factors occur in pairs (C); the discrete unit controlling a character is called a factor (D); and only one parental character is expressed in a monohybrid cross (E). Statement B is incorrect/not part of this law (alleles don't both appear unexpressed in F2 - it describes something else entirely, like codominance absence). So A, C, D and E only. 12th NCERT Page No. 59.

questions.text: Which one of the following techniques does not serve the purpose of early diagnosis of a disease for its early treatment?
questions.topic: Techniques for Early Diagnosis of Disease
questions.explanation: Recombinant DNA Technology is a technique used for genetic engineering and production of biological products, not directly for early diagnosis of disease. Serum/urine analysis, PCR, and ELISA are all techniques used for early disease diagnosis.

questions.text: The following are the stages of life cycle of Plasmodium. Arrange the stages in the proper order: A. The parasites reproduce asexually in RBCs, bursting the cells. B. The parasites reproduce asexually in liver cells, bursting the cells and releasing into blood. C. Gametocytes develop in RBCs. D. Sporozoites reach the liver through the blood. E. Female mosquito injects sporozoites into humans during bite.
questions.explanation: Sequence: mosquito injects sporozoites (E) → sporozoites reach liver (D) → asexual reproduction in liver cells (B) → asexual reproduction in RBCs (A) → gametocytes develop in RBCs (C): E, D, B, A, C.

questions.text: The fruit fly has 8 chromosomes (2n) in each cell. During interphase of Mitosis if the number of chromosomes at G1 phase is 8, what would be the number of chromosomes after S phase?
questions.explanation: DNA replication during S phase doubles the DNA content (each chromosome now has two sister chromatids), but the number of CHROMOSOMES remains 8 — it is the DNA content/chromatid number that doubles, not the chromosome count.

questions.text: Name the plant growth regulator which upon spraying on sugarcane crop, increases the length of stem, thus increasing the yield of sugarcane crop.
questions.topic: Gibberellins and stem elongation in sugarcane
questions.explanation: Gibberellins promote stem elongation (internode elongation), and spraying them on sugarcane crops increases stem length, thereby increasing the sugar yield per plant.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a natural/traditional contraceptive method?
questions.explanation: Vaults (like cervical caps) are barrier contraceptive devices, not natural/traditional methods. Lactational amenorrhea, coitus interruptus, and periodic abstinence are all natural/traditional contraceptive methods that don't involve any device or medication.

questions.text:
Read the following statements on plant growth and development.
A. Parthenocarpy can be induced by auxins.
B. Plant growth regulators can be involved in promotion as well as inhibition of growth.
C. Dedifferentiation is a pre-requisite for re-differentiation.
D. Abscisic acid is a plant growth promoter.
E. Apical dominance promotes the growth of lateral buds.
Choose the options with all correct statements.
questions.explanation: Parthenocarpy can be induced by auxins (A, correct). Growth regulators like auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins are promoters, while ABA is an inhibitor - so PGRs are involved in both promotion and inhibition (B, correct). Dedifferentiation (cell division forming new cells) is a pre-requisite for redifferentiation into permanent tissues (C, correct). Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor, not promoter (D, incorrect). Apical dominance suppresses (not promotes) the growth of lateral buds (E, incorrect). So A, B, C Only.

questions.text: Which of the following components provides sticky character to the bacterial cell?
questions.explanation: The glycocalyx, a loose sheath surrounding the bacterial cell wall (which can be a slime layer or capsule), gives the bacterial cell its sticky character, aiding attachment to surfaces.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an attribute of a population?
questions.explanation: Sex ratio, natality and mortality are all intrinsic attributes/characteristics of a population itself, while species interaction refers to relationships between different populations/species, not an attribute of a single population.

questions.text:
Given below are some stages of human evolution. Arrange them in correct sequence. (Past to Recent)
A. Homo habilis B. Homo sapiens C. Homo neanderthalensis D. Homo erectus
Choose the correct sequence of human evolution from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The correct chronological sequence of human evolution from past to recent is: Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo neanderthalensis → Homo sapiens, giving the sequence A-D-C-B.

questions.text: Tegmina in cockroach, arises from
questions.explanation: The tegmina (thickened, leathery forewings) of the cockroach arise from the mesothorax, while the hindwings arise from the metathorax.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct about Klinefelter's Syndrome? A. This disorder was first described by Langdon Down (1866). B. Such an individual has overall masculine development. However, the feminine development is also expressed. C. The affected individual is short statured. D. Physical, psychomotor and mental development is retarded. E. Such individuals are sterile. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement B is correct — individuals with Klinefelter's syndrome (XXY) show overall masculine development, but some feminine development (like gynecomastia) is also expressed. Statement E is correct — such individuals are typically sterile. Statement A is incorrect — Klinefelter's syndrome was described by Klinefelter, not Langdon Down (who described Down syndrome). Statement C is incorrect — affected individuals are typically tall statured, not short. Statement D is not characteristic in the way stated for this answer key.

questions.text: In Hardy-Weinberg equation, the frequency of heterozygous individual is represented by:
questions.explanation: In the Hardy-Weinberg equation p² + 2pq + q² = 1, the term 2pq represents the frequency of heterozygous individuals.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): A person goes to high altitude and experiences 'altitude sickness' with symptoms like breathing difficulty and heart palpitations.
Reason (R): Due to low atmospheric pressure at hight altitude, the body does not get sufficient oxygyen. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Altitude sickness occurs because at high altitude, atmospheric pressure is low, resulting in insufficient oxygen availability to the body, causing breathing difficulty and heart palpitations. Both statements are true and R correctly explains A.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. Heroin, B. Marijuana, C. Cocaine, D. Morphine. List II: I. Effect on cardiovascular system, II. Slow down body function, III. Painkiller, IV. Interferes with transport of dopamine. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.topic: Drugs of Abuse and Their Effects
questions.explanation: Heroin slows down body function (A-II). Marijuana affects the cardiovascular system (B-I). Cocaine interferes with the transport of dopamine (C-IV). Morphine acts as a painkiller (D-III). So the correct match is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (a) Bronchioles (b) Goblet cell (c) Tendons (d) Adipose Tissue
List-II: (i) Dense Regular Connective tissue (ii) Loose Connective Tissue (iii) Glandular Tissue (iv) Ciliated Epithelium
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Bronchioles are lined with ciliated epithelium (iv); Goblet cells are glandular tissue (iii) secreting mucus; Tendons are dense regular connective tissue (i); Adipose tissue is loose connective tissue (ii). (NCERT Class 11, Pg 102-103)

questions.text: All of the following are part of an operon except
questions.explanation: An operon (a prokaryotic concept) consists of a promoter, an operator and structural genes under common regulatory control. Enhancers are regulatory elements typically associated with eukaryotic gene expression, not part of the bacterial operon.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) S phase, (b) G2 phase, (c) Quiescent stage, (d) G1 phase with (i) Proteins are synthesized, (ii) Inactive phase, (iii) Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication, (iv) DNA replication.
questions.explanation: S phase involves DNA replication (iv); G2 phase involves protein synthesis (i); Quiescent stage (G0) is an inactive phase (ii); G1 phase is the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication (iii). (a)-(iv),(b)-(i),(c)-(ii),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: Inspite of interspecific competition in nature, which mechanism the competing species might have evolved for their survival?
questions.explanation: Resource partitioning allows competing species to coexist by differentiating their niches (e.g., different feeding times, microhabitats) to avoid direct competition for the same resources.

questions.text: The gaseous plant growth regulator is used in plants to:
options: promote root growth and root hair formation to increase the absorption surface
kill dicotyledonous weeds in the fields
questions.explanation: Ethylene (the gaseous plant growth regulator) promotes root growth and root hair formation, increasing the absorptive surface area, among its other effects like fruit ripening and senescence promotion.

questions.text:
After maturation, in primary lymphoid organs, the lymphocytes migrate for interaction with antigens to secondary lymphoid organs(s)/tissue(s) like:
A. Thymus
B. Bone marrow
C. Spleen
D. lymph nodes
E. Peyer's patches
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: B and T lymphocytes are produced and differentiated in primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow and thymus), but after maturation they migrate to secondary lymphoid organs/tissues - spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, and Peyer's patches (MALT) - where they interact with antigens to produce immune responses. So C, D, E only. Class 12th NCERT Page No. 138.

questions.text: In male cockroaches, sperms are stored in which part of the reproductive system?
questions.explanation: In male cockroaches, sperms produced in the testes travel via vasa deferentia and are stored in the seminal vesicles before ejaculation.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: The logistic growth model of populations is considered more realistic than the exponential growth model.
Reason R: Resources are finite.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The logistic growth model is considered more realistic than the exponential growth model because it accounts for environmental carrying capacity and resource limitation, unlike the exponential model which assumes unlimited resources -- Assertion A is correct. This is precisely because, in reality, resources (food, space, etc.) are finite, which limits population growth as it approaches carrying capacity -- Reason R is correct and correctly explains A.

questions.text: Select the incorrect statements from the following: A. Digestive system in Platyhelminthes is incomplete. B. Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of adult Echinoderms. C. Pseudocoelom is possessed by Aschelminthes. D. Notochord is persistent throughout life in the class Chondrichthyes. E. Members of class Reptilia maintain a constant body temperature.
questions.explanation: B is incorrect (adult echinoderms show radial, not bilateral, symmetry — only larvae are bilateral); E is incorrect (reptiles are ectothermic, not constant body temperature). A, C, D are correct statements. B and E only incorrect; per key matches option B and D only.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Forelimbs of human and bats are homologous.
Reason R: Forelimbs of humans and bats have similar anatomical structure.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The forelimbs of humans and bats are homologous organs -- they evolved from a common ancestral structure but are adapted to perform different functions (grasping vs. flying) -- Assertion A is correct. Homology is defined by similar anatomical (structural) origin despite different functions, so forelimbs having similar underlying anatomical structure (bone arrangement) is indeed the basis for them being called homologous -- Reason R is correct and correctly explains A.

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 9 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: In the equation GPP - R = NPP, where GPP is Gross Primary Productivity and NPP is Net Primary Productivity, R here is ______.
questions.explanation: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) minus respiratory losses (R) by plants. So R stands for respiratory loss.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Fatty acids and glycerols cannot be absorbed into the blood. Statement II: Specialized lymphatic capillaries called lacteals carry chylomicrons into lymphatic vessels and ultimately into the blood. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: fatty acids and glycerol (reformed into triglycerides/chylomicrons) cannot be directly absorbed into blood capillaries; instead, they enter via lacteals (specialized lymphatic capillaries) as chylomicrons, which eventually reach the blood through the lymphatic system.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding mitochondria is incorrect?
options: Inner membrane is convoluted with infoldings.
Mitochondrial matrix contains single circular DNA molecule and ribosomes.
Outer membrane is permeable to monomers of carbohydrates, fats and proteins.
Enzymes of electron transport are embedded in outer membrane.
questions.explanation: Enzymes of the electron transport chain are embedded in the INNER mitochondrial membrane, not the outer membrane. This makes statement 4 incorrect.

questions.text: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) may not be a good index for pollution for water bodies receiving effluents from:
questions.explanation: BOD measures oxygen consumed by microbial degradation of biodegradable organic matter; petroleum industry effluents contain largely non-biodegradable toxic pollutants, so BOD is not a good pollution index for them.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is correct, with reference to enzymes?
questions.explanation: A holoenzyme is the complete, catalytically active enzyme formed by the combination of the protein part (apoenzyme) and a non-protein cofactor or coenzyme: Holoenzyme = Apoenzyme + Coenzyme.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Osteoporosis is characterised by decreased bone mass and increased chance of fractures. Reason (R): Common cause of osteoporosis is increased levels of estrogen. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct: osteoporosis involves decreased bone mass and increased fracture risk. Reason (R) is incorrect: osteoporosis is actually caused by DECREASED (not increased) estrogen levels, commonly seen after menopause.

questions.text: Which of the following is an in situ conservation method?
questions.explanation: Sacred Groves are an in situ conservation method, protecting species in their natural habitat; seed banks and botanical gardens are ex situ.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Bt toxins are insect group specific and coded by a gene cry IAc.
Statement II: Bt toxin exists as inactive protoxin in B. thuringiensis. However, after ingestion by the insect the inactive protoxin gets converted into active form due to acidic pH of the insect gut.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.explanation: Statement I is true - Bt toxins are indeed insect group specific and coded by cry genes like cry IAc. Statement II is false - the Bt protoxin gets converted to its active form due to the ALKALINE pH of the insect gut, not acidic pH. 12th NCERT Page No. 179-180.

questions.text: Mitochondrial inner membrane encloses __________.
questions.explanation: The inner mitochondrial membrane encloses the matrix, a semi-fluid substance containing enzymes of the Krebs cycle, mitochondrial DNA, ribosomes, and other components.

questions.text: The organelles that are included in the endomembrane system are:
options: Golgi complex, Endoplasmic reticulum, Mitochondria and Lysosomes
Endoplasmic reticulum, Mitochondria, Ribosomes and Lysosomes
Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, Lysosomes and Vacuoles
Golgi complex, Mitochondria, Ribosomes and Lysosmsomes
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system includes endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Mitochondria and ribosomes are not part of the endomembrane system as they function independently.

questions.text: Which of the following in female gametophyte of an angiosperm helps in guiding the pollen tube for fertilizing the eggs?
questions.explanation: Synergid cells, located at the micropylar end of the embryo sac alongside the egg cell, possess a specialized filiform apparatus that helps guide and attract the pollen tube towards the egg for fertilization.

questions.text: Which one of the following never occurs during mitotic cell division?
options: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes
Movement of centrioles towards opposite poles
Coiling and condensation of the chromatids
questions.explanation: Pairing of homologous chromosomes (synapsis) occurs only during meiosis (prophase I), not during mitosis. Spindle fiber attachment, centriole movement, and chromatid condensation all occur during mitosis.

questions.text: The genotypes of a Husband and Wife are IAIB and IAi. Among the blood types of their children, how many different genotypes and phenotypes are possible?
questions.explanation: Crossing IAIB x IAi gives offspring genotypes IAIA, IAIB, IAi, and IBi (4 genotypes). Phenotypically, IAIA and IAi are both blood group A, IAIB is group AB, and IBi is group B, giving only 3 distinct phenotypes (A, AB, B).

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List I: (a) Scapula (b) Cranium (c) Sternum (d) Vertebral column
List-II: (i) Cartilaginous joints (ii) Flat bone (iii) Fibrous joints (iv) Triangular flat bone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Scapula is a triangular flat bone; Cranium bones are joined by fibrous joints; Sternum is a flat bone; Vertebral column has cartilaginous joints between vertebrae.

questions.text: Which of the following is commonly used as a vector for introducing a DNA fragment in human lymphocytes?
questions.explanation: Retroviral vectors are commonly used for introducing DNA fragments into human lymphocytes and other mammalian cells, as retroviruses can efficiently infect and integrate into the host genome.

questions.text: Identify the type of flowers based on the position of calyx, corolla and androecium with respect to the ovary from the given figures (a) and (b) [Figure: two flower longitudinal sections showing different ovary positions]
questions.topic: Flower Types - Perigynous vs Epigynous Identification from Figure
questions.explanation: Based on the figure, both flower (a) and flower (b) show the perigynous condition, where the ovary is in the centre and other floral parts arise from the rim of a cup-shaped thalamus at the same level. 11th NCERT Page No. 62.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List I: (a) Vaults (b) IUDs (c) Vasectomy (d) Tubectomy
List-II: (i) Entry of sperm through Cervix is blocked (ii) Removal of Vas deferens (iii) Phagocytosis of sperms within the Uterus (iv) Removal of fallopian tube
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Vaults cause phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus; IUDs block entry of sperm through the cervix; Vasectomy removes the vas deferens; Tubectomy removes/blocks the fallopian tube.

questions.text: Regarding Meiosis, which of the statements is incorrect?
options: There are two stages in Meiosis, Meiosis-I and II
DNA replication occurs in S phase of Meiosis-II
Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination occurs in Meiosis-I
Four haploid cells are formed at the end of Meiosis-II
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs only once, during the S phase before Meiosis-I begins (interphase I), not during Meiosis-II. Meiosis-II proceeds without further DNA replication, making statement 2 incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Fig fruit is a non-vegetarian fruit as it has enclosed fig wasps in it.
Statement II: Fig wasp and fig tree exhibit mutual relationship as fig wasp completes its life cycle in fig fruit and fig fruit gets pollinated by fig wasp.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and Statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are incorrect. Statement I is debatable/considered incorrect as fig fruit is used during religious fasting and not strictly classified as non-vegetarian in this context. Statement II is incorrect because pollination occurs in the fig inflorescence (syconium), not the fig fruit itself - the fruit develops after pollination.

questions.text: 2(C51H98O6)+145O2 → 102CO2+98H2O+energy. The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of a biomolecule used for respiration, as per the above equation, would be:
questions.explanation: RQ=CO2 evolved/O2 consumed=102/145≈0.70, which is between 0.5 and 0.95 (this is a fat, giving RQ<1).

questions.text: Identify the vertebrate group of animals characterized by crop and gizzard in its digestive system.
questions.topic: Classification of vertebrates by digestive features
questions.explanation: Birds (Aves) have a crop for temporary food storage and a muscular gizzard for grinding food, both specialised parts of their digestive system adapted for a toothless beak.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: A. Spherical, B. Rod, C. Comma, D. Spirillum
List-II: I. Vibrio, II. Cocci, III. Spirilla, IV. Bacilli
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Spherical-shaped bacteria are called Cocci (II). Rod-shaped bacteria are called Bacilli (IV). Comma-shaped bacteria are called Vibrio (I). Spirillum-shaped (spiral) bacteria are called Spirilla (III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct sequence of steps in a PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
questions.explanation: PCR steps proceed in the order: Denaturation (separating DNA strands at high temp) → Annealing (primers bind) → Extension (DNA polymerase extends new strand).

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of plant cells in the phase of elongation?
questions.topic: Characteristic not seen in elongation phase of plant cells
questions.explanation: In the phase of elongation (not meristematic/division phase), cells enlarge, vacuolate, but do not show large conspicuous nuclei (characteristic of actively dividing meristematic cells, not elongating cells).

questions.text: Name the ion responsible for unmasking of active sites for myosin for cross-bridge activity during muscle contraction.
questions.explanation: Calcium ions bind to troponin, causing a conformational change that shifts tropomyosin and unmasks the active sites on actin for myosin cross-bridge formation.

questions.text: Which of the following is not the function of conducting part of respiratory system?
options: It clears inhaled air from foreign particles
Temperature of inhaled air is brought to body temperature
Provides surface for diffusion of O2 and CO2
questions.explanation: The conducting part (nostrils to terminal bronchioles) only transports, cleans, humidifies and warms air. Gas diffusion occurs in the respiratory part (alveoli), not the conducting part.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about lac-operon is correct?
options: Lactose activates repressor to bind to the operator
Genes i, z, y and a share single common promoter
Galactose can act as an inducer of lac operon
questions.explanation: The regulatory gene 'i' (encoding the lac repressor) is constitutively expressed, i.e., it is always transcribed at a low, constant level, independent of lactose presence. (Lactose/allolactose actually INACTIVATES the repressor, not activates it, to allow transcription; the structural genes z, y, a share a common promoter, but gene i has its own separate promoter.)

questions.text: Match the following concerning essential elements and their functions in plants: (a) Iron, (b) Zinc, (c) Boron, (d) Manganese with (i) Photolysis of water, (ii) Pollen germination, (iii) Required for chlorophyll biosynthesis, (iv) IAA biosynthesis
questions.topic: Functions of essential elements in plants
questions.explanation: Iron is required for chlorophyll biosynthesis (iii), Zinc is needed for IAA (auxin) biosynthesis (iv), Boron is important for pollen germination (ii), and Manganese is involved in the photolysis of water (i). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Broad palm with single palm crease is visible in a person suffering from:
questions.explanation: A broad palm with a single palm crease (simian crease) is a characteristic phenotypic feature of Down's syndrome, caused by trisomy of chromosome 21.

questions.text: DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes transcription on one strand of the DNA which is called the:
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase uses the template strand (antisense strand) of DNA to synthesize a complementary RNA strand during transcription; the other strand is the coding strand.

questions.text: Lippe's loop is a type of contraceptive used as:
questions.explanation: Lippes loop is a non-medicated (inert) intrauterine device (IUD), made of plastic, unlike medicated IUDs like Copper-T which release copper ions.

questions.text: The QRS complex in a standard ECG represents:
questions.explanation: The QRS complex in an ECG represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which triggers ventricular contraction.

questions.text: The method of directly injecting a sperm into ovum in assisted reproductive technology is called:
questions.explanation: Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is the assisted reproductive technique where a sperm is directly injected into the cytoplasm of an ovum (egg) to facilitate fertilization, typically used in cases of male infertility.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a method of in situ conservation of biodiversity?
questions.explanation: Botanical Garden is a method of EX SITU conservation (conservation outside natural habitat), while Sacred Grove, Biosphere Reserve, and Wildlife Sanctuary are all in situ conservation methods (conservation within natural habitat).

questions.text: Which one of the following equations represents the Verhulst-pearl Logistic Growth of population?
questions.explanation: The Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth of population is described by the equation dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K, where N is population size, r is intrinsic rate of natural increase, K is carrying capacity.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. Gene 'a', B. Gene 'y', C. Gene 'i', D. Gene 'z'. List II: I. beta-galactosidase, II. Transacetylase, III. Permease, IV. Repressor protein. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: In the lac operon, gene 'a' codes for transacetylase (A-II), gene 'y' codes for permease (B-III), gene 'i' codes for the repressor protein (C-IV), and gene 'z' codes for beta-galactosidase (D-I). So the correct match is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Cohesion, (b) Adhesion, (c) Surface tension, (d) Guttation
List-II: (i) More attraction in liquid phase, (ii) Mutual attraction among water molecules, (iii) Water loss in liquid phase, (iv) Attraction towards polar surfaces
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
(2) a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
(3) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
(4) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
questions.explanation: Cohesion = mutual attraction among water molecules (ii); Adhesion = attraction towards polar surfaces (iv); Surface tension = more attraction in liquid phase (i); Guttation = water loss in liquid phase (iii). So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

questions.text: Spliceosomes are not found in cells of:
questions.explanation: Spliceosomes carry out RNA splicing to remove introns from pre-mRNA, a process that occurs in eukaryotic cells (fungi, animals, plants). Bacteria are prokaryotes and lack introns in most genes and spliceosomes altogether.

questions.text: Which one of the following plants shows vexillary aestivation and diadelphous stamens?
questions.explanation: Pisum sativum (pea, family Fabaceae) shows vexillary (papilionaceous) aestivation and diadelphous stamens (9+1 arrangement), both characteristic features of the Fabaceae family.

questions.text: The region of Biosphere Reserve which is legally protected and where no human activity is allowed is known as:
questions.explanation: The core zone of a Biosphere Reserve is a legally protected area where no human activity is allowed, preserving the natural ecosystem in its pristine state.

questions.text:
Which of the following are Autoimmune disorders?
A. Myasthenia gravis B. Rheumatoid arthritis C. Gout D. Muscular dystrophy E. Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Myasthenia gravis, Rheumatoid arthritis, and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) are all autoimmune disorders where the immune system attacks the body's own tissues. Gout is a metabolic disorder caused by uric acid crystal deposition, and Muscular dystrophy is a genetic disorder, neither of which is autoimmune.

questions.text: If the distance between two consecutive base pairs is 0.34 nm and the total number of base pairs of a DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell is 6.6×10^9 bp, then the length of the DNA is approximately:
questions.topic: Length of DNA calculation from base pairs
questions.explanation: Length = number of base pairs × distance per base pair = 6.6×10^9 × 0.34×10^-9 m = 2.244 ≈ 2.2 meters.

questions.text: The product formed from the following reaction sequence is (benzonitrile with LiAlH4/H2O, then NaNO2+HCl, then H2O)
questions.explanation: LiAlH4 reduces the nitrile to a primary amine, which is then diazotized and hydrolyzed to give benzyl alcohol.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a component of Fallopian tube?
questions.explanation: The Fallopian tube (oviduct) consists of the infundibulum, ampulla, and isthmus. The uterine fundus is the upper rounded part of the uterus itself, not a component of the Fallopian tube.

questions.text: In the seeds of cereals, the outer covering of endosperm separates the embryo by a protein-rich layer called :
questions.explanation: The outer covering of the endosperm separates the embryo by a proteinous (protein-rich) layer called the aleurone layer.

tests.title: NEET Biology Practice Test 10 (45 Questions)
tests.description: A 45-question, 45-minute NEET Biology practice test built from real NEET previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Hydrocolloid carrageen is obtained from:
questions.explanation: Carrageenan (carrageen) is a hydrocolloid extracted specifically from red algae (Rhodophyceae), such as Chondrus and Gigartina species.

questions.text: Under normal physiological conditions in human being every 100 ml of oxygenated blood can deliver _______ ml of O2 to the tissues.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, 100 ml oxygenated blood delivers approximately 5 ml of O2 to the tissues.

questions.text: During cell growth, DNA synthesis takes place in:
questions.explanation: DNA synthesis (replication) occurs during the S (synthesis) phase of the cell cycle.

questions.text: The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features: (a) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath. (b) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. (c) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed. (d) Phloem parenchyma absent. Identify the category of plant and its part:
questions.topic: Identifying monocot/dicot stem/root from anatomical features
questions.explanation: Scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed bundle type, absence of phloem parenchyma, and a large parenchymatous ground tissue are all characteristic anatomical features of a monocotyledonous stem.

questions.text: Winged pollen grains are present in
questions.topic: Winged pollen grains (adaptation for wind dispersal)
questions.explanation: Pinus (a conifer, wind-pollinated gymnosperm) has pollen grains with two air sacs (wings), which aid in their buoyancy and dispersal by wind.

questions.text: Lecithin, a small molecular weight organic compound found in living tissues, is an example of:
questions.explanation: Lecithin (phosphatidylcholine) is a classic example of a phospholipid found in living tissues. 11th NCERT Page No. 107.

questions.text: The process of appearance of recombination nodules occurs at which sub stage of prophase I in meiosis?
questions.explanation: Recombination nodules, the sites of crossing over, appear during the pachytene substage of prophase I in meiosis.

questions.text: MALT constitutes about __________ percent of the lymphoid tissue in human body.
questions.explanation: Mucosa Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT), found in the lining of the gastrointestinal, respiratory, and urogenital tracts, constitutes about 50% of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Aspergillus niger, (b) Acetobacter aceti, (c) Clostridium butylicum, (d) Lactobacillus
List-II: (i) Acetic Acid, (ii) Lactic Acid, (iii) Citric Acid, (iv) Butyric Acid
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
(2) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
(3) a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
(4) a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
questions.explanation: Aspergillus niger = Citric acid; Acetobacter aceti = Acetic acid; Clostridium butylicum = Butyric acid; Lactobacillus = Lactic acid. So a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

questions.text: Which one is wrongly matched?
questions.topic: Classification features of algae and fungi
questions.explanation: Chlorella is correctly a unicellular green alga, so this pairing is actually correct; per the official answer key, the pairing marked as wrong among the options is 'Unicellular organism - Chlorella'.

questions.text: In an E.coli strain i gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?
options: z, y, a genes will be transcribed
z, y, a genes will not be translated
RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
Only z gene will get transcribed
questions.explanation: If the repressor (i gene product) cannot bind the inducer (lactose), it remains permanently active and bound to the operator, blocking RNA polymerase from transcribing the structural genes. As a result, z, y, a genes are not transcribed and hence not translated, regardless of lactose presence. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 116-117)

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
