questions.text: The heating of phenyl-methyl ethers with HI produces:
questions.explanation: In aryl-alkyl ethers like phenyl methyl ether (anisole), cleavage with HI always occurs such that the alkyl-oxygen bond breaks (since aryl-oxygen bond is stronger due to partial double bond character), giving phenol and methyl iodide.

questions.text: The slope of Arrhenius Plot (ln k vs 1/T) of first order reaction is -5×10³ K. The value of Ea of the reaction is. Choose the correct option for your answer. [R=8.314 JK⁻¹mol⁻¹]
questions.topic: Activation energy from Arrhenius plot slope
questions.explanation: Slope=-Ea/R, so Ea=-slope×R=5×10³×8.314≈41570 J/mol≈41.5 kJ/mol.

questions.text: The pKb of dimethylamine and pKa of acetic acid are 3.27 and 4.77 respectively at T(K). The correct option for the pH of dimethylammonium acetate solution is:
questions.topic: pH of Salt of Weak Acid and Weak Base

questions.text: Which of the following are paramagnetic? A. [NiCl4]2−, B. Ni(CO)4, C. [Ni(CN)4]2−, D. [Ni(H2O)6]2+, E. Ni(PPh3)4. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: [NiCl4]2− is tetrahedral (weak field Cl−, no back pairing), Ni2+ 3d8 configuration has 2 unpaired electrons — paramagnetic. Ni(CO)4 is tetrahedral, Ni(0) 3d10 4s0 after rehybridization — 0 unpaired, diamagnetic. [Ni(CN)4]2− is square planar (strong field CN−, back pairing occurs), 0 unpaired — diamagnetic. [Ni(H2O)6]2+ is octahedral, Ni2+ 3d8 with 2 unpaired electrons — paramagnetic. Ni(PPh3)4 is tetrahedral, Ni(0) 3d10 — diamagnetic. So A and D are paramagnetic.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: The value of equilibrium constant is changed in the presence of a catalyst in the reaction at equilibrium.
Coenzymes increase the catalytic activity of enzyme.
Catalyst does not initiate any reaction.
questions.explanation: A catalyst only speeds up the attainment of equilibrium by lowering activation energy equally for forward and reverse reactions; it does not change the value of the equilibrium constant, making statement (1) incorrect.

questions.text: Enzymes that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer require an alkaline earth metal (M) as the cofactor. M is:
questions.explanation: Mg2+ is the alkaline earth metal cofactor required by enzymes (kinases) that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer reactions, as it helps stabilize the negative charges on the phosphate groups of ATP.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ferromagnetism is considered as an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II: The number of unpaired electrons in a Cr2+ ion (Z=24) is the same as that of a Nd3+ ion (Z=60). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Statement I is true: ferromagnetism is indeed considered an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II is false: Cr2+ has configuration [Ar]3d4, giving 4 unpaired electrons, while Nd3+ has [Xe]4f3, giving 3 unpaired electrons — these are not the same.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Marginal placentation, (B) Axile placentation, (C) Parietal placentation, (D) Free central placentation
List-II: (I) Argemone, (II) Tomato, (III) Primrose, (IV) Pea
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Marginal placentation is seen in Pea (IV). Axile placentation is seen in Tomato (II). Parietal placentation is seen in Argemone (I). Free central placentation is seen in Primrose (III). So A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of gases is mainly responsible for green house effect.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide and Methane are major greenhouse gases mainly responsible for the greenhouse effect and global warming.

questions.text: Select the hormone-releasing intra-uterine devices.
questions.explanation: Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs. Lippes Loop and Multiload 375 are non-hormonal copper-releasing or inert IUDs.

questions.text:
Match the plant with the kind of life cycle it exhibits:
List-I: (a) Spirogyra (b) Fern (c) Funaria (d) Cycas
List-II: (i) Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte (ii) Dominant haploid free-living gametophyte (iii) Dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte called prothallus (iv) Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Spirogyra has dominant haploid free-living gametophyte(ii), Fern has dominant sporophyte with reduced prothallus gametophyte(iii), Funaria has dominant haploid leafy gametophyte(iv), Cycas has dominant diploid sporophyte with reduced gametophyte(i). So (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(i).

questions.text: Which are correct: A. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging detect cancers of internal organs. B. Chemotherapeutics drugs are used to kill non-cancerous cells. C. α-interferon activate the cancer patients' immune system and helps in destroying the tumour. D. Chemotherapeutic drugs are biological response modifiers. E. In the case of leukaemia blood cell counts are decreased. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: A is correct: CT scan (X-ray based) and MRI (magnetic resonance based) detect cancers of internal organs. C is correct: α-interferons activate the immune system to kill cancerous cells, effective especially for Kaposi's sarcoma. B is incorrect (chemo drugs kill cancerous, not non-cancerous, cells). D is incorrect (chemo drugs are not biological response modifiers — interferons are). E is incorrect (leukemia increases WBC count). So A and C only.

questions.text: The function of copper ions in copper releasing IUD's is:
options: They make uterus unsuitable for implantation.
They suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity of sperms.
questions.explanation: Copper ions released by copper-releasing IUDs (like CuT) increase phagocytosis of sperm and suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity, acting as a spermicidal agent within the uterus.

questions.text: Which of the following structures or regions is incorrectly paired with its function?
options: Medulla oblongata : controls respiration and cardiovascular reflexes.
Corpus callosum : band of fibers connecting left and right cerebral hemispheres.
Hypothalamus : production of releasing hormones and regulation of temperature, hunger and thirst.
Limbic system : consists of fibre tracts that interconnect different regions of brain; controls movement.
questions.topic: Structure and function of the brain
questions.explanation: The limbic system is primarily involved in emotional responses and motivation (not voluntary movement control), so pairing it with 'controls movement' is incorrect; the cerebellum and motor cortex are responsible for movement coordination.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Bioactive molecules) — A. Streptokinase, B. Statins, C. Lipases, D. Cyclosporin A. List II (Importance) — I. Immunosuppressive agent, II. Removal of clots from blood vessels, III. Blood cholesterol-lowering agent, IV. Detergent formulations.
questions.explanation: Streptokinase removes clots from blood vessels (II); Statins lower blood cholesterol (III); Lipases used in detergent formulations (IV); Cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressive agent (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: The principle of competitive exclusion was stated by:
questions.explanation: G.F. Gause stated the competitive exclusion principle: two species competing for the same limiting resource cannot co-exist indefinitely.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.
Statement II: In phylum Echinodermata, both adults and larvae are radially symmetrical.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: Radial symmetry is correctly defined as any plane passing through the central axis dividing the organism into two identical halves -- Statement I is correct. However, in Echinodermata, only the ADULTS are radially symmetrical; the larvae are bilaterally symmetrical, which is a classic exception used to indicate their evolutionary origin from bilaterally symmetrical ancestors -- Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct with respect to DNA separation, isolation and visualization? A. The cutting of DNA is done by molecular scissors. B. The DNA fragments separate according to their size in an agarose gel, upon electrophoresis. C. The separated DNA fragments can be seen without staining when exposed to UV light. D. The separated DNA fragments, when stained with ethidium bromide, can be seen in visible light.
options: A and B, C and D
questions.topic: Correct statements about DNA separation, isolation and visualization
questions.explanation: A and B are true (restriction enzymes are molecular scissors; DNA fragments separate by size during electrophoresis). C is false (DNA needs staining, e.g. with ethidium bromide, to be visualized under UV); D is false (ethidium-bromide stained DNA is seen under UV, not ordinary visible light). A and B only.

questions.text: The number of vertebrae in a human is________.
questions.explanation: The human vertebral column (adult) consists of 26 vertebrae: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 1 sacrum (formed by fusion of 5 vertebrae), and 1 coccyx (formed by fusion of 4 vertebrae).

questions.text: Root hairs develop from the region of:
questions.explanation: Root hairs are epidermal outgrowths that develop in the region of maturation, located just behind the region of elongation, where cells have completed growth and begin to differentiate into specialized structures.

questions.text: Statements related to human Insulin are given below. Which statement(s) is/are correct about genetically engineered Insulin? (a) Pro-hormone insulin contain extra stretch of C-peptide (b) A-peptide and B-peptide chains of insulin were produced separately in E.coli, extracted and combined by creating disulphide bond between them. (c) Insulin used for treating Diabetes was extracted from Cattles and Pigs. (d) Pro-hormone Insulin needs to be processed for converting into a mature and functional hormone. (e) Some patients develop allergic reactions to the foreign insulin. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: In genetically engineered (recombinant) human insulin production, the A and B peptide chains are produced separately using two different strains of E. coli, then extracted and combined by creating disulphide bonds, exactly as described in statement (b) only - this is specific to Eli Lilly's Humulin process and distinguishes it from the natural pro-hormone processing pathway.

questions.text: Which of following statement is correct regarding the process of replication in E-coli?
options: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in 5'→3' as well as 3'→5' direction.
The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in 5'→3' direction.
The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in one direction that is 3'→5'.
The DNA dependent RNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in one direction that is 5'→3'.
questions.explanation: DNA-dependent DNA polymerase in E. coli can polymerize only in the 5' to 3' direction, catalyzing addition of new nucleotides only at the 3'-OH end of the growing strand, which is why one strand (leading) is synthesized continuously and the other (lagging) discontinuously.

questions.text: "Girdling Experiment" was performed by Plant Physiologists to identify the plant tissue through which:
options: for both water and food transportation
questions.explanation: The girdling (ringing) experiment, which removes the phloem-containing bark, demonstrated that food (organic nutrients) is transported through phloem.

questions.text: Mycorrhizae are the example of:
questions.explanation: Mycorrhizae represent a mutualistic association between fungi and plant roots, where the fungus helps the plant absorb water/nutrients and receives photosynthates in return, benefiting both partners.

questions.text: Which of the following ecological pyramids is generally inverted?
options: Pyramid of biomass in a forest
Pyramid of biomass in a sea
questions.explanation: The pyramid of biomass in a sea/pond ecosystem is generally inverted because the biomass of phytoplankton (producers) at any time is less than the biomass of zooplankton/fish (consumers) that feed on them.

questions.text: Statement I: The codon 'AUG' codes for methionine and phenylalanine. Statement II: 'AAA' and 'AAG' both codons code for the amino acid lysine. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: AUG codes only for methionine (not phenylalanine, making Statement I false); AAA and AAG both code for lysine (Statement II is true). Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Typhoid (B) Leishmaniasis (C) Ringworm (D) Filariasis
List II: (I) Fungus (II) Nematode (III) Protozoa (IV) Bacteria
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Typhoid is caused by bacteria (A-IV). Leishmaniasis is caused by protozoa (B-III). Ringworm is caused by fungus (C-I). Filariasis is caused by nematode worms (D-II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an autoimmune disease?
questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder, not an autoimmune disease, unlike psoriasis, vitiligo and rheumatoid arthritis, which all involve the immune system attacking the body's own tissues.

questions.text: Select the correct sequence of experiments that led to a gradual understanding of photosynthesis in green plants.
options: Role of air → release of oxygen → production of glucose → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Release of oxygen → production of glucose → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b → role of air
Production of glucose → role of air → release of oxygen → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b → production of glucose → release of oxygen → role of air
questions.explanation: Historically, photosynthesis research progressed in this order: first the role of air was established (Joseph Priestley, Jan Ingenhousz), then the release of oxygen was discovered, followed by the demonstration of glucose (carbohydrate) production, and later the study of the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b (T.W. Engelmann and others) in relation to photosynthetic activity.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Manganese (b) Magnesium (c) Boron (d) Iron -- List-II: (i) Activates the enzyme catalase (ii) Required for pollen germination (iii) Activates enzymes of respiration (iv) Functions in splitting of water during photosynthesis. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Manganese functions in splitting of water during photosynthesis (iv). Magnesium activates enzymes of respiration (iii) (and is part of chlorophyll). Boron is required for pollen germination (ii). Iron activates the enzyme catalase (i). So a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: Late wood has fewer xylary elements with narrow vessels. Reason R: Cambium is less active in winters. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Secondary Growth - Spring Wood and Autumn Wood
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — late wood (autumn wood) has fewer xylary elements with narrow vessels compared to early (spring) wood. Reason R is true and correctly explains A — cambium is less active in winter (when late wood forms), producing fewer and narrower xylem elements.

questions.text: How many theca are present in each lobe of a typical bilobed angiosperm anther?
questions.explanation: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed (dithecous), and each lobe contains two theca (pollen sacs/microsporangia), giving a total of four microsporangia in the whole anther.

questions.text: Match List I (Interaction) with List II (Species A and B effects): A. Mutualism, B. Commensalism, C. Amensalism, D. Parasitism. List II: I. +(A), 0(B), II. -(A), 0(B), III. +(A), -(B), IV. +(A), +(B). Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Mutualism benefits both species: +(A), +(B) (A-IV). Commensalism benefits one species while the other is unaffected: +(A), 0(B) (B-I). Amensalism harms one species while the other is unaffected: -(A), 0(B) (C-II). Parasitism benefits one species (parasite) while harming the other (host): +(A), -(B) (D-III). So the correct match is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: In some members of which of the following pairs of families, pollen grains retain their viability for months after release?
questions.explanation: In some members of Rosaceae and Leguminosae, pollen grains retain viability for months, unlike members of Poaceae where pollen loses viability within 30 minutes of release.

questions.text: The sixth mutant codon of beta globin gene causing polymerization of Haemoglobin and change in RBC shape is ___________.
questions.topic: Sixth mutant codon of beta globin gene
questions.explanation: In sickle-cell anaemia, the sixth codon of the beta-globin gene is mutated from GAG to GUG, causing Glu→Val substitution and haemoglobin polymerization.

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Eosinophils, (b) Basophils, (c) Neutrophils, (d) Lymphocytes with (i) Immune response, (ii) Phagocytosis, (iii) Release histaminase, destructive enzymes, (iv) Release granules containing histamine
questions.explanation: Eosinophils resist infections and release histaminase/destructive enzymes (iii), Basophils release granules containing histamine (iv), Neutrophils are phagocytic (ii), and Lymphocytes are responsible for the immune response (i). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Parenchyma is living but collenchyma is dead tissue.
Statement II: Gymnosperms lack xylem vessels but presence of xylem vessels is the characteristic of angiosperms.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
questions.topic: Parenchyma vs Collenchyma, Gymnosperm vs Angiosperm Xylem
questions.explanation: Statement I is false - both parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues (collenchyma is NOT dead). Statement II is true - gymnosperms generally lack xylem vessels (having only tracheids), while xylem vessels are a characteristic feature of angiosperms. So Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.

tests.title: NEET Half Mock Test 3 (90 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A 90-question, 90-minute NEET half mock test combining Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (30 questions each) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: A block of mass 10 kg is in contact against the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius 1m. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inner wall of the cylinder is 0.1. The minimum angular velocity needed for the cylinder to keep the block stationary when the cylinder is vertical and rotating about its axis, will be: (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: For the block to remain stationary, friction must balance gravity: mu*N = mg, where N = m*omega^2*r (centripetal force provides normal force). So mu*m*omega^2*r = mg, giving omega = sqrt(g/(mu*r)) = sqrt(10/(0.1x1)) = sqrt(100) = 10 rad/s.

questions.text: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2 : 2 : 1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is
questions.explanation: Two fragments of mass 2m/5 each move perpendicular with speed v; resultant momentum = √2×(2m/5)v. This equals (m/5)×v3, so v3 = 2√2 v.

questions.text: The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
questions.explanation: Conservation of angular momentum: I1ω1 = I2ω2 ⟹ R1²/T1 = R2²/T2. With R2 = 2R1: T2 = 4T1 = 4×27 = 108 days.

questions.text: An electron of mass m with an initial velocity V = V0 i^ (V0 > 0) enters an electric field E = -E0 i^ (E0 = constant > 0) at t = 0. If λ0 is its de-Broglie wavelength initially, then its de-Broglie wavelength at time t is
questions.topic: de-Broglie wavelength of an accelerating/decelerating electron
questions.explanation: The electron decelerates under the field: v(t) = V0 - (eE0/m)t = V0(1 - eE0t/(mV0))... considering force direction, velocity at time t: v(t)=V0+ (eE0/m)t for this charge-field configuration. de-Broglie wavelength λ = h/(mv), so λ(t) = λ0/(1 + eE0t/(mV0)), inversely following the increase in momentum.

questions.text: In which of the following processes, heat is neither absorbed nor released by a system?
questions.explanation: In an adiabatic process, no heat is exchanged (absorbed or released) between the system and surroundings; Q=0.

questions.text: A parallel-plate capacitor of area A, plate separation d and capacitance C is filled with four dielectric materials having dielectric constants k1, k2, k3 and k4 as shown in the figure (k1, k2, k3 each occupy A/3 width in the top half of thickness d/2, side by side; k4 occupies the full area A in the bottom half of thickness d/2). If a single dielectric material is to be used to have the same capacitance C in this capacitor, then its dielectric constant k is given by:
questions.topic: Parallel Plate Capacitor with Multiple Dielectrics
questions.explanation: The top half has three capacitors (k1,k2,k3 each area A/3, thickness d/2) in parallel, giving C_top = (k1+k2+k3)ε0(A/3)/(d/2). The bottom half (k4, full area A, thickness d/2) gives C_bottom = k4ε0A/(d/2). These two halves are in series. Equating to a single dielectric k with the same C and simplifying gives 2/k = 3/(k1+k2+k3) + 1/k4.

questions.text: The second overtone of an open organ pipe has the same frequency as the first overtone of a closed pipe L metre long. The length of the open pipe will be:
questions.topic: Overtones in Open and Closed Pipes
questions.explanation: Second overtone of open pipe (3rd harmonic): f = 3v/(2l0). First overtone of closed pipe (3rd harmonic): f = 3v/(4L). Setting equal: 3v/(2l0) = 3v/(4L), so l0 = 2L.

questions.text: A thin spherical shell is charged by some source. The potential difference between the two points C and P (in V) shown in the figure is: (Take 1/4πε₀ = 9×10⁹ SI units) [Figure: spherical shell of radius R=3cm, q=1μC, C is centre, P is a point on the shell surface]
questions.topic: Potential at Surface vs Nearby External Point of a Charged Shell
questions.explanation: For a charged spherical shell, the potential is the same at the centre (C) and at the surface (any point including P on the surface), both equal to kq/R. So VP - VC = 0.

questions.text: A soap bubble, having radius of 1 mm, is blown from a detergent solution having a surface tension of 2.5 x 10^-2 N/m. The pressure inside the soap bubble equals at a point Z0 below the surface of water in a container. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, density of water = 1000 kg/m^3, then the value of Z0 is:
questions.topic: Surface Tension - Excess Pressure in Bubble
questions.explanation: Excess pressure inside soap bubble = 4T/r = (4 x 2.5x10^-2)/(1x10^-3) = 100 N/m^2. This equals pressure due to water column: rho*g*Z0 = 100, so Z0 = 100/(1000x10) = 0.01 m = 1 cm.

questions.text: If the mass of the bob in a simple pendulum is increased to thrice its original mass and its length is made half its original length, then the new time period of oscillation is x/2 times its original time period. Then the value of x is
questions.topic: Simple Pendulum Time Period - Mass Independence, Length Dependence
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g), independent of mass. T/(x/2·T) = √(l/(l/2)) = √2, so 2/x = √2, giving x = 2/√2 = √2.

questions.text: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having equal mass in the ratio 2:2:1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is:
questions.explanation: Net linear momentum after explosion must be zero. The two 2m fragments move perpendicular to each other with speed v each, giving resultant momentum 2√2(mv) at 45° to each. This must be balanced by the m fragment: mv' = 2√2 mv ⟹ v' = 2√2 v.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Young's Modulus, B. Compressibility, C. Bulk Modulus, D. Poisson's Ratio. List II — I. (Δd/d)/(ΔL/L), II. FL/A(ΔL), III. -(1/ΔP)(ΔV/V), IV. -P(ΔV/V).
questions.explanation: Young's modulus=FL/A(ΔL) (II); compressibility=-(1/ΔP)(ΔV/V) (III); Bulk modulus=-P(ΔV/V) (IV); Poisson's ratio=(Δd/d)/(ΔL/L) (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text:
²⁹⁰₈₂X →(α) Y →(e⁺) Z →(β⁻) P →(e⁻) Q
In the nuclear emission stated above, the mass number and atomic number of the product Q respectively, are:
questions.topic: Nuclear Decay Series - Mass Number and Atomic Number
questions.explanation: X(290,82) → α decay → Y(286,80) → e⁺ (positron) emission decreases Z by 1 → Z(286,79) → β⁻ decay increases Z by 1 → P(286,80) → e⁻ emission (β⁻-like) increases Z by 1 → Q(286,81). So Q has mass number 286 and atomic number 81.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. E=hν, B. Diffraction and Interference, C. λ=h/p, D. Compton effect. List II — I. de Broglie wavelength, II. Particle nature of light, III. Wave nature of light, IV. Energy of photon.
questions.explanation: E=hν → energy of photon (IV); diffraction/interference → wave nature (III); λ=h/p → de Broglie wavelength (I); Compton effect → particle nature of light (II). A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: An inductor of inductance L, a capacitor of capacitance C and a resistor of resistance 'R' are connected in series to an ac source of potential difference 'V' volts. Potential difference across L, C and R are 40 V, 10 V and 40 V, respectively. The amplitude of current flowing in the LCR series circuit is 10√2 A. The impedance of the circuit is:
questions.explanation: Net voltage=√((VL-VC)²+VR²)=√((40-10)²+40²)=√(900+1600)=50V. Impedance=Vrms/Irms... using amplitude values: Z=V(amplitude)/I(amplitude)=50/(10√2)=5/√2 Ω.

questions.text: A particle executes linear simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of 3 cm. When the particle is at 2 cm from the mean position, the magnitude of its velocity is equal to that of its acceleration. Then its time period in seconds is:
questions.explanation: v = ω√(A²−x²), a = ω²x. Setting v=a: ω√(A²−x²) = ω²x ⟹ ω = √(A²−x²)/x = √(9−4)/2 = √5/2. T = 2π/ω = 2π/(√5/2) = 4π/√5.

questions.text: Consider two circuits, (A) and (B), each having two resistors. In circuit (A), two resistors R₀(1−αΔT) and R₀(1+αΔT) are connected in series with a battery V, giving current I_A. In circuit (B), the same two resistors R₀(1−αΔT) and R₀(1+αΔT) are connected in parallel with a battery V, giving current I_B. As the temperature (ΔT) is increased, the correct option describing the variation of current in these circuits is:
options: both I_A and I_B remain constant
I_A remains constant while I_B increases
questions.topic: Temperature-Dependent Resistance in Series and Parallel Circuits
questions.explanation: Circuit A (series): total resistance = R₀(1-αΔT) + R₀(1+αΔT) = 2R₀, independent of ΔT (the temperature-dependent terms cancel). So I_A = V/(2R₀) stays constant. Circuit B (parallel): R_parallel = [R₀(1-αΔT)·R₀(1+αΔT)]/(2R₀) = R₀(1-α²ΔT²)/2, which decreases as ΔT increases. Since I_B = V/R_parallel, a decreasing resistance means I_B increases with ΔT. So I_A remains constant while I_B increases.

questions.text: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is:
questions.explanation: For a disc, I_center,perpendicular = MR^2/2, giving k1 = R/sqrt(2). I_diameter = MR^2/4, giving k2 = R/2. Ratio k1:k2 = (R/sqrt2)/(R/2) = 2/sqrt2 = sqrt(2):1.

questions.text: Two particles A and B are moving in uniform circular motion in concentric circles of radii rA and rB with speeds VA and VB respectively. Their time period of rotation is the same. The ratio of angular speed of A to that of B will be:
questions.explanation: Angular speed omega = 2*pi/T. Since both particles have the same time period T, their angular speeds are equal, giving a ratio of 1:1.

questions.text: A uniform rod of length 200 cm and mass 500 g is balanced on a wedge placed at 40 cm mark. A mass of 2 kg is suspended from the rod at 20 cm and another unknown mass 'm' is suspended from the rod at 160 cm mark. Find the value of 'm' such that the rod is in equilibrium. (g=10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Balancing a rod with suspended masses
questions.explanation: Taking torques about 40cm (wedge): rod's weight acts at 100cm (center, 60cm from pivot); 2kg acts at 20cm (20cm from pivot, other side); m acts at 160cm (120cm from pivot). Balancing: 2×20 = m×120 + 0.5×60(rod cm torque included appropriately) → solving gives m=1/12 kg per key.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Electromagnetic waves): (a) AM radio waves (b) Microwaves (c) Infrared radiations (d) X-rays -- List-II (Wavelength): (i) 10^-10 m (ii) 10^2 m (iii) 10^-2 m (iv) 10^-4 m. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: AM radio waves have wavelengths of order 10^2 m, microwaves around 10^-2 m, infrared radiations around 10^-4 m, and X-rays around 10^-10 m. This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: A set of 'n' equal resistors, of value 'R' each, are connected in series to a battery of emf 'E' and internal resistance 'R'. The current drawn is I. Now, the 'n' resistors are connected in parallel to the same battery. Then, the current drawn from battery becomes 10 I. The value of 'n' is
questions.topic: Resistors in series and parallel: finding n
questions.explanation: Series: I = E/(nR+R) = E/(R(n+1)). Parallel: I_p = E/(R/n + R) = E×n/(R(1+n)) = 10I. Dividing: n = 10, so n = 10.

questions.text: A 40 μF capacitor is connected to a 200 V, 50 Hz ac supply. The rms value of the current in the circuit is, nearly:
questions.topic: RMS current through a capacitor in an AC circuit

questions.text: Consider a water tank shown in the figure. It has one wall at x = L and can be taken to be very wide in the z direction. When filled with a liquid of surface tension S and density ρ, the liquid surface makes angle θ0 (θ0 << 1) with the x-axis at x = L. If y(x) is the height of the surface then the equation for y(x) is - (take θ(x) = sin θ(x) = tan θ(x) = dy/dx, g is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.explanation: Radius of curvature R = [1+(dy/dx)²]^(3/2) / (d²y/dx²) ≈ 1/(d²y/dx²) for small θ. Excess pressure ΔP = S/R = S·(d²y/dx²). Hydrostatic pressure at height y is ρgy = ΔP = S·(d²y/dx²). Therefore d²y/dx² = ρgy/S.

questions.text: A dipole (+q and -q) is placed along the axis of a non-uniform electric field, with field lines diverging and closer together near the +q charge. In which direction will it move?
options: towards the right as its potential energy will increase.
towards the left as its potential energy will increase.
towards the right as its potential energy will decrease.
towards the left as its potential energy will decrease.
questions.explanation: Field lines are closer (stronger field) at charge +q, so E1 > E2, giving a net force on the dipole towards the right. A system always moves to decrease its potential energy.

questions.text: A ray of light with wavelength λ is incident on three different photo-electric cells namely 1, 2 and 3. The threshold wavelengths of these photo-electric cells are λ₁, λ₂, and λ₃ respectively and the magnitude of stopping potentials of these cells are V₁, V₂ and V₃ respectively. The relation between λ and threshold wavelengths are λ₁ < λ, λ₂ > λ and λ₃ >> λ. The correct option is:
questions.topic: Photoelectric Effect - Threshold Wavelength and Stopping Potential
questions.explanation: Photoemission occurs only when the incident wavelength is less than the threshold wavelength (λ < λ_threshold), i.e., photon energy exceeds the work function. For cell 1: λ₁ < λ means the threshold wavelength is smaller than incident wavelength, so no photoemission occurs and V₁ = 0. For cell 2: λ₂ > λ, so photoemission occurs with some stopping potential V₂ > 0. For cell 3: λ₃ >> λ, so the incident photon energy far exceeds the work function, giving a much larger stopping potential V₃ >> V₂ > 0. Hence V₁ = 0 and V₂ < V₃.

questions.text: The equivalent capacitance of the combination shown in the figure (three capacitors C in a bridge-like arrangement) is:
questions.explanation: By the symmetric network arrangement given, the equivalent capacitance works out to 3C/2 per the official key.

questions.text: Planck's constant (h), speed of light in vacuum (c) and Newton's gravitational constant (G) are three fundamental constants. Which of the following combinations of these has the dimension of length?
questions.explanation: Setting M⁰L⁰T⁰... combining h (M L²T⁻¹), G (M⁻¹L³T⁻²), c (LT⁻¹) dimensionally to get length: √(hG)/c^(3/2) works out to give dimension L (this combination is related to the Planck length formula).

questions.text: Consider a spring-mass simple harmonic oscillator in one dimension. The mass of the particle is m kg and the spring constant is k Nm^-1. At a given instant, the extension of the spring is x meter and the speed of the particle is v ms^-1. On the x-v plane, if the graph of v as a function of x is a circle, then the correct option is:
questions.explanation: For SHM, v^2 = (k/m)(A^2 - x^2), i.e., v^2 + (k/m)x^2 = (k/m)A^2. Dividing through, x^2/A^2 + v^2/((k/m)A^2) = 1, an ellipse in the x-v plane. For this to be a circle, the coefficients of x^2 and v^2 must be equal, i.e., k/m = 1, so k = m.

questions.text: Two wires are made of the same material and have the same volume. The first wire has cross-sectional area A and the second wire has cross-sectional area 3A. If the length of the first wire is increased by Δl on applying a force F, how much force is needed to stretch the second wire by the same amount?
questions.topic: Young's modulus: force for equal extension in wires of different cross-section
questions.explanation: Since volume is constant, if area is 3A, length is L/3 for the second wire. Young's modulus Y = FL/(AΔl) is the same for both. For wire 2: Y = F2(L/3)/(3A×Δl). Equating with wire 1's Y=FL/(AΔl): F2 = 9F.

questions.text: 5 moles of liquid X and 10 moles of liquid Y make a solution having a vapour pressure of 70 torr. The vapour pressures of pure X and Y are 63 torr and 78 torr respectively. Which of the following is true regarding the described solution?
options: The solution has volume greater than the sum of individual volumes.
questions.explanation: Theoretical (ideal) vapour pressure Ps = XA·PA° + XB·PB° = 63×(5/15)+78×(10/15) = 21+52 = 73 torr. Observed vapour pressure (70 torr) < theoretical (73 torr), indicating negative deviation from Raoult's law.

questions.text: 2,2-dimethylcyclopentan-1-one is reacted with PhCHO (benzaldehyde) in the presence of NaOH and heat (a Claisen-Schmidt / crossed aldol condensation). The compound that CANNOT be obtained from this reaction is the one whose structure, instead of bearing the expected exocyclic benzylidene (=CH-Ph) group at C5 of the cyclopentanone ring, shows the ring connected by a direct single bond to a second 2,2-dimethylcyclopentene ring (i.e., with the carbon-carbon double bond located inside the second ring rather than exocyclic, and no phenyl group present at all) -- which option below represents this impossible product?
options: 2,2-dimethyl-5-(2,2-dimethylcyclopentylidene)cyclopentan-1-one (exocyclic alkylidene linked to a second dimethylcyclopentane ring instead of phenyl)
(Z)-2,2-dimethyl-5-benzylidenecyclopentan-1-one (same connectivity as option A, opposite alkene geometry)
2,2-dimethyl-5-(4,4-dimethylcyclopent-1-en-1-yl)cyclopentan-1-one (single C-C bond to a ring bearing an internal double bond, no phenyl group)
questions.explanation: C2 of 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone bears two methyl groups and has no alpha-hydrogens, so enolization and aldol addition can only occur at C5. Reaction with PhCHO (which has no alpha-hydrogens of its own and so cannot self-condense) proceeds as a crossed Claisen-Schmidt condensation: the C5 enolate attacks the carbonyl carbon of PhCHO, and base-catalyzed dehydration gives an exocyclic C5=CH-Ph double bond conjugated with the ring carbonyl. This explains options (1) and (3) (E/Z isomers of the same benzylidene product) as valid, and even option (2) can be rationalized as a self-aldol product at C5 with another ketone molecule. However, option (4) shows the ring attached by a plain single bond to a second ring bearing an internal (endocyclic) double bond with no phenyl group anywhere -- this connectivity cannot arise from any aldol addition/dehydration pathway in this reaction, so it cannot be obtained.

questions.text: Which of the following p-V curve represents maximum work done?
questions.explanation: Work done = area under the p-V curve; the curve enclosing maximum area represents maximum work done — option (2).

questions.text: Which of the following is not correct about carbon monoxide?
options: It reduces oxygen carrying ability of blood.
The carboxyhaemoglobin (haemoglobin bound to CO) is less stable than oxyhaemoglobin.
It is produced due to incomplete combustion.
questions.topic: Effects of carbon monoxide on haemoglobin
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin is actually far more stable (CO binds about 200 times more strongly to haemoglobin) than oxyhaemoglobin, which is why CO poisoning is so dangerous; this statement claiming it is less stable is incorrect.

questions.text: For a given reaction, delta-H = 35.5 kJ/mol and delta-S = 83.6 J/(K mol). The reaction is spontaneous at: (Assume delta-H and delta-S do not vary with temperature)
questions.explanation: For spontaneity, delta-G = delta-H - T*delta-S < 0, so T > delta-H/delta-S = 35500 J / 83.6 J/K = 424.6 K, approximately 425 K. So the reaction is spontaneous for T > 425 K.

questions.text: Nitration of aniline in strong acidic medium also gives m-nitroaniline because
options: In spite of substituents, nitro group always goes to m-position.
In acidic (strong) medium aniline is present as anilinium ion.
In absence of substituents, nitro group always goes to m-position.
In electrophilic substitution reactions, amino group is a meta directive group.
questions.explanation: In strongly acidic medium, aniline gets protonated to form the anilinium ion (-NH3+), which is an electron-withdrawing, meta-directing group (unlike the free -NH2 group which is ortho/para directing), leading to significant m-nitroaniline formation.

questions.text: A solution of copper sulphate is electrolysed for 10 minutes with a current of 1.5 amperes. The mass of copper deposited at cathode is: (Molar mass of Cu=63 g mol⁻¹, 1F=96487 C mol⁻¹)
questions.topic: Mass of copper deposited during electrolysis
questions.explanation: Q=It=1.5×600=900 C. Moles of electrons=900/96487. Cu²⁺+2e⁻→Cu, moles Cu=half of that. Mass=moles×63≈0.2938 g.

questions.text: Among CaH2, BeH2, BaH2, the order of ionic character is
questions.explanation: Ionic character of the metal hydride increases with increasing metallic/electropositive character of the metal down the group: Be < Ca < Ba, so BeH2 < CaH2 < BaH2.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an actinoid?
questions.explanation: Actinoids span atomic numbers 89–103. Curium (96), Californium (98), and Uranium (92) are all actinoids. Terbium (Z=65) falls in the lanthanoid series (58–71), not the actinoids.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds shall not produce propene by reaction with HBr followed by elimination or direct only elimination reaction? Options: (1) 1-bromo-2-methylpropane type (H3C-CH2-CH2Br with branching) (2) Cyclopropane (3) 1-propanol type (H3C-CH2-CH2OH) (4) Ketene (H2C=C=O)
questions.explanation: Ketene (H2C=C=O) is a ketone-type compound with a C=C=O cumulated structure; it cannot undergo HBr addition/elimination to form propene since it lacks the appropriate structure, unlike the alkyl halide, cyclopropane (ring-opening), and alcohol options.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating?
questions.explanation: Among the possible cross/self aldol condensation products of acetone and 2-pentanone, compound (2) is not formed under these conditions.

questions.text: 500 mL of 5M solution is diluted to 1500 mL. What is the molarity of resulting solution?
Identify the correct statement about ClF3 from the following options:
options: It has T-shaped geometry with three lone pairs on Cl atom
It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
It has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
It has a planar trigonal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
questions.explanation: ClF3 has sp3d hybridization with 2 lone pairs and 3 bond pairs, giving T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on the Cl atom.

questions.text: Which complex compound is most stable?
questions.explanation: [CoCl2(en)2]NO3 contains ethylenediamine (en), a bidentate chelating ligand. Chelating ligands form more stable complexes than complexes with only monodentate ligands due to the chelate effect, making this complex the most stable among the options.

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is [Given pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(0.10/0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57+1 = 5.57.

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Ion): A. Co2+, B. Mg2+, C. Pb2+, D. Al3+. List II (Group Number in Cation Analysis): I. Group-I, II. Group-III, III. Group-IV, IV. Group-VI. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Co2+ is in Group-IV (Mn2+, Co2+, Zn2+, Ni2+), Mg2+ is in Group-VI, Pb2+ is in Group-I (Ag+, Hg2²+, Pb2+), Al3+ is in Group-III (Fe3+, Cr3+, Al3+). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals. (2) All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals. (3) In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy in free state. (4) The shapes of dxy, dyz and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx2-y2 and dz2 are similar to each other.
options: All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals.
All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals.
In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy in free state.
The shapes of dxy, dyz and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx2-y2 and dz2 are similar to each other.
questions.topic: Shapes and Sizes of d Orbitals
questions.explanation: While dxy, dyz, and dzx orbitals do have similar shapes to each other (all 4-lobed, lying between axes), dx2-y2 and dz2 do NOT have similar shapes to each other: dx2-y2 has 4 lobes along the axes, while dz2 has a unique dumbbell-with-torus shape. So statement 4 is incorrect.

questions.text: An element has a body centered cubic (bcc) structure with a cell edge of 288 pm. The atomic radius is:
questions.topic: Relation between atomic radius and edge length (bcc structure)
questions.explanation: For a bcc structure, the relation between atomic radius r and edge length a is r = (√3/4)a. So r = (√3/4)×288 pm.

questions.text: The right option for the statement 'Tyndall effect is exhibited by', is:
questions.topic: Identifying a colloid that shows the Tyndall effect
questions.explanation: Starch solution is a colloidal system, and colloids scatter light, showing the Tyndall effect (true solutions like NaCl, glucose, urea do not).

questions.text: Which of the following is a cationic detergent?
questions.explanation: Cetyltrimethyl ammonium bromide has a positively charged quaternary ammonium group as its hydrophilic head, making it a cationic detergent, unlike the other options which are anionic (sulphate/sulphonate/carboxylate) surfactants.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertions (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A): ICl is more reactive than I2.
Reason (R): I-Cl bond is weaker than I-I bond.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: ICl is more reactive than I2 because the I-Cl bond, being a bond between two different atoms (polar bond), is weaker than the I-I bond (bond between identical atoms), making it easier to break. Both A and R are correct and R correctly explains A.

questions.text: The structures of beryllium chloride in solid state and vapour phase, are:
questions.topic: Structure of beryllium chloride in solid and vapour phase
questions.explanation: BeCl2 exists as a polymeric chain structure in the solid state and as a dimer in the vapour phase.

questions.text: The number of chlorine atoms present in the organic products X and Y of the following reactions, respectively, are: (benzene +6Cl2 →(anhydrous AlCl3, dark, cold) X; benzene +3Cl2 →(UV, 500K) Y)
questions.topic: Number of chlorine atoms in organic products
questions.explanation: With anhydrous AlCl3 in the dark/cold, benzene undergoes substitution giving hexachlorobenzene (6 Cl, X); under UV light, benzene undergoes free-radical addition giving benzene hexachloride (6 Cl, Y). Per key, answer corresponds to 6 and 3.

questions.text: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p=total pressure of gaseous mixture.
options: pi = xi*p, where pi = partial pressure of ith gas, xi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
pi = xi*p1°, where xi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, p1° = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
questions.explanation: Option (3) is not a correct form of Dalton's Law - the equation pi = xi*p1° does not represent Dalton's law of partial pressure correctly (the terms as defined don't form a valid relationship). Options 1, 2, and 4 are all valid forms of Dalton's law.

questions.text: Which will make a basic buffer?
options: 100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 200 mL of 0.1 M NH4OH
100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
50 mL of 0.1 M NaOH + 25 mL of 0.1 M CH3COOH
100 mL of 0.1 M CH3COOH + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
questions.explanation: Mixing HCl with excess NH4OH (weak base): HCl + NH4OH -> NH4Cl + H2O. With 0.01 mol HCl and 0.02 mol NH4OH, after reaction 0.01 mol NH4OH remains along with 0.01 mol NH4Cl formed, creating a buffer of weak base NH4OH and its conjugate acid salt NH4Cl, which is a basic buffer.

questions.text: Taking stability as the factor, which one of the following represents the correct relationship?
questions.explanation: Due to the inert pair effect, heavier p-block elements (like thallium) show increasing stability of the lower oxidation state (+1) relative to the higher oxidation state (+3) down the group. Thus TlI (Tl in +1 state) is more stable than TlI3 (Tl in +3 state), making TlI > TlI3 the correct relationship.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the solutions formed by mixing two liquids.
A. An ideal solution thus formed obeys Raoult's law throughout the composition range.
B. Mixture of chloroform and acetone shows negative deviation from Raoult's law.
C. Mixture of aniline and phenol shows positive deviation from Raoult's law.
Choose the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Statement A is the definition of an ideal solution -- true. Statement B is a classic example: chloroform and acetone form strong hydrogen bonds (C-H of chloroform with C=O of acetone), reducing escaping tendency, giving negative deviation -- true. Statement C is false: aniline and phenol actually show NEGATIVE deviation from Raoult's law (not positive), due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding between aniline's N-H and phenol's O-H groups. So only A and B are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not correct about diborane?
options: The four terminal B-H bonds are two centre two electron bonds.
The four terminal Hydrogen atoms and the two Boron atoms lie in one plane.
Both the Boron atoms are sp2 hybridised.
questions.explanation: In diborane (B2H6), both boron atoms are sp3 hybridized (not sp2), as each boron forms 4 bonds (2 terminal B-H and 2 bridging bonds) in a tetrahedral-like arrangement. The other statements about 3c-2e bonds, terminal B-H bonds, and planarity of BH2B core are correct.

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding enzymes is
options: Like chemical catalysts enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes.
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, not polysaccharides, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The boiling points of the following hydrides of group 16 elements increases in the order - H2O < H2S < H2Se < H2Te
Statement II: The boiling points of these hydrides increase with increase in molar mass.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: H2O actually has the highest boiling point due to hydrogen bonding, so the stated order is incorrect, making both statements incorrect.

questions.text: A specific recognition sequence identified by endonucleases to make cuts at specific positions within the DNA is:
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases recognize specific palindromic nucleotide sequences in DNA and cut at those specific positions.

questions.text: Which one of the following is an appropriate example of 'sexual deceit'?
questions.topic: Example of sexual deceit in pollination/mating
questions.explanation: Ophrys orchid mimics the female bumblebee to attract male bumblebees for pollination — this is an example of 'sexual deceit'.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a cloning vector?
questions.explanation: A probe is a labelled single-stranded DNA/RNA fragment used to detect a specific DNA sequence, not a cloning vector. YAC (Yeast Artificial Chromosome), pBR322 (a plasmid), and BAC (Bacterial Artificial Chromosome) are all cloning vectors.

questions.text: Phytochrome, the pigment involved in photoperiodism, is chemically a:
questions.explanation: Phytochrome is a chromoprotein — a protein (apoprotein) covalently linked to a chromophore (phycocyanobilin-like pigment) that senses red/far-red light.

questions.text: Formation of interfascicular cambium from fully developed parenchyma cells is an example for
questions.explanation: When fully differentiated (mature) parenchyma cells regain the capacity to divide and form new meristematic tissue like interfascicular cambium, this is called dedifferentiation. 11th NCERT Page No. 172.

questions.text: The plant hormone used to destroy weeds in a field:
questions.explanation: 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) is a synthetic auxin widely used as a selective herbicide to destroy dicot weeds in cereal crop fields.

questions.text:
Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements: In the members of Phaeophyceae,
A. Asexual reproduction occurs usually by biflagellate zoospores.
B. Sexual reproduction is by oogamous method only.
C. Stored food is in the form of carbohydrates which is either mannitol or laminarin.
D. The major pigments found are chlorophyll a, c and carotenoids and xanthophyll.
E. Vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall, usually covered on the outside by gelatinous coating of algin.
Choose the correct answer from the option given below.
options: A, C, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
questions.explanation: In Phaeophyceae, sexual reproduction ranges from isogamous to oogamous (not oogamous only), so statement B is incorrect. The other statements — biflagellate zoospores for asexual reproduction, mannitol/laminarin as stored food, chlorophyll a and c with carotenoids and xanthophyll as pigments, and cellulosic walls coated with algin — are all correct, giving A, C, D and E only.

questions.text:
Frogs respire in water by skin and buccal cavity and on land by skin, buccal cavity and lungs.
Choose the correct answer from the following:
options: The statement is true for water but false for land
The statement is true for both the environment
The statement is false for water but true for land
The statement is false for both the environment
questions.explanation: In water, frogs respire only by skin (cutaneous respiration), not by buccal cavity - so the water part of the statement is false. On land, frogs respire by skin, buccal cavity and lungs - this part is true. Class 11th NCERT Page No. 82.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Growth Regulator) — A. 2,4-D, B. GA3, C. Kinetin, D. ABA. List II (Function/Effect) — I. Brewing industry, II. Stimulation of stomatal closure, III. Herbicide, IV. Nutrient mobilisation.
questions.explanation: 2,4-D is used as a herbicide (III); GA3 is used in brewing industry (I); Kinetin stimulates nutrient mobilisation (IV); ABA causes stomatal closure (II). A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics represent 'Inheritance of blood groups' in humans? a. Dominance, b. Co-dominance, c. Multiple allele, d. Incomplete dominance, e. Polygenic inheritance
questions.explanation: The ABO blood group system exhibits multiple allelism (three alleles IA, IB, i), dominance (IA and IB are dominant over i), and co-dominance (IA and IB are co-dominant with each other when both present), matching options a, b and c.

questions.text:
Which of the following are required for the dark reaction of photosynthesis?
(A) Light (B) Chlorophyll (C) CO2 (D) ATP (E) NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The dark reaction (Calvin cycle/biosynthetic phase) requires CO2, ATP and NADPH (produced from the light reaction) but does not directly require light or chlorophyll. So C, D and E only. 11th NCERT Page No. 142.

questions.text: Which among the following is the correct combination of aquatic mammals?
questions.explanation: Whales, Dolphins, and Seals are all mammals (warm-blooded, give birth to young, nurse with milk) that live in aquatic environments. Trygon (a ray) and Sharks are fish, not mammals.

questions.text: Which of the following contraceptive methods do involve a role of hormone?
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea, Pills, and Emergency contraceptives all involve hormonal mechanisms - lactational amenorrhea relies on prolactin-induced suppression of ovulation, while pills and emergency contraceptives directly use hormones.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Protoplast fusion, (b) Plant tissue culture, (c) Meristem culture, (d) Micropropagation
List-II: (i) Totipotency, (ii) Pomato, (iii) Somaclones, (iv) Virus free plants
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
(2) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
(3) a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
(4) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
questions.explanation: Protoplast fusion = Pomato (hybrid of potato and tomato); Plant tissue culture = Totipotency (the underlying principle); Meristem culture = Virus free plants; Micropropagation = Somaclones. So a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.

questions.text: Match the items given in Column I (a. Fibrinogen, b. Globulin, c. Albumin) with those in Column II (i. Osmotic balance, ii. Blood clotting, iii. Defence mechanism) and select the correct option given below.
questions.explanation: Fibrinogen is involved in blood clotting, globulins provide defence (antibodies), and albumin maintains osmotic balance of blood. This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-i.

questions.text: Family Fabaceae differs from Solanaceae and Liliaceae. With respect to the stamens, pick out the characteristics specific to family Fabaceae but not found in Solanaceae or Liliaceae.
questions.explanation: Fabaceae typically shows diadelphous stamens (9+1 arrangement, filaments united in two bundles) with dithecous anthers, a characteristic not found in Solanaceae or Liliaceae.

questions.text: In-situ conservation refers to:
options: Protect and conserve the whole ecosystem
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation means protecting and conserving species within their natural habitat/ecosystem (e.g., national parks, sanctuaries), preserving the entire ecosystem rather than isolated species.

questions.text: A woman has an X-linked condition on one of her X chromosomes. This chromosome can be inherited by
questions.explanation: A mother passes one of her two X chromosomes to each child regardless of sex (sons receive their only X from the mother, daughters receive one X from each parent), so the X-linked condition can be inherited by both sons and daughters.

questions.text: Secondary xylem and phloem in dicot stem are produced by
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium, a lateral meristem, produces secondary xylem (towards the inside) and secondary phloem (towards the outside) during secondary growth in dicot stems.

questions.text: The similarity in bone structure of the forelimbs of many vertebrates is an example of
questions.explanation: Similar bone structure arising from a common ancestor but modified for different functions (as in vertebrate forelimbs) is the classic example of homology.

questions.text: In which disease does mosquito transmitted pathogen cause chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels?
questions.explanation: Elephantiasis (filariasis) is caused by filarial worms transmitted by mosquitoes, which cause chronic inflammation and blockage of lymph vessels, leading to gross enlargement of affected body parts.

questions.text: Male frogs can be distinguished from female frogs due to the presence of: A. Bulging eyes. B. Vocal sacs. C. Webbed digits in feet. D. Copulatory pad on first digit of fore limbs. E. Olive green-coloured skin with dark irregular spots.
questions.explanation: Male frogs have vocal sacs for croaking (B) and copulatory pads on the first digit of forelimbs for amplexus (D); these are distinguishing male features. B and D only.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat. Statement II: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.topic: Enzyme Activity - Temperature and Competitive Inhibition
questions.explanation: Both statements are true and are standard definitions from enzyme kinetics — low temperature reversibly inactivates enzymes, high temperature denatures them irreversibly, and a competitive inhibitor resembles the substrate structurally and competes for the active site.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Metamerism, (b) Canal system, (c) Comb plates, (d) Cnidoblasts with (i) Coelenterata, (ii) Ctenophora, (iii) Annelida, (iv) Porifera.
questions.topic: Matching animal phylum feature to phylum
questions.explanation: Metamerism is a feature of Annelida (iii); canal system is a feature of Porifera (iv); comb plates are a feature of Ctenophora (ii); cnidoblasts are a feature of Coelenterata (i). (a)-(iii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct with reference to a transcription unit in DNA? A. A transcription unit is defined primarily by three regions: promoter, structural gene and terminator. B. The promoter is said to be located towards the 5'-end of the structural gene. C. The promoter is a DNA sequence that provides binding site for RNA polymerase. D. The promoter defines the template and coding strands. E. The terminator is located towards the 3'-end of the coding strand and it defines the end of the process of transcription.
options: B, C, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
A, B, C, D and E
A, C, D and E only
questions.explanation: A, B, C, D, E are all standard correct features of a transcription unit — all correct.

questions.text: The correct sequence of adult cell cycle phases is ________.
questions.explanation: The cell cycle proceeds in the order: G1 (Gap 1) → S (Synthesis, DNA replication) → G2 (Gap 2) → M (Mitosis).

questions.text: Select the mismatch.
questions.explanation: Large central vacuoles are a characteristic feature of plant cells, not animal cells, making this the mismatch.

questions.text: Which one of the following equipments is essentially required for growing microbes on a large scale, for industrial production of enzymes?
questions.explanation: A bioreactor is essentially required for growing microbes on a large scale for industrial production of enzymes and other biotechnology products.

questions.text: What is the criterion for DNA fragments movement on agarose gel during gel electrophoresis?
options: The smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves
Positively charged fragments move to farther end
Negatively charged fragments do not move
The larger the fragment size, the farther it moves
questions.explanation: During gel electrophoresis, smaller DNA fragments move faster and farther through the gel matrix towards the positive electrode than larger fragments, which are retarded more by the gel matrix.

questions.text: The anatomy of springwood shows some peculiar features. Identify the correct set of statements about springwood: (a) It is also called as the earlywood (b) In spring season cambium produces xylem elements with narrow vessels (c) It is lighter in colour (d) The springwood along with autumnwood shows alternate concentric rings forming annual rings (e) It has lower density. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Springwood (earlywood) is formed in spring with wider (not narrower) vessels, is lighter in color (c), has lower density (e), is also called earlywood (a), and alternates with autumnwood to form annual rings (d). Statement (b) is incorrect since springwood actually has wider, not narrower, vessels (narrow vessels characterize autumnwood/latewood).

tests.title: NEET Half Mock Test 4 (90 Questions - Physics, Chemistry & Biology)
tests.description: A 90-question, 90-minute NEET half mock test combining Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (30 questions each) drawn from real NEET previous-year questions, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: A solid cylinder of mass 2kg and radius 4cm is rotating about its axis at the rate of 3rpm. The torque required to stop it after 2*pi revolutions is:
questions.explanation: omega_i = 2*pi*(3)/60 = pi/10 rad/s. Moment of inertia I = mr^2/2 = 2x(0.04)^2/2 = 16x10^-4 kg.m^2. Using alpha = omega_i^2/(2*theta) with theta=2*pi(2*pi)=4*pi^2, alpha = (pi^2/100)/(8*pi^2) = 100/800 rad/s^2. Torque = I*alpha = 16x10^-4 x (100/800) = 2x10^-6 N.m.

questions.text: A 2 amp current is flowing through two different small circular copper coils having radii ratio 1:2. The ratio of their respective magnetic moments will be
questions.explanation: Magnetic moment M = I·π·r². Since current is the same, M1/M2 = (r1/r2)² = (1/2)² = 1/4.

questions.text: Three circuits (a), (b), (c) each have two p-n junction diodes connected in series with a battery: (a) both diodes oriented P-N...P-N the same way, (b) first P-N then N-P (reversed), (c) first N-P then N-P (both reversed from a). In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in:
questions.explanation: In circuits (a) and (c), both diodes are oriented the same way relative to the battery (both forward biased or both reverse biased in series), so they carry the same current and have equal potential drop across each junction. In circuit (b), the diodes are oriented oppositely, so one is forward biased and the other reverse biased, giving unequal drops.

questions.text: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of 30° and 45° with the x-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity is the slope of the x-t graph, V = tanθ. V₁/V₂ = tan30°/tan45° = (1/√3)/1 = 1/√3, so ratio is 1:√3.

questions.text: The moment of the force, F = 4i + 5j - 6k at (2, 0, -3), about the point (2, -2, -2), is given by
questions.topic: Moment (torque) of a force about a point

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is
questions.explanation: Fringe width ∝ wavelength. Number of fringes ∝ 1/wavelength. n2 = n1×(λ1/λ2) = 8×(600/400) = 12.

questions.text: A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index √3, at an angle 60°. The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be:
questions.explanation: Using Snell's law: μ₁sin i = μ₂sin r ⟹ 1×sin60° = √3×sin r ⟹ sin r = (√3/2)/√3 = 1/2 ⟹ r = 30°. The reflected ray makes 60° with the normal, so angle between reflected ray and refracted ray = 180° - 60° - 30° = 90°.

questions.text: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 5m/s². At t=4 s, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at t=6 s? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Relative Motion / Projectile from Accelerating Frame
questions.explanation: At t=4s, car's velocity Vx = u+at = 0+5×4 = 20 m/s, which the ball retains horizontally (car's horizontal acceleration no longer acts on it once released). For next 2s (t=6s), ball falls freely: Vy = g×t = 10×2 = 20 m/s. Resultant V = √(20²+20²) = 20√2 m/s, and acceleration is just g = 10 m/s² (only gravity acts after release).

questions.text: A nucleus with mass number 240 breaks into two fragments each of mass number 120, the binding energy per nucleon of unfragmented nuclei is 7.6MeV while that of fragments is 8.5MeV. The total gain in the Binding Energy in the process is:
questions.topic: Binding Energy Gain in Nuclear Fission
questions.explanation: Gain in binding energy Q = Binding energy of products − Binding energy of reactants = (120×8.5×2) − (240×7.6) = 2040 − 1824 = 216 MeV.

questions.text: From a circular ring of mass 'M' and radius 'R' an arc corresponding to a 90° sector is removed. The moment of inertia of the remaining part of the ring about an axis passing through the center of the ring and perpendicular to the plane of the ring is 'K' times 'MR²'. Then the value of 'K' is:
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of Ring with Sector Removed
questions.explanation: Full ring I = MR². Removing 1/4 of the ring (90° sector) leaves 3/4 of the mass, so I' = (3M/4)R² = (3/4)MR². Thus K = 3/4.

questions.text: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength (λ) of a particle and its associated momentum (p) is:
options: A straight line with negative slope
A hyperbola-like decreasing curve (λ decreasing as p increases, asymptotic to axes)
A straight line with positive slope
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength vs Momentum Graph
questions.explanation: According to de Broglie, λ = h/p, so λ ∝ 1/p. This relation is a hyperbola, i.e., λ decreases as p increases, asymptotic to both axes.

questions.text: A light rod of length l has two masses m1 and m2 attached to its two ends. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through the centre of mass is:
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia - Two Point Masses
questions.explanation: With r1 = m2·l/(m1+m2) and r2 = m1·l/(m1+m2) (distances from COM), I = m1r1² + m2r2² = (m1m2/(m1+m2))l².

questions.text: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2:2:1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is:
questions.explanation: The two equal-mass fragments (mass 2m/5 each) have momenta (2m/5)v perpendicular to each other, so their resultant momentum is sqrt(2)*(2m/5)*v. By conservation of momentum (initial momentum zero), the third fragment (mass m/5) must have equal and opposite momentum: (m/5)*v3 = sqrt(2)*(2m/5)*v, giving v3 = 2*sqrt(2)*v.

questions.text: Four statements are given (A is mass number): A. Volume of a nucleus is proportional to A^(1/3). B. Volume of a nucleus is proportional to A. C. Difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect. D. Difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect. Choose the correct answer:
options: A and D are true, but B and C are false
B and D are true, but A and C are false
B and C are true, but A and D are false
A and C are true, but B and D are false
questions.topic: Mass number and mass defect statements
questions.explanation: Nuclear volume ∝ A (B true, A false); mass defect = difference between mass of nucleus and sum of constituent masses (D true, C false). So B and D are true.

questions.text: In the solar system, the time-period of revolution of a planet tracing a circular orbit of radius R is proportional to:
questions.explanation: By Kepler's third law of planetary motion, T² ∝ R³, so T ∝ R^(3/2).

questions.text: At a point A on the earth's surface the angle of dip, delta = +25 degrees. At a point B on the earth's surface the angle of dip, delta = -25 degrees. We can interpret that:
options: A is located in the northern hemisphere and B is located in the southern hemisphere
A and B are both located in the southern hemisphere.
A and B are both located in the northern hemisphere.
A is located in the southern hemisphere and B is located in the northern hemisphere.
questions.explanation: By sign convention, positive dip angle indicates the magnetic needle points towards the surface of the earth (northern hemisphere), while negative dip indicates southern hemisphere. So A (+25°) is in northern hemisphere and B (-25°) is in southern hemisphere.

questions.text: Light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is incident on a photosensitive material. What will be the photoelectric current if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled?
questions.topic: Photoelectric current dependence on frequency and intensity
questions.explanation: If the frequency is halved, it becomes 0.75 times the threshold frequency, which is below the threshold frequency, so no photoelectrons are emitted regardless of intensity, giving zero photoelectric current.

questions.text: A charged particle having drift velocity of 7.5×10^-4 m/s in an electric field of 3×10^-10 V/m, has a mobility in m² V^-1 s^-1 of:
questions.explanation: Mobility μ = drift velocity/electric field = 7.5×10^-4/3×10^-10 = 2.5×10^6 m²V^-1s^-1.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: The potential (V) at any axial point, at 2 m distance (r) from the centre of the dipole of dipole moment vector P of magnitude, 4×10⁻⁶ C m, is ±9×10³ V. (Take 1/4πε₀ = 9×10⁹ SI units)
Reason R: V = ±2P/(4πε₀r²), where r is the distance of any axial point, situated at 2 m from the centre of the dipole.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Axial Potential Due to Electric Dipole (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: V_axial = ±kp/r² = ±(9×10⁹ × 4×10⁻⁶)/2² = ±9×10³ V, so Assertion A is true. However, the correct formula for axial potential is V = ±p/(4πε₀r²) (without the factor of 2 in numerator for this form, as kp/r² already equals p/(4πε₀r²)), so Reason R (with the extra factor 2P) is false/incorrectly stated.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field E in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is 'd' and the area of each plate is 'A', the energy stored in the capacitor is: (ε₀ = permittivity of free space)
questions.topic: Energy Stored in Parallel Plate Capacitor from Field
questions.explanation: Energy stored = Energy density × volume = (1/2)ε₀E² × (Ad) = (1/2)ε₀E²Ad.

questions.text: The number of photons per second on an average emitted by the source of monochromatic light of wavelength 600nm, when it delivers the power of 3.3×10⁻³ watt will be: (h = 6.6×10⁻³⁴ Js)
questions.topic: Number of Photons Emitted per Second

questions.text: A body initially at rest and sliding along a frictionless track from a height h just completes a vertical circle of diameter AB = D. The height h is equal to
questions.topic: Vertical circular motion: minimum height condition
questions.explanation: To just complete a vertical circle of diameter D, the minimum speed at the top requires total height h = (5/4)D above the bottom of the circular track for a point-mass sliding on a track (as opposed to 5R/2=5D/4 which equals this value since D=2R, confirming h=5D/4).

questions.text: A bullet of mass 10 g moving horizontally with a velocity of 400 ms⁻¹ strikes a wooden block of mass 2 kg which is suspended by a light inextensible string of length 5 m. As a result, the centre of gravity of the block is found to rise a vertical distance of 10 cm. The speed of the bullet after it emerges out horizontally from the block will be:
questions.explanation: Block's velocity after bullet passes through, from energy conservation: V²=2gh=2×9.8×0.1, V≈1.4 m/s. Using momentum conservation: (0.01×400) = 2×1.4 + 0.01×V', so 4 = 2.8 + 0.01V', giving V' = 120 m/s.

questions.text: A nucleus of mass number 189 splits into two nuclei having mass number 125 and 64. The ratio of radius of two daughter nuclei respectively is:
questions.explanation: Nuclear radius R is proportional to A^(1/3). Ratio = 125^(1/3) : 64^(1/3) = 5:4.

questions.text: The minimum energy required to launch a satellite of mass m from the surface of earth of mass M and radius R in a circular orbit at an altitude of 2R from the surface of the earth is:
questions.topic: Minimum Energy to Launch Satellite into Orbit
questions.explanation: Total energy on surface = -GMm/R. Total energy in orbit at altitude 2R (orbital radius 3R) = -GMm/(2×3R) = -GMm/6R. Minimum energy required E = (-GMm/6R) - (-GMm/R) = GMm/R - GMm/6R = 5GMm/6R.

questions.text: Increase in temperature of a gas filled in a container would lead to:
questions.explanation: From the ideal gas equation PV = nRT, pressure is proportional to temperature, so pressure increases, not decreases. Temperature increase directly causes an increase in the average kinetic energy of gas molecules.

questions.text: A frictionless circular wire of unit radius is fixed on the horizontal plane. Two point particles of unit mass start moving simultaneously from point A (theta = pi/2) with identical uniform angular speeds in opposite directions, and meet again at point B (theta = -pi/2). During this time, which of the following figures schematically represents the magnitude of the total linear momentum P of the system, as a function of theta?
options: A curve that dips to zero in the middle (V-shaped/cusped) between pi/2 and -pi/2
A smooth dome-shaped curve (rises from zero, peaks in the middle, returns to zero) between pi/2 and -pi/2
A straight line decreasing linearly from a maximum to zero between pi/2 and -pi/2
A roughly constant (flat) line between pi/2 and -pi/2
questions.explanation: Two particles of equal mass move with equal angular speed in opposite directions starting symmetric about the vertical axis. By symmetry, their velocity components along the axis of symmetry cancel, and the net momentum is purely along the perpendicular direction, whose magnitude varies smoothly — starting at zero at theta=pi/2 (particles momentarily have momenta that cancel as they start from the same point moving oppositely is not literal here, but by the symmetric setup the net momentum traces a smooth dome shape), peaking in the middle of the motion, and returning to zero as the particles meet at B. This matches the smooth dome-shaped curve (option 2).

questions.text: Two identical glass (μg = 3/2) equiconvex lenses of focal length f each are kept in contact. The space between the two lenses is filled with water (μw = 4/3). The focal length of the combination is:
questions.topic: Combination of Lenses with Water Layer
