MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn2+ + 4H2O, E° (Mn2+/MnO4-) = -1.510V
1/2 O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O, E° (O2/H2O) = +1.223V
Will the permanganate ion, MnO4- liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode, MnO4-/Mn2+ reduction) - E°(anode, O2/H2O oxidation) = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287 V. Since E°cell is positive, the reaction is spontaneous, so MnO4- will liberate O2 from water in the presence of acid.

questions.text: An organic compound contains 78% (by wt.) carbon and remaining percentage of hydrogen. The right option for the empirical formula of this compound is: [Atomic wt. of C is 12, H is 1]
Among the species given below, the spin-only magnetic moment is highest for: (Given: Atomic number of Ti = 22, Mn = 25, Fe = 26 and Co = 27)
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]3−: Fe3+ is d5; CN⁻ is strong field, low spin, giving t2g5eg0 with 1 unpaired electron, μ=√3≈1.73 BM. [Co(NH3)6]3+: Co3+ is d6, low spin (common for Co3+), t2g6eg0, 0 unpaired electrons, μ=0. [Ti(H2O)6]3+: Ti3+ is d1, 1 unpaired electron, μ=√3≈1.73 BM. [Mn(CN)6]3−: Mn3+ is d4; even with strong-field CN⁻, low-spin d4 gives t2g4eg0 with 2 unpaired electrons, μ=√(2×4)=√8≈2.83 BM, which is the highest among these four.

questions.text: The product formed from the following reaction sequence is: Benzonitrile (Ph-CN) treated with (i) LiAlH4, H2O (ii) NaNO2 + HCl (iii) H2O
questions.topic: Reactions of Nitriles and Diazonium Salts
questions.explanation: Benzonitrile is reduced by LiAlH4/H2O to benzylamine (Ph-CH2-NH2). This reacts with NaNO2+HCl to form an unstable primary aliphatic diazonium salt (Ph-CH2-N2+Cl-), which on treatment with H2O undergoes hydrolysis to give benzyl alcohol (Ph-CH2-OH) releasing N2.

questions.text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction (y vs x at constant temperature T). The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t½ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t½ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t½)
questions.explanation: For zero order, rate is constant with concentration (horizontal line: y=rate, x=concentration); for first order, t½ is constant with concentration (horizontal line: y=t½, x=concentration).

questions.text: For a reaction A→B, enthalpy of reaction is -4.2 kJ mol^-1 and enthalpy of activation is 9.6 kJ mol^-1. The correct potential energy profile for the reaction is shown in option (exothermic reaction with product B at lower PE than reactant A, with activation energy hump of 9.6 kJ/mol above A):
options: Profile showing A below B (endothermic-looking, B higher than A, large hump)
Profile showing A and B at the same level with hump between them
Profile showing A higher than B (exothermic), with activation energy hump from A to peak
Profile showing A and B at nearly the same height with a small symmetric hump
questions.topic: Potential Energy Profile and Activation Energy
questions.explanation: ΔH=(Ea)f-(Ea)b. -4.2=9.6-(Ea)b, so (Ea)b=13.8. Since ΔH is negative (exothermic), product B has lower potential energy than reactant A, with forward activation energy 9.6 kJ/mol.

questions.text: What will be the number of sulphate (H2SO4) molecules in 100 mL of 0.02M H2SO4 solution?
questions.explanation: Moles of H2SO4 = 0.02 M × 0.1 L = 0.002 mol. Number of molecules = 0.002 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.2044 × 10²¹ = 12.044 × 10²⁰.

questions.text: The lanthanide ion having four unpaired electrons is: (Given: Atomic numbers of Ce = 58, Nd = 60, Tb = 65 and Ho = 67)
questions.topic: Electronic Configuration of Lanthanide Ions - Unpaired Electrons
questions.explanation: Ce3+: [Xe]4f1, 1 unpaired electron. Tb3+: [Xe]4f8, which has 6 unpaired electrons (7 orbitals, 8 electrons: 7 fill singly, 1 pairs up, leaving 6 unpaired). Ho3+: [Xe]4f10, which has 4 unpaired electrons (7 orbitals, 10 electrons: 7 fill singly, then 3 more pair up in 3 of those orbitals, leaving 7-3=4 unpaired). Nd3+: [Xe]4f3, 3 unpaired electrons. So Ho3+ has 4 unpaired electrons.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements related to lanthanons is incorrect?
options: Ce (+4) solutions are widely used as oxidizing agent in volumetric analysis.
The basicity decreases as the ionic radius decreases from Pr to Lu.
All the lanthanons are much more reactive than aluminium.
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids are not all much more reactive than aluminium; this is a false generalization, making statement (4) incorrect.

questions.text: Mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol acts as:
questions.explanation: A mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol is used as an antiseptic (commonly known as Dettol), applied on wounds, cuts, and skin to prevent microbial infection.

questions.text: The intermediate compound X in the following chemical reaction is: Toluene + CrO2Cl2, CS2 → X, then H3O+ → Benzaldehyde
questions.explanation: This is the Etard reaction. The intermediate X formed is Ph-CH(OCrOHCl2)2, a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis with H3O+ gives benzaldehyde.

questions.text: RMgX + CO2 --dry ether--> Y --H3O+--> RCOOH. What is Y in the above reaction?
questions.explanation: Grignard reagent reacts with CO2 to form a magnesium carboxylate salt, RCOO⁻Mg⁺X, which on hydrolysis gives RCOOH.

questions.text: Conjugate base for Bronsted acids H2O and HF are:
questions.explanation: A conjugate base is formed when a Bronsted acid loses a proton (H+). H2O loses H+ to form OH-, and HF loses H+ to form F-.

questions.text: Calculate the mass percent of different elements present in carbon dioxide. Mass percent of carbon is
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO2 = 44 g/mol, mass of carbon = 12 g. Mass % of C = (12/44) × 100 = 27.27%.

questions.text: For the reaction A(g)⇌2B(g), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K. [Given: R = 0.0831 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹] KP for the reaction at 1000 K is
Which of the following contains the greatest number of atoms?
questions.explanation: Moles: He(4g)=1 mol, Na(46g)=46/23=2 mol, Ca(0.40g)=0.40/40=0.01 mol, He(12g)=12/4=3 mol. Since all are monatomic, the number of atoms is proportional to moles — 12 g He (3 mol) gives the greatest number of atoms.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is: a hexane chain with Cl on C2, a methyl branch on C3, OH on C4 (counting to give lowest locants), and Br on C6 (terminal carbon): CH3-CHCl-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-Br
questions.explanation: Numbering from the end nearer to the OH group (principal characteristic group, suffix -ol gets lowest locant) and naming substituents alphabetically (bromo, chloro, methyl): 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol.

questions.text: In which of the following molecules, all atoms are coplanar? (Options: (1) Bicyclohexyl (2) Biphenyl (3) Cyclohexane (4) Tetramethylethylene dicarbonitrile, (CH3)2C=C(CN)2)
questions.explanation: Biphenyl, due to resonance/conjugation between the two phenyl rings connected by a single bond, tends to be planar (or near-planar), with all atoms in the same plane, unlike cyclohexane (chair conformation) or bicyclohexyl (sp3 carbons, non-planar).

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Quantum Numbers: n, l) — A. n=2,l=1, B. n=4,l=0, C. n=5,l=3, D. n=3,l=2. List II (Orbital) — I. 3d, II. 2p, III. 4s, IV. 5f.
questions.explanation: n=2,l=1 → 2p (II); n=4,l=0 → 4s (III); n=5,l=3 → 5f (IV); n=3,l=2 → 3d (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: It is because of inability of ns2 electrons of the valence shell to participate in bonding that:
options: Sn2+ is oxidising while Pb4+ is reducing
Sn2+ and Pb2+ are both oxidising and reducing
Sn4+ is reducing while Pb4+ is oxidising
Sn2+ is reducing while Pb4+ is oxidising
questions.explanation: Due to the inert pair effect, the ns2 electrons resist participating in bonding, making the lower oxidation state more stable down the group. This makes Sn2+ a reducing agent (it readily gets oxidised to the more stable Sn4+) while Pb4+ is a strong oxidising agent (it readily gets reduced to the more stable Pb2+).

questions.text: The concentration of glucose, (C6H12O6) in blood, is 0.9 g L⁻1. What will be the molarity of glucose in blood?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of glucose = 180 g/mol. Molarity = 0.9/180 = 0.005 mol L⁻1.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of an element with atomic number 119 is:
questions.explanation: Using IUPAC systematic element naming rules (un=1, un=1, enn=9), atomic number 119 is named ununennium (1-1-9 -> un-un-enn-ium).

questions.text: In the structure of ClF3, the number of lone pairs of electrons on central atom 'Cl' is
questions.explanation: ClF3 has a T-shaped structure derived from trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry, with 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on the central Cl atom.

questions.text: Identify the correct orders against the property mentioned: A. H2O > NH3 > CHCl3 – dipole moment. B. XeF4 > XeO3 > XeF2 – number of lone pairs on central atom. C. O–H > C–H > N–O – bond length. D. N2 > O2 > H2 – bond enthalpy. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Dipole Moment, Lone Pairs, Bond Length, Bond Enthalpy Comparisons
questions.explanation: A is correct: dipole moments H2O(1.85D) > NH3(1.47D) > CHCl3(1.04D). B is incorrect: lone pairs are XeF4(2) = XeF2(3)... actual order differs (XeF2 has 3 lone pairs, XeF4 has 2, XeO3 has 1), so stated order is wrong. C is incorrect bond length order stated. D is correct: bond enthalpy N2(941) > O2(498) > H2(436) kJ/mol (triple bond strongest). So A, D only.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following
options: Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
questions.explanation: In KO2 (potassium superoxide), K has oxidation state +1, not +4, making statement (2) incorrect.

questions.text: C(s)+2H2(g)→CH4(g); ΔH=−74.8 kJ mol⁻¹. Which of the following diagrams gives an accurate representation of the above reaction? [R → reactants; P → products]
options: R at lower energy than P, with 74.8 gap marked between the peak and the trough above P (R below P, hump between)
R at lower energy, P at higher energy, 74.8 marked near P at top
R at a level, P below R by 74.8, hump in between (R higher starting point, correct exothermic drop)
R at lower energy than P with hump, 74.8 near P
questions.explanation: Since the reaction is exothermic (ΔH negative), products (P) must be at lower energy than reactants (R), with an activation energy hump in between, and the 74.8 kJ/mol gap representing the energy difference between R and P (reactants higher, products 74.8 kJ/mol lower).

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs -- List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Uses of Alkali Metals and Compounds
questions.explanation: Li is used in electrochemical cells (ii) (lithium batteries). Na is used as a coolant in fast breeder reactors (iii). KOH is used as an absorbent for carbon dioxide (i). Cs is used in photoelectric cells (iv). So a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.

questions.text: The complex which has facial and meridional isomers is: (Given: py = pyridine and en = H2N–CH2–CH2–NH2)
questions.explanation: Facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism occurs specifically in octahedral complexes of the type MA3B3, with three identical ligands of each of two kinds. [Cr(py)3Cl3] is of this type (three pyridine and three chloride ligands) and shows fac/mer isomerism. [Cr(H2O)6]3+ has only one type of ligand (no isomerism of this kind). [Co(NH3)4(H2O)2]3+ is an MA4B2 type, which shows cis/trans isomerism, not fac/mer. [Ni(en)2(H2O)2]2+ involves a bidentate ligand and doesn't fit the MA3B3 pattern either.

questions.text: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives:
questions.explanation: Sucrose, upon hydrolysis, breaks down into one molecule of α-D-glucose and one molecule of β-D-fructose.

questions.text: Following solutions were prepared by mixing different volumes of NaOH and HCl of different concentrations: a. 60 mL (M/10) HCl + 40 mL (M/10) NaOH; b. 55 mL (M/10) HCl + 45 mL (M/10) NaOH; c. 75 mL (M/5) HCl + 25 mL (M/5) NaOH; d. 100 mL (M/10) HCl + 100 mL (M/10) NaOH. pH of which one of them will be equal to 1?
questions.topic: pH of mixtures of strong acid and base
questions.explanation: For solution c: excess HCl = (75×M/5 - 25×M/5)/100 = (15M-5M)/100 = 0.1M = M/10 effectively giving [H+] = 0.1 M, so pH = 1. The other mixtures give different excess acid/base concentrations not corresponding to pH 1.

questions.text: Which of the statements given below is not true about formation of annual rings in trees?
options: Activity of cambium depends upon variation in climate.
Annual rings are not prominent in trees of temperate region.
Annual ring is combination of spring wood and autumn wood produced in a year.
Differential activity of cambium causes light and dark bands of tissue - early and late wood respectively.
questions.explanation: Annual rings ARE prominent in trees of temperate regions due to pronounced seasonal climate variation, not absent/not prominent as stated. This makes statement 2 false/not true.

questions.text: In which of the following forms is iron absorbed by plants?
questions.topic: Forms of iron absorbed by plants
questions.explanation: Plants can absorb iron in both the ferric (Fe3+) and ferrous (Fe2+) forms from the soil, though ferrous iron is generally more readily absorbed.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Electrostatic precipitator is most widely used in thermal power plant. Statement II: Electrostatic precipitator in thermal power plant removes ionising radiations. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — electrostatic precipitators are widely used in thermal power plants to control particulate emissions. Statement II is incorrect — electrostatic precipitators remove particulate matter (ash, dust particles) from flue gases, not ionising radiations.

questions.text: Purines found both in DNA and RNA are:
questions.explanation: Adenine and Guanine are purines found in both DNA and RNA. Cytosine is a pyrimidine found in both, while thymine is found only in DNA and uracil only in RNA.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: A flower is defined as modified shoot wherein the shoot apical meristem changes to floral meristem. Reason R: Internode of the shoot gets condensed to produce different floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — a flower is indeed a modified shoot where the shoot apical meristem transforms into a floral meristem. Reason R correctly explains this — the internodes of the shoot condense, producing floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves.

questions.text: Which of the following immune responses is responsible for rejection of kidney graft?
questions.explanation: Cell-mediated immune response (involving T-lymphocytes) is primarily responsible for the rejection of transplanted organs like a kidney graft.

questions.text: The unique mammalian characteristics are:
options: pinna, monocondylic skull and mammary glands
hairs, tympanic membrane and mammary glands
questions.explanation: Hairs, external ear (pinna), and mammary glands are unique characteristics found only in mammals among vertebrates, as per the NCERT textbook classification.

questions.text: Homozygous purelines in cattle can be obtained by:
options: mating of unrelated individuals of same breed.
mating of individuals of different breed.
mating of individuals of different species.
mating of related individuals of same breed.
questions.explanation: Inbreeding, the mating of closely related individuals within the same breed, increases homozygosity, allowing desirable recessive traits to be exposed and homozygous purelines to be developed.

questions.text: The morphological nature of the edible part of coconut is:
questions.explanation: The edible white fleshy part of coconut is the endosperm, which stores food reserves and is consumed as coconut meat.

questions.text: The difference between spermiogenesis and spermiation is
options: In spermiogenesis spermatids are formed, while in spermiation spermatozoa are formed.
In spermiogenesis spermatozoa are formed, while in spermiation spermatozoa are released from sertoli cells into the cavity of seminiferous tubules.
In spermiogenesis spermatozoa from sertoli cells are released into the cavity of seminiferous tubules, while in spermiation spermatozoa are formed.
In spermiogenesis spermatozoa are formed, while in spermiation spermatids are formed.
questions.explanation: Spermiogenesis is the process by which spermatids transform into mature spermatozoa, and spermiation is the subsequent release of these mature spermatozoa from the Sertoli cells into the lumen of the seminiferous tubules.

questions.text: The partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli of the lungs is:
options: Less than that of carbon dioxide
Equal to that in the blood
More than that in the blood
Less than that in the blood
questions.explanation: The partial pressure of O2 in alveolar air (~104 mm Hg) is higher than in deoxygenated blood (~40 mm Hg) arriving at the lungs, which drives diffusion of oxygen from alveoli into blood.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
questions.explanation: The α-cells of the islets of Langerhans secrete glucagon, not insulin. Insulin is secreted by the β-cells. Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis (breakdown of glycogen to glucose) in the liver. So the incorrect statement is that α-cells secrete insulin.

questions.text: In bryophytes, the gemmae help in which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction in liverworts (bryophytes) takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialised structures called gemmae (singular: gemma). Class 11th NCERT Page No 29.

questions.text: Casparian strips occur in
questions.explanation: Casparian strips are bands of suberin and lignin found in the radial and transverse walls of the endodermal cells of roots, regulating the movement of water and minerals into the vascular tissue.

questions.text: A lake which is rich in organic waste may result in:
options: Mortality of fish due to lack of oxygen
Increased population of aquatic organisms due to minerals
Drying of the lake due to algal bloom
Increased population of fish due to lots of nutrients
questions.explanation: Organic waste enrichment causes eutrophication — excessive microbial decomposition depletes dissolved oxygen, leading to fish mortality.

questions.text: The highest DDT concentration in aquatic food chain shall occur in:
questions.explanation: Due to biomagnification, DDT concentration increases at each successive trophic level; the seagull, being a top predator/highest trophic level among the options, accumulates the highest concentration.

questions.text: The enzyme enterokinase helps in conversion of:
questions.explanation: Enterokinase, secreted by the intestinal mucosa, activates the inactive trypsinogen (secreted by the pancreas) into its active form, trypsin.

questions.text: The ciliated epithelial cells are required to move particles or mucus in a specific direction. In humans, these cells are mainly present in:
questions.explanation: Ciliated epithelial cells that move particles or mucus in a specific direction are mainly present in the bronchioles (respiratory tract, to move mucus) and fallopian tubes (to move the ovum towards the uterus).

questions.text: Secondary metabolites such as nicotine, strychnine and caffeine are produced by plants for their:
questions.topic: Secondary metabolites and their defensive role
questions.explanation: Secondary metabolites like nicotine, strychnine and caffeine often serve a defensive role for plants, deterring herbivores and pathogens due to their toxic or bitter properties.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Adaptive radiation, (b) Convergent evolution, (c) Divergent evolution, (d) Evolution by anthropogenic action with (i) Selection of resistant varieties due to excessive use of herbicides and pesticides, (ii) Bones of forelimbs in Man and Whale, (iii) Wings of Butterfly and Bird, (iv) Darwin Finches.
questions.explanation: Adaptive radiation is exemplified by Darwin's finches (iv); Convergent evolution by wings of butterfly and bird (iii); Divergent evolution by bones of forelimbs in man and whale (ii); Evolution by anthropogenic action by selection of resistant varieties (i). (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Down's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X-chromosomes.
Statement II: Turner's syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of the chromosomes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.topic: Chromosomal Disorders - Down's and Turner's Syndrome
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome is actually caused by the presence of an extra copy (trisomy) of chromosome 21, not the absence of an X-chromosome -- Statement I is incorrect (this description actually fits Turner's syndrome, which is monosomy of X). Turner's syndrome is actually caused by the ABSENCE of one X-chromosome (45, X0), not the presence of an additional chromosome (which would describe conditions like Klinefelter's or Down's syndrome) -- Statement II is incorrect. Both statements describe the conditions in reverse of reality.

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Placenta, (b) Zona pellucida, (c) Bulbo-urethral glands, (d) Leydig cells with (i) Androgens, (ii) Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG), (iii) Layer of the ovum, (iv) Lubrication of the Penis
questions.explanation: Placenta secretes human Chorionic Gonadotropin, hCG (ii), Zona pellucida is a layer surrounding the ovum (iii), Bulbo-urethral glands secrete fluid for lubrication of the penis (iv), and Leydig cells secrete androgens (i). This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct? A. An excessive loss of body fluid from the body switches off osmoreceptors. B. ADH facilitates water reabsorption to prevent diuresis. C. ANF causes vasodilation. D. ADH causes increase in blood pressure. E. ADH is responsible for decrease in GFR. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement B is correct — ADH facilitates water reabsorption, preventing diuresis. Statement C is correct — ANF causes vasodilation, lowering blood pressure. Statement D is correct — ADH increases blood pressure (via vasoconstriction and water retention). Statement A is incorrect — excessive loss of body fluid activates (not switches off) osmoreceptors. Statement E is incorrect — ADH decreases urine output primarily by increasing water reabsorption, not specifically by decreasing GFR as the primary mechanism described here.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of arrangement of vertebrate column from the head to toe?
options: Sacrum, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, cervical vertebra
Cervical vertebra, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum
Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, lumbar vertebra, sacrum
Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum, lumbar vertebra
questions.explanation: From head to toe, the vertebral column is arranged as: Cervical vertebrae (neck) → Thoracic vertebrae (chest) → Lumbar vertebrae (lower back) → Sacrum (pelvic region) → Coccyx.

questions.text: Goblet cells of alimentary canal are modified from:
questions.explanation: Goblet cells, which secrete mucus in the alimentary canal, are modified (specialised) columnar epithelial cells.

questions.text: Among 'The Evil Quartet', which one is considered the most important cause driving extinction of species?
questions.topic: Causes of Biodiversity Loss - The Evil Quartet
questions.explanation: Habitat loss and fragmentation is considered the most important of the 'Evil Quartet' causes driving species extinction, as per the NCERT textbook.

questions.text: Match the items given in Column I (a. Eutrophication, b. Sanitary landfill, c. Snow blindness, d. Jhum cultivation) with those in Column II (i. UV-B radiation, ii. Deforestation, iii. Nutrient enrichment, iv. Waste disposal) and select the correct option given below.
questions.explanation: Eutrophication is caused by nutrient enrichment (iii), sanitary landfill is a method of waste disposal (iv), snow blindness is caused by UV-B radiation (i), and Jhum cultivation (shifting cultivation) is associated with deforestation (ii). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text: What is the function of tassels in the corn cob?
questions.topic: Corn Cob Structure - Function of Tassels
questions.explanation: Tassels in corn bear the staminate (male) flowers at the top of the plant, and the silky styles/stigmas of the female flowers hang to trap pollen grains released from the tassels during wind pollination. (Per the NCERT reference, tassels here trap pollen grains.)

questions.text: Cortex is the region found between:
questions.explanation: Cortex is the region found between the epidermis and the stele (vascular cylinder)

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Respiratory Volume) — A. ERV (Expiratory Reserve Volume), B. RV (Residual Volume), C. IRV (Inspiratory Reserve Volume), D. TV (Tidal Volume). List II (Capacity in mL) — I. 2500-3000 mL, II. 500 mL, III. 1000-1100 mL, IV. 1100-1200 mL.
questions.explanation: ERV is about 1000-1100 mL (III); RV is about 1100-1200 mL (IV); IRV is about 2500-3000 mL (I); TV is about 500 mL (II). A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: With regard to insulin choose correct options, (a) C-peptide is not present in mature insulin. (b) The insulin produced by rDNA technology has C-peptide. (c) The pro-insulin has C-peptide. (d) A-peptide and B-peptide of insulin are interconnected by disulphide bridges. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Mature insulin lacks the C-peptide (it is removed during processing). Pro-insulin contains the C-peptide. The A and B peptide chains of mature insulin are held together by disulphide bridges. Insulin produced by rDNA technology (recombinant) does not have the C-peptide since only A and B chains are synthesized separately and joined.

questions.text: Name the blood cells, whose reduction in number can cause clotting disorder, leading to excessive loss of blood from the body.
questions.explanation: Thrombocytes (platelets) are essential for blood clotting; their reduced number (thrombocytopenia) causes clotting disorders and excessive bleeding.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Chromosomes are fully condensed at the end of prophase I.
Statement II: Meiosis I resembles mitosis.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.topic: Meiosis I - Prophase I and Comparison with Mitosis
questions.explanation: By the end of prophase I (diakinesis stage), chromosomes are fully condensed -- Statement I is correct. Meiosis I is a reductional division involving pairing of homologous chromosomes, crossing over, and separation of homologs, which is fundamentally different from mitosis (where sister chromatids separate and chromosome number is maintained) -- so Statement II is false.

questions.text: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorous and calcium present in the soil at any given time, is referred as:
questions.explanation: The 'standing state' refers to the amount of nutrients present in the soil at any given time, as part of nutrient cycling studies in ecosystems.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. CCK, B. GIP, C. ANF, D. ADH. List II: I. Kidney, II. Heart, III. Gastric gland, IV. Pancreas. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: CCK (Cholecystokinin) acts on the pancreas (A-IV). GIP (Gastric Inhibitory Peptide) inhibits gastric gland secretion (B-III). ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor) is released from the heart (C-II). ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) acts on the kidney (D-I). So the correct match is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Types of Stamens): (A) Monoadelphous (B) Diadelphous (C) Polydelphous (D) Epiphyllous
List II (Example): (I) Citrus (II) Pea (III) Lily (IV) China-rose
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Epiphyllous (attached to perianth) stamens are seen in Lily, giving D-III. Monoadelphous (filaments united into one bundle) is seen in China-rose, giving A-IV. Diadelphous (two bundles) is seen in Pea, giving B-II. Polydelphous (many bundles) is seen in Citrus, giving C-I. So A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III is correct.

questions.text: Vital capacity of lung is ____________.
questions.topic: Lung Volumes and Capacities - Vital Capacity
questions.explanation: Vital capacity is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a maximal inspiration, and is calculated as IRV (Inspiratory Reserve Volume) + ERV (Expiratory Reserve Volume) + TV (Tidal Volume).

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
A. Annelids are true coelomates
B. Poriferans are pseudocoelomates
C. Aschelminthes are acoelomates
D. Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomates
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Annelids are true coelomates (A is correct). Poriferans lack a body cavity altogether (not pseudocoelomate), Aschelminthes/Nematodes are pseudocoelomates (not acoelomates), and Platyhelminthes are acoelomates (not pseudocoelomates). So only statement A is correct.

questions.text: In frog, the Renal portal system is a special venous connection that acts to link:
options: Kidney and lower part of body
questions.explanation: The Renal Portal System in frogs is a special venous connection linking the kidney and the lower part of the body. The renal portal vein carries deoxygenated blood (containing excretory substances) from the lower body to the kidney. 11th NCERT, Frog. Page - 82.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement with regard to the G1 phase (Gap 1) of interphase.
options: DNA synthesis or replication takes place.
Reorganisation of all cell components takes place.
Cell is metabolically active, grows but does not replicate its DNA.
questions.explanation: During G1 phase, the cell is metabolically highly active and grows in size, synthesising proteins and RNA needed for DNA replication, but DNA replication itself (which occurs in S phase) has not yet begun.

questions.text: Serum differs from blood in:
questions.explanation: Serum is blood plasma without clotting factors (like fibrinogen), which are consumed during the clotting process. Antibodies, globulins and albumins remain present in serum.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Drug) — A. Nicotine, B. Morphine, C. Heroin, D. Cocaine. List II (Effect) — I. Causes sense of euphoria and increased energy, II. Stimulates adrenal gland to release catecholamines into blood circulation, III. Effective sedative and painkiller, IV. A depressant; slows down body function.
questions.explanation: Nicotine stimulates adrenal gland release of catecholamines (II); Morphine is an effective sedative/painkiller (III); Heroin is a depressant slowing body function (IV); Cocaine causes euphoria and increased energy (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: The inactive form of Bt toxin is converted to the active form in the insect gut_______
questions.explanation: Bt toxin is produced by Bacillus thuringiensis as an inactive protoxin. In the insect gut, the alkaline pH environment solubilizes and helps convert the inactive protoxin into its active, toxic form, which then binds to the gut epithelium and causes cell lysis.

questions.text: The flightless bird with forelimbs modified as paddle-like structures suited for swimming is known as:
questions.explanation: Aptenodytes (penguin genus) has flightless, paddle-like flippers suited for swimming.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Pleurobrachia (B) Radula (C) Stomochord (D) Air bladder
List-II: (I) Mollusca (II) Ctenophora (III) Osteichthyes (IV) Hemichordata
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Pleurobrachia belongs to phylum Ctenophora (A-II). Radula is a feeding structure found in Mollusca (B-I). Stomochord is found in Hemichordata (C-IV). Air bladder is found in Osteichthyes/bony fish (D-III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III is correct.

questions.text: Insertion of a foreign DNA at BamHI site in a cloning vector pBR322 results in the loss of antibiotic resistance towards:
questions.topic: Effect of inserting foreign DNA at BamHI site in pBR322
questions.explanation: The BamHI site in pBR322 lies within the tetracycline resistance gene, so insertion there inactivates tetracycline resistance.

questions.text: If a geneticist uses the blind approach for sequencing the whole genome of an organism, followed by assignment of function to different segments, the methodology adopted by him is called as:
questions.explanation: Sequence annotation is the process of identifying genes and assigning functions to different segments of a genome after it has been sequenced using a 'blind' (shotgun-type) sequencing approach, as was done in the Human Genome Project.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about RuBisCO is true?
options: It is active only in the dark
It has higher affinity for oxygen than carbon dioxide.
it is an enzyme involved in the photolysis of water
It catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP.
questions.explanation: RuBisCO (Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase) is active both in light and dark, has a higher affinity for CO2 than O2 when both are at equal concentration, and catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP (ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate) in the Calvin cycle, not the photolysis of water.

questions.text: Which one of the following is related to Ex-situ conservation of threatened animals and plants?
questions.explanation: Ex-situ conservation involves protecting species outside their natural habitat, such as in wildlife safari parks, zoos, botanical gardens, and seed banks. Biodiversity hotspots, the Amazon rainforest, and the Himalayan region are all examples of in-situ conservation (protecting species within their natural habitat).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Vas deferens receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct. Statement II: The cavity of the cervix is called cervical canal which along with vagina forms birth canal. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.topic: Male and Female Reproductive Tract Anatomy
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — the vas deferens receives a duct from the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct, which opens into the urethra. Statement II is correct — the cervical canal, along with the vagina, forms the birth canal.

questions.text: Three types of muscles are given as a, b and c. Identify the correct matching pair along with their location in human body. [Figure shows (a) striated muscle fibres, (b) spindle-shaped smooth muscle fibres, (c) branched cardiac muscle fibres]
options: (a) Skeletal - Biceps, (b) Involuntary - Intestine, (c) Smooth - Heart
(a) Involuntary - Nose tip, (b) Skeletal - Bone, (c) Cardiac - Heart
(a) Smooth - Toes, (b) Skeletal - Legs, (c) Cardiac - Heart
(a) Skeletal - Triceps, (b) Smooth - Stomach, (c) Cardiac - Heart
questions.explanation: Figure (a) shows striated skeletal muscle fibres found in muscles like the triceps, (b) shows smooth, spindle-shaped muscle fibres found in organs like the stomach, and (c) shows branched cardiac muscle fibres found in the heart. So the correct matching is (a) Skeletal-Triceps, (b) Smooth-Stomach, (c) Cardiac-Heart.

questions.text: When gene targetting involving gene amplification is attempted in an individual's tissue to treat disease, it is known as:
questions.topic: Term for gene amplification therapy in tissues
questions.explanation: Gene therapy involves correcting a genetic defect by introducing a normal gene or modifying gene expression in target tissues.

questions.text: Which of the following structure is not a part of the male reproductive system?
questions.explanation: Infundibulum is the funnel-shaped opening of the fallopian tube (oviduct) near the ovary, and is part of the FEMALE reproductive system. Epididymis, vasa efferentia, and rete testis are all parts of the male reproductive system (the duct system associated with the testis).

questions.text: The first phase of translation is:
questions.explanation: The first step of translation is aminoacylation (charging) of tRNA, where the appropriate amino acid is attached to its specific tRNA using ATP, before the tRNA-amino acid complex participates in polypeptide synthesis at the ribosome.

questions.text: The factor that leads to Founder effect in a population is:
questions.explanation: The Founder effect occurs when a small group (founders) colonizes a new habitat, carrying only a fraction of the genetic variation of the original population — this is a form of genetic drift.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Biological Molecules): (a) Glycogen (b) Globulin (c) Steroids (d) Thrombin. List-II (Biological functions): (i) Hormone (ii) Biocatalyst (iii) Antibody (iv) Storage product. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Glycogen is a storage polysaccharide, Globulin is an antibody (immunoglobulin), Steroids like cholesterol derivatives act as hormones, and Thrombin is an enzyme (biocatalyst) involved in blood clotting. This matches (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

questions.text: Which of the following refer to correct example(s) of organisms which have evolved due to changes in environment brought about by anthropogenic action? (a) Darwin's Finches of Galapagos islands. (b) Herbicide resistant weeds. (c) Drug resistant eukaryotes. (d) Man-created breeds of domesticated animals like dogs.
questions.explanation: Herbicide-resistant weeds, drug-resistant eukaryotes (pathogens) and man-created dog breeds have all evolved due to human (anthropogenic) activity; Darwin's finches evolved through natural environmental pressures, not direct anthropogenic action.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not true regarding the release of energy during ATP synthesis through chemiosmosis? It involves:
options: Movement of protons across the membrane to the stroma
Reduction of NADP to NADPH2 on the stroma side of the membrane
questions.explanation: Chemiosmosis involves the breakdown of the proton gradient (not an 'electron gradient', which is not a standard term in this context) as protons flow through ATP synthase, driving ATP synthesis. The other statements about proton movement to stroma and NADPH formation on the stroma side are correct aspects of the process.

questions.text: In India, the organisation responsible for assessing the safety of introducing genetically modified organisms for public use is
options: Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
questions.topic: Regulatory bodies for genetically modified organisms in India
questions.explanation: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC), functioning under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, is the apex regulatory body responsible for assessing the safety of releasing genetically modified organisms and products for public use in India.

questions.text: The "Ti plasmid" of Agrobacterium tumefaciens stands for:
questions.explanation: The Ti (Tumor inducing) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens naturally causes crown gall disease in plants and has been modified by scientists into a vector for delivering genes of interest into plant cells.

questions.text: The process of separation and purification of expressed protein before marketing is called:
questions.explanation: Downstream processing refers to the series of steps (separation, purification, formulation, and preservation) applied to a biotechnologically produced product before it is marketed.

questions.text: If '8' Drosophila in laboratory population of '80' died during a week, the death rate in the population is ___________ individuals per Drosophila per week.
questions.explanation: Death rate = number of deaths/original population = 8/80 = 0.1 individuals per Drosophila per week. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 83)

questions.text: In tissue culture experiments, leaf mesophyll cells are put in a culture medium to form callus. This phenomenon may be called as:
questions.explanation: Dedifferentiation is the phenomenon where living differentiated cells (like leaf mesophyll cells) regain the capacity to divide under appropriate conditions, forming a mass of undifferentiated cells (callus).

questions.text: Bt cotton variety that was developed by the introduction of toxin gene of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is resistant to:
questions.explanation: Bt cotton expresses the Cry toxin protein from Bacillus thuringiensis, which is toxic specifically to certain insect pests (like the cotton bollworm), making the plant resistant to these insect pests.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are true for spermatogenesis but do not hold true for Oogenesis?
(a) It results in the formation of haploid gametes
(b) Differentiation of gamete occurs after the completion of meiosis
(c) Meiosis occurs continuously in a mitotically dividing stem cell population
(d) It is controlled by the Luteinising hormone (LH) and Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) secreted by the anterior pituitary
(e) It is initiated at puberty
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: (a) is true for both. (d) is true for both (both are controlled by LH and FSH). (b) differentiation (spermiogenesis) occurs only after meiosis completes in spermatogenesis, whereas in oogenesis the secondary oocyte is released before meiosis II completes. (c) In spermatogenesis, meiosis occurs continuously in a mitotically dividing stem cell (spermatogonia) population throughout reproductive life, unlike oogenesis where oogonial divisions are completed in fetal life. (e) Spermatogenesis is initiated at puberty, while oogenesis begins in the fetal stage. So (b), (c), (e) are true only for spermatogenesis.

questions.text: Cardiac activities of the heart are regulated by : A. Nodal tissue, B. A special neural centre in the medulla oblongata, C. Adrenal medullary hormones, D. Adrenal cortical hormones. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: The heart is myogenic, auto-regulated by the nodal tissue (A). A special neural centre in the medulla oblongata moderates cardiac function via the autonomic nervous system (B). Adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline) also increase cardiac output (C). Adrenal cortical hormones are not involved in direct cardiac regulation (D is false). So A, B and C only.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (a) Metacentric chromosome (b) Acrocentric chromosome (c) Submetacentric (d) Telocentric chromosome
List-II: (i) Centromere situated close to the end forming one extremely short and one very long arms (ii) Centromere at the terminal end (iii) Centromere in the middle forming two equal arms of chromosomes (iv) Centromere slightly away from the middle forming one shorter arm and one longer arm
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Metacentric: centromere in middle, equal arms(iii). Acrocentric: centromere near end, one short one long arm(i). Submetacentric: centromere slightly away from middle(iv). Telocentric: centromere at terminal end(ii). So (a)-(iii),(b)-(i),(c)-(iv),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: Bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate animals are exemplified by:
questions.topic: Bilateral symmetry and acoelomate body plan
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate (lack a true body cavity), unlike Ctenophora (radially symmetrical), Aschelminthes (pseudocoelomate) and Annelida (coelomate).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Chromosomes become gradually visible under light microscope during leptotene stage.
Statement-II: The beginning of diplotene stage is recognized by dissolution of synaptonemal complex.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
questions.topic: Meiotic Prophase I - Leptotene and Diplotene Stages
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct - during leptotene, chromosomes gradually condense and become visible under a light microscope; the beginning of diplotene is marked by dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and separation of homologous chromosomes except at chiasmata. 11th NCERT Page No. 126.

questions.text: Which of the following functions is not performed by secretions from salivary glands?
questions.explanation: Saliva contains salivary amylase, which digests complex carbohydrates (starch) into simpler sugars, but it does not digest disaccharides. Saliva also lubricates the oral cavity and controls bacterial population via lysozyme.

questions.text: Which of the following options correctly represents the lung conditions in asthma and emphysema, respectively?
options: Inflammation of bronchioles; Decreased respiratory surface
Decreased respiratory surface; Inflammation of bronchioles
Increased respiratory surface; Inflammation of bronchioles
Increased number of bronchioles; Increased respiratory surface
questions.explanation: Asthma involves inflammation of the bronchioles causing difficulty in breathing, while emphysema involves damage to the alveolar walls, leading to a decreased respiratory surface area for gas exchange.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct for r-selected species?
options: Small number of progeny with large size
Large number of progeny with small size
Large number of progeny with large size
Small number of progeny with small size
questions.explanation: r-selected species produce a large number of progeny, each of small size, with high reproductive rate and little parental care.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true for spermatogenesis but do not hold true for Oogenesis? (a) It results in the formation of haploid gametes (b) Differentiation of gamete occurs after the completion of meiosis (c) Meiosis occurs continuously in a mitotically dividing stem cell population (d) It is controlled by the Luteinising hormone (LH) and Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) secreted by the anterior pituitary (e) It is initiated at puberty. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: (b) In spermatogenesis, differentiation (spermiogenesis) occurs after meiosis completion, unlike oogenesis where differentiation can occur during meiotic arrest. (c) Meiosis in spermatogenesis occurs continuously in a mitotically active stem cell population (spermatogonia), unlike oogenesis which has a fixed number of oocytes. (e) Spermatogenesis begins at puberty, while oogenesis begins prenatally. (a) and (d) are true for both processes.

questions.text: Xylem translocates:
options: Water mineral salts and some organic nitrogen only
Water mineral salts some organic nitrogen and hormones
questions.explanation: Xylem translocates water, mineral salts, some organic nitrogen compounds, and hormones (like cytokinins synthesized in roots) upward to the shoot system.

questions.text: Identify the asexual reproductive structure associated with Penicillium:
questions.explanation: Penicillium reproduces asexually by producing exogenous, non-motile spores called conidia on specialized structures called conidiophores.

questions.text: In cockroach, excretion is brought about by: A. Phallic gland, B. Urecose gland, C. Nephrocytes, D. Fat body, E. Collaterial glands. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: In cockroaches, excretion is carried out by uricose glands (B), nephrocytes (C), and the fat body (D), which store and process nitrogenous waste (uric acid). Phallic gland and collaterial glands are reproductive accessory glands, not excretory structures.

questions.text: Non-membrane bound cell organelles found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are ___________.
questions.topic: Non-membrane bound cell organelles in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles present in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

questions.text: The flippers of the Penguins and Dolphins are the example of the:
questions.explanation: Convergent evolution occurs when unrelated species independently evolve similar structures due to adapting to similar environments/functions. Penguin flippers (modified wings) and Dolphin flippers (modified limbs) are structurally different in origin but functionally similar, making this an example of convergent evolution.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In ecosystem, there is unidirectional flow of energy of sun from producers to consumers.
Statement II: Ecosystems are exempted from 2nd law of thermodynamics.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.topic: Unidirectional Energy Flow and Second Law of Thermodynamics
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct - energy flows unidirectionally from the sun to producers to consumers in an ecosystem. Statement II is incorrect - ecosystems are NOT exempt from the 2nd law of thermodynamics; they require a constant supply of energy to synthesize the molecules needed to maintain structure and function.

questions.text: DNA fragments are:
options: Either positively or negatively charged depending on their size
questions.explanation: DNA fragments carry an overall negative charge due to the phosphate groups in their backbone, which is why they migrate towards the positive electrode (anode) during gel electrophoresis.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List – I: A. Head, B. Middle piece, C. Acrosome, D. Tail. List-II: I. Enzymes, II. Sperm motility, III. Energy, IV. Genetic material. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Sperm head contains the nucleus with genetic material (IV). Middle piece has mitochondria that produce energy (III). Acrosome is filled with hydrolytic enzymes (I). Tail provides motility (II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The atrio-ventricular node (AVN) generates an action potential to stimulate atrial contraction
The tricuspid and the bicuspid valves open due to the pressure exerted by the simultaneous contraction of the atria
Blood moves freely from atrium to the ventricle during joint diastole.
Increased ventricular pressure causes closing of the semilunar valves.
questions.explanation: During joint diastole, both atria and ventricles are relaxed and the AV valves are open, allowing blood to move freely from the atria into the ventricles, which is the correct statement among the options.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a step in Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer Technology (MOET)?
options: Fertilized eggs are transferred to surrogate mothers at 8-32 cell stage
Cow is administered hormone having LH like activity for super ovulation
Cow yields about 6-8 eggs at a time
Cow is fertilized by artificial insemination
questions.explanation: In MOET, the cow is administered FSH-like hormone (not LH-like) for superovulation to yield 6-8 eggs, which are then fertilized by artificial insemination and transferred to surrogate mothers at the 8-32 cell stage.

questions.text: In the taxonomic categories which hierarchical arrangement in ascending order is correct in case of animals?
options: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: The correct taxonomic hierarchy in descending order (which the question calls ascending, as officially keyed) is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Cristae, (b) Thylakoids, (c) Centromere, (d) Cisternae
List-II: (i) Primary constriction in chromosome, (ii) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus, (iii) Infoldings in mitochondria, (iv) Flattened membranous sacs in stroma of plastids
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
(2) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
(3) a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
(4) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
questions.explanation: Cristae = infoldings in mitochondria; Thylakoids = flattened membranous sacs in stroma of plastids; Centromere = primary constriction in chromosome; Cisternae = disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus. So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Mendel's law of Independent assortment does not hold good for the genes that are located closely on the same chromosome. Reason (R): Closely located genes assort independently. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct: genes located closely together (linked genes) tend to be inherited together, violating independent assortment. Reason (R) is incorrect: closely located (linked) genes do NOT assort independently - that is precisely why linkage violates Mendel's law.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) The Evil Quartet (B) Ex situ conservation (C) Lantana camara (D) Dodo
List-II: (I) Cryopreservation (II) Alien species invasion (III) Causes of biodiversity losses (IV) Extinction
Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.topic: Causes of Biodiversity Loss - The Evil Quartet (Match List)
questions.explanation: The Evil Quartet refers to the causes of biodiversity losses (III). Ex situ conservation includes methods like cryopreservation (I). Lantana camara is an example of alien species invasion (II). Dodo is an example of extinction (IV). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Decomposition is a process in which the detritus is degraded into simpler substances by microbes. Statement II: Decomposition is faster if the detritus is rich in lignin and chitin. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: decomposition is the microbial breakdown of detritus into simpler substances. Statement II is incorrect: decomposition is actually slower (not faster) when detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, as these are resistant to microbial breakdown.

questions.text: Spraying of which of the following phytohormone on juvenile conifers helps in hastening the maturity period, that leads to early seed production?
questions.explanation: Spraying gibberellic acid (GA3) on juvenile conifers hastens maturity and leads to early seed production, a well-documented commercial application of gibberellins.

questions.text: Stomata in grass leaf are
questions.explanation: In grasses (monocot leaves), the guard cells of stomata are dumb-bell shaped, unlike the kidney-shaped guard cells found in most dicot leaves.

tests.title: NEET Full Mock Test 3 (180 Questions - Physics 45 + Chemistry 45 + Biology 90)
tests.description: A full-length 180-question, 180-minute NEET mock test in the real exam pattern - Physics 45, Chemistry 45, Biology 90 - built from real NEET previous-year questions, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Three sound waves of equal amplitudes have frequencies (n-1), n, (n+1). They superimpose to give beats. The number of beats produced per second will be:
questions.explanation: The number of beats per second equals the maximum difference between any two frequencies present. Here the max difference is between (n-1) and (n+1), which is 2.

questions.text: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of V volt. If the de Broglie wavelength of the electron is 1.227×10^-2 nm, the potential difference is:
questions.explanation: Using λ = 1.227/√V nm (standard formula with V in volts, λ in nm): 1.227×10^-2 = 1.227/√V, so √V = 100, V = 10^4 V.

questions.text: Light with an average flux of 20 W/cm² falls on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence having surface area 20 cm². The energy received by the surface during time span of 1 minute is:
questions.explanation: Power = flux × area = 20×20 = 400 W. Energy = Power × time = 400×60 = 24000 J = 24×10^3 J.

questions.text: In a series LCR circuit, the inductance L is 10 mH, capacitance C is 1 μF and resistance R is 100Ω. The frequency at which resonance occurs is:

A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 20 microfarad is being charged by a voltage source whose potential is changing at the rate of 3 V/s. The conduction current through the connecting wires, and the displacement current through the plates of the capacitor, would be, respectively:
questions.explanation: q = CV, so dq/dt = C(dV/dt) = 20 microF x 3 V/s = 60 microA. This is the conduction current ic. By Maxwell's theory, the displacement current id always equals the conduction current in such a circuit, so id = ic = 60 microA.

questions.text: Five capacitors of capacitances C1=C2=C3=C4=10 μF and C5=2.5 μF are connected as shown, along with a battery of 50 V. The equivalent capacitance and the charges on each capacitor respectively are:
options: 4 μF, 250 μC on C1 to C4 and 125 μC on C5
5 μF, 125 μC on C1 to C4 and 25 μC on C5
questions.explanation: By the symmetric bridge network, equivalent capacitance = 5 μF with 125 μC charge on all capacitors.

questions.text: The velocity of a small ball of mass M and density d, when dropped in a container filled with glycerine becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is d/2, then the viscous force acting on the ball will be:
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, viscous force = weight - upthrust = Mg - (d/2 density fluid)(V)g = Mg - (1/2)Mg = Mg/2.

questions.text: A thin prism having refracting angle 10° is made of glass of refractive index 1.42. This prism is combined with another thin prism of glass of refractive index 1.7. This combination produces dispersion without deviation. The refracting angle of second prism should be:
questions.explanation: For dispersion without deviation, net deviation = 0: A₁(μ₁−1) = A₂(μ₂−1). So A₂ = A₁(μ₁−1)/(μ₂−1) = 10×(0.42)/(0.7) = 6°.

questions.text: In the given figure, a = 15 m/s² represents the total acceleration of a particle moving in the clockwise direction in a circle of radius R = 2.5 m at a given instant of time, with the acceleration vector making a 30° angle with the radius. The speed of the particle is:
questions.topic: Circular Motion - Tangential and Radial Acceleration
questions.explanation: Total acceleration a_r² + a_t² = 225 (15²). Since tan30° = a_t/a_r, a_r = a_t√3, giving (4/3)a_r² = 225, so a_r² = 168.75, a_r = 7.5√3/... solving: a_r = (15/2)√3 ≈ 12.99 m/s². Using v²/R = a_r: v² = 15×2.5×√3/2 ≈ 32.48, v ≈ 5.7 m/s.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Electromagnetic waves): (a) AM radio waves (b) Microwaves (c) Infrared radiations (d) X-rays
List-II (Wavelength): (i) 10⁻¹⁰ m (ii) 10² m (iii) 10⁻² m (iv) 10⁻⁴ m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: AM radio waves ~10² m (ii), Microwaves ~10⁻² m (iii), Infrared ~10⁻⁴ m (iv), X-rays ~10⁻¹⁰ m (i). So (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

questions.text: Two bodies of mass 4 kg and 6 kg are tied to the ends of a massless string. The string passes over a pulley which is frictionless. The acceleration of the system in terms of acceleration due to gravity (g) is:
questions.topic: Atwood machine: acceleration of connected masses
questions.explanation: For an Atwood machine, a = (m2-m1)g/(m1+m2) = (6-4)g/(6+4) = 2g/10 = g/5.

questions.text: A long solenoid of 50 cm length having 100 turns carries a current of 2.5 A. The magnetic field at the centre of the solenoid is: (μ0=4π×10^-7 T m A^-1)
questions.topic: Magnetic field at the centre of a solenoid

questions.text: A radioactive nucleus (A,Z)X undergoes spontaneous decay in the sequence X→(Z-1)B→(Z-3)C→(Z-2)D, where Z is the atomic number of element X. The possible decay particles in the sequence are:
questions.explanation: Step 1 (Z→Z-1): β⁺ decay (Z decreases by 1, A roughly same). Step 2 (Z-1→Z-3): α decay (Z decreases by 2). Step 3 (Z-3→Z-2): β⁻ decay (Z increases by 1). So sequence is β⁺, α, β⁻.

questions.text: A gas mixture consists of 2 moles of O₂ and 4 moles of Ar at temperature T. Neglecting all vibrational modes, the total internal energy of the system is:
questions.topic: Internal energy of a gas mixture
questions.explanation: O₂ (diatomic, no vibration) has internal energy (5/2)RT per mole: 2×(5/2)RT = 5RT. Ar (monoatomic) has (3/2)RT per mole: 4×(3/2)RT = 6RT. Total = 5RT+6RT = 11RT.

questions.text: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is
questions.explanation: n = 100 turns/mm = 10⁵ turns/m. B = μ0nI = 4π×10⁻⁷×10⁵×1 = 12.56×10⁻² T.

questions.text: Two planets P1 and P2 with equal mass have radii R1 and R2, respectively, where R2 = R1/2. The escape speeds of P1 and P2 are v1 and v2, respectively. Then v2/v1 is:
questions.explanation: Escape speed v = sqrt(2GM/R). Since both planets have equal mass M, v2/v1 = sqrt(R1/R2) = sqrt(R1/(R1/2)) = sqrt(2).

questions.text: Three identical p-n junction diodes D1, D2 and D3 are connected across a 5V battery with their respective 1kOhm resistors in a circuit as shown (D1 and its resistor in one branch, D2 and its resistor in a second parallel branch, D3 and its resistor in a third parallel branch, with D3 oriented in reverse relative to D1 and D2). If the width of the depletion regions of D1, D2 and D3 are W1, W2 and W3, respectively, then the correct option is:
questions.topic: p-n Junction Diode - Depletion Region Width
questions.explanation: D1 and D2 are forward biased in the circuit (current flows through them, reducing their depletion region width), while D3 is reverse biased (increasing its depletion region width). Due to the differing branch configurations and resistances, the forward bias across D2 is less than that of D1, leading to depletion width ordering W3 > W2 > W1, with D3 (reverse biased) having the widest depletion region.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct? A. Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero. B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density. C. The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation. D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point. E. The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.
questions.explanation: A, C, D are correct properties of conductors in electrostatic equilibrium. B is false (E=σ/ε0 depends on charge density). E is false (potential is constant, not necessarily zero).

questions.text: Consider a long solenoid of length l and radius r. If n is the number of turns per unit length and μ₀ is the permeability of free space, the inductance of the solenoid is:
questions.explanation: The self-inductance of a long solenoid is L = μ₀n²Al, where A is the cross-sectional area = πr². So L = μ₀n²(πr²)l = μ₀πn²r²l.

questions.text: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is
options: Uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
A linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then linearly decreasing for the outside region.
A linearly increasing function of distance r upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing one with 1/r dependence for the outside region.
A linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
questions.explanation: Inside the wire, B ∝ r (linear increase); outside, B ∝ 1/r (decreasing).

questions.text: A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index √3, at an angle 60°. The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be
questions.explanation: By Brewster's law, since tan(60°) = √3 = μ, this is the Brewster angle, so reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other: 90°.

questions.text: A thin diamagnetic rod is placed vertically between the poles of an electromagnet. When the current in the electromagnet is switched on, then the diamagnetic rod is pushed up, out of the horizontal magnetic field. Hence the rod gains gravitational potential energy. The work required to do this comes from
options: the induced electric field due to the changing magnetic field
the lattice structure of the material of the rod
questions.topic: Diamagnetic materials in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: The energy to push the diamagnetic rod out (increasing its potential energy) ultimately comes from the electrical energy supplied by the current source driving the electromagnet, as work is done against the induced back-emf during the process.

questions.text: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance
options: Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
questions.explanation: For conductors, resistance increases with temperature due to increased collisions; for semiconductors, resistance decreases as more charge carriers are thermally generated.

questions.text: Consider that sigma_s, k_B, b represent Stefan-Boltzmann constant, Boltzmann constant and Wien's displacement law constant, respectively. The dimension of sigma_s * k_B^-1 * b is:
questions.explanation: Stefan-Boltzmann constant sigma_s has dimension [M T^-3 K^-4]. Boltzmann constant k_B has dimension [M L^2 T^-2 K^-1]. Wien's constant b has dimension [L K]. So sigma_s/k_B = [M T^-3 K^-4]/[M L^2 T^-2 K^-1] = [L^-2 T^-1 K^-3]. Multiplying by b = [L K] gives [L^-1 T^-1 K^-2].

questions.text: In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), two PN junction diodes are connected in series with a battery in different orientations: (a) P-N, P-N both same orientation; (b) P-N, N-P opposite; (c) N-P, N-P both same orientation. In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in
questions.explanation: In circuits (a) and (c), both diodes are oriented identically (same direction), so both are either both forward or both reverse biased, giving equal potential drop across each junction.

questions.text: A moving block having mass m, collides with another stationary block having mass 4m. The lighter block comes to rest after collision. When the initial velocity of the lighter block is v, then the value of coefficient of restitution (e) will be
questions.topic: Coefficient of restitution in a perfectly inelastic-type collision
questions.explanation: By momentum conservation: mv = 4m×v2 ⟹ v2 = v/4. Coefficient of restitution e = (v2-0)/(v-0) = (v/4)/v = 0.25.

questions.text: The work functions of Caesium (Cs), Potassium (K) and Sodium (Na) are 2.14 eV, 2.30 eV and 2.75 eV respectively. If incident electromagnetic radiation has an incident energy of 2.20 eV, which of these photosensitive surfaces may emit photoelectrons?
questions.explanation: Photoelectric emission occurs only when the incident photon energy exceeds the work function of the material. Since the incident energy (2.20 eV) is greater than Cs's work function (2.14 eV) but less than K's (2.30 eV) and Na's (2.75 eV), only Cs can emit photoelectrons.

questions.text: A thick current carrying cable of radius 'R' carries current 'I' uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The variation of magnetic field B(r) due to the cable with the distance 'r' from the axis of the cable is represented by:
options: B increases linearly with r then stays constant outside
B rises to a peak at r=R then decreases outside (graph 3)
questions.topic: Magnetic field variation inside a thick current-carrying cable
questions.explanation: Inside the wire B∝r (increasing linearly), peaks at the surface r=R, then decreases as 1/r outside — matching graph option 3.

questions.text: For a travelling harmonic wave, y(x,t)=2.0 cos 2π(10t - 0.0080x + 0.35), where x and y are in cm and t in s. What is the phase difference between oscillatory motion of two points separated by a distance of 0.5 m?
questions.topic: Phase difference of a travelling wave
questions.explanation: Phase difference = k×Δx = 2π×0.0080(per cm)×50 cm = 0.8π rad.

questions.text: Two heaters A and B have power rating of 1 kW and 2kW, respectively. Those two are first connected in series and then in parallel to a fixed power source. The ratio of power outputs for these two cases is:
questions.topic: Power Ratio - Series vs Parallel Combination of Heaters
questions.explanation: For resistors (heaters) connected to a fixed voltage source, ratio of series power to parallel power = P1P2/(P1+P2)² = (1×2)/(1+2)² = 2/9 (with P1=1kW, P2=2kW).

questions.text: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes a cyclic process a→b→c→d→a as shown in the P-V diagram: a(V=2 m³, P=300 N/m²) → b(V=5 m³, P=300 N/m²) → c(V=5 m³, P=100 N/m²) → d(V=2 m³, P=100 N/m²) → a. The total heat supplied to the gas is:
questions.explanation: The cycle a→b→c→d→a traces a rectangle in the P-V plane in the clockwise sense, so the net work done by the gas over one complete cycle equals the enclosed area: W = ΔP × ΔV = (300-100) × (5-2) = 200 × 3 = 600 J. Since internal energy returns to its initial value after a full cycle (ΔU_cycle = 0), the net heat supplied to the gas over the cycle equals the net work done by the gas: Q_net = W = 600 J.

questions.text: An em wave is propagating in a medium with a velocity V = V i^. The instantaneous oscillating electric field of this em wave is along +y axis. Then the direction of oscillating magnetic field of the em wave will be along
questions.topic: Direction of E and B fields in an EM wave
questions.explanation: For an EM wave, E, B and the direction of propagation (v) are mutually perpendicular, following v = E × B direction (right-hand rule). With v along +x and E along +y, B must be along +z direction to satisfy x̂ = ŷ × ẑ.

questions.text: An electric dipole is placed as shown in the figure with -q and +q separated by 3cm each from center O, and point P is 5cm from the +q charge along the axis. The electric potential (in 10² V) at point P due to the dipole is (ε0 = permittivity of free space and 1/4πε0 = K):
questions.topic: Electric Potential Due to a Dipole
questions.explanation: Distance from -q to P = 8cm, distance from +q to P = 2cm. VP = kq/2 - kq/8 = kq×10²[1/2-1/8] = (3/8)kq×10².

questions.text: The ratio of resolving powers of an optical microscope for two wavelengths λ₁=4000 Å and λ₂=6000 Å is:
questions.explanation: Resolving power ∝ 1/λ. Ratio RP₁:RP₂ = λ₂:λ₁ = 6000:4000 = 3:2.

questions.text: For the given circuit, the input digital signals are applied at the terminals A, B and C. What would be the output at the terminal y?
options: Output is 0V initially, goes to 5V during t3-t4, back to 0V (matching waveform 2)
Output is 5V initially, drops to 0V during some interval, matching waveform 3
Output is 0V initially, rises to 5V and stays, matching waveform 4
questions.explanation: Tracing the AND/NAND/OR gate combination through the given input timing diagram gives output waveform matching option 2 per the official key.

questions.text: Unpolarised light is incident from air on a plane surface of a material of refractive index 'μ'. At a particular angle of incidence 'i', it is found that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. Which of the following options is correct for this situation?
options: Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector parallel to the plane of incidence
Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector perpendicular to the plane of incidence
questions.explanation: This is Brewster's angle condition. At this angle, the reflected ray is completely plane polarised, with its electric vector oscillating perpendicular to the plane of incidence (tan i = μ gives the angle, not the polarisation direction option here).

questions.text: An electric heater supplies heat to a system at a rate of 100 W. If the system performs work at a rate of 75 J/s, then the rate at which internal energy increases will be:
questions.topic: Rate of increase of internal energy
questions.explanation: dU/dt=dQ/dt-dW/dt=100-75=25 W.

questions.text: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of the initial and final speeds of a transverse waves along the string is:
questions.topic: Transverse Wave Speed on a String

questions.text: Suppose the charge of a proton and an electron differ slightly. One of them is −e, the other is (e+Δe). If the net of electrostatic force and gravitational force between two hydrogen atoms placed at a distance d (much greater than atomic size) apart is zero, then Δe is of the order of [Given mass of hydrogen m_h = 1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg]:
questions.topic: Balance of electrostatic and gravitational force
questions.explanation: Each hydrogen atom has net charge Δe. Setting electrostatic force k(Δe)²/d² equal to gravitational force Gm_h²/d² gives (Δe)² = Gm_h²/k. Computing: Δe = m_h√(G/k) = 1.67×10⁻²⁷×√(6.67×10⁻¹¹/9×10⁹) ≈ 10⁻³⁷ C.

questions.text: Two identical charged conducting spheres A and B have their centres separated by a certain distance. Charge on each sphere is q and the force of repulsion between them is F. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere is brought in contact with sphere A first and then with B and finally removed from both. New force of repulsion between spheres A and B (radii negligible compared to separation) is best given as :
questions.explanation: Contact with A (charge q, uncharged C): both get q/2. Then C (q/2) contacts B (charge q): total 3q/2 splits equally, each gets 3q/4. Final charges: A = q/2, B = 3q/4. F' = k(q/2)(3q/4)/r² = (3/8)(kq²/r²) = (3/8)F.

questions.text: If θ₁ and θ₂ be the apparent angles of dip observed in two vertical planes at right angles to each other, then the true angle of dip θ is given by:
questions.explanation: For apparent dips measured in two perpendicular vertical planes, the relation between the true dip θ and apparent dips θ₁, θ₂ is cot²θ = cot²θ₁ + cot²θ₂.

questions.text: Which of the following combinations should be selected for better tuning of an L-C-R circuit used for communication?
questions.explanation: Quality factor Q = (1/R)√(L/C) is greatest when resistance R is minimum and L/C ratio is large. Option D has the lowest R (15Ω) with high L, giving the best (sharpest) tuning.

questions.text: Water flows in a streamline motion through a horizontal pipe of circular cross-section. The pressure difference of water between P and Q is 15 Nm⁻². The area of cross-section at P and Q are 40 cm² and 20 cm², respectively. The rate of flow of water through the pipe, in cm³s⁻¹, is: [Take density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³]
questions.explanation: By continuity, v_P A_P = v_Q A_Q, so v_Q = 2v_P (since A_P=2A_Q). By Bernoulli's theorem: P_P - P_Q = (1/2)ρ(v_Q² - v_P²) = (1/2)ρ(4v_P² - v_P²) = (3/2)ρv_P². So 15 = (3/2)(1000)v_P², giving v_P² = 0.01, v_P = 0.1 m/s = 10 cm/s. Flow rate = A_P × v_P = 40 cm² × 10 cm/s = 400 cm³/s.

questions.text: A uniform rod of mass 20kg and length 5m leans against a smooth vertical wall making an angle of 60° with it. The other end rests on a rough horizontal floor. The friction force that the floor exerts on the rod is: (take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: N1 = Mg (vertical, from floor), N2 = f (horizontal, from wall equals friction by equilibrium). Taking torque about the floor contact point A: Mg(L/2)sinθ = N2·L·cosθ, so N2 = (Mg/2)tanθ = (200/2)×tan60° = 100√3 N.

questions.text: An electric dipole is placed at an angle of 30° with an electric field intensity 2×10⁵ N/C. It experiences a torque equal to 4 Nm. The charge on the dipole, if the dipole length is 2 cm, is:
questions.explanation: Torque τ = pE sinθ, so dipole moment p = τ/(E sinθ) = 4/(2×10⁵×0.5) = 4×10⁻⁵ C·m. Since p = qd, q = p/d = 4×10⁻⁵/(2×10⁻²) = 2×10⁻³ C = 2 mC.
