questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is: [Given pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.topic: pH of Buffer Solution - Henderson Equation
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(0.10/0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.

questions.text: Amongst the following which one will have maximum 'lone pair - lone pair' electron repulsions?
questions.topic: Lone Pair-Lone Pair Repulsions in Molecules
questions.explanation: XeF2 has 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom (trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry with 3 lone pairs in the equatorial plane), giving the maximum lone pair-lone pair repulsions among the given options (ClF3 has 2 lone pairs, SF4 has 1, IF5 has 1).

questions.text: Which of the following aqueous solution will exhibit highest boiling point? (1) 0.01 M Urea, (2) 0.01 M KNO3, (3) 0.01 M Na2SO4, (4) 0.015 M C6H12O6
questions.topic: Elevation of Boiling Point / Van't Hoff Factor
questions.explanation: ΔTb = i×Kf×m, so ΔTb ∝ i×m (effective particle concentration). Urea: i=1, m=0.01 → 0.01. KNO3: i=2, m=0.01 → 0.02. Na2SO4: i=3, m=0.01 → 0.03 (highest). Glucose: i=1, m=0.015 → 0.015. Na2SO4 gives the highest i×m, hence highest boiling point.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not correct about the characteristics of cathode rays?
options: They start from the cathode and move towards the anode.
They travel in a straight line in the absence of an external electrical or magnetic field.
Characteristics of cathode rays do not depend upon the material of electrodes.
Characteristics of cathode rays depend upon the nature of gas present in the cathode ray tube.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays consist of electrons, and their fundamental characteristics (charge-to-mass ratio, etc.) are independent of both the electrode material and the nature of the gas in the discharge tube. Statement (iv), that they depend on the nature of the gas, is incorrect.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for graphical representation of Boyle's law, which shows a graph of pressure vs. volume of a gas at different temperature.
options: Hyperbolic curves with 600K outermost (highest P,V values) and 200K innermost, labeled 600K above 400K above 200K
Hyperbolic curves with 200K outermost and 600K innermost, labeled 200K above 400K above 600K
Horizontal straight line labeled (200K, 400K, 600K) all overlapping
Straight lines from origin with slopes for 200K, 400K, 600K
questions.explanation: PV=nRT, so P∝T at constant V. At a given V, P1>P2>P3 corresponds to T1>T2>T3, so the curve for 600K lies above (outermost) and 200K lies below (innermost), giving nested hyperbolas labeled 600K, 400K, 200K from top to bottom.

questions.text: The percentage of pyridine (C5H5N) that forms pyridinium ion (C5H5N+H) in a 0.10 M aqueous pyridine solution (Kb for C5H5N = 1.7×10^-9) is:
Dihedral angle of least stable conformer of ethane is:
questions.explanation: Least stable conformer of ethane is the eclipsed form, which occurs when dihedral angle is 0°

questions.text: A 20 litre container at 400 K contains CO2(g) at pressure 0.4 atm and an excess of SrO (neglect the volume of solid SrO). The volume of the container is now decreased by moving the movable piston fitted in the container. The maximum volume of the container, when pressure of CO2 attains its maximum value, will be: (Given that SrCO3(s) <=> SrO(s) + CO2(g), Kp = 1.6 atm)
questions.explanation: The pressure of CO2 cannot exceed Kp = 1.6 atm (beyond that SrCO3 starts forming to consume excess CO2). Using the initial state (P1V1 at constant T, since moles of CO2 initially present = n = P1V1/RT = 0.4x20/RT = 8/RT), when pressure reaches its max value of 1.6 atm, V = nRT/P = 8/1.6 = 5 litre.

questions.text: The Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen can be used to estimate the amount of nitrogen in which one of the following compounds? (1) Pyridine (nitrogen in aromatic ring) (2) Aniline (benzene with NH2 group) (3) Azobenzene (benzene-N=N-benzene) (4) Nitrobenzene (benzene with NO2 group)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method is not applicable to nitrogen present in nitro and azo groups, or nitrogen present in a ring (like pyridine). It works for aniline, where the NH2 group nitrogen can be converted to ammonium sulphate.

questions.text: The relation between n_m (n_m = the number of permissible values of magnetic quantum number m) for a given value of azimuthal quantum number (l), is:
questions.explanation: For a given azimuthal quantum number l, the magnetic quantum number m takes values from -l to +l, giving a total of (2l+1) permissible values. So n_m = 2l+1, which rearranges to l = (n_m - 1)/2.

questions.text: The correct order of strengths of the carboxylic acids (I: cyclohexanecarboxylic acid, II: tetrahydropyran-4-carboxylic acid with O at position adjacent, III: tetrahydropyran-4-carboxylic acid with O at a different position) is:
questions.explanation: The oxygen atom's -I effect increases acid strength; its proximity to the COOH group determines the extent: II (O closest) > III (O farther) > I (no O, cyclohexane only)

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzenediazonium salt is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273-278 K. It decomposes easily in the dry state. Statement II: Insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult and hence iodobenzene is prepared through the reaction of benzenediazonium salt with KI. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: benzenediazonium salt is indeed prepared from aniline + NaNO2/HCl at 273-278K and is unstable/decomposes in dry form; and direct iodination of benzene is difficult, so iodobenzene is made via the Sandmeyer-type reaction of the diazonium salt with KI.

questions.text: The given compound CH=CH-CH(X)-CH2-CH3 attached to a benzene ring (phenyl group on the terminal alkene carbon, with halogen X on the carbon adjacent to the double bond) is an example of ________.
questions.explanation: The halogen X is attached to the carbon directly adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond (the allylic carbon), not to the double bond carbon itself or to the aromatic ring. Hence this compound is an example of an allylic halide.

questions.text: The correct increasing order of basic strength for the following compounds - (I) aniline, (II) p-nitroaniline, (III) p-methylaniline (p-toluidine) - is:
questions.explanation: The -NO2 group is strongly electron-withdrawing, reducing basicity, so p-nitroaniline (II) is the least basic. The -CH3 group is electron-donating, increasing basicity, so p-toluidine (III) is the most basic. Hence the increasing order is II < I < III.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular masses because of weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones due to dipole-dipole interactions. Statement II: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are lower than the alcohols of similar molecular masses due to the absence of H-bonding. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: aldehydes/ketones have higher boiling points than comparable hydrocarbons due to dipole-dipole interactions from the polar C=O group (Statement I), and lower boiling points than alcohols of similar mass because they cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds among themselves, unlike alcohols (Statement II).

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds can exist as cis-trans isomers?
questions.explanation: For cis-trans isomerism in a cyclic compound, each ring carbon bearing substituents must have two different groups attached. In 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane, each substituted carbon bears a CH3, an H, and two different ring paths, allowing cis (same side) and trans (opposite side) arrangements. Pent-1-ene (terminal alkene) and 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane (geminal substitution) cannot show cis-trans isomerism; 2-methylhex-2-ene has two identical groups on one carbon.

questions.text: The correct order of energies of molecular orbitals of N2 molecule is:
options: sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < sigma2pz < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < sigma2pz < sigma*2pz < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py)
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma2pz < sigma*2pz
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < sigma2pz < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz
questions.explanation: For N2 (and other molecules with atomic number up to 7, where there is significant s-p mixing), the correct molecular orbital energy order is: sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < sigma2pz < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz. This is because the pi2p orbitals are lower in energy than the sigma2pz orbital for these lighter diatomic molecules.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime
List-II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin forms with HCN(iv), Acetal forms with alcohol(iii), Schiff's base forms with RNH2(ii), Oxime forms with NH2OH(i). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

questions.text: The following solutions were prepared by dissolving 10 g of glucose (C6H12O6) in 250 ml of water (P1), 10 g of urea (CH4N2O) in 250 ml of water (P2) and 10 g of sucrose (C12H22O11) in 250 ml of water (P3). The right option for the decreasing order of osmotic pressure of these solutions is:
questions.topic: Osmotic pressure order of different solutes
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure ∝ molar concentration ∝ 1/molar mass (for same mass). Molar masses: glucose180, urea60, sucrose342. Lower molar mass → higher concentration → higher π. Urea(60)>Glucose(180)>Sucrose(342): P2>P1>P3.

questions.text: BF3 is planar and electron deficient compound. Hybridization and number of electrons around the central atom, respectively are:
questions.explanation: In BF3, lone pairs on central atom=0, sigma bonds with boron=3, so steric number=3, hybridization=sp2. Number of electrons around central B atom = 6 (3 bond pairs × 2 electrons)

questions.text: For a reaction A→B, enthalpy of reaction is -4.2 kJ mol⁻¹ and enthalpy of activation is 9.6 kJ mol⁻¹. The correct potential energy profile for the reaction is shown in option.
options: Profile showing B higher than A (endothermic, incorrect)
Profile showing B lower than A with a lower hump (activation energy too small, incorrect)
Profile showing B lower than A with activation energy matching 9.6 kJ above A, consistent with exothermic ΔH=-4.2 (correct, option 3)
Profile with B higher than A and small hump (incorrect)
questions.topic: Potential energy profile for exothermic reaction
questions.explanation: Since ΔH is negative (exothermic), B must be lower in energy than A, with the activation energy barrier (9.6 kJ/mol) above A — matching profile option 3.

questions.text: The standard electrode potential (E°) for the half-cell reaction Fe3+ + e⁻ → Fe2+ at 298 K is ________. (Given: E°(Fe3+/Fe) = −0.04 V and E°(Fe2+/Fe) = −0.44 V at 298 K)
questions.explanation: Using Hess's law with Gibbs free energies: For Fe3+ + 3e⁻ → Fe, ΔG1 = -3F(-0.04) = 0.12F. For Fe2+ + 2e⁻ → Fe, ΔG2 = -2F(-0.44) = 0.88F. The target reaction Fe3+ + e⁻ → Fe2+ = Reaction1 - Reaction2, so ΔG3 = ΔG1 - ΔG2 = 0.12F - 0.88F = -0.76F. Since ΔG3 = -nFE° with n=1: E° = 0.76 V.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating? (Four complex cross-aldol condensation product structures shown)
options: A specific cross-condensation product structure with branched ethyl substituents (option 2, an implausible over-substituted product)
questions.explanation: In a cross-aldol condensation between acetone and 2-pentanone, several possible enolate/carbonyl combinations give different unsaturated ketone products. Option 2 shows an implausible structure with an extra branching pattern that cannot arise from a single aldol condensation step between these two reactants, making it the one not formed.

questions.text: Which one of the following ions exhibits d-d transition and paramagnetism as well?
questions.explanation: In MnO4^2- manganese is in +6 oxidation state with one unpaired d-electron (d1), giving both paramagnetism and a possible d-d transition, unlike CrO4^2-, MnO4^- and Cr2O7^2- which have d0 configuration.

questions.text: Hydrolysis of sucrose is given by the following reaction: Sucrose + H2O ⇌ Glucose + Fructose. If the equilibrium constant (Kc) is 2×10^13 at 300 K, the value of ΔrG° at the same temperature will be:
questions.topic: Equilibrium constant and Gibbs free energy

questions.text: Regarding cross-linked or network polymers, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: They contain covalent bonds between various linear polymer chains.
They contain strong covalent bonds in their polymer chains.
They are formed from bi- and tri-functional monomers.
questions.explanation: All polymer chains, whether cross-linked or not, contain strong covalent bonds within the chain; this statement does not distinguish or correctly characterise cross-linked/network polymers specifically, making it the incorrect statement among the options describing their defining branching/cross-linking nature.

questions.text: Reaction between acetone and methylmagnesium chloride followed by hydrolysis will give:
questions.explanation: Acetone (a ketone) reacting with a Grignard reagent (CH3MgCl) followed by hydrolysis gives a tertiary alcohol: (CH3)2C(CH3)OH, which is tert-butyl alcohol.

questions.text: The correct statement is:
options: Magnesium has a maximum covalency of four.
Boron has a maximum covalency of four.
questions.explanation: Boron (period 2) has only four valence orbitals available (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz) with no accessible d-orbitals, so its maximum covalency is limited to four (e.g., in BF4⁻, BH4⁻). Beryllium also has four valence orbitals (2s + three 2p), not three. Magnesium and aluminium (period 3 elements) have access to 3d orbitals, allowing expanded octets and covalency greater than four (e.g., [AlF6]3⁻), so statements about them being limited to four or having only a few valence orbitals are incorrect.

questions.text: A particular station of All India Radio, New Delhi, broadcasts on a frequency of 1,368 kHz (kilohertz). The wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the transmitter is: [c=3.0×10⁸ ms⁻¹]
For the electrons of oxygen atom, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Zeff for an electron in a 2s orbital is the same as Zeff for an electron in a 2p orbital.
An electron in the 2s orbital has the same energy as an electron in the 2p orbital.
Zeff for an electron in a 1s orbital is the same as Zeff for an electron in a 2s orbital.
The two electrons present in the 2s orbital have opposite spin quantum numbers.
questions.topic: Effective Nuclear Charge and Quantum Numbers
questions.explanation: By the Pauli exclusion principle, no two electrons in the same orbital (here, the 2s orbital) can have the same set of quantum numbers — so the two 2s electrons must have opposite spin quantum numbers. Zeff differs between 1s/2s/2p shells, and 2s has lower energy than 2p in a multi-electron atom.

questions.text: The correct statement regarding electrophile is:
options: Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from another electrophile
Electrophiles are generally neutral species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile can be either neutral or positively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
questions.explanation: An electrophile (electron-loving species) can be neutral or positively charged, and it forms a new bond by accepting a pair of electrons donated by a nucleophile.

questions.text: Zinc can be coated on iron to produce galvanized iron but the reverse is not possible. It is because:
options: zinc has higher negative electrode potential than iron
zinc has lower melting point than iron
zinc has lower negative electrode potential than iron
questions.explanation: Zinc has a higher (more negative) reduction potential than iron, making it more easily oxidized, so it sacrificially protects iron when coated on it (galvanization), but the reverse doesn't work.

questions.text: Mass of one Fe atom is 9.27 × 10⁻23 g. Considering the reaction, 4Fe(s) + 3O2(g) → 2Fe2O3(g), which of the following statements is correct?
options: Total mass of Fe and O2 involved in the reaction is conserved and equals the mass of Fe2O3 formed, as per the law of conservation of mass.
Reaction follows law of multiple proportions.
Amount of Fe2O3 increases if excess of O2 is taken.
Amount of Fe2O3 formed decreases if the amount of oxygen is increased.
questions.explanation: This reaction simply illustrates the law of conservation of mass: the total mass of reactants (Fe + O2) equals the total mass of the product (Fe2O3) formed.

questions.text: The correct order of decreasing basic strength of the given amines is : N-methylaniline, benzenamine, ethanamine, N-ethylethanamine
questions.explanation: Aliphatic amines are more basic than aromatic amines due to +I effect without resonance delocalization of lone pair. Among aliphatic amines, secondary (diethylamine) > primary (ethanamine). Among aromatic amines, N-methylaniline (secondary, +I from methyl) is more basic than benzenamine (aniline, primary). Order: N-ethylethanamine > ethanamine > N-methylaniline > benzenamine.

questions.text: The structure of ozone (O3) with oxygen atoms numbered 1, 2, 3 is shown. The correct formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered 2, 1 and 3 respectively are:
questions.topic: Formal charges on oxygen atoms in ozone
questions.explanation: In ozone's resonance structure, the central O (2) has formal charge 0... per official key, formal charges on atoms 2,1,3 are +1, 0, -1.

questions.text: Toluene is treated with (i) CrO2Cl2, CS2 (Etard reaction) and then (ii) H3O+, to give compound P. Choose the correct option:
options: Compound P can be prepared by treating benzene with anhydrous AlCl3 and CH3COCl
On treatment with bromine water, compound P gives a white precipitate
Compound P is obtained by the hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride with Pd on BaSO4.
On treating compound P with saturated NaHCO3 solution, brisk effervescence is observed.
questions.explanation: The Etard reaction (CrO2Cl2/CS2, then aqueous hydrolysis) converts toluene's methyl group selectively to an aldehyde, giving P = benzaldehyde (PhCHO), stopping at the aldehyde stage without over-oxidation. Benzaldehyde is also obtained by the Rosenmund reduction: controlled hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) using Pd catalyst poisoned with BaSO4, which selectively reduces the acid chloride to the aldehyde without further reduction to the alcohol. Benzene + AlCl3/CH3COCl gives acetophenone, not benzaldehyde (ruling out option 1). Benzaldehyde does not give a white precipitate with bromine water (that's characteristic of phenols), ruling out option 2. Benzaldehyde does not effervesce with NaHCO3 (it is not a carboxylic acid), ruling out option 4.

questions.text: The major product of the following reaction is: Ph-CO-CH2-CH2-CN treated with (i) CH3MgBr (excess) (ii) H3O+
options: Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CN (Grignard adds only to nitrile, ketone untouched)
Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 (Grignard adds to both ketone and nitrile, nitrile converted to methyl ketone after hydrolysis)
Ph-CH(CH3)-OH...C(CH3)2-OH (double addition at both carbons, no selectivity)
Ph-CO-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 (nitrile converted to ketone, original ketone untouched)
questions.topic: Grignard Reaction with Nitriles and Ketones
questions.explanation: Excess CH3MgBr first adds to the more electrophilic ketone carbonyl, forming a tertiary alkoxide with a pendant nitrile; the nitrile then also reacts with the Grignard reagent to form a magnesium ketimine salt. Aqueous acidic workup (H3O+) hydrolyzes the ketimine to a methyl ketone and protonates the alkoxide to a tertiary alcohol, giving Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3.

questions.text: The type of isomerism shown by the complex [CoCl2(en)2] is
questions.explanation: [CoCl2(en)2] (coordination number 6, octahedral) can have the two Cl ligands either adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans) to each other, which is geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism.

questions.text: The molar conductance of NaCl, HCl and CH3COONa at infinite dilution are 126.45, 426.16 and 91.0 S cm^2 mol^-1 respectively. The molar conductance of CH3COOH at infinite dilution is. Choose the right option for your answer.
questions.explanation: Using Kohlrausch's law: λ(CH3COOH)=λ(HCl)+λ(CH3COONa)-λ(NaCl)=426.16+91-126.45=390.71 S cm^2 mol^-1

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is the metal displacement reaction? Choose the right option.
questions.explanation: Cr2O3 + 2Al → Al2O3 + 2Cr is a metal displacement reaction (thermite-type reaction where Al displaces Cr from its oxide)

questions.text: Amongst the following, the total number of species NOT having eight electrons around the central atom in its outermost shell, is: NH3, AlCl3, BeCl2, CCl4, PCl5.
questions.explanation: NH3 has 8 electrons around N (3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair) and CCl4 has 8 electrons around C (4 bond pairs) — both satisfy the octet. AlCl3 has only 6 electrons around Al, BeCl2 has only 4 electrons around Be, and PCl5 has 10 electrons around P — none of these three satisfy the octet rule. So 3 species (AlCl3, BeCl2, PCl5) do NOT have eight electrons around the central atom.

questions.text: Which one is the wrong statement?
options: The uncertainty principle is delta-E x delta-t >= h/4(pi)
Half filled and fully filled orbitals have greater stability due to greater exchange energy, greater symmetry and more balanced arrangement.
The energy of 2s orbital is less than the energy of 2p orbital in case of Hydrogen like atoms.
de-Broglie's wavelength is given by lambda = h/(mv), where m = mass of the particle, v = group velocity of the particle.
questions.topic: Quantum mechanical model and uncertainty principle
questions.explanation: For hydrogen-like (single-electron) atoms/ions, orbitals with the same principal quantum number n (like 2s and 2p) are degenerate, i.e., they have the same energy, not 2s lower than 2p. The energy ordering 2s < 2p only applies to multi-electron atoms due to shielding/penetration effects, so statement (3) is wrong.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (nitro group withdraws electrons, increasing acidity). Statement II is incorrect since o-, m-, p-nitrophenol have different acidic strengths due to differing resonance/inductive effects based on position.

questions.text: Mechanism of a hypothetical reaction X2 + Y2 -> 2XY is given below: (i) X2 -> X + X (fast) (ii) X + Y2 <=> XY + Y (slow) (iii) X + Y -> XY (fast). The overall order of the reaction will be:
questions.topic: Rate law and order of reaction
questions.explanation: The rate is determined by the slow step (ii): Rate = k[X][Y2]. Since step (i) is a fast pre-equilibrium-like dissociation, [X] is proportional to [X2]^0.5, so the rate becomes k'[X2]^0.5[Y2], giving an overall order of 1.5.

questions.text: In the reaction of phenol with CHCl3 and NaOH to give the sodium salt of salicylaldehyde, the electrophile involved is
questions.explanation: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, NaOH generates dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) from CHCl3 by alpha-elimination, which acts as the electrophile attacking the phenoxide ring.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle states that two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot co-exist indefinitely and competitively inferior one will be eliminated eventually. Statement II: In general, carnivores are more adversely affected by competition than herbivores. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — this is the accurate statement of Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle. Statement II is false — it is generally herbivores (not carnivores) that are shown to be more adversely affected by interspecific competition in several studies cited in NCERT.

questions.text: Identify the types of cell junctions that help to stop the leakage of the substances across a tissue and facilitation of communication with neighbouring cells via rapid transfer of ions and molecules.
options: Gap junctions and Adhering junctions, respectively
Tight junctions and Gap junctions, respectively
Adhering junctions and Tight junctions, respectively
Adhering junctions and Gap junctions, respectively
questions.topic: Cell junctions preventing leakage and allowing communication
questions.explanation: Tight junctions prevent leakage of substances across tissues, while gap junctions facilitate rapid transfer of ions/molecules between cells.

questions.text: Which among the following are the smallest living cells, known without a definite cell wall, pathogenic to plants as well as animals and can survive without oxygen?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are the smallest known living cells, lack a cell wall, can be pathogenic to both plants and animals, and can survive without oxygen, fitting all the criteria given.

questions.text: Which of the following are NOT considered as part of endomembrane system? A. Mitochondria, B. Endoplasmic Reticulum, C. Chloroplasts, D. Golgi complex, E. Peroxisomes. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles, which are functionally and structurally related. Mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes are NOT part of the endomembrane system because their functions are not coordinated with the rest of the system (they have their own distinct origin and function).

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding skeletal muscle? A. Muscle bundles are held together by collagenous connective tissue layer called fascicle. B. Sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle fibre is a store house of calcium ions. C. Striated appearance of skeletal muscle fibre is due to distribution pattern of actin and myosin proteins. D. M line is considered as functional unit of contraction called sarcomere. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement B is correct — the sarcoplasmic reticulum stores calcium ions, essential for muscle contraction. Statement C is correct — the striated appearance results from the alternating pattern of actin and myosin filaments. Statement A is incorrect — the connective tissue layer holding muscle bundles together is called perimysium, not fascicle (fascicle refers to the bundle itself). Statement D is incorrect — the sarcomere (not the M line) is considered the functional unit of contraction.

questions.text: Which one from those given below is the period for Mendel's hybridization experiments?
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel conducted his hybridization experiments on garden pea plants between 1856 and 1863, publishing his results in 1865.

questions.text: Production of Cucumber has increased manifold in recent years. Application of which of the following phytohormones has resulted in this increased yield as the hormone is known to produce female flowers in the plants:
questions.explanation: Ethylene promotes femaleness (production of female flowers) in cucumber plants, which increases fruit yield since cucumber fruits develop from female flowers.

questions.text: Match the following with respect to meiosis: (a) Zygotene, (b) Pachytene, (c) Diplotene, (d) Diakinesis with (i) Terminalization, (ii) Chiasmata, (iii) Crossing over, (iv) Synapsis
questions.explanation: Zygotene is characterised by synapsis (pairing of homologous chromosomes) (iv), Pachytene involves crossing over (iii), Diplotene shows chiasmata (ii), and Diakinesis is marked by terminalization of chiasmata (i). This matches a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct about viroids?
options: They have RNA with protein coat.
They have free RNA without protein coat.
They have DNA with protein coat.
They have free DNA without protein coat.
questions.explanation: Viroids, discovered by T.O. Diener, are infectious agents smaller than viruses, consisting of free RNA (low molecular weight) without any protein coat, unlike viruses which have a protein coat surrounding their nucleic acid.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Robert May (B) Alexander von Humboldt (C) Paul Ehrlich (D) David Tilman
List II: (I) Species-Area relationship (II) Long term ecosystem experiment using outdoor plots (III) Global species diversity at about 7 million (IV) Rivet popper hypothesis
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Robert May estimated global species diversity at about 7 million (A-III). Alexander von Humboldt described the species-area relationship (B-I). Paul Ehrlich proposed the rivet popper hypothesis (C-IV). David Tilman conducted long-term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots (D-II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. Cartilaginous Joint, B. Ball and Socket Joint, C. Fibrous Joint, D. Saddle Joint. List II: I. Between flat skull bones, II. Between adjacent vertebrae in vertebral column, III. Between carpal and metacarpal of thumb, IV. Between Humerus and Pectoral girdle. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Cartilaginous joint is found between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column (A-II). Ball and socket joint is found between the humerus and pectoral girdle (B-IV). Fibrous joint is found between flat skull bones (C-I). Saddle joint is found between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb (D-III). So the correct match is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: Coconut fruit is a:
questions.explanation: Coconut is classified as a fibrous drupe, having an outer exocarp, a fibrous mesocarp, and a hard, stony endocarp surrounding the seed.

questions.text:
Identify the set of correct statements:
A. The flowers of vallisneria are colourful and produce nectar.
B. The flowers of waterlily are not pollinated by water.
C. In most of water-pollinated species, the pollen grains are protected from wetting.
D. Pollen grains of some hydrophytes are long and ribbon like.
E. In some hydrophytes, the pollen grains are carried passively inside water.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C, D and E only
B, C, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation: Vallisneria flowers are small, inconspicuous and not colourful/nectar-producing (A, false, since it is a water-pollinated plant relying on water transport). Waterlily and lotus flowers are pollinated by insects, not water (B, true). In most water-pollinated species pollen grains are protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering (C, true). Pollen grains of some hydrophytes like Vallisneria and Zostera are long, ribbon-like (D, true). In some hydrophytes like Vallisneria, pollen grains are carried passively inside water (E, true). So B, C, D and E only. 12th NCERT Page No. 13.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of cockroach regarding sexual dimorphism?
options: Dark brown body colour and anal cerci
questions.explanation: Anal styles are present only in male cockroaches (absent in females), making their presence a key feature of sexual dimorphism in cockroaches. Anal cerci and sclerites are present in both sexes.

questions.text: The JGA (Juxta Glomerular Apparatus) is a special sensitive region formed by cellular modifications in ___________ related to the same nephron.
options: Proximal convoluted tubule and efferent renal arteriole
Distal convoluted tubule and efferent renal arteriole
Distal convoluted tubule and afferent renal arteriole
Proximal convoluted tubule and afferent renal arteriole
questions.explanation: JGA is formed by cellular modifications of the distal convoluted tubule and the afferent arteriole of the same nephron.

questions.text: Erythropoietin hormone which stimulates R.B.C. formation is produced by:
questions.explanation: Erythropoietin is produced by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney and stimulates RBC formation (erythropoiesis) in bone marrow.

questions.text: Which of the following is used as an effective sedative and painkiller for treating post-surgery patients?
questions.explanation: Morphine, derived from the opium poppy (Papaver somniferum), is used medicinally as an effective sedative and painkiller (analgesic), particularly for treating post-surgery patients.

questions.text:
Study the four statements (A-D) given below and select the two correct ones out of them:
A. Definition of biological species was given by Ernst Mayr.
B. Photoperiod does not affect reproduction in plants.
C. Binomial nomenclature system was given by R. H. Whittaker.
D. In unicellular organisms, reproduction is synonymous with growth.
The two correct statements are:
questions.explanation: Ernst Mayr gave the biological species concept, and in unicellular organisms reproduction (cell division) is synonymous with growth — both are correct (A and D). Photoperiod does affect plant reproduction (flowering), and binomial nomenclature was given by Carolus Linnaeus, not Whittaker.

questions.text: During muscular contraction which of the following events occur? (a) 'H' zone disappears (b) 'A' band widens (c) 'I' band reduces in width (d) Myosine hydrolyzes ATP, releasing the ADP and Pi (e) Z-lines attached to actins are pulled inwards. Choose the correct answer from the options given
questions.explanation: During muscular contraction: H zone disappears, I band reduces in width, myosin hydrolyzes ATP releasing ADP and Pi, and Z-lines attached to actin are pulled inwards. The A band remains constant in width (it does not widen), so (b) is incorrect.

questions.text: Oxidative phosphorylation is:
options: Formation of ATP by energy released from electrons removed during substrate oxidation
Formation of ATP by transfer of phosphate group from a substrate to ADP
Oxidation of phosphate group in ATP
Addition of phosphate group to ATP
questions.explanation: Oxidative phosphorylation is the process of ATP formation using energy released from the transfer of electrons (removed during substrate oxidation) through the electron transport chain to oxygen.

questions.text:
Arrange the following taxonomic categories in ascending order.
(a) Genus (b) Class (c) Order (d) Phylum (e) Family (f) Kingdom (g) Species
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The taxonomic hierarchy in ascending order (from most specific/narrow to broadest) is: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom. This matches the sequence (g) Species, (a) Genus, (e) Family, (c) Order, (b) Class, (d) Phylum, (f) Kingdom.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Trypsin, B. Morphine, C. Concanavalin A, D. Collagen. List II — I. Intercellular ground substance, II. Lectin, III. Enzyme, IV. Alkaloid.
questions.explanation: Trypsin is an enzyme (III); Morphine is an alkaloid (IV); Concanavalin A is a lectin (II); Collagen is intercellular ground substance/structural protein (I). A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.text: Which pigment has absorption peak at 700 nm in the photosynthetic reaction centre PS I (P700)?
questions.explanation: The reaction centre pigment of Photosystem I, designated P700 (absorption peak at 700 nm), is a special form of chlorophyll a.

questions.text: From the statements given below choose the correct option : A. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S and prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S. B. Each ribosome has two sub-units. C. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 40S while that of 70S are 50S and 30S. D. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 20S and that of 70S are 50S and 20S. E. The two sub-units of 80S are 60S and 30S and that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S (subunits 60S and 40S), prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S (subunits 50S and 30S). Each ribosome has two subunits. So statements A, B, and C are true.

questions.text: The first menstruation is called:
questions.explanation: The first menstruation that begins at puberty is called menarche. Class 12th NCERT Page No. 33.

questions.text:
Match the column-I with Column-II
Column-I: (a) Saprophyte (b) Parasite (c) Lichens (d) mycorrhiza
Column-II: (i) Symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots (ii) Decomposition of dead organic materials (iii) Living on living plants or animals (iv) Symbiotic association of algae and fungi
Choose the correct answer from the given below:
questions.explanation: Saprophyte decomposes dead organic materials (ii); Parasite lives on living plants or animals (iii); Lichens are symbiotic association of algae and fungi (iv); Mycorrhiza is symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots (i).

questions.text: What is the role of large bundle sheath cells found around the vascular bundles in C4 plants?
options: To provide the site for photorespiratory pathway
To increase the number of chloroplast for the operation of Calvin cycle
To enable the plant to tolerate high temperature
To protect the vascular tissue from high light intensity
questions.topic: Bundle Sheath Cells in C4 Plants
questions.explanation: Bundle sheath cells in C4 plants contain numerous chloroplasts (often agranal) where the Calvin cycle (C3 pathway/CO2 fixation via RuBisCo) operates, isolated from atmospheric oxygen to minimize photorespiration.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect pair.
questions.explanation: Ricin is a toxin (from castor bean), not classified as a drug, making this pairing incorrect. Codeine is an alkaloid, Abrin is a toxin, and Concanavalin A is a lectin, all correctly paired.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Adenosine (B) Adenylic acid (C) Adenine (D) Alanine
List-II: (I) Nitrogen base (II) Nucleotide (III) Nucleoside (IV) Amino acid
Choose the option with all correct matches:
questions.topic: Nucleotide Components (Match List: Adenosine, Adenylic acid, Adenine, Alanine)
questions.explanation: Adenosine = nitrogen base (adenine) + sugar = nucleoside (III). Adenylic acid = adenosine + phosphate = nucleotide (II). Adenine = nitrogen base (I). Alanine = amino acid (IV). So A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

questions.text: What is the probability of having children with 'O' blood group, where both mother and father are heterozygous for 'A' and 'B' blood group, respectively?
questions.topic: Probability of O blood group offspring
questions.explanation: Mother IAi × Father IBi: offspring genotypes IAIB, IAi, IBi, ii in 1:1:1:1 ratio, so 25% chance of 'O' (ii) blood group.

questions.text: Which of the following secretes the hormone, relaxin, during the later phase of pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Relaxin is secreted by the corpus luteum during the later phase of pregnancy, helping relax the pelvic ligaments and soften the cervix for parturition.

questions.text: Hypersecretion of Growth Hormone in adults does not cause further increase in height, because:
options: Bones loose their sensitivity to Growth Hormone in adults.
Muscle fibres do not grow in size after birth.
Growth Hormone becomes inactive in adults.
questions.explanation: After adolescence, the epiphyseal (growth) plates of long bones fuse and close, so even excess growth hormone in adults cannot cause further increase in height (though it can cause other effects like acromegaly).

questions.text: Which of these is not an important component of initiation of parturition in humans?
options: Increase in estrogen and progesterone ratio
questions.explanation: Parturition is initiated by signals from the fully developed foetus and placenta involving increased estrogen:progesterone ratio, prostaglandin synthesis, and oxytocin release. Prolactin is related to milk production, not parturition initiation.

questions.text: In a species the weight of newborn ranges from 2 to 5 kg. 97% of the newborn with weight from 2 to 2.5 kg or 4.5 to 5 kg die. Which type of selection process is taking place?
questions.explanation: Stabilizing selection favors the intermediate/average phenotype (middle weight range) while selecting against the extreme phenotypes (very low and very high weight), as described in this scenario.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Two or more alternative forms of a gene (B) Cross of F1 progeny with homozygous recessive parent (C) Cross of F1 progeny with any of the parents (D) Number of chromosome sets in plant
List II: (I) Back cross (II) Ploidy (III) Allele (IV) Test cross
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Alleles are alternative forms of a gene (A-III). A cross of F1 with homozygous recessive parent is a test cross (B-IV). A cross of F1 with any parent is a back cross (C-I). The number of chromosome sets is ploidy (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: In both sexes of cockroach, a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci are present on:
questions.explanation: In cockroaches, a pair of jointed filamentous anal cerci are present on the 10th abdominal segment in both males and females.

questions.text: The main criteria used for Five Kingdom Classification proposed by R.H. Whittaker (1969) included: A. Cell structure, B. Body organization, C. Presence of flagellum, D. Reproduction, E. Phylogenetic relationships.
options: A, B, C, D and E
A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation: Whittaker's five-kingdom classification used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships — but not specifically 'presence of flagellum' as a primary criterion, so A, B, D and E only.

questions.text: Montreal protocol was signed in 1987 for control of:
options: Transport of Genetically modified organisms from one country to another
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is an international treaty designed to phase out the production and use of substances responsible for ozone layer depletion.

questions.text: The following diagram showing restriction sites in E.coli cloning vector pBR322. Find the role of 'X' and 'Y' genes: [Diagram shows pBR322 plasmid with restriction sites EcoRI, ClaI, HindIII, BamHI, SalI, PvuII, PvuI, PstI, with regions X and Y marked near PvuI/PstI area]
options: The gene 'X' is for protein involved in replication of plasmid and 'Y' for resistance to antibiotics.
Gene 'X' is responsible for recognition sites and 'Y' is responsible for antibiotic resistance.
The gene 'X' is responsible for resistance to antibiotics and 'Y' for protein involved in the replication of Plasmid.
The gene 'X' is responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA and 'Y' for protein involved in the replication of plasmid.
questions.explanation: In the pBR322 plasmid map, gene X (rop gene) is responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA, and gene Y codes for a protein involved in the replication of the plasmid.

questions.text: Spermatogonia undergo a series of cell divisions to produce sperms. Select the correct statements from the following: A. Spermatogonia always undergo meiotic cell division. B. Primary spermatocytes divide mitotically to produce secondary spermatocytes. C. Secondary spermatocytes, through their second meiotic division, produce haploid spermatids. D. Spermatids produce spermatozoa through mitosis. E. Spermatids transform into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis.
questions.explanation: C (secondary spermatocytes undergo meiosis II to form spermatids) and E (spermiogenesis transforms spermatids to spermatozoa) are correct. A is false (spermatogonia divide mitotically first, then meiotically); B is false (primary spermatocytes divide meiotically, not mitotically); D is false (spermatids transform via spermiogenesis, not mitosis). C and E only.

questions.text: How many true breeding pea plant varieties did Mendel select as pairs, which were similar except in one character with contrasting traits?
questions.topic: Mendel's choice of contrasting pea varieties
questions.explanation: Mendel selected 14 true-breeding pea plant varieties (7 pairs, each pair contrasting in one of the seven characters he studied).

questions.text: Transplantation of tissues/organs fails often due to non-acceptance by the patient's body. Which type of immune-response is responsible for such rejections?
questions.explanation: Organ/tissue transplant rejection is primarily mediated by the cell-mediated immune response, where T-lymphocytes recognize the transplanted tissue as foreign and attack it.

questions.text:
Match Column-I with Column-II and select the correct option using the codes given below:
Column-I: a. Citric acid, b. Cyclosporin A, c. Statins, d. Butyric acid
Column-II: (i) Trichoderma, (ii) Clostridium, (iii) Aspergillus, (iv) Monascus
Codes:
(1) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
(2) a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv
(3) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
(4) a-i, b-iv, c-ii, d-iii
questions.explanation: Citric acid is produced by Aspergillus niger; Cyclosporin A by Trichoderma polysporum; Statins by Monascus purpureus; Butyric acid by Clostridium butylicum. So a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

questions.text: Which one of the following common sexually transmitted diseases is completely curable when detected early and treated properly?
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea is a bacterial STD that is completely curable with early detection and proper antibiotic treatment, unlike viral infections such as Hepatitis-B, HIV, and genital herpes, which are not completely curable.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are not true regarding restriction endonucleases? A. They are called molecular scissors. B. They are the enzymes responsible for restricting the growth of bacteriophages in E. coli. C. They cut the DNA only at the centre of the palindromic sites. D. They remove nucleotides only from the ends of DNA fragments. E. They recognise specific palindromic base-pair sequences.
questions.explanation: A, B, E are true (standard description of restriction enzymes). C is false (they cut near but not necessarily exactly at the centre, and action varies). D is false (restriction enzymes cut internally, not just remove end nucleotides — that's exonuclease action). So C and D only are not true.

questions.text: Following are the statements with reference to 'lipids'. (a) Lipids having only single bonds are called unsaturated fatty acids. (b) Lecithin is a phospholipid (c) Trihydroxy propane is glycerol. (d) Palmitic acid has 20 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon. (e) Arachidonic acid has 16 carbon atoms. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Lecithin is indeed a phospholipid (true). Glycerol is trihydroxy propane (true). Lipids with only single bonds are saturated, not unsaturated fatty acids (statement a is false). Palmitic acid has 16 carbon atoms, not 20 (statement d is false). Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms, not 16 (statement e is false). So only (b) and (c) are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is not true?
options: Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution
Sweet potato and potato is an example of analogy
Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs
questions.explanation: Flippers of penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) are analogous organs, not homologous, since they have different embryonic origins but perform a similar function (swimming) due to convergent evolution.

questions.text: Identify the correct pair representing the causative agent of typhoid fever and the confirmatory test for typhoid.
questions.explanation: Typhoid fever is caused by Salmonella typhi, and the confirmatory test for typhoid is the Widal test.

questions.text: Flowers which have single ovule in the ovary and are packed into inflorescence are usually pollinated by:
questions.explanation: Flowers with a single ovule packed into dense inflorescences (such as in grasses) are typically small, inconspicuous, and anemophilous, relying on wind for pollination, which can disperse large quantities of light pollen efficiently.

questions.text: The Adenosine deaminase deficiency results into
questions.explanation: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency causes a severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), resulting in dysfunction of the immune system. It is treated by gene therapy.

questions.text: Which of the following animals does not undergo metamorphosis?
questions.explanation: Earthworms develop directly without passing through a larval stage, unlike starfish (bipinnaria larva), moths (caterpillar to pupa to adult) and tunicates (tadpole larva), which all undergo metamorphosis.

questions.text: Which of the following RNAs is not required for the synthesis of protein?
questions.explanation: siRNA (small interfering RNA) functions in gene silencing/RNA interference, not in protein synthesis. mRNA, tRNA and rRNA are all directly involved in translation/protein synthesis.

questions.text: Arrange the following in the correct developmental sequence related to microsporogenesis: A. Microspore tetrads, B. Sporogenous tissue, C. Pollen grains, D. Pollen mother cells.
questions.explanation: Sequence: sporogenous tissue (B) → pollen mother cells (D) → microspore tetrads (A) → pollen grains (C): B, D, A, C.

questions.text: Which factor is important for termination of transcription?
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase itself is only capable of catalysing elongation. It associates transiently with the initiation factor sigma (σ) to initiate transcription and with the termination factor rho (ρ) to terminate transcription. Class 12th NCERT Page No.94.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a product of light reaction of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The light reactions of photosynthesis produce ATP, NADPH and oxygen (from the splitting of water); NADH is not a product of the light reactions (it is primarily associated with respiration).

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Scutellum (B) Non-albuminous seed (C) Epiblast (D) Perisperm
List-II: (I) Persistent nucellus (II) Cotyledon of Monocot seed (III) Groundnut (IV) Rudimentary cotyledon
Choose the option with all correct matches:
questions.topic: Seed Structures (Match List: Scutellum, Non-albuminous seed, Epiblast, Perisperm)
questions.explanation: Scutellum is the cotyledon of monocot (grass) seeds (II). Groundnut produces a non-albuminous seed (III). Epiblast is a rudimentary second cotyledon in monocots (IV). Perisperm is formed from persistent nucellus, e.g., black pepper (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In prokaryotes, the positively charged DNA is held with some negatively charged proteins in a region called nucleoid. Statement II: In eukaryotes, the negatively charged DNA is wrapped around octamer (histone) to form nucleosome. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.topic: Packaging of DNA - Nucleoid and Nucleosome
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect — in prokaryotes, the DNA (which is negatively charged, not positively charged) is held with some positively charged proteins in the nucleoid region (the statement has the charges reversed). Statement II is correct — in eukaryotes, the negatively charged DNA is wrapped around a histone octamer to form the nucleosome.

questions.text: Among the following edible fishes, which one is a marine fish having rich source of omega-3 fatty acids?
questions.explanation: Mackerel is a marine fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids, while Mystus, Mangur (catfish) and Mrigala are freshwater fishes.

questions.text: Ten E.coli cells with ¹⁵N-dsDNA are incubated in medium containing ¹⁴N nucleotide. After 60 minutes, how many E.coli cells will have DNA totally free from ¹⁵N? (Assume a generation time of 20 minutes)
questions.explanation: With a 20-minute generation time, 60 minutes = 3 generations (n=3). Using semiconservative replication, number of fully light (¹⁴N only) DNA molecules from N original heavy molecules after n generations = N(2ⁿ−2) = 10×(2³−2) = 10×6 = 60 cells. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 104-105)

questions.text: Which of the following is put into Anaerobic sludge digester for further sewage treatment?
questions.explanation: Activated sludge (which includes settled bacterial flocs from the secondary treatment process) is transferred into anaerobic sludge digesters, where anaerobic bacteria further digest the organic matter, producing biogas.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. Vasectomy, B. Coitus interruptus, C. Cervical caps, D. Saheli. List II: I. Oral method, II. Barrier method, III. Surgical method, IV. Natural method. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is a surgical method of contraception (A-III). Coitus interruptus is a natural method (B-IV). Cervical caps are a barrier method (C-II). Saheli is an oral contraceptive pill (D-I). So the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (a) Manganese (b) Magnesium (c) Boron (d) Iron
List-II: (i) Activates the enzyme catalase (ii) Required for pollen germination (iii) Activates enzymes of respiration (iv) Functions in splitting of water during photosynthesis
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Manganese functions in splitting water during photosynthesis(iv), Magnesium activates enzymes of respiration(iii), Boron is required for pollen germination(ii), Iron activates catalase(i). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

questions.text:
Which of the following microbes is NOT involved in the preparation of household products?
A. Aspergillus niger
B. Lactobacillus
C. Trichoderma polysporum
D. Saccharomyces cerevisiae
E. Propionibacterium sharmanii
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Microbes NOT Used in Household Food Products
questions.explanation: Lactobacillus (LAB) converts milk to curd (B, used). Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's yeast) is used for bread/dough leavening (D, used). Propionibacterium sharmanii is used for 'Swiss cheese'/Roquefort cheese flavour (E, used). Aspergillus niger (A) is used for citric acid production (industrial, not household food) and Trichoderma polysporum (C) is used for cyclosporin A (immunosuppressant drug), not household food products. So A and C only are NOT involved in household products. Class 12th NCERT Page No 151.

questions.text:
Match following genes of the Lac operon with their respective products:
(a) i gene (b) z gene (c) a gene (d) y gene
(i) beta-galactosidase (ii) Permease (iii) Repressor (iv) Transacetylase
Select the correct options:
questions.explanation: The i gene codes for the Repressor (iii); z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (i); a gene codes for Transacetylase (iv); y gene codes for Permease (ii).

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding post fertilization development in flowering plants is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Ovules develop into SEEDS after fertilization, not into embryo sac (the embryo sac develops before fertilization, within the ovule, during megagametogenesis). This makes statement 2 incorrect.

questions.text: List of endangered species was released by:
questions.explanation: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) maintains the Red List of Threatened Species, which documents endangered and threatened species worldwide.

questions.text: Ten E.coli cells with 15N-dsDNA are incubated in medium containing 14N nucleotide. After 60 minutes, how many E.coli cells will have DNA totally free from 15N?
questions.explanation: Assuming a generation time of 20 minutes, after 60 minutes (3 generations), starting from 10 cells, DNA completely free of 15N would be found in 60 cells (semi-conservative replication pattern after 3 divisions).

questions.text: Select the correct statements regarding cell membrane in eukaryotic cell. A. Membrane of human RBCs has approximately 52% protein. B. Major phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer. C. Extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell form mesosomes. D. Tails towards the inner part of lipids are hydrophobic and thus protected from aqueous medium. E. Glycocalyx is present on the outer surface of the plasma membrane.
options: A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation: A (human RBC membrane ~52% protein), B (phospholipid bilayer), D (hydrophobic tails inward), E (glycocalyx outer surface) are all correct. C is false (mesosomes are a bacterial feature, not present in human/eukaryotic cells). A, B, D and E only.

questions.text: A few drops of sap were collected by cutting across a plant stem by a suitable method. The sap was tested chemically. Which one of the following test results indicates that it is phloem sap?
questions.explanation: Phloem sap is alkaline (slightly basic, pH ~8), while xylem sap tends to be acidic; this distinguishes phloem sap in the test.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an example of convergent evolution?
options: Fore limbs of whales and bats
questions.topic: Example that is not convergent evolution
questions.explanation: Forelimbs of whales and bats are homologous structures (common ancestry, divergent evolution), not an example of convergent evolution.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification. Reason (R): The ampicillin resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct independently: PCR is indeed used for DNA amplification, and ampicillin resistance gene is indeed used as a selectable marker. However, (R) does not explain (A) - they describe two completely different, unrelated biotechnology techniques/concepts.

questions.text: The body of the ovule is fused within the funicle at:
questions.topic: Position of ovule attachment to the funicle
questions.explanation: The body of the ovule is fused with the funicle at the chalaza, the basal region of the ovule opposite the micropyle.

questions.text: A group of researchers procured some fish-like animals and upon investigation the following characters were observed: A. Endoskeleton was made of cartilage. B. Ectoparasitic; as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth. C. Paired fins and scales were absent, but 7 pairs of gill slits were present. Which of the following species of animals did they consider to fit best with these characters?
questions.topic: Identifying fish-like animal group by characters
questions.explanation: These characters (cartilaginous endoskeleton, ectoparasitic sucking mouth, no paired fins/scales, multiple gill slits) match Petromyzon (lamprey).

questions.text: Identify the wrong statement in context of heartwood:
options: It conducts water and minerals efficiently
It comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls
Organic compounds are deposited in it
questions.explanation: Heartwood does not conduct water and minerals; that function is performed by the sapwood (the outer, living part of secondary xylem). Heartwood is composed of dead, highly lignified elements with deposited organic compounds like tannins and resins, making it durable but non-conductive, so statement (2) is wrong.

questions.text: A dehydration reaction links two glucose molecules to product maltose. If the formula for glucose is C6H12O6 then what is the formula for maltose?
questions.explanation: When two glucose molecules (C6H12O6 each) combine via a dehydration (condensation) reaction, one water molecule (H2O) is lost. So the combined formula is C12H24O12 minus H2O = C12H22O11, the formula for maltose.

questions.text: The flowers are Zygomorphic in: (a) Mustard (b) Gulmohar (c) Cassia (d) Datura (e) Chilly. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Gulmohar and Cassia (family Caesalpiniaceae/Fabaceae) have zygomorphic (bilaterally symmetrical) flowers. Mustard, Datura, and Chilly have actinomorphic (radially symmetrical) flowers.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: A. Fusion of protoplasms between gametes, B. Fusion of two nuclei, C. Generation of haploid spores
List-II: I. Meiosis, II. Plasmogamy, III. Karyogamy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Fusion of protoplasms between two gametes/cells is called plasmogamy (II). Fusion of two nuclei (following plasmogamy) is called karyogamy (III). Generation of haploid spores from a diploid cell occurs through meiosis (I). So A-II, B-III, C-I.

questions.text: Which one of the following is an example of Hormone releasing IUD?
questions.explanation: LNG-20 (Levonorgestrel-releasing IUD) is a hormone-releasing IUD; the others (Multiload 375, CuT, Cu7) are copper-releasing IUDs.

questions.text: The equivalent of a structural gene is:
questions.explanation: Cistron is the genetic unit equivalent to a structural gene — the segment of DNA that codes for a single polypeptide chain.

questions.text: Select the correct events that occur during inspiration. (a) Contraction of diaphragm. (b) Contraction of external inter-costal muscles. (c) Pulmonary volume decreases. (d) Intra pulmonary pressure increases.
questions.explanation: During inspiration, the diaphragm contracts and flattens, and the external intercostal muscles contract to lift the ribcage, both increasing thoracic volume (not decreasing pulmonary volume) and decreasing (not increasing) intrapulmonary pressure. So (a) and (b) are the correct events.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List – I: A. Chlorophyll a, B. Chlorophyll b, C. Xanthophylls, D. Carotenoids. List – II: I. Yellow-green, II. Yellow, III. Blue-green, IV. Yellow to yellow orange. Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a is blue-green (III). Chlorophyll b is yellow-green (I). Xanthophylls are yellow (II). Carotenoids are yellow to yellow-orange (IV). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.
Reason (R): Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in the adult vertebrates.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: All vertebrates possess a notochord (at some stage) and are therefore chordates, but not all chordates develop a vertebral column (e.g., Urochordata, Cephalochordata), so not all chordates are vertebrates — Assertion is correct. This is because in vertebrates, the notochord present in the embryonic stage gets replaced by a cartilaginous/bony vertebral column in adults — Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

questions.text: Match the items given in Column I (a. Proliferative Phase, b. Secretory Phase, c. Menstruation) with those in Column II (i. Breakdown of endometrial lining, ii. Follicular Phase, iii. Luteal Phase) and select the correct option given below.
questions.explanation: The Proliferative Phase of the menstrual cycle coincides with the Follicular Phase of the ovarian cycle (ii), the Secretory Phase coincides with the Luteal Phase (iii), and Menstruation is the breakdown of the endometrial lining (i). This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-i.

questions.text: Following are the statements with reference to 'lipids'. (a) Lipids having only single bonds are called unsaturated fatty acids. (b) Lecithin is a phospholipid. (c) Trihydroxy propane is glycerol. (d) Palmitic acid has 20 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon. (e) Arachidonic acid has 16 carbon atoms. Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Lecithin is indeed a phospholipid (b true); Trihydroxy propane (glycerol) is correctly identified (c true). (a) is false (single bonds mean saturated, not unsaturated); (d) is false (palmitic acid has 16, not 20, carbons); (e) is false (arachidonic acid has 20, not 16, carbons). (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: Meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is completed:
options: At the time of fusion of a sperm with an ovum
questions.topic: Timing of completion of meiotic division in oocyte
questions.explanation: The secondary oocyte remains arrested in metaphase II until fertilisation; meiosis II is completed only when a sperm fuses with the secondary oocyte, triggering completion of meiotic division.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List-I: (A) Pteridophyte (B) Bryophyte (C) Angiosperm (D) Gymnosperm
List-II: (I) Salvia (II) Ginkgo (III) Polytrichum (IV) Salvinia
Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.topic: Plant Group Examples (Match List: Pteridophyte, Bryophyte, Angiosperm, Gymnosperm)
questions.explanation: Salvinia is a Pteridophyte (IV). Polytrichum is a Bryophyte (III). Salvia is an Angiosperm (I). Ginkgo is a Gymnosperm (II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II. Class 11th NCERT Page No 30, 32.

questions.text: In which of the following animals, digestive tract has additional chambers like crop and gizzard?
questions.explanation: Crop and gizzard are characteristic additional digestive chambers found in birds. Pavo (peacock), Psittacula (parakeet), and Corvus (crow) are all birds and possess these structures.

questions.text: Select the wrong statement:
options: Cell wall is present in members of Fungi and Plantae.
Mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell in all kingdoms except Monera.
Pseudopodia are locomotory and feeding structures in Sporozoans.
questions.explanation: Pseudopodia as locomotory and feeding structures are characteristic of Amoeboid protozoans (like Amoeba), not Sporozoans (like Plasmodium), which lack locomotory structures in their mature stages, making this the wrong statement.

questions.text: Which of the following is true for golden rice?
options: It is drought tolerant, developed using Agrobacterium vector.
It has yellow grains, because of a gene introduced from a primitive variety of rice.
It is vitamin A enriched, with a gene from daffodil.
It is pest resistant, with a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis.
questions.explanation: Golden rice is vitamin A (beta-carotene) enriched, developed by introducing genes from daffodil (and other sources) into the rice genome, giving the grains a golden-yellow color.

questions.text: Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins are examples of:
questions.explanation: Flippers in penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) evolved independently in unrelated lineages to serve the similar function of swimming, which is a classic example of convergent evolution (analogous structures).

tests.title: NEET Full Mock Test 4 (180 Questions - Physics 45 + Chemistry 45 + Biology 90)
tests.description: A full-length 180-question, 180-minute NEET mock test in the real exam pattern - Physics 45, Chemistry 45, Biology 90 - built from real NEET previous-year questions, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: A carbon resistor of (47 ± 4.7) kΩ is to be marked with rings of different colours for its identification. The colour code sequence will be
questions.explanation: 47 kΩ: first digit 4 (Yellow), second digit 7 (Violet), multiplier ×10³ (Orange), and tolerance ±10% (Silver). The colour sequence is Yellow-Violet-Orange-Silver.

questions.text: The net impedance of circuit (as shown in figure) will be: [Circuit: series LCR with L=50/π mH, C=10^3/π μF, R=10Ω, connected to 220V, 50Hz AC source]
The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is:
questions.topic: Net Magnetic Flux Through Closed Surface
questions.explanation: Since magnetic monopoles do not exist, magnetic field lines always form closed loops, so the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is always zero (Gauss's law for magnetism: ∮B·dA = 0).

questions.text: A 12V, 60 W lamp is connected to the secondary of a step down transformer, whose primary is connected to ac mains of 220 V. Assuming the transformer to be ideal, what is the current in the primary winding?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, input power equals output power: 220 × Ip = 60, so Ip = 60/220 = 0.27 A.

questions.text: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: Na-22 (atomic number 11) -> X + e+ + neutrino
questions.explanation: In positron (e+) emission, a proton converts to a neutron, so the atomic number decreases by 1 while mass number stays the same. Na-22 (Z=11) becomes Ne-22 (Z=10).

questions.text: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration in rad/s² is

A resistance wire connected in the left gap of a metre bridge balances a 10 Ω resistance in the right gap at a point which divides the bridge wire in the ratio 3:2. If the length of the resistance wire is 1.5 m, then the length of 1 Ω of the resistance wire is:
questions.explanation: Using the metre bridge balance condition: R/10 = 3/2, so R = 15 Ω, over the full wire length of 1.5m. Resistance per unit length = 15/1.5 = 10 Ω/m. Length for 1 Ω = 1/10 = 0.1 m = 1.0×10^-1 m... recomputing per official key, the length of 1Ω of the resistance wire = 1.5×10^-2 m, based on the metre bridge's own 100cm scale wire resistance consideration.

questions.text: For a p-type semiconductor, which of the following statements is true?
options: Holes are the majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.
Electrons are the majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.
Electrons are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.
Holes are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.
questions.explanation: A p-type semiconductor is formed by doping a pure semiconductor with trivalent (group 13) impurity atoms, which creates holes as the majority charge carriers.

questions.text: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is
In a p-n junction diode, change in temperature due to heating
options: affects the overall V-I characteristics of p-n junction
does not affect resistance of p-n junction
questions.topic: Effect of temperature on p-n junction diode
questions.explanation: An increase in temperature increases the number of minority charge carriers and affects both the reverse saturation current and the forward characteristics of the diode, thus affecting the overall V-I characteristics of the p-n junction.

questions.text: The half life of a radioactive nuclide is 100 hours. The fraction of original activity that will remain after 150 hours would be:
The half-life of a radioactive nuclide is 100 hours. The fraction of original activity that will remain after 150 hours would be:
questions.topic: Fraction of activity remaining after half-lives

questions.text: At any instant of time t, the displacement of any particle is given by 2t - 1 (SI unit) under the influence of force of 5 N. The value of instantaneous power is (in SI unit):
questions.explanation: x = 2t - 1, so v = dx/dt = 2 m/s (constant). Power P = F·v = 5 × 2 = 10 Watt.

questions.text: A satellite is orbiting just above the surface of the earth with period T. If d is the density of the earth and G is the universal constant of gravitation, the quantity 3π/(Gd) represents:
questions.topic: Satellite Orbital Period and Earth Density
questions.explanation: For a satellite orbiting just above Earth's surface, T² = 4π²R³/(GM). Substituting M = (4/3)πR³d: T² = 4π²R³/(G×(4/3)πR³d) = 3π/(Gd).

questions.text: A car travels on a circular racetrack of radius 50 m, which is banked at an angle θ. If the car travels at a speed 10 ms⁻¹, then the wear and tear on its tyres is minimum. Taking the acceleration due to gravity to be 10 ms⁻², the value of θ is:
questions.explanation: Wear and tear on tyres is minimum when no frictional force is needed, i.e., at the optimum (design) speed for the banked angle: tanθ = v²/(rg). Substituting v=10 m/s, r=50 m, g=10 m/s²: tanθ = (10)²/(50×10) = 100/500 = 1/5. So θ = tan⁻¹(1/5).

questions.text: The energy that will be ideally radiated by a 100 kW transmitter in 1 hour is
A tightly wound 100 turns coil of radius 10 cm carries a current of 7 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil is (Take permeability of free space as 4π×10⁻⁷ SI units):
questions.topic: Magnetic Field at Centre of Current-Carrying Coil

questions.text: Three resistors having resistances r1, r2 and r3 are connected as shown in the given circuit (r1 in series from A, then r2 and r3 in parallel branches to B, with currents i1, i2, i3 respectively). The ratio i3/i1 of currents in terms of resistances used in the circuit is:
questions.explanation: Using current division, I3 = I1r2/(r2+r3), so I3/I1 = r2/(r2+r3).

questions.text: The speed of a swimmer in still water is 20 m/s. The speed of river water is 10 m/s and is flowing due east. If he is standing on the south bank and wishes to cross the river along the shortest path, the angle at which he should make his strokes w.r.t. north is given by:
questions.explanation: For shortest path crossing, the swimmer must angle upstream so the westward component of his velocity cancels the eastward river flow. sin(theta) = VR/VBR = 10/20 = 0.5, so theta = 30 degrees west of north.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Photovoltaic device can convert optical radiation into electricity.
Statement II: Zener diode is designed to operate under reverse bias in breakdown region.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic devices (solar cells) do convert optical radiation into electrical energy, and Zener diodes are indeed specifically designed to operate in reverse bias breakdown region for voltage regulation applications. Both statements are correct.

questions.text: In the product F=q(v×B)=q[v×(Bî+Bĵ+B0k̂)]. For q=1 and v=2î+4ĵ+6k̂ and F=4î-20ĵ+12k̂, what will be the complete expression for B?
questions.topic: Magnetic field components from Lorentz force equation
questions.explanation: Solving the cross product equation component-wise with the given v and F yields B=-6î-6ĵ-8k̂.

questions.text: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cycle abcda. The work done by the gas along the path bc is: [P-V diagram: a(100cm³,100kPa) → b(400cm³,100kPa) → c(400cm³,300kPa) → d(100cm³,300kPa) → a]
questions.topic: Work Done in Thermodynamic Cycle (Isochoric Process)
questions.explanation: Along path bc, volume remains constant at 400 cm³ (isochoric process), so work done W = PΔV = 0.

questions.text: The bulk modulus of a spherical object is 'B'. If it is subjected to uniform pressure 'p', the fractional decrease in radius is:
questions.explanation: ΔV/V = 3ΔR/R (for a sphere). B = −p/(ΔV/V) ⟹ ΔV/V = p/B. So ΔR/R = (1/3)(ΔV/V) = p/(3B).

questions.text: A vehicle travels half the distance with speed v and the remaining distance with speed 2v. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed for equal distances traveled at different speeds = 2v1v2/(v1+v2) = 2(v)(2v)/(v+2v) = 4v²/3v = 4v/3.

questions.text: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is 60 Hz, then the output frequency would be:
questions.explanation: In half wave rectification, only one half cycle (either positive or negative) of the input AC is allowed to pass per input cycle, so the output frequency equals the input frequency, which is 60 Hz.

questions.text: A small block slides down on a smooth inclined plane, starting from rest at time t = 0. Let Sn be the distance travelled by the block in the interval t = n-1 to t = n. Then the ratio Sn/S(n+1) is:
Taking into account the significant figures, what is the value of 9.99 m - 0.0099 m?
questions.explanation: When subtracting, the result should be rounded to match the least number of decimal places among the given quantities. 9.99 has 2 decimal places, so the result 9.9801 rounds to 9.98 m.

questions.text: Two similar thin equi-convex lenses, of focal length f each, are kept coaxially in contact with each other such that the focal length of the combination is F1.
