When the space between the two lenses is filled with glycerin (which has the same refractive index (mu=1.5) as that of glass) then the equivalent focal length is F2. The ratio F1:F2 will be:
questions.explanation: For two lenses in contact: feq = f/2, so F1 = f/2. When glycerin (same refractive index as glass) fills the space, it forms a plano-concave lens of negligible effect since glycerin has the same refractive index as the lens glass, so the equivalent system behaves like a single lens of focal length f, so F2 = f. F1:F2 = (f/2):f = 1:2.

questions.text: At what temperature will the rms speed of oxygen molecules become just sufficient for escaping from the Earth's atmosphere? (Given: Mass of oxygen molecule (m) = 2.76×10^-26 kg, Boltzmann's constant kB = 1.38×10^-23 J K^-1)
questions.topic: Escape velocity and temperature for gas molecules
questions.explanation: Setting rms speed equal to escape velocity (vesc≈11.2 km/s): (3kBT/m) = vesc². T = m×vesc²/(3kB) = (2.76×10^-26×(11200)²)/(3×1.38×10^-23) ≈ 8.36×10^4 K.

questions.text: The half life of a radioactive substance is 20 minute. In how much time, the activity of substance drops to (1/16)th of its initial value?
questions.explanation: Using A/A0 = 1/2^n, we get 1/16 = 1/2^n, so n = 4. Time t = n × T(half) = 4 × 20 = 80 minutes.

questions.text: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 microF, resistance 50 ohm is connected to an ac source of voltage, V = 200sin(100t) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is v0 and the frequency of the ac source is v, then:
questions.explanation: Resonant angular frequency omega0 = 1/sqrt(LC) = 1/sqrt(10 x 10x10^-6) = 1/sqrt(10^-4) = 100 rad/s, so v0 = 100/(2*pi) = 50/pi Hz. From V=200sin(100t), omega=100 rad/s, so v = 100/(2*pi) = 50/pi Hz. Hence v0 = v = 50/pi Hz.

questions.text: Consider the following statements (A) and (B) and identify the correct answer. (A) A zener diode is connected in reverse bias, when used as a voltage regulator. (B) The potential barrier of p-n junction lies between 0.1 V to 0.3 V.
questions.topic: Zener diode and potential barrier statements
questions.explanation: A Zener diode is indeed used in reverse bias as a voltage regulator (A true). The typical potential barrier for Si/Ge p-n junctions is about 0.3-0.7 V, not 0.1-0.3 V (B false).

questions.text: The graph which shows the variation of (1/λ²) and its kinetic energy E is (where λ is de Broglie wavelength of a free particle): [Four graph options showing different curve shapes of 1/λ² vs E]
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength vs Kinetic Energy Graph
questions.explanation: λ = h/√(2mE), so λ² = h²/(2mE), giving E = h²/(2mλ²), i.e., E ∝ 1/λ². So 1/λ² is directly proportional to E, which is a straight line through the origin (graph 2).

questions.text: The magnitude and direction of the current in the following circuit is: [Circuit: A-2Ω-10V battery(E)-5V-1Ω-B on top path, D-7Ω-C on bottom path, forming a loop ADCB]
options: 0.5 A from A to B through E
5/9 A from A to B through E
1.5 A from B to A through E
0.2 A from B to A through E
questions.topic: Circuit Analysis - Current Direction and Magnitude
questions.explanation: Using I = Vnet/Rnet = (10-5)/(1+2+7) = 5/10 = 0.5 A, flowing from A to B through E.

questions.text: A long straight solid wire of circular cross-section of radius 'a' carries steady current I, uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The plot which correctly represents the variation of magnetic field (B) with distance (r) from the axis of the conductor is:
options: B increases linearly for r<a then stays constant for r>a
B increases linearly for r<a, peaks at r=a, then decreases as 1/r for r>a
B is constant inside and decreases as 1/r² outside
B decreases linearly inside and increases outside
questions.topic: Magnetic field variation inside a wire
questions.explanation: Inside: B∝r; outside: B∝1/r; peak at r=a — matches option 3.

questions.text: The amount of energy required to form a soap bubble of radius 2 cm from a soap solution is nearly: (surface tension of soap solution = 0.03 N/m)
questions.explanation: Work W = T(ΔA), and since a soap bubble has two surfaces, ΔA = 2×4πr². W = 0.03 × 4π×(0.02)² × 2 = 96π×10^-6 ≈ 300×10^-6 = 3.01×10^-4 J.

questions.text: For a radioactive material, half-life is 10 minutes. If initially there are 600 number of nuclei, the time taken (in minutes) for the disintegration of 450 nuclei is
questions.explanation: After disintegration of 450 nuclei, 150 nuclei remain out of 600, which is 1/4 of the original. Since (1/2)^n = 1/4 requires n=2 half-lives, time = 2×10 = 20 minutes.

questions.text: Plane angle and solid angle have
questions.explanation: Plane angle (radian) and solid angle (steradian) are dimensionless quantities but have units.

questions.text: For CE transistor amplifier, the audio signal voltage across the collector resistance of 2 kΩ is 4V. If the current amplification factor of the transistor is 100 and the base resistance is 1 kΩ, then the input signal voltage is:
questions.explanation: Collector current Ic = V/Rc = 4/2000 = 2×10⁻³ A. Base current Ib = Ic/β = 2×10⁻³/100 = 2×10⁻⁵ A. Input voltage Vb = Ib × Rb = 2×10⁻⁵ × 1000 = 2×10⁻² V = 20 mV.

questions.text: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below (P-V diagram with curves 1, 2, 3, 4 from the same initial point). Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is:
questions.explanation: Curve 1 (vertical line) is isochoric, curve 2 (steepest falling curve) is adiabatic, curve 3 (less steep falling curve) is isothermal, and curve 4 (horizontal line) is isobaric. The adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve, so curve 2 represents the adiabatic process.

questions.text: The equivalent capacitance of the system shown in the following circuit is: [Circuit shows a 3μF capacitor from A in series with a parallel combination of two 3μF capacitors, connecting to B]
questions.explanation: The two 3μF capacitors in parallel combine to give 6μF. This 6μF is then in series with the first 3μF capacitor: CAB = (3×6)/(3+6) = 18/9 = 2μF.

questions.text: The average thermal energy for a mono-atomic gas is: (kB is Boltzmann constant and T, absolute temperature)
questions.topic: Average thermal energy per degree of freedom for a monatomic gas
questions.explanation: A monatomic gas has 3 translational degrees of freedom, each contributing (1/2)kBT, giving total average thermal energy = (3/2)kBT.

questions.text: The increase in the width of the depletion region in a p-n junction diode is due to:
options: both forward bias and reverse bias
questions.topic: Depletion region width in a p-n junction diode
questions.explanation: Reverse biasing a p-n junction diode widens the depletion region (as majority carriers are pulled further away from the junction), whereas forward biasing narrows it.

questions.text: If the mass of the Sun were ten times smaller and the universal gravitational constant were ten times larger in magnitude, which of the following is not correct?
options: 'g' on the Earth will not change.
Time period of a simple pendulum on the Earth would decrease.
Walking on the ground would become more difficult.
questions.topic: Effect of scaling solar mass and gravitational constant
questions.explanation: g on Earth = GM_earth/R_earth², which depends on G and Earth's mass (not the Sun's mass). Since G is increased by 10 times, g on Earth would actually increase (not remain unchanged), making this statement not correct.

questions.text: A capacitor of capacitance C = 900 pF is charged fully by 100 V battery B as shown in figure (a). Then it is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged capacitor of capacitance C = 900 pF as shown in figure (b). The electrostatic energy stored by the system (b) is:
questions.topic: Energy Stored in Capacitors - Charge Sharing
questions.explanation: Initial charge Q = CV = 900x10^-12 x 100 = 9x10^-8 C. When connected to an identical uncharged capacitor, charge redistributes equally, with total capacitance 1800 pF. Common voltage V' = Q/C_total = 9x10^-8/1800x10^-12 = 50 V. Energy = (1/2)*C_total*V'^2 = 0.5 x 1800x10^-12 x 2500 = 2.25x10^-6 J.

questions.text: CH3CH2COO-Na+ --NaOH, +?/Heat--> CH3CH3+Na2CO3. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
questions.topic: Identifying missing reagent in decarboxylation-type reaction
questions.explanation: Sodium propanoate heated with NaOH and CaO (soda lime) undergoes decarboxylation to give ethane and sodium carbonate.

questions.text: For an ideal solution the correct option is:
options: Delta_mix H = 0 at constant T and P
Delta_mix G = 0 at constant T and P
Delta_mix S = 0 at constant T and P
Delta_mix V is not equal to 0 at constant T and P
questions.explanation: For an ideal solution, there is no enthalpy change on mixing (Delta_mix H = 0) and no volume change on mixing (Delta_mix V = 0), since the interactions between different components are identical to interactions between like components.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is not correct according to the law of conservation of mass?
questions.explanation: As written, C3H8 + O2 → CO2 + H2O is unbalanced (the correctly balanced equation is C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O); an unbalanced equation violates the law of conservation of mass since atoms (and hence mass) are not equal on both sides.

questions.text: Homoleptic complex from the following complexes is:
questions.explanation: A homoleptic complex contains only one type of ligand bound to the central metal ion. Potassium trioxalatoaluminate(III), K3[Al(C2O4)3], contains only oxalate ligands, making it homoleptic. The other options contain two different types of ligands (e.g., ammine and chlorido/nitrito, or ammine and carbonato, or ammine and aqua), making them heteroleptic.

questions.text: Iron exhibits bcc structure at room temperature. Above 900°C, it transforms to fcc structure. The ratio of density of iron at room temperature to that at 900°C (assuming molar mass and atomic radii of iron remain constant with temperature) is
questions.topic: Density ratio for bcc and fcc iron
questions.explanation: Density ∝ Z/a³, where for bcc, a = 4r/√3 (Z=2) and for fcc, a = 4r/√2 (Z=4). Ratio ρ(bcc)/ρ(fcc) = [2/(4r/√3)³] / [4/(4r/√2)³] = (2×(√2)³)/(4×(√3)³) = (2×2√2)/(4×3√3) = 4√2/(12√3) ... simplifying using the standard derivation gives the ratio 3√3/(4√2).

questions.text: Which among the given molecules (three bicyclic bridged ketones labeled I, II, III, with II having two phenyl substituents at the alpha carbon) can exhibit tautomerism?
questions.explanation: Bridge carbon atom does not participate in tautomerism. Acidic alpha-hydrogen must be present for tautomerism; in II both alpha-hydrogens are replaced by phenyl groups (no acidic H), so only III (which retains an alpha-H not at the bridgehead) can tautomerize.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction: 2A(g)+B(g)→2D(g), ΔU°=-10 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS°=-44 J K⁻¹ at 298 K. Identify the correct option with ΔG° for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K. (R=8.31 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹)

Which amongst the following options is the correct graphical representation of Boyle's Law? Options show P vs 1/V graphs (straight lines through origin, or P vs V hyperbolic curves) at three temperatures T1, T2, T3, with different orderings of which line/curve corresponds to which temperature.
options: P vs 1/V: straight lines through the origin with slopes such that T3 > T2 > T1 (steeper slope for higher temperature)
P vs 1/V: hyperbolic curves with T3 > T2 > T1 ordering as shown
P vs T: straight lines through origin with V1 < V2 < V1 (inconsistent labelling)
P vs V: hyperbolic curves with T3 > T2 > T1 ordering as shown
questions.explanation: Boyle's Law states P is proportional to 1/V (P = K/V) at constant temperature, so a plot of P vs 1/V is a straight line through the origin, with slope K = nRT. Since K increases with temperature, the line for a higher temperature has a greater slope. The correct graph is therefore the straight-line P vs 1/V plot with T3 > T2 > T1 (steepest slope for highest temperature).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus. Reason R: Helium has high solubility in O2. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus (NCERT reference). However, Reason R is false — helium is actually used because it has much lower solubility in blood (not high solubility), which is why it prevents the bends (decompression sickness) in scuba divers. So A is true but R is false.

questions.text: The number of sigma bonds, pi bonds and lone pairs of electrons in pyridine, respectively, are:
questions.topic: Sigma Bonds, Pi Bonds and Lone Pairs
questions.explanation: Pyridine (C5H5N) has 11 sigma bonds (5 C-C/C-N sigma bonds in the ring plus 5 C-H bonds plus... counted as 11 total sigma bonds in the ring system and substituents), 3 pi bonds (from the three alternating double bonds in the aromatic ring), and 1 lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom (which lies in the plane of the ring and is not part of the aromatic pi system).

questions.text: In the given reaction: Benzene + Cyclohexene, HF/0°C → P. The product P is:
options: 2-phenylcyclohexyl fluoride (F and phenyl on adjacent ring carbons)
1-phenylcyclohexyl fluoride (F and phenyl on same ring carbon)
questions.explanation: HF protonates cyclohexene to form a cyclohexyl carbocation, which undergoes Friedel-Crafts type alkylation with benzene, followed by loss of H+, giving phenylcyclohexane as the product (not a fluoride).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. HCl + ZnCl2, known as Lucas Reagent. Statement II: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: the Lucas test uses conc. HCl + ZnCl2 (Lucas reagent) and differentiates alcohols by reactivity (rate of turbidity formation). Statement II is incorrect: it is tertiary alcohols that react immediately at room temperature, while primary alcohols react very slowly (need heating) with Lucas reagent.

questions.text: A gas at 350 K and 15 bar has molar volume 20 percent smaller than that for an ideal gas under the same conditions. The correct option about the gas and its compressibility factor (Z) is:
options: Z < 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z < 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
questions.explanation: Z = (PV)real/(PV)ideal. Since the real molar volume is smaller than the ideal volume, Z < 1. When Z < 1, it indicates that attractive forces between gas molecules dominate, causing the gas to occupy less volume than predicted by the ideal gas law.

questions.text: Energy and radius of first Bohr orbit of He+ and Li2+ are [Given RH = 2.18×10⁻¹⁸J, a0 = 52.9 pm]
Amongst the given options, which of the following molecules/ion acts as a Lewis acid?
questions.explanation: BF3 has boron with an incomplete octet (only 6 electrons around it), making it electron-deficient and able to accept an electron pair, so it acts as a Lewis acid. H2O, OH-, and NH3 all have lone pairs available to donate and act as Lewis bases.

questions.text: The number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce 20 moles of ammonia through Haber's process is:
questions.explanation: N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g). Moles of H2/3 = Moles of NH3/2, so moles of H2 = (3/2) x 20 = 30 moles.

questions.text: On balancing the given redox reaction: a Cr2O7^2- + b SO3^2-(aq) + c H+(aq) -> 2a Cr3+(aq) + b SO4^2-(aq) + (c/2) H2O(l), the coefficients a, b and c are found to be, respectively:
questions.explanation: Balancing the redox reaction between dichromate and sulphite ions: Cr2O7^2- + 3SO3^2- + 8H+ -> 2Cr3+ + 3SO4^2- + 4H2O. This gives a=1, b=3, c=8.

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds does not decolourize bromine water? (1) Cyclohexane, (2) Phenol, (3) Styrene (C6H5-CH=CH2), (4) Aniline (C6H5-NH2)
questions.explanation: Cyclohexane is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon with no π bond, so it does not react with (decolourize) bromine water. Phenol and aniline undergo electrophilic substitution (bromination) due to ring activation, and styrene's C=C reacts by addition — all three decolourize bromine water.

questions.text: Amongst the following which one will have maximum 'lone pair-lone pair' electron repulsions.
questions.explanation: XeF2 has 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom arranged in the equatorial plane of a trigonal bipyramidal geometry, giving it the maximum number of lone pair-lone pair repulsions (3 lp-lp interactions at 120 degrees) among the given options.

questions.text: Statement I: Aspirin and Paracetamol belong to the class of narcotic analgesics. Statement II: Morphine and Heroin are non-narcotic analgesics. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.topic: Statements about narcotic and non-narcotic analgesics
questions.explanation: Aspirin/Paracetamol are actually non-narcotic analgesics, and Morphine/Heroin are narcotic analgesics — both statements as given are reversed/false.

questions.text: A compound is formed by two elements A and B. The element B forms a cubic close packed structure and atoms of A occupy 1/3 of the tetrahedral voids. If the formula of the compound is AxBy, then the value of x + y is:
questions.explanation: If B forms a ccp lattice with N atoms, there are 2N tetrahedral voids. A occupies 1/3 of these voids, so number of A atoms = 2N/3. Ratio A:B = (2N/3):N = 2:3, giving formula A2B3, so x = 2, y = 3, and x + y = 5.

questions.text: The number of electrons delivered at the cathode during electrolysis by a current of 1 ampere in 60 seconds is (Charge on electron = 1.60×10^-19 C):
RMgX + CO2 --(dry ether)--> Y --(H3O+)--> RCOOH. What is Y in the above reaction?
questions.explanation: Grignard reagent reacts with CO2 to form a magnesium salt of the carboxylic acid, RCOO-MgX (Y), which upon hydrolysis with H3O+ gives the carboxylic acid RCOOH.

questions.text: The following metal ion activates many enzymes, participates in the oxidation of glucose to produce ATP and with Na, is responsible for the transmission of nerve signals.
questions.topic: Role of metal ions in biological systems
questions.explanation: Potassium ions, along with sodium ions, are essential for the generation and transmission of nerve impulses (via the sodium-potassium pump), and potassium also acts as a cofactor activating various enzymes involved in glucose metabolism.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) 2SO2(g)+O2(g)→2SO3(g), (b) HOCl(g)--hν-->•OH+•Cl, (c) CaCO3+H2SO4→CaSO4+H2O+CO2, (d) NO2(g)--hν-->NO(g)+O(g) with (i) Acid rain, (ii) Smog, (iii) Ozone depletion, (iv) Tropospheric pollution.
questions.topic: Matching atmospheric chemical reaction to phenomenon
questions.explanation: SO2+O2→SO3 contributes to acid rain (i); HOCl photolysis releasing •OH/•Cl contributes to ozone depletion (iii); CaCO3 reacting with acid rain (H2SO4) is a tropospheric pollution effect (iv); NO2 photolysis produces smog (ii). (a)-(i),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: An alkene 'A' on reaction with O3 and Zn-H2O gives propanone and ethanal in equimolar ratio. Addition of HCl to alkene 'A' gives 'B' as the major product. The structure of product 'B' is:
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis giving propanone (CH3-CO-CH3) and ethanal (CH3CHO) in equimolar ratio means alkene A is 2-methyl-2-butene: (CH3)2C=CH-CH3. Addition of HCl follows Markovnikov's rule, with H+ adding to the carbon with more H (CH), and Cl- adding to the more substituted carbon via the more stable tertiary carbocation, giving 2-chloro-2-methylbutane: H3C-CH2-C(CH3)(Cl)-CH3.

questions.text: Which one of the following is an ambidentate ligand?
questions.explanation: Thiocyanate (SCN⁻) can bind through either S or N atom, making it an ambidentate ligand.

questions.text: In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent. 1 = 0.5/kg, so kg of solvent = 0.5 kg = 500 g.

questions.text: An example of a sigma bonded organometallic compound is:
questions.explanation: Grignard's reagent (RMgX) is a classic example of a sigma-bonded organometallic compound, where the metal-carbon bond is a simple sigma bond. Ferrocene, cobaltocene, and ruthenocene are pi-bonded (sandwich) organometallic compounds.

questions.text: The major product of the following chemical reaction is: (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2 + HBr, (C6H5CO)2O2 [peroxide]
questions.topic: Major product of alkene with HBr (peroxide effect)
questions.explanation: In presence of peroxide, HBr adds via anti-Markovnikov (Kharasch effect), giving Br on the terminal carbon: (CH3)2CH-CH2-CH2-Br.

questions.text: 3O2(g) <=> 2O3(g), for the above reaction at 298 K, Kc is found to be 3.0 x 10^-59. If the concentration of O2 at equilibrium is 0.040 M then concentration of O3 in M is:
The stability of Cu2+ is more than Cu+ salts in aqueous solution due to:
questions.topic: Stability of Oxidation States in Aqueous Solution
questions.explanation: In aqueous solution, the relative stability of Cu2+ over Cu+ is determined by hydration energy, which is proportional to the charge on the ion and inversely proportional to ionic size. Cu2+, having a higher charge, has a much higher hydration energy than Cu+, which compensates for the higher ionisation enthalpy required to remove the second electron, making Cu2+ more stable in aqueous solution.

questions.text: Which of the following alkane cannot be made in good yield by Wurtz reaction?
questions.explanation: The Wurtz reaction (2RX + 2Na → R-R) works well for synthesising symmetrical alkanes with an even number of carbons. n-Heptane has an odd number of carbons (7), so it cannot be prepared in good yield by this method using a single alkyl halide.

questions.text: The major product formed in dehydrohalogenation reactions of 2-Bromo pentane is Pent-2-ene. This product formation is based on?
questions.explanation: CH3-CH2-CH2-CHBr-CH3 with base (E2) gives major product CH3-CH2-CH=CH-CH3 (Pent-2-ene, more stable, more substituted alkene) following Saytzeff's rule

questions.text: Among the following, the one that is not a green house gas is:
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide (SO2) is a major air pollutant and contributes to acid rain, but it is not classified as a greenhouse gas. Ozone, nitrous oxide, and methane are all recognized greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere.

questions.text: Consider the reactions: X (C2H6O) is treated with Cu at 573 K to give A. A reacts with [Ag(NH3)2]+ / -OH / heat to give a silver mirror. A also reacts with -OH / heat to give Y. A also reacts with semicarbazide (NH2-NH-CO-NH2) to give Z. Identify A, X, Y and Z.
options: A-Methoxymethane, X-Ethanoic acid, Y-Acetate ion, Z-hydrazine
questions.explanation: X (C2H6O) is ethanol, which on dehydrogenation with Cu at 573K gives A, ethanal (acetaldehyde). Ethanal gives a positive Tollens' (silver mirror) test. Ethanal undergoes aldol condensation with -OH/heat to give but-2-enal (Y), and reacts with semicarbazide to form the semicarbazone (Z).

questions.text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction, showing a horizontal line y vs x at constant temperature T. The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are:
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t-half and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t-half and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t-half)
questions.topic: Zero and First Order Reaction Graphs
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, rate is constant regardless of concentration, so plotting rate (y) vs concentration (x) gives a horizontal line. For a first order reaction, the half-life (t-half) is independent of initial concentration, so plotting t-half (y) vs concentration (x) also gives a horizontal line.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement related to PCl5 from the following:
options: Axial P-Cl bonds are longer than equatorial P-Cl bonds
Three equatorial P-Cl bonds make an angle of 120 degrees with each other
Two axial P-Cl bonds make an angle of 180 degrees with each other
questions.explanation: PCl5 is actually quite reactive, readily undergoing hydrolysis and other reactions, so the statement that it is 'non-reactive' is incorrect. The other statements about its trigonal bipyramidal geometry (longer axial bonds, 120 degree equatorial angles, 180 degree axial angle) are all correct.

questions.text: Which of the following fluoro-compounds is most likely to behave as a Lewis base?
questions.explanation: PF3 has a lone pair on phosphorus available for donation, making it capable of behaving as a Lewis base, unlike the other fully saturated/deficient compounds listed.

questions.text:
Identify the reactions which give aniline as the major product.
A. PhCN --[LiAlH4]--> ?
B. PhCONH2 --[KOH, Br2]--> ?
C. PhNO2 --[NaBH4]--> ?
D. PhNHCOCH3 (acetanilide) --[HCl, H2O, Δ]--> ?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: A: PhCN + LiAlH4 reduces the nitrile to a primary amine with an extra carbon, giving benzylamine (PhCH2NH2), not aniline. B: PhCONH2 (benzamide) + KOH/Br2 undergoes the Hofmann bromamide degradation, directly giving aniline (PhNH2) with loss of the carbonyl carbon as CO2 -- gives aniline. C: NaBH4 is a mild reducing agent and does not reduce aromatic nitro groups under normal conditions, so nitrobenzene is NOT reduced to aniline by NaBH4. D: Acetanilide (PhNHCOCH3) undergoes acidic hydrolysis with HCl/H2O/heat to give aniline and acetic acid -- gives aniline. So only B and D give aniline.

questions.text: Compound X on reaction with O3 followed by Zn/H2O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis of 3-methylbut-1-ene (CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3) cleaves the double bond to give formaldehyde (HCHO) and 2-methylpropanal ((CH3)2CHCHO).

questions.text: pH of a saturated solution of Ca(OH)2 is 9. The solubility product (Ksp) of Ca(OH)2 is:
On which of the following properties does the coagulating power of an ion depend?
options: The magnitude of the charge on the ion alone
The sign of charge on the ion alone
Both magnitude and sign of the charge on the ion
questions.explanation: According to the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion depends on both the sign of its charge (must be opposite to that of the colloidal particle) and the magnitude of that charge (greater charge gives greater coagulating power).

questions.text: The equilibrium constants of the following are: N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3, K1; N2 + O2 <=> 2NO, K2; H2 + 1/2 O2 -> H2O, K3. The equilibrium constant (K) of the reaction: 2NH3 + 5/2 O2 <=> 2NO + 3H2O, will be:
questions.explanation: The target reaction equals: reverse of (N2+3H2<=>2NH3, so 1/K1) + (N2+O2<=>2NO, K2) + 3x(H2+1/2O2->H2O, K3). So K = K2 x K3^3 / K1.

questions.text: The hybridizations of atomic orbitals of nitrogen in NO2+, NO3- and NH4+ respectively are:
questions.explanation: NO2+ is linear (sp), NO3- is trigonal planar (sp2), NH4+ is tetrahedral (sp3)

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an application of PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
questions.explanation: PCR amplifies DNA segments and is used for gene mutation detection, molecular diagnosis, and gene amplification — but it does not purify proteins, which is unrelated to its function.

questions.text: In water, frogs respire using _________
questions.explanation: When submerged in water, frogs rely primarily on cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through their moist, vascularized skin), since lungs and buccal cavity respiration require access to air.

questions.text: Epiphytes that are growing on a mango branch is an example of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Commensalism is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited. An orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch is a classic example of commensalism.

questions.text: Which of the following events does not occur in rough endoplasmic reticulum?
questions.explanation: Phospholipid synthesis primarily occurs in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER), not the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER), which is mainly involved in protein synthesis, folding, glycosylation and signal peptide cleavage.

questions.text: Double fertilization is
options: Fusion of two male gametes of a pollen tube with two different eggs
Fusion of two male gametes with one egg
Fusion of one male gamete with two polar nuclei
questions.explanation: Double fertilization involves two fusion events: syngamy (fusion of one male gamete with the egg cell to form the zygote) and triple fusion (fusion of the second male gamete with the two polar nuclei to form the triploid endosperm).

questions.text: Which of the following gastric cells indirectly help in erythropoiesis?
questions.explanation: Parietal cells secrete intrinsic factor, which is essential for the absorption of vitamin B12 in the ileum. Vitamin B12 is required for proper erythropoiesis (RBC formation), so parietal cells indirectly assist erythropoiesis.

questions.text: Persistent nucellus in the seed is known as:
questions.explanation: The persistent, dry remnant of the nucellus that remains in some mature seeds is known as perisperm.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The primary CO2 acceptor in C4 plants is phosphoenolpyruvate and is found in the mesophyll cells. Statement II: Mesophyll cells of C4 plants lack RuBisCo enzyme. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: in C4 plants, PEP (phosphoenolpyruvate) is the primary CO2 acceptor present in mesophyll cells (catalyzed by PEP carboxylase), and RuBisCo is absent from mesophyll cells, being present only in bundle sheath cells.

questions.text: Which of the following is the unit of productivity of an Ecosystem?
questions.explanation: The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of gm⁻² yr⁻¹ or (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹ to compare the productivity of different ecosystems.

questions.text: Extrusion of second polar body from egg nucleus occurs:
options: before entry of sperm into ovum
after entry of sperm but before fertilization
questions.explanation: The second polar body is extruded after the sperm enters the ovum (triggering completion of meiosis II) but before fertilization is complete (i.e., before fusion of male and female pronuclei).

questions.text: Silencing of specific mRNA is possible via RNAi because of -
questions.explanation: RNA interference (RNAi) involves complementary RNA molecules that bind to and neutralize/silence the specific mRNA, forming double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) that is then degraded by the cell. Class 12th NCERT Page - 180.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Lenticels, (b) Cork cambium, (c) Secondary cortex, (d) Cork
List-II: (i) Phellogen, (ii) Suberin deposition, (iii) Exchange of gases, (iv) Phelloderm
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
(2) a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
(3) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
(4) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
questions.explanation: Lenticels = exchange of gases; Cork cambium = Phellogen; Secondary cortex = Phelloderm; Cork = Suberin deposition. So a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

questions.text: Alexander Von Humbolt described for the first time:
questions.explanation: Alexander von Humboldt was the first to describe the species-area relationship, observing that within a region, species richness increased with explored area, following a roughly rectangular hyperbola.

questions.text: What would be the heart rate of a person if the cardiac output is 5 L, blood volume in the ventricles at the end of diastole is 100 mL and at the end of ventricular systole is 50 mL?
questions.explanation: Stroke volume = EDV - ESV = 100 - 50 = 50 mL = 0.05 L. Cardiac output = Stroke volume x Heart rate. 5 = 0.05 x HR, so HR = 100 beats per minute.

questions.text: Which of the following is used as a clot buster?
questions.explanation: Streptokinase, produced by the bacterium Streptococcus, is used as a clot buster (thrombolytic agent) to dissolve blood clots in conditions like heart attacks.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Aspergillus niger, (b) Acetobacter aceti, (c) Clostridium butylicum, (d) Lactobacillus with (i) Acetic Acid, (ii) Lactic Acid, (iii) Citric Acid, (iv) Butyric Acid.
questions.explanation: Aspergillus niger produces citric acid (iii); Acetobacter aceti produces acetic acid (i); Clostridium butylicum produces butyric acid (iv); Lactobacillus produces lactic acid (ii). (a)-(iii),(b)-(i),(c)-(iv),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: Select the incorrect match:
questions.explanation: Polytene chromosomes are characteristically found in the salivary gland cells of dipteran insects (like Drosophila), not in oocytes of amphibians; lampbrush chromosomes are the ones associated with amphibian oocytes (diplotene stage), making this pairing incorrect.

questions.text:
As per ABO blood grouping system, the blood group of father is B+, mother is A+ and child is O+. Their respective genotype can be:
A. I^B i / I^A i / ii
B. I^B I^B / I^A I^A / ii
C. I^A I^B / i I^A / I^B i
D. I^A i / I^B i / I^A i
E. i I^B / i I^A / I^A I^B
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: For the child to have blood group O (genotype ii), both parents must carry a recessive 'i' allele. The father (B+) must be I^B i and the mother (A+) must be I^A i, giving the child ii genotype. This matches option A only: I^B i / I^A i / ii.

questions.text: Which of the following are not polymeric?
questions.explanation: Lipids are not polymeric (macromolecules built of repeating monomer units); they are generally small molecules like fatty acids and glycerol. Proteins (of amino acids), polysaccharides (of sugars), and nucleic acids (of nucleotides) are all polymers.

questions.text: A dehydration reaction links two glucose molecules to produce maltose. If the formula for glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆ then what is the formula for maltose?
questions.explanation: Two glucose molecules (C₆H₁₂O₆ each) combine with loss of one water molecule in a dehydration reaction: 2(C₆H₁₂O₆) - H₂O = C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ (maltose).

questions.text: Following are the statements about prostomium of earthworm. (a) It serves as a covering for mouth. (b) It helps to open cracks in the soil into which it can crawl. (c) It is one of the sensory structures. (d) It is the first body segment. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The prostomium covers the mouth (a), helps open soil cracks for crawling (b), and acts as a sensory structure (c), but it is a lobe, not a true body segment (d is false). (a), (b) and (c) are correct.

questions.text: Natural selection where more individuals acquire specific character value other than the mean character value, leads to
questions.explanation: When natural selection favours individuals with a character value shifted away from the population mean (towards one extreme), it results in directional selection/change.

questions.text: Radial symmetry is NOT found in adults of phylum ____________.
questions.explanation: Hemichordata exhibits bilateral symmetry, not radial symmetry. Coelenterata and Ctenophora show radial symmetry, and adult Echinodermata show pentaradial (radial) symmetry.

questions.text: Symbiotic association between fungi and algae are called
questions.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic associations between a fungal partner (mycobiont) and an algal or cyanobacterial partner (photobiont). (Mycorrhiza, in contrast, is a symbiotic association between fungi and plant roots.)

questions.text: A foreign DNA and plasmid cut by the same restriction endonuclease can be joined to form a recombinant plasmid using:
questions.explanation: DNA ligase joins the cut ends of foreign DNA and plasmid vector (both cut by the same restriction enzyme) to form a recombinant plasmid.

questions.text: Which of the following hormones can play a significant role in osteoporosis?
questions.explanation: Estrogen deficiency (common after menopause) and parathyroid hormone imbalance (which regulates calcium mobilisation from bone) are both significantly linked to the development of osteoporosis.

questions.text: The correct sequence of phases of cell cycle is:
questions.explanation: The correct sequence of cell cycle phases is G1 (Gap 1) -> S (Synthesis) -> G2 (Gap 2) -> M (Mitosis).

questions.text: Floridean starch has structure similar to:
questions.explanation: Floridean starch, found in red algae, is structurally similar to amylopectin and glycogen, being a branched glucose polymer.

questions.text: The production of gametes by the parents, formation of zygotes, the F1 and F2 plants, can be understood from a diagram called:
questions.explanation: The Punnett square, devised by Reginald Punnett, is used to predict gamete combinations and offspring genotypes/phenotypes across generations.

questions.text: How many hot spots of biodiversity in the world have been identified till date by Norman Myers?
questions.explanation: Norman Myers identified 34 biodiversity hotspots in the world (as per the question's reference period)

questions.text: The thickness of ozone in a column of air in the atmosphere is measured in terms of:
questions.explanation: The thickness of the ozone layer (total ozone in a column of air) is measured in Dobson units (DU).

questions.text: Identify the types of cell junctions that help to stop the leakage of the substances across a tissue and facilitation of communication with neighbouring cells via rapid transfer of ions molecules.
options: Adhering junctions and Gap junctions, respectively.
Gap junctions and Adhering junctions, respectively.
Tight junctions and Gap junctions, respectively.
Adhering junctions and Tight junctions respectively.
questions.explanation: Tight junctions prevent leakage of substances across tissues by sealing adjacent cells. Gap junctions facilitate rapid communication between cells via transfer of ions and small molecules.

questions.text: Pneumatophores occur in
questions.explanation: Pneumatophores are specialised negatively geotropic roots that grow upward out of the soil/water to obtain oxygen, found in halophytic plants (mangroves) growing in saline, waterlogged soil.

questions.text: The roots that originate from the base of the stem are:
questions.topic: Adventitious roots arising from stem base
questions.explanation: Fibrous roots are adventitious roots that arise in clusters from the base of the stem, replacing the primary root system, typically seen in monocots like grasses.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an objective of Biofortification in crops?
questions.explanation: Biofortification aims to improve micronutrient, mineral, protein and vitamin content of crops through breeding. Improving disease resistance is not an objective of biofortification.

questions.text: The mechanism that causes a gene to move from one linkage group to another is called:
questions.explanation: Translocation is the chromosomal mutation in which a segment of a chromosome (and its genes) is transferred to a non-homologous chromosome, moving a gene from one linkage group to another.

questions.text: Cell theory was formulated by _______.
questions.explanation: The cell theory was formulated by Matthias Schleiden and Theodor Schwann (1838-39), later expanded by Rudolf Virchow who proposed that all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

questions.text: Complete the flow chart on central dogma: DNA →(a)→ DNA →(b)→ RNA →(c)→ Protein... with the given options identifying steps (a), (b), (c), (d):
questions.explanation: The central dogma flow is: DNA replication (DNA→DNA) → Transcription (DNA→RNA) → Translation (RNA→Protein), ending in the protein product. So (a)-Replication, (b)-Transcription, (c)-Translation, (d)-Protein.

questions.text: Length of the stem at time 0 is 20 cm. The arithmetic growth rate is 30 cm per day. What is the length of the stem at the end of the 7th day?
questions.explanation: For arithmetic growth, Length at time t = L0 + (growth rate × t) = 20 + (30 × 7) = 20 + 210 = 230 cm.

questions.text: The ovary is half inferior in:
questions.explanation: In plum flowers, the ovary is half-inferior (perigynous), positioned partway between superior and inferior, with the floral parts arising from around the middle of the ovary.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: A. Cristae, B. Cisternae, C. Thylakoids, D. Phospholipid
List-II: I. Flat membrane sacs in stroma of chloroplast, II. Infoldings in mitochondria, III. Cell membrane, IV. Disc shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane (II). Cisternae are the disc-shaped sacs stacked in the Golgi apparatus (IV). Thylakoids are flat membrane sacs within the stroma of the chloroplast (I). Phospholipids are the major structural component of the cell membrane (III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: Snow-blindness in Antarctic region is due to:
options: Freezing of fluids in the eye by low temperature
Inflammation of cornea due to high dose of UV-B radiation
High reflection of light from snow
Damage to retina caused by infra-red rays
questions.explanation: Snow blindness is caused by inflammation of the cornea (photokeratitis) due to excessive exposure to UV-B radiation, which is intensified by reflection off snow in regions with a depleted ozone layer, like Antarctica.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) GLUT-4 (B) Insulin (C) Trypsin (D) Collagen
List II: (I) Hormone (II) Enzyme (III) Intercellular ground substance (IV) Enables glucose transport into cells
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: GLUT-4 enables glucose transport into cells (A-IV). Insulin is a hormone (B-I). Trypsin is an enzyme (C-II). Collagen is an intercellular ground substance/structural protein (D-III). So A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III is correct.

questions.text: How many ATP and NADPH molecules are required to make one molecule of glucose through the Calvin pathway?
questions.topic: ATP and NADPH required for one glucose via Calvin pathway
questions.explanation: The Calvin cycle requires 18 ATP and 12 NADPH to synthesize one molecule of glucose.

questions.text: Which of the following rRNAs acts as structural RNA as well as ribozyme in bacteria?
questions.explanation: In bacteria, 23S rRNA (large ribosomal subunit) acts both as a structural RNA and as a ribozyme, catalyzing peptide bond formation (peptidyl transferase activity) during translation.

questions.text: In Bougainvillea thorns are the modifications of:
questions.explanation: In Bougainvillea, the axillary bud develops into a hard, pointed structure called a thorn, which is a modification of the stem, used for protection against browsing animals.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a steroid hormone?
questions.explanation: Glucagon is a peptide hormone secreted by pancreatic alpha cells, not a steroid hormone. Progesterone, Cortisol, and Testosterone are all steroid hormones derived from cholesterol.

questions.text: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called:
questions.explanation: Plasticity is the ability of plants to follow different developmental pathways in response to environmental conditions or life phases, forming different structures (e.g., heterophylly).

questions.text: Hormones secreted by the placenta to maintain pregnancy are
questions.explanation: The placenta secretes hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin), hPL (human placental lactogen), progestogens and estrogens, all of which play roles in maintaining pregnancy.

questions.text: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are produced at the end of glycolysis from 206 molecules of glucose?
questions.explanation: In glycolysis, each molecule of glucose (6 carbon) is broken down into 2 molecules of pyruvic acid (3 carbon each). So 206 molecules of glucose yield 206 × 2 = 412 molecules of pyruvic acid.

questions.text: Main steps in the formation of Recombinant DNA are given below. Arrange these steps in a correct sequence. (A) Insertion of recombinant DNA into the host cell. (B) Cutting of DNA at specific location by restriction enzyme. (C) Isolation of desired DNA fragment. (D) Amplification of gene of interest using PCR. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is: first cut the DNA at specific locations using restriction enzymes (B), then isolate the desired DNA fragment (C), amplify the gene of interest using PCR (D), and finally insert the recombinant DNA into the host cell (A). So the order is B, C, D, A.

questions.text: Which of the following stages of meiosis involves division of centromere?
questions.explanation: In Anaphase II of meiosis, the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles, similar to mitotic anaphase. In meiosis I, centromeres do not divide.

questions.text: Match Column-I with Column-II (floral formulae) with (i) Brassicaceae, (ii) Liliaceae, (iii) Fabaceae, (iv) Solanaceae.
questions.explanation: Matching each floral formula to its characteristic family pattern gives (a)-(iii) Fabaceae, (b)-(iv) Solanaceae, (c)-(ii) Liliaceae, (d)-(i) Brassicaceae.

questions.text: Oxygen is not produced during photosynthesis by
questions.explanation: Green sulphur bacteria perform anoxygenic photosynthesis, using H2S instead of H2O as the electron donor, and therefore do not produce oxygen, unlike Chara, Cycas and Nostoc which perform oxygenic photosynthesis.

questions.text: Identify the correct statements: A. Lenticels are the lens-shaped opening permitting the exchange of gases. B. Bark formed early in the season is called hard bark. C. Bark is a technical term that refers to all tissues exterior to vascular cambium. D. Bark refers to periderm and secondary phloem. E. Phellogen is single-layered in thickness. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.topic: Secondary Growth - Bark, Periderm and Lenticels
questions.explanation: Statement A is correct — lenticels are lens-shaped openings in the periderm that permit gas exchange. Statement B is incorrect — bark formed early in the season is called soft bark (not hard bark); hard bark forms late in the season. Statement C is incorrect — bark technically refers to all tissues exterior to the vascular cambium as a general term, but in this answer key it's marked incorrect; the specific correct term is given in D. Statement D is correct — bark specifically refers to the periderm and secondary phloem. Statement E is correct in general biology but marked not part of the correct set here. So A and D only are correct per the answer key.

questions.text: Among the following characters, which one was not considered by Mendel in his experiments on pea?
questions.explanation: Mendel studied seven contrasting characters in garden pea: seed shape, seed colour, pod shape, pod colour, flower colour, flower/pod position, and stem height. Trichome type (glandular or non-glandular) was not among the characters Mendel studied.

questions.text: Complete the flow chart on central dogma: (a)DNA --(b)--> mRNA --(c)--> (d)
questions.topic: Completing the central dogma flow chart
questions.explanation: Central dogma: DNA replicates (a-Replication), is transcribed to mRNA (b-Transcription), then translated to protein (c-Translation, d-Protein).

questions.text: Which of the following algae contains mannitol as reserve food material?
questions.explanation: Ectocarpus, a brown alga, stores mannitol (along with laminarin) as reserve food material.

questions.text: In gene therapy of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency, the patient requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes because:
options: Retroviral vector is introduced into these lymphocytes.
Gene isolated from marrow cells producing ADA is introduced into cells at embryonic stages
Lymphocytes from patient's blood are grown in culture, outside the body.
Genetically engineered lymphocytes are not immortal cells.
questions.explanation: Since the genetically engineered lymphocytes used in ADA gene therapy are not immortal cells, they eventually die out, requiring periodic infusion of the engineered cells to sustain therapeutic effect.

questions.text: For a person with blood group 'O', which of the following is not a possible combination of parents' blood group genotypes?
questions.explanation: Blood group O requires genotype ii, meaning both parents must be able to contribute an 'i' allele. Father IAIB has only IA and IB alleles to contribute (no 'i' allele), so this parent can never contribute an 'i' allele to produce an ii offspring -- making option (3) impossible. In options (1), (2), and (4), both parents carry an 'i' allele that they can pass on, making an ii (blood group O) offspring possible.

questions.text: Persons with 'AB' blood group are called as 'Universal recipients'. This is due to:
options: Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs
Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
Presence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, on RBCs
Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma
questions.topic: Reason AB blood group is universal recipient
questions.explanation: AB blood group individuals lack anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their plasma, allowing them to receive blood from any ABO group.

questions.text: When gene targeting involving gene amplification is attempted in an individual's tissue to treat disease, it is known as:
questions.explanation: Gene therapy involves correction of a gene defect by delivering a normal gene into an individual's cells/tissue to treat disease, as was done for ADA deficiency.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ligaments are dense irregular tissue. Statement II: Cartilage is dense regular tissue. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.explanation: Statement I is true — ligaments are made of dense irregular connective tissue (highly elastic). Statement II is false — cartilage is not a dense regular tissue; it is a specialized connective tissue with a solid matrix (chondrin), distinct from dense regular connective tissue like tendons.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I (Biological Molecules): (a) Glycogen (b) Globulin (c) Steroids (d) Thrombin
List-II (Biological functions): (i) Hormone (ii) Biocatalyst (iii) Antibody (iv) Storage product
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Glycogen is a storage product(iv), Globulin functions as antibody(iii), Steroids act as hormones(i), Thrombin is a biocatalyst/enzyme(ii). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(i),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: Which of the following protocols did aim for reducing emission of chlorofluorocarbons into the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol (1987) specifically aimed at reducing and phasing out emissions of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) that deplete the ozone layer.

questions.text:
Match Column-I with Column-II for housefly classification and select the correct option using the codes given below:
Column-I: a. Family, b. Order, c. Class, d. Phylum
Column-II: (i) Diptera, (ii) Arthropoda, (iii) Muscidae, (iv) Insecta
Codes:
(1) a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
(2) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
(3) a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
(4) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
questions.explanation: Housefly classification: Family = Muscidae, Order = Diptera, Class = Insecta, Phylum = Arthropoda. So a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

questions.text: Natality refers to
options: Number of individuals entering a habitat
Number of individuals leaving the habitat
questions.explanation: Natality is the birth rate within a population, representing the number of new individuals added through reproduction.

questions.text: Grass leaves curl inwards during very dry weather. Select the most appropriate reason from the following:
options: Shrinkage of air spaces in spongy mesophyll
questions.explanation: Grass leaves curl inward during dry weather due to flaccidity (loss of turgor) of bulliform cells, which reduces water loss by decreasing the exposed leaf surface area.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Ovulation is caused by LH surge leading to rupture of Graafian follicles.
Statement II: Graafian follicle remaining after ovulation transforms into corpus luteum and secretes large amount of estrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.topic: Menstrual Cycle - Ovulation and Corpus Luteum
questions.explanation: Ovulation is indeed triggered by a surge in luteinizing hormone (LH), which causes rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum -- Statement I is correct. However, the corpus luteum (formed from the remaining follicle after ovulation) primarily secretes large amounts of PROGESTERONE, not estrogen -- Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Bt cotton, (b) Adenosine deaminase deficiency, (c) RNAi, (d) PCR with (i) Gene therapy, (ii) Cellular defence, (iii) Detection of HIV infection, (iv) Bacillus thuringiensis
questions.explanation: Bt cotton involves the toxin gene from Bacillus thuringiensis (iv), Adenosine deaminase deficiency is treated via gene therapy (i), RNAi is used as a cellular defence mechanism against invading viruses/transposons (ii), and PCR is used for detection of HIV infection (iii). This matches a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

questions.text: The main function of bulliform cells in grasses is:
options: to minimize water loss during water stress
to make the leaf impermeable to fungal spores
questions.topic: Function of bulliform cells in grasses
questions.explanation: Bulliform cells help curl/roll the leaf during water stress, minimizing water loss through transpiration.

questions.text: All of the following are included in 'Ex-situ conservation' except
questions.explanation: Sacred groves are examples of in-situ conservation (protecting species within their natural habitat), whereas wildlife safari parks, seed banks and botanical gardens are all forms of ex-situ conservation (conservation outside the natural habitat).

questions.text: Select the correct statement.
options: Insulin acts on pancreatic cells and adipocytes.
questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids (like cortisol) stimulate gluconeogenesis (the formation of glucose from non-carbohydrate sources) in the liver, raising blood glucose levels; glucagon is associated with hyperglycemia (not hypoglycemia), insulin lowers (not raises) blood glucose and acts on liver/muscle/adipose tissue broadly, not specifically pancreatic cells.

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Clostridium butylicum, (b) Trichoderma polysporum, (c) Monascus purpureus, (d) Aspergillus niger with (i) Cyclosporin-A, (ii) Butyric Acid, (iii) Citric Acid, (iv) Blood cholesterol lowering agent
questions.explanation: Clostridium butylicum produces Butyric Acid (ii), Trichoderma polysporum is the source of the immunosuppressant Cyclosporin-A (i), Monascus purpureus produces the blood cholesterol-lowering agent statin (iv), and Aspergillus niger is used for Citric Acid production (iii). This matches a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Scapula, (b) Cranium, (c) Sternum, (d) Vertebral column with (i) Cartilaginous joints, (ii) Flat bone, (iii) Fibrous joints, (iv) Triangular flat bone.
questions.topic: Matching skeletal structure to bone/joint type
questions.explanation: Scapula is a triangular flat bone (iv); Cranium bones joined by fibrous joints (iii); Sternum is a flat bone (ii); Vertebral column has cartilaginous joints (i). (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II with respect to methods of Contraception and their respective actions.
List-I: (a) Diaphragms (b) Contraceptive Pills (c) Intra Uterine Devices (d) Lactational Amenorrhea
List-II: (i) Inhibit ovulation and Implantation (ii) Increase phagocytosis of sperm within uterus (iii) Absence of Menstrual cycle and ovulation following parturition (iv) They cover the cervix blocking the entry of sperms
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Diaphragms cover the cervix blocking sperm entry (iv); Contraceptive pills inhibit ovulation and implantation (i); IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperm within the uterus (ii); Lactational amenorrhea causes absence of menstrual cycle and ovulation following parturition (iii). (NCERT Class 12, Pg 60-61)

questions.text: Which of the following is not a prokaryote?
questions.explanation: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms (they have a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles). Blue green algae (cyanobacteria), Mycoplasma, and Bacteria are all prokaryotes.

questions.text: Which of the following algae produce Carrageen?
questions.explanation: Carrageenan (Carrageen) is a polysaccharide extracted from red algae (like Chondrus), used commercially as a gelling and thickening agent.

questions.text: Which micronutrient is required for splitting of water molecule during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Manganese is a required micronutrient for the photolysis (splitting) of water during the light reactions of photosynthesis, as part of the oxygen-evolving complex.

questions.text: In an ecosystem the Net Primary productivity (NPP) of first trophic level is 100x (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹, what would be the GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) of the third trophic level of the same ecosystem.
questions.explanation: Using the 10% law of energy transfer across trophic levels: NPP of first trophic level (producers) = 100x. Energy reaching second trophic level = 10x. Energy reaching third trophic level (GPP, taken as equal to energy received) = x (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹.

questions.text: With regard to insulin choose correct options. (a) C-peptide is not present in mature insulin. (b) The insulin produced by rDNA technology has C-peptide. (c) The pro-insulin has C-peptide. (d) A-peptide and B-peptide of insulin are interconnected by disulphide bridges.
questions.explanation: Mature insulin lacks the C-peptide, which is removed from pro-insulin (a, c true); A and B chains are connected by disulphide bridges (d true). rDNA-produced mature insulin also lacks C-peptide (b false). (a), (c) and (d) only.

questions.text: How many meiotic and mitotic divisions need to occur for the development of a mature female gametophyte from the megaspore mother cell in an angiosperm plant?
questions.topic: Megasporogenesis - Meiotic/Mitotic Divisions for Female Gametophyte
questions.explanation: The megaspore mother cell undergoes one meiotic division (meiosis) to form four haploid megaspores, and the functional megaspore undergoes 3 successive mitotic divisions to form the 8-nucleate, 7-celled mature embryo sac (female gametophyte). 12th NCERT - Page 11.

questions.text: How many molecules of ATP and NADPH are required for every molecule of CO2 fixed in the Calvin cycle?
options: 3 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
questions.topic: Calvin Cycle - ATP and NADPH Requirement per CO2
questions.explanation: For every CO2 molecule fixed in the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH are utilized. 11th NCERT Page No. 145.

questions.text: Conversion of glucose-6-phosphate, the first irreversible reaction of glycolysis, is catalyzed by:
questions.explanation: Hexokinase catalyzes the conversion of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, which is the first irreversible reaction in glycolysis.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Pterophyllum (B) Myxine (C) Pristis (D) Exocoetus
List II: (I) Hag fish (II) Saw fish (III) Angel fish (IV) Flying fish
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Pterophyllum is commonly known as angel fish (A-III). Myxine is the hag fish (B-I). Pristis is the saw fish (C-II). Exocoetus is the flying fish (D-IV). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV is correct.

questions.text:
The blue and white selectable markers have been developed which differentiate recombinant colonies from non-recombinant colonies on the basis of their ability to produce colour in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.
Given below are two statements about this method:
Statement I: The blue coloured colonies have DNA insert in the plasmid and they are identified as recombinant colonies.
Statement II: The colonies without blue colour have DNA insert in the plasmid and are identified as recombinant colonies.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Insertion of DNA into the lacZ gene region disrupts (inactivates) the gene, so recombinant colonies (with the DNA insert) cannot produce the enzyme that acts on the chromogenic substrate, and appear WHITE (colourless), not blue. Non-recombinant colonies (without insert) retain a functional lacZ gene and appear blue. So Statement I is incorrect, Statement II (colonies without blue colour = recombinant) is correct. 12th NCERT Page - 170 (Insertional inactivation).

questions.text: Select the incorrect statement regarding synapses:
options: The membranes of presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons are in close proximity in an electrical synapse.
Electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other across the electrical synapse.
Impulse transmission across a chemical synapse is always faster than that across an electrical synapse.
questions.explanation: Electrical synapses transmit impulses faster than chemical synapses because they allow direct current flow without the delay caused by neurotransmitter release and diffusion, making statement (4) incorrect.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: RNA mutates at a faster rate. Statement II: Virus having RNA genome and shorter life span mutate and evolve faster. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true — RNA mutates at a faster rate than DNA (due to lack of proofreading), and RNA viruses with shorter life spans consequently mutate and evolve faster, as per the NCERT reference on viral evolution (e.g., HIV, influenza).

questions.text: The plant hormone used to destroy weeds in a field is:
questions.topic: Plant hormone used as a weed killer
questions.explanation: 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) is a synthetic auxin widely used as a selective herbicide to kill broad-leaved weeds.

questions.text: Genus represents____________.
options: A population of plants and animals
A group of closely related species
A group of closely related families
questions.explanation: A genus is a taxonomic category comprising a group of closely related species that share more characteristics with each other than with species of other genera.

tests.title: NEET Full Mock Test 5 (180 Questions - Physics 45 + Chemistry 45 + Biology 90)
tests.description: A full-length 180-question, 180-minute NEET mock test in the real exam pattern - Physics 45, Chemistry 45, Biology 90 - built from real NEET previous-year questions, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: Two objects of mass 10 kg and 20 kg respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 10 m with negligible mass. The distance of the center of mass of the system from the 10 kg mass is:
questions.explanation: Taking the 10 kg mass as origin, center of mass distance = (m1*0 + m2*L)/(m1+m2) = (20*10)/(10+20) = 200/30 = 20/3 m.

questions.text: The ratio of frequencies of fundamental harmonic produced by an open pipe to that of closed pipe having the same length is:
questions.topic: Fundamental Frequency - Open vs Closed Pipe
questions.explanation: For an open pipe, fundamental frequency f0 = v/2l. For a closed pipe, fundamental frequency fc = v/4l. The ratio f0:fc = (v/2l):(v/4l) = 2:1.

questions.text: A small telescope has an objective of focal length 140 cm and an eye piece of focal length 5.0 cm. The magnifying power of telescope for viewing a distant object is:
questions.explanation: Magnifying power m = fo/fe = 140/5 = 28.

questions.text: The moment of inertia of a thin rod about an axis passing through its mid-point and perpendicular to the rod is 2400 g cm². The length of the 400 g rod is nearly:
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of a Rod - Finding Length

questions.text: Two particles of mass 5 kg and 10 kg respectively are attached to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 1 m with negligible mass. The centre of mass of the system from the 5 kg particle is nearly at a distance of:
questions.topic: Centre of mass of a two-particle system
questions.explanation: Distance of COM from 5kg mass = (m2×L)/(m1+m2) = (10×1)/(5+10) = 10/15 ≈ 0.67 m = 67 cm.

questions.text: A hollow metal sphere of radius R is uniformly charged. The electric field due to the sphere at a distance r from the centre:
options: Zero as r increases from r < R increases as r increases for r > R
decreases as r increases for r < R and for r > R
increases as r increases for r < R and for r > R
zero as r increases for r < R, decreases as r increases for r > R
questions.topic: Electric Field due to Charged Sphere
questions.explanation: For a hollow charged sphere, inside the sphere (r<R) the electric field is zero everywhere (no charge enclosed). Outside the sphere (r>R), field E=kQ/r^2, which decreases as r increases.

questions.text: A balloon is made of a material of surface tension S and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area A. It is filled with a gas of density ρ and takes a spherical shape of radius R. When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius r changes from R to 0(zero) in time T. If the speed v(r) of gas coming out of the balloon depends on r as rᵃ and T ∝ Sᵅ Aᵝ ργ Rᵟ then
questions.explanation: Using dimensional analysis on T ∝ SᵅAᵝργRᵟ: [M⁰L⁰T] = [MT⁻²]ᵅ[L²]ᵝ[ML⁻³]γ[L]ᵟ. Equating powers of M, L, T and solving gives option (3): a=−1/2, α=−1/2, β=−1, γ=1/2, δ=7/2.

If the magnitude of magnetic moment of the needle is x×10⁻⁵ A m²; then the value of 'x' is: [Figure: magnetic needle NS in uniform field B]
questions.topic: Oscillating Magnetic Needle - Magnetic Moment Calculation
