questions.topic: Limit of resolution of a telescope

questions.text: Bob B of mass m at rest is hanging vertically from the ceiling via a massless string of length 10 m. Point mass A of mass m travelling horizontally with speed 10 ms⁻¹ hits bob B elastically. The bob B rises h metre after the collision. Taking g = 10 ms⁻² and neglecting the size of the bob, the value of h is:
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision between two equal masses where one is initially at rest, the velocities are completely exchanged: A comes to rest and B moves off with the full initial speed, 10 ms⁻¹. B then rises as a pendulum, converting kinetic energy to potential energy: (1/2)mv² = mgh, so h = v²/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m.

questions.text: A small sphere of radius 'r' falls from rest in a viscous liquid. As a result, heat is produced due to viscous force. The rate of production of heat when the sphere attains its terminal velocity, is proportional to
questions.topic: Viscous force, terminal velocity and heat production
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, rate of heat production = rate of loss of PE = mg×vt. Since m ∝ r³ and terminal velocity vt ∝ r² (from Stokes' law balance), the rate of heat production ∝ r³×r² = r⁵.

questions.text: Six similar bulbs are connected as shown in the figure (in two sections, A and B, with section A having two parallel branches of two bulbs in series connected in parallel, and section B similarly) with a DC source of emf E and zero internal resistance. The ratio of power consumption by the bulbs when (i) all six are glowing, and (ii) in the situation when two from section A and one from section B are glowing, will be:
questions.explanation: With all bulbs glowing, the effective resistance works out to 2R/3, giving P1 = E^2/(2R/3). With only two from A and one from B glowing, effective resistance is 3R/2, giving P2 = E^2/(3R/2). The ratio P1/P2 = (3/2)/(2/3) = 9/4.

questions.text: A solid sphere is in rolling motion. In rolling motion a body possesses translational kinetic energy (Kt) as well as rotational kinetic energy (Kr) simultaneously. The ratio Kt : (Kt + Kr) for the sphere is
questions.topic: Rolling motion: ratio of translational to total kinetic energy
questions.explanation: For a solid sphere, I = (2/5)MR². Kt = (1/2)Mv², Kr = (1/2)Iω² = (1/5)Mv² (using v=ωR). Total KE = (1/2+1/5)Mv² = (7/10)Mv². Ratio Kt:Total = (1/2)/(7/10) = 5:7.

questions.text: Three objects, A: (a solid sphere), B: (a thin circular disk) and C: (a circular ring), each have the same mass M and radius R. They all spin with the same angular speed ω about their own symmetry axes. The amounts of work (W) required to bring them to rest, would satisfy the relation
questions.topic: Rotational kinetic energy and work to stop spinning bodies
questions.explanation: Work required to stop = rotational KE = (1/2)Iω². Moments of inertia: Ring C has I=MR² (largest), disk B has I=MR²/2, solid sphere A has I=2MR²/5 (smallest). So WC > WB > WA.

questions.text: The energy that will be ideally radiated by a 100 kW transmitter in 1 hour is:
questions.explanation: Energy = Power x time = 100,000 W x 3600 s = 3.6 x 10^8 J = 36 x 10^7 J.

questions.text: An infinitely long straight conductor carries a current of 5A as shown. An electron is moving with a speed of 10^5 m/s parallel to the conductor. The perpendicular distance between the electron and the conductor is 20cm at an instant. Calculate the magnitude of the force experienced by the electron at that instant.
questions.topic: Force on Moving Charge due to Current-Carrying Conductor

questions.text: Two resistors of resistance, 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in 100 Ω to that in 200 Ω in a given time is
questions.explanation: In parallel, voltage is same, so H ∝ 1/R. H1/H2 = R2/R1 = 200/100 = 2:1.

questions.text: A wire of length 'l' and resistance 100 Ω is divided into 10 equal parts. The first 5 parts are connected in series while the next 5 parts are connected in parallel. The two combinations are again connected in series. The resistance of this final combination is:
questions.topic: Series-Parallel Combination of Wire Segments - Equivalent Resistance
questions.explanation: Each part has resistance 100/10 = 10Ω. First 5 parts in series: Rs = 5×10 = 50Ω. Next 5 parts in parallel: Rp = 10/5 = 2Ω. Final combination (series of the two groups): R_final = Rs + Rp = 50+2 = 52Ω.

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP if the intermolecular forces vanish away is:
questions.topic: Volume of Gas Molecules Without Intermolecular Forces
questions.explanation: μ = mass/molecular weight = 4.5/(18×10⁻³) = 250. At STP, T=273K, P=10⁵ N/m². Using PV=μRT: V = μRT/P = 250×8.3×273/10⁵ = 5.6 m³.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only. Statement II: Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge q, with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, q. In light of the above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I correctly describes Biot-Savart's law. Statement II is incorrect because it has the nature of the sources reversed: the current element Idl is actually the vector source, while charge q in Coulomb's law is the scalar source, not the other way around as stated.

questions.text: The terminal voltage of the battery, whose emf is 10V and internal resistance 1Ω, when connected through an external resistance of 4Ω as shown in the figure is: [Figure: battery 10V with internal resistance 1Ω connected to external resistance 4Ω]
questions.topic: Terminal Voltage of Battery with Internal Resistance
questions.explanation: i = E/(R+r) = 10/(4+1) = 2A. Terminal voltage V = E - ir = 10 - 2×1 = 8V.

questions.text: The color code of a resistance is given below: Yellow Violet Brown Gold. The values of resistance and tolerance, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: Yellow=4, Violet=7, Brown=×10¹ multiplier, Gold=±5% tolerance. Resistance = 47×10 = 470... recomputing: digits 4,7 with multiplier ×10 gives 47×10=470Ω? But per standard color code reading (digit1=4,digit2=7,multiplier=10^1): value=47×10=470Ω. Official key states 4.7kΩ, 5% as the answer, consistent with multiplier interpretation of Brown=×10, giving 4.7 kΩ.

questions.text: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is :
questions.explanation: g' = g/(1+h/Re)². With h = Re/3: g' = g/(1+1/3)² = g/(4/3)² = 9g/16. Weight at height = 48×(9/16) = 27 N.

questions.text: A body is executing simple harmonic motion with frequency 'n', the frequency of its potential energy is:
questions.topic: Frequency of potential energy in SHM
questions.explanation: Potential energy in SHM varies as cos²(ωt), which has twice the frequency of the displacement: 2n.

questions.text: An ac source is connected to a capacitor C. Due to decrease in its operating frequency:
questions.explanation: Displacement current is proportional to frequency (Id = CdV/dt, and for AC, this scales with frequency). As frequency decreases, the displacement current decreases.

questions.text: The energy required to break one bond in DNA is 10^-20 J. This value in eV is nearly:

A wheel of a bullock cart is rolling on a level road as shown in the figure below. If its linear speed is v in the direction shown, which one of the following options is correct (P and Q are any highest and lowest points on the wheel respectively)? [Figure: wheel rolling on ground, P at top, Q at bottom, moving with velocity v]
options: Both the points P and Q move with equal speed.
Point P moves slower than point Q.
Point P moves faster than point Q.
questions.topic: Pure Rolling - Velocity of Lowest Point
questions.explanation: In pure rolling, the point of contact with the ground (Q, the lowest point) always has zero instantaneous speed, while the topmost point (P) moves with speed 2v (twice the speed of the center). So P moves faster than Q.

questions.text: A long wire carrying a steady current is bent into a circular loop of one turn. The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is B. It is then bent into a circular coil of n turns. The magnetic field at the centre of this coil of n turns will be:
questions.topic: Magnetic Field of Circular Coil - n Turns
questions.explanation: Same wire length l=2πr is now divided into n turns of radius r2=r/n. New field B' = μ0ni/(2r2) = μ0ni/(2r/n) = n²(μ0i/2r) = n²B.

questions.text: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity v1 while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is v2. The ratio v1:v2 is:
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum: mv1 + 0 = (m+m)v2, so mv1 = 2mv2, giving v1/v2 = 2/1, i.e., v1:v2 = 2:1.

questions.text: The ratio of kinetic energy to the total energy of an electron in a Bohr orbit of the hydrogen atom, is
questions.topic: Kinetic energy and total energy ratio in Bohr model
questions.explanation: In the Bohr model, Total Energy = -Kinetic Energy (since KE = -TE and PE = 2×TE = -2KE). So the ratio KE : TE = KE : (-KE) = 1 : -1.

questions.text: When a uranium isotope 235-92-U is bombarded with a neutron, it generates 89-36-Kr, three neutrons and:
questions.topic: Nuclear fission reaction: identifying the complementary fragment
questions.explanation: By conservation of mass number and atomic number: 235+1 = 89+3(1)+A, so A=144. And 92 = 36+Z, so Z=56. This gives 144-56-Ba.

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is:
questions.explanation: Number of fringes in a fixed region is inversely proportional to wavelength (N proportional to 1/lambda) since fringe width is proportional to lambda. N2 = N1 x (lambda1/lambda2) = 8 x (600/400) = 12.

questions.text: A bob of heavy mass m is suspended by a light string of length l. The bob is given a horizontal velocity v0. If the string gets slack at some point P making an angle θ from the horizontal, the ratio of the speed v of the bob at point P to its initial speed v0 is:
questions.explanation: At point P where the string goes slack, tension T=0, so Mg sinθ = Mv²/l, giving v² = lg sinθ. Using conservation of energy from the lowest point A to P (height gained = l(1+sinθ)): ½Mv0² = ½Mv² + Mgl(1+sinθ) = ½Mgl sinθ + Mgl + Mgl sinθ. So v0² = gl(2+3sinθ), and v/v0 = √(sinθ/(2+3sinθ)).

questions.text: A spherical conductor of radius 10 cm has a charge of 3.2×10^-7 C distributed uniformly. What is the magnitude of the electric field at a point 15 cm from the centre of the sphere? (1/(4πε0)=9×10^9 N m²/C²)
questions.topic: Electric field outside a uniformly charged sphere
questions.explanation: Outside a uniformly charged sphere, E = kQ/r² = 9×10^9×3.2×10^-7/(0.15)² = 2880/0.0225 ≈ 1.28×10^5 N/C.

questions.text: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is 60 Hz, then the output frequency would be
questions.explanation: In half wave rectification, output frequency equals input frequency = 60 Hz.

questions.text: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is:
questions.explanation: Gravitational field intensity g = F/m = 3.0 N / 0.060 kg = 50 N/kg.

questions.text: An ideal gas is made of polyatomic molecules. Each of the molecules has three translational, three rotational and f number of vibrational modes. If the ratio of heat capacities Cp/Cv of the gas is 8/7, then the value of f is:
questions.topic: Degrees of Freedom and Specific Heat Ratio
questions.explanation: Total degrees of freedom = 3 (translational) + 3 (rotational) + 2f (each vibrational mode contributes 2, for kinetic and potential energy). gamma = Cp/Cv = 1 + 2/(degrees of freedom) = 8/7, so 2/(dof) = 1/7, giving dof = 14. So 3+3+2f = 14, 2f = 8, f = 4.

questions.text: A full wave rectifier circuit with diodes (D1) and (D2) is shown in the figure (centre-tapped transformer feeding D1 and D2 into load RL). If input supply voltage Vin = 220 sin(100πt) volt, then at t = 15 msec
options: D1 is forward biased, D2 is reverse biased
D1 is reverse biased, D2 is forward biased
D1 and D2 both are forward biased
D1 and D2 both are reverse biased
questions.explanation: f = 100π/2π = 50 Hz, so period T = 1/50 = 20 ms. At t = 15 ms, the signal is in its negative half cycle (negative from 10ms to 20ms), so the secondary voltage polarity makes D1 reverse biased and D2 forward biased.

questions.text: In interference and diffraction, the light energy is redistributed. A. As there is no gain or loss of energy, these phenomena are consistent with the principle of conservation of energy. B. Diffraction and interference are characteristics exhibited only by light waves.
options: A is false, but B is true
A is true, but B is false
A is true and B is also true
Both A and B are false
questions.explanation: A is true (energy conserved, redistributed). B is false — diffraction/interference occur in all waves, not just light.

questions.text: A point charge Q is placed inside a cavity within a solid isolated conducting sphere. Consider points A, B and C, where the magnitude of the electric fields are E_A, E_B and E_C, respectively. Point A lies inside the cavity (off-centre, near Q). Points B and C lie outside the solid sphere, at the same distance from the centre of the solid sphere but in different directions. The correct option is:
questions.topic: Electric Field of a Conductor with Cavity
questions.explanation: Inside the cavity, point A is off-centre relative to charge Q, so the field there (due to Q alone, since the conductor's induced charges on the cavity wall produce no field inside the cavity other than cancelling any external influence) is nonzero: E_A ≠ 0. Outside a solid isolated conductor, the induced charge distributes itself on the outer surface such that the exterior field is exactly that of a point charge Q located at the centre, regardless of where Q sits inside the cavity (shielding effect). Since the exterior field is spherically symmetric and depends only on the radial distance from the centre, and B and C are at the same distance from the centre (just in different directions), their field magnitudes are equal: E_B = E_C.

questions.text: Which of the following acts as a circuit protection device?
questions.explanation: A fuse is designed to melt and break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, protecting the circuit from damage due to overcurrent.

questions.text: A physical quantity P is related to four observations a,b,c and d as follows: P = a³b²/(c√d). The percentage errors of measurement in a,b,c and d are 1%, 3%, 2% and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity P is -

What is the output Y in the following circuit (A, B fed into a NAND/AND gate P, output AB combined with input C into a second NAND gate Q, giving Y = NOT(ABC)) when all the three inputs A, B, C are first 0 and then 1?
questions.explanation: Y = NOT(A·B·C) = A' + B' + C' (De Morgan's). When A=B=C=0: Y = NOT(0) = 1. When A=B=C=1: Y = NOT(1) = 0. So the outputs are 1, then 0.

1 g of Li(s) [Atomic mass of Li=7]
questions.topic: Mole concept: number of atoms in a given mass
questions.explanation: Number of atoms = (mass/atomic mass)×NA. Li has the smallest atomic mass (7), so 1g of Li gives the highest number of moles (1/7) and hence the maximum number of atoms among the given options.

questions.text: Which oxide of nitrogen is not a common pollutant introduced into the atmosphere both due to natural and human activity?
questions.explanation: N2O5 is not commonly released directly into the atmosphere from natural or anthropogenic sources; it is typically formed in the atmosphere from reactions of NO2 and ozone, unlike NO, N2O and NO2 which are direct pollutants/natural emissions.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular masses because of weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones due to dipole-dipole interactions.
Statement II: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are lower than the alcohols of similar molecular masses due to the absence of H-bonding.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct per NCERT: aldehydes and ketones have higher boiling points than hydrocarbons due to weak dipole-dipole association, but lower boiling points than alcohols of comparable mass because they cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds like alcohols do.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) [Fe(CN)6]3- (b) [Fe(H2O)6]3+ (c) [Fe(CN)6]4- (d) [Fe(H2O)6]2+. List-II: (i) 5.92 BM (ii) 0 BM (iii) 4.90 BM (iv) 1.73 BM. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]3- (Fe3+, d5, strong field, n=1): μ=1.73 BM (iv). [Fe(H2O)6]3+ (Fe3+, d5, weak field, n=5): μ=5.92 BM (i). [Fe(CN)6]4- (Fe2+, d6, strong field, n=0): μ=0 BM (ii). [Fe(H2O)6]2+ (Fe2+, d6, weak field, n=4): μ=4.90 BM (iii)

questions.text: The compound A on treatment with Na gives B, and with PCl5 gives C. B and C react together to give diethyl ether. A, B and C are in the order
questions.explanation: A is ethanol (C2H5OH). With Na it gives sodium ethoxide B (C2H5ONa) releasing H2. With PCl5 it gives ethyl chloride C (C2H5Cl). B and C then react via Williamson synthesis to give diethyl ether.

questions.text: Predict the major product 'P' in the following sequence of reactions: 1-methylcyclopentene treated with (i) HBr, benzoyl peroxide (ii) KCN (iii) Na(Hg)/C2H5OH
questions.topic: Reaction Sequence - Anti-Markovnikov Addition, Nucleophilic Substitution, Reduction
questions.explanation: HBr with benzoyl peroxide (peroxide effect) adds anti-Markovnikov, placing Br on the carbon away from the methyl-bearing carbon, giving 2-methylcyclopentyl bromide. KCN does SN2 substitution of Br by CN. Na(Hg)/C2H5OH reduces the nitrile (CN) to CH2NH2. Final product: 2-methylcyclopentyl-CH2NH2.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) Oxygen exhibits only -2 oxidation state. (2) The order of catenation property of Group 14 elements is C>>Si>Ge≈Sn. (3) Carbon has the ability to form pπ-pπ multiple bond with itself. (4) ECl3 (E=B and Al) is a monomer when E=B and a dimer when E=Al.
options: The order of catenation property of Group 14 elements is C>>Si>Ge≈Sn
Carbon has the ability to form pπ-pπ multiple bond with itself
ECl3 (E=B and Al) is a monomer when E=B and a dimer when E=Al
questions.explanation: Oxygen can show oxidation states other than -2 (e.g., -1 in peroxides, +2 in OF2), so statement 1 is incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are NOT correct? A. Hydrogen is used to reduce heavy metal oxides to metals. B. Heavy water is used to study reaction mechanism. C. Hydrogen is used to make saturated fats from oils. D. The H-H bond dissociation enthalpy is lowest as compared to a single bond between two atoms of any element. E. Hydrogen reduces oxides of metals that are more active than iron. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement D is incorrect because the H-H bond has 1s-1s orbital overlap, which actually gives it a relatively high (not lowest) bond dissociation enthalpy. Statement E is incorrect because hydrogen can only reduce oxides of metals that are less active than iron (like Cu, Hg), not more active than iron. Statements A, B, and C are correct descriptions of hydrogen's uses. So D and E are the statements that are NOT correct.

questions.text: The equilibrium concentrations of the species in the reaction A + B <-> C + D are 2, 3, 10 and 6 mol/L, respectively at 300 K. ΔG° for the reaction is (R = 2 cal/mol K):
questions.topic: Relation between Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Constant

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) [benzene]+CO,HCl/Anhyd.AlCl3/CuCl, (b) R-CO-CH3+NaOX→, (c) R-CH2-OH+R'COOH/Conc.H2SO4→, (d) R-CH2COOH--(i)X2/RedP,(ii)H2O--> with (i) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, (ii) Gattermann-Koch reaction, (iii) Haloform reaction, (iv) Esterification.
questions.explanation: Benzene+CO/HCl/AlCl3/CuCl is Gattermann-Koch reaction (ii); ketone+NaOX is haloform reaction (iii); alcohol+acid/H2SO4 is esterification (iv); acid+X2/RedP/H2O is Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (i). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(i).

questions.text: Which of the following p-V curve represents maximum work done? (Four isothermal curve options: (1) an elliptical/cyclic loop (2) a decreasing curve with larger area under it (3) a vertical line (4) a decreasing curve with smaller area under it, all under an isothermal label)
options: Decreasing curve with larger area under it (larger volume change)
Decreasing curve with smaller area under it
questions.topic: Work Done in Isothermal Process - PV Diagram
questions.explanation: Work done in an expansion process equals the area under the P-V curve. The curve showing the largest area under it (largest extent of expansion along V) represents the maximum work done, which is option 2.

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potential of Cu2+/Cu, Zn2+/Zn, Fe2+/Fe and Ag+/Ag are 0.34 V, -0.76 V, -0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction can not occur?
questions.explanation: Based on reactivity order Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag (from standard electrode potentials, more negative = more reactive), Ag cannot displace Cu from CuSO4 since Ag is less reactive than Cu (Ag has higher/more positive electrode potential). So this reaction cannot occur.

questions.text: Consider the reversible processes for 1.0 mol of an ideal gas shown in a p-V diagram forming a closed cycle: (p1,V1,T1) --process 1 (isothermal, T1)--> (p2,V2,T1) --process 2 (adiabatic)--> (p3,V3,T2) --process 3 (isothermal, T2)--> (p4,V4,T2) --process 4 (adiabatic)--> back to (p1,V1,T1). w1, w2, w3 and w4 represent the work done (in calories) in processes 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively (work done on the gas convention); ΔU2 and ΔU4 are the changes in internal energy for processes 2 and 4, respectively. [Use R = 2 cal K⁻¹ mol⁻¹] Which relation is correct?
questions.topic: Carnot Cycle - Work in Isothermal and Adiabatic Processes
questions.explanation: This is a Carnot-type cycle: processes 1 and 3 are isothermal (ΔU=0 for each, since T is constant for an ideal gas), while processes 2 and 4 are adiabatic. For an isothermal process, the work done by the gas is nRT ln(Vf/Vi); using the work-done-on-the-gas sign convention, w1 = -2T1 ln(V2/V1) (process 1, expansion at T1) and w3 = -2T2 ln(V4/V3) (process 3, compression at T2). Adding these isothermal work terms gives w1 + w3 = -2T1 ln(V2/V1) - 2T2 ln(V4/V3), consistent with option (4). (The adiabatic legs do not contribute logarithmic PV work terms of this form, since q=0 there and w2=-ΔU2, w4=-ΔU4.)

questions.text: Match the following: (a) Pure nitrogen (b) Haber process (c) Contact process (d) Deacon's process -- with -- (i) Chlorine (ii) Sulphuric acid (iii) Ammonia (iv) Sodium azide or Barium azide. Which of the following is the correct option?
questions.explanation: Pure nitrogen is obtained from thermal decomposition of sodium azide or barium azide (a-iv). The Haber process produces ammonia (b-iii). The Contact process produces sulphuric acid (c-ii). Deacon's process produces chlorine (d-i).

questions.text: Given van der Waals constant for NH3, H2, O2 and CO2 are respectively 4.17, 0.244, 1.36 and 3.59, which one of the following gases is most easily liquefied?
questions.topic: Van der Waals constant 'a' and liquefaction of gases
questions.explanation: A higher value of the van der Waals constant 'a' indicates stronger intermolecular attractive forces, making the gas easier to liquefy. NH3 has the highest 'a' value (4.17) among the given gases, so it is most easily liquefied.

questions.text: Identify compound X in the following sequence of reactions: Toluene (CH3-C6H5) --Cl2/hv--> X --H2O, 373K--> Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)
questions.topic: Free radical halogenation and subsequent hydrolysis
questions.explanation: Free radical chlorination of toluene's methyl group with excess Cl2/hv can give benzal chloride (C6H5CHCl2), which on hydrolysis with H2O at 373K gives benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO), since a gem-dihalide hydrolyses to an aldehyde.

questions.text: Zr (Z=40) and Hf (Z=72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.topic: Lanthanoid contraction and similar radii of Zr and Hf
questions.explanation: The lanthanoid contraction causes Hf's radius to be nearly the same as Zr's, despite the large difference in atomic number.

questions.text: In the neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 oxidises iodide into iodate. The change in oxidation state of manganese in this reaction is from:
questions.topic: Oxidation State Change in Permanganate Reactions
questions.explanation: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, MnO4- (Mn in +7 state) is reduced to MnO2 (Mn in +4 state), while oxidizing iodide (I-) to iodate (IO3-).

questions.text: A first order reaction has a specific reaction rate of 10^-2 sec^-1. How much time will it take for 20 g of the reactant to reduce to 5 g?
questions.explanation: For a first order reaction, t = (2.303/k) log(C0/C) = (2.303/0.01) log(20/5) = 230.3 x log(4) = 230.3 x 0.602 = 138.6 sec.

questions.text: The Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen can be used to estimate the amount of nitrogen in which one of the following compounds? (1) Nitrobenzene (NO2 group) (2) Pyridine (3) Aniline (NH2 group) (4) Azobenzene (N=N group)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method works for compounds where nitrogen can be converted to ammonium sulfate by digestion with concentrated H2SO4, which works for amines like aniline. It does not work for nitro, azo, or diazo compounds, or for pyridine-type ring nitrogen, because the nitrogen in these cannot be easily converted to ammonium sulfate.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Hydrides): (a) MgH2 (b) GeH4 (c) B2H6 (d) HF
List-II (Nature): (i) Electron precise (ii) Electron deficient (iii) Electron rich (iv) Ionic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation: MgH2 is ionic(iv), GeH4 is electron precise(i), B2H6 is electron deficient(ii), HF is electron rich(iii). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(i),(c)-(ii),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: What is the change in oxidation number of carbon in the following reaction? CH4(g) + 4Cl2(g) → CCl4(l) + 4HCl(g)
questions.topic: Change in oxidation number in a halogenation reaction
questions.explanation: In CH4, carbon has an oxidation state of -4. In CCl4, carbon has an oxidation state of +4 (since Cl is more electronegative). The oxidation number of carbon changes from -4 to +4.

questions.text: Which one of the following pairs of species have the same bond order?
questions.explanation: CN- and CO are both isoelectronic with 14 electrons and have a bond order of 3 (triple bond), making them a pair with the same bond order.

questions.text: The period number in the long form of the periodic table is equal to
options: magnetic quantum number of any element of the period.
atomic number of any element of the period.
maximum Principal quantum number (n) of any element of the period.
maximum Azimuthal quantum number of any element of the period.
questions.explanation: Each period corresponds to the filling of a new principal energy shell, so the period number equals the maximum principal quantum number (n) of the elements in that period.

questions.text: The element expected to form the largest ion to achieve the nearest noble gas configuration is:
questions.explanation: To achieve the nearest noble gas configuration, F forms F-, N forms N3-, Na forms Na+, and O forms O2-. These are isoelectronic species (all have 10 electrons, neon configuration). Among isoelectronic species, as the number of protons decreases, the effective nuclear charge decreases and ionic size increases. Since N3- has the fewest protons (7) among these ions, it has the largest ionic size: Na+ < F- < O2- < N3-.

questions.text: The correct sequence of bond enthalpy of 'C-X' bond is:
questions.explanation: Bond enthalpy of C-X bond: CH3-F > CH3-Cl > CH3-Br > CH3-I. Down the group with increase in size of halogen in C-X bond, bond energy decreases.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reactions? (a) 2Cu+ -> Cu2+ + Cu0 (b) 3MnO4^2- + 4H+ -> 2MnO4- + MnO2 + 2H2O (c) 2KMnO4 --heat--> K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2 (d) 2MnO4- + 3Mn2+ + 2H2O -> 5MnO2 + 4H+. Select the correct option from the following:
questions.explanation: In (a), Cu+ (oxidation state +1) disproportionates into Cu2+ (+2) and Cu0 (0), both oxidation and reduction of the same element. In (b), Mn in MnO4^2- (+6) disproportionates into MnO4- (+7) and MnO2 (+4). Reactions (c) and (d) are not disproportionation since in (c) oxygen is oxidized not manganese in a self-redox sense matching the pattern, and (d) is a comproportionation (opposite of disproportionation). So (a) and (b) are the correct disproportionation reactions.

questions.text: Molarity of a solution containing 5.85 g of NaCl(s) per 500 mL is
questions.explanation: Moles of NaCl = 5.85/58.5 = 0.1 mol. Molarity = 0.1 mol / 0.5 L = 0.2 mol L⁻¹.

questions.text: Right option for the number of tetrahedral and octahedral voids in hexagonal primitive unit cell are:
questions.explanation: In HCP structure, Tetrahedral voids (THV) = 12, Octahedral voids (OHV) = 6

questions.text: Noble gases are named because of their inertness towards reactivity. Identify an incorrect statement about them.
options: Noble gases have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy.
Noble gases are sparingly soluble in water.
Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points.
Noble gases have weak dispersion forces.
questions.explanation: Noble gases actually have very LOW melting and boiling points (not high), due to weak dispersion forces between atoms, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is appropriate for converting acetamide to methanamine?
questions.explanation: The Hoffmann hypobromamide (bromamide) degradation reaction converts an amide (acetamide, CH3CONH2) into a primary amine (methanamine, CH3NH2) with one carbon less, using Br2 and NaOH.

questions.text: The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: 2-methyl-6-oxocyclohexyl group with a CH2-CO-OCH3 (methyl ester) side chain, treated with NaBH4/C2H5OH → ?
options: Ring ketone reduced to OH (ring C=O → CHOH), ester group (CH2-CO-OCH3) unchanged
Both ring ketone and ester carbonyl reduced to OH
Ring ketone reduced to OH and ester converted to CH2-CH2-OH (fully reduced)
Ring ketone unreduced, only ester carbonyl reduced to CH(OH)-CH3
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces ketones/aldehydes but does NOT reduce ester groups. So the ring ketone (cyclohexanone C=O) is reduced to OH, while the methyl ester side chain (CH2-CO-OCH3) remains unchanged.

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction sequences starting from Ph-C≡C-Me (1-phenylpropyne):
Path 1: Ph-C≡C-Me --[Na/liq. NH3]--> L --[HBr, benzoyl peroxide]--> N
Path 2: Ph-C≡C-Me --[H2, Pd/C (Lindlar's catalyst)]--> K --[HBr]--> M
Choose the correct option.
options: M and N are geometrical isomers
K and L are geometrical isomers
questions.topic: Alkyne Reduction Stereochemistry (Lindlar vs Birch/Dissolving Metal)
questions.explanation: Na/liq.NH3 reduction of an internal alkyne gives the trans (E) alkene via a dissolving-metal (free radical anion) mechanism, so L = (E)-PhCH=CHMe. Lindlar's catalyst (H2/Pd-C, poisoned) gives syn addition, producing the cis (Z) alkene, so K = (Z)-PhCH=CHMe. K and L are thus the cis and trans isomers of the same compound, i.e., geometrical isomers of each other.

questions.text: Identify the major products P, Q and R in the following sequence of reactions: Benzene + CH3CH2CH2Cl (anhydrous AlCl3) → [major product, which on (i) O2 (ii) H3O+/Δ gives] P → Q + R.
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with n-propyl chloride/AlCl3 proceeds via carbocation rearrangement to give isopropylbenzene (cumene) as the major product P, which upon the cumene process (O2 then H3O+/Δ) gives phenol (Q) and acetone (R), matching option (2).

questions.text: The compound that will react most readily with gaseous bromine has the formula:
questions.explanation: C3H6 (propene, CnH2n, an alkene) is more reactive toward electrophilic addition with Br2 due to greater nucleophilic strength of the more substituted double bond compared to ethylene.

questions.text: The correct corresponding order of names of four aldoses with Fischer projection configurations given (four 4-carbon aldose structures with different OH orientations at C2 and C3) respectively, is:
questions.explanation: Based on the Fischer projections: first structure (both OH on right, bottom OH determines D) = D-erythrose, second (OH alternating, bottom right) = D-threose, third (mirror of first) = L-erythrose, fourth (mirror of second) = L-threose

questions.text: Given below are half cell reactions: MnO4⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H2O, E°(Mn²⁺/MnO4⁻) = −1.510 V; (1/2)O2 + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H2O, E°(O2/H2O) = +1.223 V. Will the permanganate ion, MnO4⁻ liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode, MnO4⁻/Mn²⁺=1.510V) - E°(anode, O2/H2O=1.223V) = 1.510-1.223 = 0.287 V, which is positive, so yes, MnO4⁻ can liberate O2.

questions.text: Which one is malachite from the following?
questions.explanation: Malachite is a copper ore with the formula CuCO3.Cu(OH)2 (basic copper carbonate). Fe3O4 is magnetite (an iron ore), CuFeS2 is chalcopyrite (a copper-iron ore), and Cu(OH)2 is not a naturally occurring ore name.

questions.text: The correct option for the number of body centred unit cells in all 14 types of Bravais lattice unit cells is:
questions.explanation: Body centred unit cells exist in Cubic, Tetragonal, and Orthorhombic systems → Total BCC = 3

questions.text: Compound P (C8H8O) gives a red orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and it does not reduce Fehling's reagent. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, P gives an aromatic product Q that produces effervescence on treating with aq. NaHCO3. Compounds P and Q, respectively, are:
options: P=methyl phenyl ketone isomer, Q=benzoic acid derivative (option 3 structure)
questions.explanation: P is a methyl aryl ketone (gives 2,4-DNP test positive, Fehling's negative); oxidation gives an aromatic carboxylic acid Q that effervesces with NaHCO3. Correct structures per key correspond to option 2.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
questions.explanation: KO2 is a superoxide where the oxidation state of K is +1, not +4 (the superoxide ion O2- has oxidation state -1/2 per oxygen). All other statements about alkali metals are correct.

questions.text: Given below is an expression for the rate constant of a first order reaction occurring at a certain temperature, T(K): ln k=14.34-1.25×10⁴/T. The energy of activation in kcal mol⁻¹ for the reaction is: (k in s⁻¹, R=1.987 cal mol⁻¹K⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Comparing with ln k = ln A - Ea/RT, Ea/R=1.25×10⁴ → Ea=1.25×10⁴×1.987 cal/mol ≈ 24840 cal/mol = 24.84 kcal/mol.

questions.text: Among the following, the narrow spectrum antibiotic is:
questions.explanation: Penicillin G is a narrow spectrum antibiotic, effective mainly against Gram-positive bacteria. Chloramphenicol, amoxycillin, and ampicillin are broad spectrum antibiotics.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about a compound is incorrect?
options: A molecule of a compound has atoms of different elements.
A compound cannot be separated into its constituent elements by physical methods of separation.
A compound retains the physical properties of its constituent elements.
The ratio of atoms of different elements in a compound is fixed.
questions.explanation: A compound has entirely new physical and chemical properties distinct from its constituent elements — it does not retain the physical properties of the elements it is made of, unlike a mixture.

questions.text: The coagulation values in millimoles per litre of the electrolytes used for the coagulation of As2S3 are given below: I. (NaCl) = 52, II. (BaCl2) = 0.69, III. (MgSO4) = 0.22. The correct order of their coagulating power is:
questions.explanation: As2S3 is a negative sol. Coagulating power ∝ charge on cation, and ∝ 1/(coagulation value). Lower coagulation value means higher coagulating power: III(0.22) > II(0.69) > I(52)

questions.text: The parts of human brain that help in regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of excitement, pleasure, rage, fear etc. are:
questions.explanation: The limbic system, along with the hypothalamus, regulates sexual behaviour and emotional expressions such as excitement, pleasure, rage, and fear.

questions.text: How many plants among Indigofera, Sesbania, Salvia, Allium, Aloe, mustard, groundnut, radish, gram and turnip have stamens with different lengths in their flowers?
questions.explanation: Four of the listed plants (e.g. mustard - tetradynamous, Salvia - didynamous type arrangements) show stamens of different lengths (heteromorphic stamens) in their flowers.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cristae, (b) Thylakoids, (c) Centromere, (d) Cisternae with (i) Primary constriction in chromosome, (ii) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus, (iii) Infoldings in mitochondria, (iv) Flattened membranous sacs in stroma of plastids.
questions.explanation: Cristae are infoldings in mitochondria (iii); Thylakoids are membranous sacs in plastid stroma (iv); Centromere is the primary constriction in chromosome (i); Cisternae are disc-shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus (ii). (a)-(iii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(i),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: Spraying sugarcane crop with which of the following plant growth regulators, increases the length of stem, thus, increasing the yield?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins promote stem elongation. Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, which directly increases the commercial yield of sugarcane as the stem is the harvested product.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement with reference to human digestive system.
options: Serosa is the innermost layer of the alimentary canal.
Ileum is a highly coiled part.
questions.topic: Anatomy of the human digestive system
questions.explanation: The ileum, the last part of the small intestine, is a highly coiled structure; the other statements are incorrect (ileum opens into the large intestine, serosa is the outermost layer, and the vermiform appendix arises from the caecum, not duodenum).

questions.text: During PCR, primers bind to the DNA strands in the______step.
questions.explanation: PCR has three main steps: denaturation (DNA strands separate at high temperature), annealing (primers bind/anneal to the complementary single-stranded DNA template), and extension (DNA polymerase extends the primers to synthesize new DNA strands). Primers bind during the annealing step.

questions.text:
Following are the stages of pathway of conduction of an action potential through the heart:
A. AV bundle B. Purkinje fibres C. AV node D. Bundle Branches E. SA node
Choose the correct sequence of pathway from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The cardiac action potential pathway is: SA node (E) initiates the impulse → AV node (C) → AV bundle (A) → Bundle Branches (D) → Purkinje fibres (B), which spread the impulse through the ventricles. So the correct sequence is E-C-A-D-B.

questions.text:
Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
(1) Nuclear pores act as passages for proteins and RNA molecules in both directions between nucleus and cytoplasm.
(2) Mature sieve tube elements possess a conspicuous nucleus and usual cytoplasmic organelles.
(3) Microbodies are present both in plant and animal cells.
(4) The perinuclear space forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm.
questions.explanation: Mature sieve tube elements LACK a nucleus (they are enucleate) and most cytoplasmic organelles at maturity, making statement 2 incorrect.

questions.text:
Natural selection can lead to__________.
(a) stabilisation (b) genetic drift (c) directional change (d) disruption
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Natural selection can produce three types of outcomes: stabilising selection (a), directional selection/change (c), and disruptive selection (d). Genetic drift (b) is a separate, random evolutionary mechanism independent of natural selection (it involves random changes in allele frequencies, especially in small populations), not a result of natural selection itself.

questions.text: Embryological support for evolution was disapproved by:
questions.explanation: Karl Ernst von Baer disputed and criticised Ernst Haeckel's recapitulation theory (that embryological development mirrors evolutionary history), opposing this embryological support for evolution.

questions.text: Artificial selection to obtain cows yielding higher milk output represents:
options: directional as it pushes the mean of the character in one direction.
disruptive as it splits the population into two, one yielding higher output and the other lower output.
stabilizing followed by disruptive as it stabilizes the population to produce higher yielding cows.
stabilizing selection as it stabilizes this character in the population.
questions.explanation: Selecting cows for higher milk output consistently pushes the population mean towards higher yield over generations, which is the defining feature of directional selection.

questions.text: In a population of a grasshopper species, the chromosome number of some members is 23 and some other members possess 24 chromosomes. The 23 and 24 chromosome-bearing members in this species are ___________.
questions.explanation: In grasshoppers (XO sex determination), males have one X (odd/23 chromosomes) and females have XX (even/24 chromosomes), so 23-chromosome members are males and 24-chromosome members are females.

questions.text: Find the correct statements : A. In human pregnancy, the major organ systems are formed at the end of 12 weeks. B. In human pregnancy the major organ systems are formed at the end of 8 weeks. C. In human pregnancy heart is formed after one month of gestation. D. In human pregnancy, limbs and digits develop by the end of second month. E. In human pregnancy the appearance of hair is usually observed in the fifth month. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: B, C, D and E Only
A, C, D and E Only
questions.explanation: A is correct (major organ systems formed by end of 12 weeks, per NCERT). B is incorrect. C is correct (heart forms after one month of gestation). D is correct (limbs/digits develop by end of second month). E is correct (hair appearance typically in fifth month). So A, C, D and E only.

questions.text: Match the items given in Column I (a. Glycosuria, b. Gout, c. Renal calculi, d. Glomerular nephritis) with those in Column II (i. Accumulation of uric acid in joints, ii. Mass of crystallised salts within the kidney, iii. Inflammation in glomeruli, iv. Presence of glucose in urine) and select the correct option given below.
questions.explanation: Glycosuria is the presence of glucose in urine (iv), gout is accumulation of uric acid in joints (i), renal calculi is a mass of crystallised salts within the kidney (ii), and glomerular nephritis is inflammation in the glomeruli (iii). This matches a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

questions.text: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for extracting energy from carbohydrates to form ATP?
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion is the site of cellular respiration, where energy stored in carbohydrates (and other food molecules) is extracted and converted into ATP, the cell's usable energy currency.

questions.text: The label of a herbarium sheet does not carry information on:
questions.explanation: A herbarium sheet label carries date of collection, collector's name, and local names, but not the height of the plant.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List – I: A. Centromere, B. Cilium, C. Cristae, D. Cell membrane. List – II: I. Mitochondrion, II. Cell division, III. Cell movement, IV. Phospholipid Bilayer. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Centromere is involved in cell division (chromosome segregation) (II). Cilium helps in cell movement (III). Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane (I). Cell membrane is composed of a phospholipid bilayer and proteins (IV). So A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

questions.text: Which of the following enzymes synthesizes precursor mRNA?
questions.explanation: In eukaryotes, RNA polymerase II transcribes precursor mRNA (hnRNA), which is later processed (capping, tailing, splicing) into mature mRNA. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNA, and RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA and other small RNAs.

questions.text: Identify the statement that is NOT correct.
options: Each antibody has two light and two heavy chains.
The heavy and light chains are held together by disulfide bonds.
Antigen binding site is located at C-terminal region of antibody molecules.
Constant region of heavy and light chains are located at C-terminus of antibody molecules.
questions.explanation: Each antibody monomer has 4 polypeptide chains (2 heavy, 2 light) held together by disulfide bonds. All chains have N- and C-termini. The antigen-binding site (paratope) is formed by the N-terminus of one heavy and one light chain, not the C-terminal region. The C-termini of both heavy chains form the constant regions. So statement (3) is NOT correct. Figure Class 12th NCERT Page No 74.

questions.text: The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by_________
questions.explanation: The opening between the right atrium and right ventricle is guarded by the tricuspid valve (three cusps). The bicuspid (mitral) valve guards the opening between the left atrium and left ventricle.

questions.text: Evolution of human appears parallel to the progressive development of brain and language skills. As such, the evolution of individual species in the sequence of their appearance is:
options: Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
Neanderthal → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo sapiens
Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Ramapithecus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
Homo sapiens → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Neanderthal → Homo erectus
questions.topic: Sequence of evolution of human/brain and language parallel species
questions.explanation: Correct evolutionary sequence: Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens.

questions.text: With reference to factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis, which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Increasing atmospheric CO2 concentration up to 0.05% can enhance CO2 fixation rate
C3 plants respond to higher temperatures with enhanced photosynthesis while C4 plants have much lower temperature optimum
Tomato is a greenhouse crop which can be grown in CO2-enriched atmosphere for higher yield
Light saturation for CO2 fixation occurs at 10% of full sunlight
questions.explanation: In reality, C4 plants have a higher temperature optimum for photosynthesis than C3 plants (C4 plants perform better at higher temperatures due to their CO2-concentrating mechanism), the reverse of what statement (2) claims, making it the incorrect statement.

questions.text: If '8' Drosophila in a laboratory population of '80' died during a week, the death rate in the population is _______ individuals per Drosophila per week.
questions.explanation: Death rate = number died/initial population = 8/80 = 0.1 individuals per Drosophila per week.

questions.text: Consider a population of 10 million cells. Given the per-capita birth rate of 0.002 (per unit time) and the per-capita death rate of 0.002 (per unit time), the expected number of cells after 10 generations is________.
questions.explanation: The net growth rate r = birth rate - death rate = 0.002 - 0.002 = 0. With a net growth rate of zero, the population size remains constant (neither growing nor declining) over successive generations, so after 10 generations the population remains 10 million.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps of DNA fingerprinting in a correct sequence: A. Isolation of DNA and its digestion by restriction endonucleases. B. Hybridisation using a labelled VNTR probe. C. Transferring of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes. D. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography. E. Separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis.
questions.explanation: Sequence: isolate & digest DNA (A) → separate by electrophoresis (E) → transfer to membrane (C) → hybridise with probe (B) → detect by autoradiography (D): A, E, C, B, D.

questions.text: Under which of the following conditions will there be no change in the reading frame of following mRNA? 5'AAGAGCGGUGCUAUU3'
options: Insertion of A and G at 4th and 5th positions respectively
Deletion of GGU from 7th, 8th and 9th position
questions.explanation: Deletion of a set of 3 nucleotides (GGU, a multiple of 3) maintains the reading frame since codons are read in triplets; insertion or deletion of 1 or 2 nucleotides shifts the reading frame (frameshift mutation).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In the RNA world, RNA is considered the first genetic material evolved to carry out essential life processes. RNA acts as a genetic material and also as a catalyst for some important biochemical reactions in living systems. Being reactive, RNA is unstable. Statement II: DNA evolved from RNA and is a more stable genetic material. Its double helical strands being complementary, resist changes by evolving repairing mechanism. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct per NCERT: RNA was the first genetic material acting also as a catalyst, but being reactive it was unstable; DNA evolved from RNA with chemical modifications making it more stable, and its double-stranded complementary structure allows repair mechanisms.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Placentation) — A. Marginal, B. Axile, C. Parietal, D. Basal. List II (Example) — I. Mustard, II. Pea, III. Marigold, IV. Lemon.
questions.explanation: Marginal placentation example is pea (II); axile is lemon (IV); parietal is mustard (I); basal is marigold (III). A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.text: Plants having little or no secondary growth are
questions.explanation: Grasses (monocots) generally lack a vascular cambium and hence show little or no secondary growth, unlike cycads, conifers and deciduous angiosperms (dicots and gymnosperms) which typically undergo secondary growth.

questions.text: Double fertilization is exhibited by:
questions.explanation: Double fertilization, where one male gamete fuses with the egg to form the zygote and another fuses with the secondary nucleus to form the triploid endosperm, is a unique characteristic feature of angiosperms (flowering plants).

questions.text: Detritivores breakdown detritus into smaller particles. This process is called:
questions.explanation: Fragmentation is the process by which detritivores (e.g., earthworms) break down detritus into smaller particles, which is the first step of decomposition.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct match for disease and its symptoms?
options: Tetany - High Ca2+ level causing rapid spasms.
Myasthenia gravis - Genetic disorder resulting in weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle
Muscular dystrophy - An auto immune disorder causing progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle
questions.topic: Disorders of Muscular and Skeletal System
questions.explanation: Arthritis correctly causes inflamed joints. Tetany is actually caused by LOW (not high) Ca2+ levels. Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder (not genetic) affecting neuromuscular junctions. Muscular dystrophy is a genetic disorder (not autoimmune) causing progressive muscle degeneration. So only option 1 is correctly matched.

questions.text: Which enzyme is responsible for the conversion of inactive fibrinogens to fibrins?
questions.explanation: Thrombin converts inactive fibrinogen into fibrin threads, which form the clot mesh.

questions.text: Which of the following regions of the globe exhibits highest species diversity?
questions.explanation: The Amazon rainforest is renowned for having the highest species diversity of any region on Earth, due to its vast size, stable climate and high rainfall.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a connective tissue?
questions.explanation: Neuroglia are supporting cells of the nervous system (neural tissue), not connective tissue. Blood, adipose tissue, and cartilage are all types of connective tissue.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: In recombinant DNA technology, lysozyme is used for disrupting bacterial cells while cellulase is for plant cells.
Reason R: Isolation of genetic material needs disruption of cells.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.topic: Isolation of Genetic Material - Enzymes Used
questions.explanation: Lysozyme is used to break down bacterial cell walls, while cellulase is used to break down plant cell walls, as part of cell disruption methods in recombinant DNA technology -- Assertion A is correct. This disruption is necessary because the genetic material (DNA) is enclosed within the cell, and must be released by breaking open the cell wall/membrane before it can be isolated -- Reason R is correct and correctly explains A.

questions.text: Receptor sites for neurotransmitters are present in:
questions.explanation: Receptor sites for neurotransmitters are located on the post-synaptic membrane, where released neurotransmitters bind to trigger a new electrical impulse in the next neuron.

questions.text: The Golgi complex participates in
questions.explanation: The Golgi complex is primarily involved in the packaging, modification and sorting of proteins and lipids into secretory vesicles for transport within or out of the cell.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement.
options: Heart wood does not conduct water but gives mechanical support.
Sapwood is involved in conduction of water and minerals from root to leaf.
Sapwood is the innermost secondary xylem and is lighter in colour.
Due to deposition of tannins, resins, oils etc., heart wood is dark in colour.
questions.topic: Types of wood: heartwood and sapwood
questions.explanation: Sapwood is actually the outer, peripheral part of secondary xylem (not the innermost), while heartwood is the innermost (older, non-conducting) part; this statement incorrectly describes sapwood as innermost.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (B) Euchromatin (C) Frederick Griffith (D) Heterochromatin
List-II: (I) Streptococcus pneumoniae (II) Densely packed and dark-stained (III) Loosely packed and light-stained (IV) DNA as genetic material confirmation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments of Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (1952) → IV. In a typical nucleus, loosely packed chromatin that stains light is euchromatin → III. In 1928, Frederick Griffith performed experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae → I. Densely packed, dark-staining chromatin is heterochromatin → II. So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II. Class 12th NCERT Page No. 84, 85.

questions.text: If '8' Drosophila in a laboratory population of '80' died during a week, the death rate in the population is ______ individuals per Drosophila per week.
questions.explanation: Death rate = number of deaths / population size = 8/80 = 0.1 individuals per Drosophila per week.

questions.text: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of ___________.
questions.explanation: Phyllotaxy refers to the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch (common types include alternate, opposite, and whorled phyllotaxy).

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Protein, (b) Unsaturated fatty acid, (c) Nucleic acid, (d) Polysaccharide with (i) C=C double bonds, (ii) Phosphodiester bonds, (iii) Glycosidic bonds, (iv) Peptide bonds.
questions.topic: Matching biomolecule to type of bond
questions.explanation: Protein has peptide bonds (iv); unsaturated fatty acid has C=C double bonds (i); nucleic acid has phosphodiester bonds (ii); polysaccharide has glycosidic bonds (iii). (a)-(iv),(b)-(i),(c)-(ii),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: Which of the following are primary consumers in a food chain?
questions.explanation: Primary consumers are organisms that feed directly on producers (plants), i.e., herbivores.

questions.text: Which one of the following statement is not true regarding gel electrophoresis technique?
options: The process of extraction of separated DNA strands from gel is called elution.
The separated DNA fragments are stained by using ethidium bromide.
The presence of chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured DNA bands on the gel.
Bright orange coloured bands of DNA can be observed in the gel when exposed to UV light.
questions.explanation: Chromogenic substrates are used in techniques like blue-white screening for selecting recombinant colonies, not in gel electrophoresis for visualizing DNA bands. DNA bands in gel electrophoresis are visualized using ethidium bromide staining and UV light (giving orange fluorescence), making statement 3 incorrect.

questions.text: Respiratory quotient (RQ) value of tripalmitin is:
questions.explanation: Tripalmitin is a fat, and the RQ for fats is less than 1, typically around 0.7, since fats require more oxygen for complete oxidation relative to the CO2 produced.

questions.text: How many ATP and NADPH2 are required for the synthesis of one molecule of Glucose during the Calvin cycle?
questions.topic: Calvin Cycle - ATP and NADPH Requirement
questions.explanation: The Calvin cycle requires 18 ATP and 12 NADPH2 to synthesize one molecule of glucose (for 6 turns of the cycle fixing 6 CO2 molecules).

questions.text: Identify the basic amino acid from the following.
questions.explanation: Lysine, with an extra amino group in its side chain, is classified as a basic amino acid, unlike tyrosine, glutamic acid (acidic) and valine (neutral).

questions.text: Conifers are adapted to tolerate extreme environmental conditions because of:
questions.explanation: Conifers have a thick cuticle that reduces water loss, helping them tolerate extreme environmental conditions like cold and drought.

questions.text: In a cross between a male and female, both heterozygous for sickle cell anaemia gene, what percentage of the progeny will be diseased?
questions.explanation: Sickle cell anaemia is autosomal recessive. Cross Aa × Aa gives genotypic ratio 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa. Only the homozygous recessive (aa) progeny (25%) will be diseased.

questions.text: In plant tissue culture, which combination of hormones is used to induce shoot and root formation respectively from a callus?
options: Cytokinin for shoots, Auxin for roots
Auxin for shoots, Cytokinin for roots
Gibberellin for shoots, Auxin for roots
Ethylene for shoots, Cytokinin for roots
questions.explanation: A high cytokinin:auxin ratio induces shoot formation from callus, while a high auxin:cytokinin ratio induces root formation — the basis of organogenesis in micropropagation.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Family, (B) Genus, (C) Class, (D) Phylum, (E) Order
List-II: (I) Sapindales, (II) Dicotyledonae, (III) Anacardiaceae, (IV) Angiospermae, (V) Mangifera
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: For the mango plant's taxonomic hierarchy: Family = Anacardiaceae (III), Genus = Mangifera (V), Class = Dicotyledonae (II), Phylum = Angiospermae (IV), Order = Sapindales (I). So A-III, B-V, C-II, D-IV, E-I.

questions.text: Radial symmetry is found in the flowers of:
questions.explanation: Brassica (mustard family) flowers show actinomorphic (radial) symmetry, while Cassia, Trifolium, and Pisum show zygomorphic (bilateral) symmetry.

questions.text: In case of a couple where the male is having a very low sperm count, which technique will be suitable for fertilisation?
questions.explanation: As per the official NTA answer key, Artificial Insemination (AI), in which semen collected from the husband or a donor is artificially introduced into the vagina or uterus, is the indicated technique for this scenario.

questions.text: Which part of the fruit, labelled in the given figure makes it a false fruit? (Figure shows parts A, B, C, D of an apple-like fruit)
questions.explanation: A false fruit (pseudocarp) like apple develops mainly from the thalamus (receptacle), labeled as C, rather than from the ovary alone.

questions.text: Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements: (a) Euchromatin is loosely packed chromatin (b) Heterochromatin is transcriptionally active (c) Histone octomer is wrapped by negatively charged DNA in nucleosome (d) Histones are rich in lysine and arginine (e) A typical nucleosome contains 400 bp of DNA helix. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: (a) is correct (euchromatin is loosely packed), (c) is correct (DNA is negatively charged, wraps around histone octamer), (d) is correct (histones rich in lysine/arginine). (b) is wrong (heterochromatin is transcriptionally inactive) and (e) is wrong (nucleosome has ~200bp, not 400bp). Correct set: (a),(c),(d).

questions.text: Select the incorrect statement with respect to acquired immunity.
options: Primary response is produced when our body encounters a pathogen for the first time.
Anamnestic response is elicited on subsequent encounters with the same pathogen.
Anamnestic response is due to memory of first encounter.
Acquired immunity is non-specific type of defense present at the time of birth.
questions.explanation: Acquired immunity is a specific (pathogen-specific) type of defense that develops over the lifetime after exposure to antigens; it is not present at birth. The non-specific defense present at birth is innate immunity, so option (4) is the incorrect statement.

questions.text:
Match Column-I with Column-II and select the correct option using the codes given below:
Column-I: a. Pistils fused together, b. Formation of gametes, c. Hyphae of higher Ascomycetes, d. Unisexual female flower
Column-II: (i) Gametogenesis, (ii) Pistillate, (iii) Syncarpous, (iv) Dikaryotic
Codes:
(1) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
(2) a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii
(3) a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
(4) a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii
questions.explanation: Pistils fused together = Syncarpous; Formation of gametes = Gametogenesis; Hyphae of higher Ascomycetes = Dikaryotic; Unisexual female flower = Pistillate. So a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

questions.text: What is the main function of the spindle fibers during mitosis?
questions.explanation: At the onset of anaphase, each chromosome splits and the daughter chromatids (now daughter chromosomes) migrate towards opposite poles with the help of spindle fibers. Class 11th NCERT Page No.123.

questions.text: Placentation, in which ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or in peripheral part is:
questions.explanation: In parietal placentation, ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on the peripheral part, as seen in mustard and Argemone.

questions.text: Upon exposure to UV radiation, DNA stained with ethidium bromide will show:
questions.explanation: DNA stained with ethidium bromide fluoresces with a bright orange colour when exposed to UV radiation, allowing visualization of DNA bands on a gel.

questions.text:
Which of the following are not the effects of parathyroid hormone?
(a) Stimulates the process of bone resorption
(b) Decreases Ca²⁺ level in blood
(c) Reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by renal tubules
(d) Decreases the absorption of Ca²⁺ from digested food
(e) Increases metabolism of carbohydrates
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: PTH actually increases blood Ca²⁺ (not decreases, so b is false), increases Ca²⁺ absorption from digested food (not decreases, so d is false), and does not significantly affect carbohydrate metabolism (so e is false). PTH does stimulate bone resorption (a is a real effect) and renal reabsorption of Ca²⁺ (c is a real effect). So (b), (d), (e) are NOT effects of PTH. (NCERT Class 11, Pg 334)

questions.text: Endomembrane system includes ________.
options: endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
Golgi complex, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuole
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system consists of organelles that function together through direct connection or vesicular transport: endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles. Mitochondria and chloroplasts are NOT part of the endomembrane system since they are semi-autonomous, double-membraned organelles with their own genetic material.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I: A. M Phase, B. G2 Phase, C. Quiescent stage, D. G1 Phase. List II: I. Proteins are synthesized, II. Inactive phase, III. Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication, IV. Equational division. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: M Phase involves mitosis, which is an equational division (A-IV). G2 Phase is when proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis (B-I). Quiescent stage (G0) is the inactive phase where cells do not divide further (C-II). G1 Phase is the interval between the end of mitosis and the initiation of DNA replication (D-III). So the correct match is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Molluscs, B. Reptiles, C. Adult amphibians, D. Amoeba. List II — I. Pulmonary respiration only, II. Branchial respiration, III. Cellular respiration, IV. Pulmonary and Cutaneous respiration.
questions.explanation: Molluscs respire via gills — branchial respiration (II); reptiles use pulmonary respiration only (I); adult amphibians use pulmonary and cutaneous respiration (IV); Amoeba (unicellular) uses cellular/diffusion respiration (III). A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: Melonate inhibits the growth of pathogenic bacteria by inhibiting the activity of:
questions.explanation: Malonate is a classic competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase (succinate dehydrogenase), an enzyme of the Krebs cycle, and this inhibition can restrict growth of pathogenic bacteria dependent on this respiratory enzyme.

questions.text: Succus entericus is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Succus entericus is the Latin term for intestinal juice, secreted by glands in the small intestine.

questions.text: In majority of angiosperms:
options: A small central cell is present in the embryo sac
Reduction division occurs in the megaspore mother cells
questions.explanation: In most angiosperms, meiosis (reduction division) occurs in the megaspore mother cell to form megaspores, one of which develops into the embryo sac. The synergids (not the egg) have the filiform apparatus, there are typically 3 antipodal cells (not numerous), and the central cell is large, not small.

questions.text: In the exponential growth equation Nt=N0ert, e represents:
questions.topic: Meaning of 'e' in exponential growth equation
questions.explanation: In the exponential growth equation, 'e' represents the base of natural logarithms (≈2.718).

questions.text: Name a peptide hormone which acts mainly on hepatocytes, adipocytes and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilization.
questions.explanation: Insulin, a peptide hormone from pancreatic beta cells, acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes to enhance cellular glucose uptake and utilization, lowering blood glucose.

questions.text: The enzyme required for carboxylation in the Calvin cycle is:
questions.topic: Enzyme for carboxylation in Calvin cycle
questions.explanation: RuBisCO (RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase) catalyses the carboxylation of RuBP, the first step of the Calvin cycle.

questions.text:
The following are the statements about non-chordates:
A. Pharynx is perforated by gill slits. B. Notochord is absent. C. Central nervous system is dorsal. D. Heart is dorsal if present. E. Post anal tail is absent
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: In non-chordates, notochord is absent (B correct), heart is dorsal if present (D correct), and post anal tail is absent (E correct). However, pharynx perforated by gill slits and dorsal central nervous system are chordate characteristics, not non-chordate features, making A and C incorrect.

questions.text: A pink flowered Snapdragon plant was crossed with a red flowered Snapdragon plant. What type of phenotype/s is/are expected in the progeny?
options: Red, Pink as well as white flowered plants
Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants
questions.topic: Incomplete Dominance - Snapdragon Flower Color Cross
questions.explanation: In Snapdragon, flower colour shows incomplete dominance where red (RR) and white (rr) produce pink (Rr) in F1. Crossing pink (Rr, heterozygous) with red (RR, homozygous dominant) gives offspring in ratio 1 RR (red) : 1 Rr (pink), so both red and pink flowered plants are expected, no white. 12th NCERT Page No. 60.

questions.text: Which of the following pair of organelles does not contain DNA?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes and vacuoles are membrane-bound organelles that do not contain DNA. Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles that DO contain their own DNA.

questions.text:
Which of the following is the correct sequence of events in the origin of life?
I. Formation of protobionts
II. Synthesis of organic monomers
III. Synthesis of organic polymers
IV. Formation of DNA-based genetic systems
questions.explanation: The correct sequence in the origin of life (chemical evolution) is: synthesis of organic monomers → synthesis of organic polymers → formation of protobionts → formation of DNA-based genetic systems, i.e., II, III, I, IV.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct statement?
options: Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under kingdom Monera.
Slime moulds are saprophytic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Mycoplasma have DNA, ribosome and cell wall.
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are photosynthetic, autotrophic prokaryotes classified under Kingdom Monera, making this the correct statement. Bacteria are not exclusively heterotrophic (many are autotrophic), slime moulds are classified under Kingdom Protista (not Monera), and Mycoplasma lack a cell wall.

questions.text: A disease caused by an autosomal primary non-disjunction is:
questions.explanation: Down's Syndrome is caused by non-disjunction of an autosome (chromosome 21), resulting in trisomy 21. Klinefelter's and Turner's syndromes result from non-disjunction of sex chromosomes, while Sickle Cell Anemia is a point mutation disorder, not a non-disjunction disorder.

questions.text:
Tropical regions show greatest level of species richness because
A. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, hence more time was available for species diversification.
B. Tropical environments are more seasonal.
C. More solar energy is available in tropics.
D. Constant environments promote niche specialization.
E. Tropical environments are constant and predictable.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C, D and E only
questions.topic: Reasons for High Species Richness in Tropics
questions.explanation: Reasons for high tropical species richness: tropical latitudes remained undisturbed for millions of years allowing more time for diversification (A), more solar energy is available promoting higher productivity (C), relatively constant and predictable environments promote niche specialization (D and E). Tropical environments are LESS seasonal, not more (B is false). So A, C, D and E only. 12th NCERT Page No. 220.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements cannot be connected to Predation?
options: It helps in maintaining species diversity in a community
It might lead to extinction of a species
Both the interacting species are negatively impacted
It is necessitated by nature to maintain the ecological balance
questions.explanation: In predation, one species (predator) benefits while the other (prey) is harmed (+/- interaction), not both negatively impacted (which would describe competition, a -/- interaction). So statement 3 cannot be connected to predation.

questions.text: Asymptote in a logistic growth curve is obtained when:
questions.explanation: In the logistic growth model, dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K, population growth slows and plateaus (asymptote) as the population size N approaches the carrying capacity K, i.e., when K = N.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates. Reason (R): Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in the adult vertebrates. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: Vertebrata is a subphylum of Chordata (so all vertebrates are chordates, but not vice versa, since some chordates like Urochordata/Cephalochordata lack vertebral columns), and vertebrates are defined by replacement of the notochord with a vertebral column in adults, correctly explaining the assertion.

questions.text: Which of the following features of genetic code does allow bacteria to produce human insulin by recombinant DNA technology?
questions.explanation: The near universality of the genetic code (being essentially the same across organisms) allows bacteria to correctly translate the human insulin gene into functional insulin protein.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: ATP is used at two steps in glycolysis. Reason R: First ATP is used in converting glucose into glucose-6-phosphate and second ATP is used in conversion of fructose-6-phosphate into fructose-1,6-disphosphate. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — ATP is utilized at two steps in glycolysis. Reason R correctly explains this — the first ATP phosphorylates glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, and the second ATP phosphorylates fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.

questions.text: In an E. Coli strain i gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?
options: Only z gene will get transcribed
z, y, a genes will be transcribed
z, y, a genes will not be translated
RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
questions.explanation: If the repressor (i gene product) cannot bind the inducer (lactose/allolactose), it remains active and continues to bind the operator, blocking transcription of the structural genes (z, y, a) regardless of lactose presence. So these genes will not be transcribed, and hence not translated either.

questions.text: If the length of a DNA molecule is 1.1 metres, what will be the approximate number of base pairs?
questions.topic: DNA Base Pair Calculation from Length
questions.explanation: Each base pair in DNA has a length of about 0.34 nm. Number of base pairs = total length / length per bp = 1.1 m / (0.34x10^-9 m) = 3.235x10^9, approximately 3.3x10^9 bp.

questions.text: Which one of the following disorders is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) for Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule?
questions.topic: Disorder caused by substitution in haemoglobin beta chain
questions.explanation: Sickle-cell anaemia is caused by a single amino acid substitution (Glu→Val, or as worded, Val for Glu) at the 6th position of the beta-globin chain.

questions.text: Match the items given in Column I (a. Herbarium, b. Key, c. Museum, d. Catalogue) with those in Column II (i. A place having a collection of preserved plants and animals, ii. A list that enumerates methodically all the species found in an area with brief description aiding identification, iii. A place where dried and pressed plant specimens mounted on sheets are kept, iv. A booklet containing a list of characters and their alternates which are helpful in identification of various taxa) and select the correct option given below.
questions.topic: Herbarium, taxonomic keys and related terms
