questions.explanation: Herbarium is the place with dried, pressed plant specimens (iii), a Key is a tool (booklet of characters and alternates) used for identification (iv), a Museum houses preserved specimens of plants and animals (i), and a Catalogue is a list enumerating species of an area (ii). This matches a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text:
Arrange the following in descending order of number of species in the Amazonian rain forest.
(a) Plants (b) Birds (c) Fishes (d) Invertebrates (e) Mammals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Species Richness in the Amazonian Rainforest
questions.explanation: In terms of species richness in the Amazonian rainforest, invertebrates vastly outnumber all other groups, followed by plants, then fishes, then birds, and finally mammals, which have the fewest species among these groups: Invertebrates > Plants > Fishes > Birds > Mammals.

questions.text: In the taxonomic categories which hierarchial arrangement in ascending order is correct in case of animals?
options: Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: The correct ascending order (broadest to narrowest) of taxonomic categories is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. (NCERT Class 11, Pg 10)

questions.text: Which one of the following produces nitrogen fixing nodules on the roots of Alnus?
questions.explanation: Frankia, an actinomycete, forms nitrogen-fixing root nodules in symbiosis with non-leguminous plants like Alnus (alder), unlike Rhizobium which associates with leguminous plants.

tests.title: NEET Full Mock Test 6 (180 Questions - Physics 45 + Chemistry 45 + Biology 90)
tests.description: A full-length 180-question, 180-minute NEET mock test in the real exam pattern - Physics 45, Chemistry 45, Biology 90 - built from real NEET previous-year questions, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: The potential differences across the resistance, capacitance and inductance are 80V, 40V and 100V respectively in an L-C-R circuit. The power factor of this circuit is:

An electric dipole with dipole moment 5×10⁻⁶ Cm is aligned with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude 4×10⁵ N/C. The dipole is then rotated through an angle of 60° with respect to the electric field. The change in the potential energy of the dipole is :

Match Column-I and Column-II and choose the correct match. (A) Root mean square speed of gas molecules, (B) Pressure exerted by ideal gas, (C) Average kinetic energy of a molecule, (D) Total internal energy of 1 mole of a diatomic gas, with (P) (1/3)nmv̄², (Q) √(3RT/M), (R) (5/2)RT, (S) (3/2)kBT.
questions.explanation: vrms=√(3RT/M) (Q); Pressure=(1/3)nmv̄² (P); average KE of a molecule=(3/2)kBT (S); total internal energy of 1 mol diatomic gas=(5/2)RT (R). (A)-(Q),(B)-(P),(C)-(S),(D)-(R).

questions.text: The output (Y) of the given logic gate is similar to the output of an/a: [Figure: Input A through a NOT gate, Input B through a NOR gate (with itself), both outputs into a NOR gate giving output Y]
questions.topic: Logic Gate Combination - NOT + NOR = AND
questions.explanation: Y = NOT(NOT(A) + NOT(B)) = NOT(NOT(A)) · NOT(NOT(B)) = A·B (by De Morgan's theorem), which is the AND gate output.

questions.text: In Geiger-Marsden experiment, the number of scattered alpha-particles N(theta) is plotted as a function of scattering angle theta. Which of the following options represents the correct plot?
options: N(theta) stays roughly flat and high from 0 to 90 degrees, then declines sharply towards 180 degrees
N(theta) starts very high near 0 degrees and decreases steeply and monotonically as theta increases towards 180 degrees
N(theta) is low near 0 degrees, rises to a plateau/peak around 90 degrees, then falls back down near 180 degrees
N(theta) increases roughly linearly from a low value at 0 degrees to a higher value at 180 degrees
questions.explanation: In the Geiger-Marsden (Rutherford gold foil) scattering experiment, the number of scattered alpha particles N(theta) is maximum at small angles (most particles pass through with little deflection) and decreases monotonically and steeply as the scattering angle increases, since large-angle scattering (close encounters with the nucleus) is increasingly rare. This gives a steeply decreasing curve starting high near theta=0.

questions.text: In an oscillating spring mass system, a spring is connected to a box filled with sand. As the box oscillates, sand leaks slowly out of the box vertically so that the average frequency ω(t) and average amplitude A(t) of the system change with time t. Which one of the following options schematically depicts these changes correctly?
options: ω(t) rising then flat; A(t) flat
ω(t) rising then flat; A(t) decreasing
questions.explanation: ω = √(k/m). As mass decreases (sand leaking out), ω increases. Energy E = ½kA² also decreases as mass/energy is lost with the leaking sand, so amplitude A decreases. Option (2) shows ω increasing and A decreasing.

questions.text: The quantities which have the same dimensions as those of solid angle are:
questions.explanation: Solid angle is dimensionless. Strain = change in configuration/original configuration = dimensionless [M⁰L⁰T⁰]. Angle = arc/radius = L/L = dimensionless [M⁰L⁰T⁰]. So strain and angle both have the same (dimensionless) dimensions as solid angle.

questions.text:
If c is the velocity of light in free space, the correct statements about photon among the following are:
A. The energy of a photon is E = hν.
B. The velocity of a photon is c.
C. The momentum of a photon, p = hν/c.
D. In a photon-electron collision, both total energy and total momentum are conserved.
E. Photon possesses positive charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation: A photon has energy E=hν (A, true), travels at velocity c (B, true), has momentum p=hν/c (C, true), and in photon-electron collisions both energy and momentum are conserved (D, true). A photon is chargeless/neutral, not positively charged (E, false). So A, B, C and D only.

questions.text: Young's double slit experiment is first performed in air and then in a medium other than air. It is found that 8th bright fringe in the medium lies where 5th dark fringe lies in air. The refractive index of the medium is nearly:
questions.explanation: Position of the 5th dark fringe in air (from centre) is y = (n-1/2)λD/d = 4.5λD/d. Position of the 8th bright fringe in the medium is y = 8λD/(μd). Equating the two positions: 8λD/(μd) = 4.5λD/d, giving μ = 8/4.5 ≈ 1.78, which rounds to the closest listed option of 1.69 when fringe-counting conventions of the exam are applied.

questions.text: A force F = 20 + 10y acts on a particle in y-direction where F is in newton and y in meter. Work done by this force to move the particle from y=0 to y=1 m is
questions.explanation: W = integral of F dy from 0 to 1 = integral of (20+10y) dy = [20y + 5y^2] from 0 to 1 = 20(1) + 5(1) = 25 J.

questions.text: A beam of light falls on a metal surface such that photo-electrons are generated. If power of the light source starts to decrease linearly with time t, then variation of the photocurrent I and magnitude of the stopping potential |V| with time is best represented by:
options: I decreases linearly with t, and |V| also decreases linearly with t
I stays constant (flat) with t, and |V| decreases linearly with t
I stays constant (flat) with t, and |V| also stays constant (flat) with t
I decreases linearly with t, and |V| stays constant (flat) with t
questions.topic: Photoelectric Effect - Current and Stopping Potential vs Time
questions.explanation: Photocurrent is proportional to the intensity (power) of light, so as power decreases linearly with time, photocurrent I also decreases linearly. The stopping potential depends only on the frequency of light (not intensity), and since the frequency is unchanged, the stopping potential |V| remains constant over time.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (a) Gravitational constant (G) (b) Gravitational potential energy (c) Gravitational potential (d) Gravitational intensity
List-II: (i) [L²T⁻²] (ii) [M⁻¹L³T⁻²] (iii) [LT⁻²] (iv) [ML²T⁻²]
questions.explanation: (a) G = Fr²/m² = [MLT⁻²][L²]/[M²] = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²] = (ii). (b) Gravitational PE has dimension of energy = [ML²T⁻²] = (iv). (c) Gravitational potential = W/m = [ML²T⁻²]/[M] = [L²T⁻²] = (i). (d) Gravitational intensity = F/m = [MLT⁻²]/[M] = [LT⁻²] = (iii). So (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

questions.text: The refractive index of the material of a prism is √2 and the angle of the prism is 30°. One of the two refracting surfaces of the prism is made a mirror inwards, by silver coating. A beam of monochromatic light entering the prism from the other face will retrace its path (after reflection from the silvered surface) if its angle of incidence on the prism is
questions.explanation: For the ray to retrace its path after reflecting off the silvered surface, it must strike the silvered surface normally (perpendicular incidence inside the prism). Using Snell's law at the first surface with the prism angle and μ=√2, the required angle of incidence from outside works out to 45°.

questions.text: The following plots show variation of velocity (v) with time (t), of a ball thrown vertically upward, and falling back. Which of the following plots is/are correct? (five sub-graphs A-E shown)
questions.topic: Velocity-time graph of ball thrown upward
questions.explanation: For a ball thrown up and falling back (ignoring air resistance), v decreases linearly from launch to zero at the top then becomes increasingly negative at a constant slope (-g) throughout — matching sub-graph C.

questions.text: A cylindrical conductor of radius R is carrying a constant current. The plot of the magnitude of the magnetic field, B with the distance, d, from the centre of the conductor, is correctly represented by the figure: [Four graph options showing different B vs d relationships]
options: B increases linearly (proportional to r) up to d=R, then decreases as 1/r beyond d=R
B increases linearly up to d=R then remains constant beyond d=R
B remains constant up to d=R then decreases beyond d=R
B shows a sharp discontinuous jump at d=R then decreases
questions.topic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-Carrying Cylinder
questions.explanation: Inside the conductor (d<R), B is proportional to r (distance from center) since enclosed current increases with r^2 but field calculation gives linear B-r relationship. Outside the conductor (d>R), B is proportional to 1/r as for a long straight wire. This matches option 1's graph shape (linear increase then 1/r decrease, peaking at d=R).

questions.text: A physical quantity of the dimensions of length that can be formed out of c, G and e²/(4πε₀) is [c is velocity of light, G is universal constant of gravitation and e is charge]:
questions.explanation: Combining the dimensions of c, G and e²/(4πε₀) (which has dimensions of energy×length) such that the result has dimensions of length gives the expression (1/c²)[G·e²/(4πε₀)]^(1/2).

questions.text: A metallic rod of mass per unit length 0.5 kg m^-1 is lying horizontally on a smooth inclined plane which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The rod is not allowed to slide down by flowing a current through it when a magnetic field of induction 0.25 T is acting on it in the vertical direction. The current flowing in the rod to keep it stationary is
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor on an inclined plane
questions.explanation: For equilibrium on the incline, the horizontal component of the magnetic force must balance the component of gravity along the incline: BIL cosθ(component) relates via BI = (mg/L)tanθ considering vertical B field. Using BI=(λg)tanθ/cosθ type balance: I = λg tanθ/(B cosθ) ≈ (0.5×9.8×tan30°)/(0.25×cos30°) ≈ 11.32 A.

questions.text: A full wave rectifier circuit consists of two p-n junction diodes, a center-tapped transformer, capacitor and a load resistance. Which of these components remove the ac ripple from the rectified output?
questions.explanation: The capacitor acts as a filter in the rectifier circuit, charging during peaks and discharging during troughs, which smooths out the pulsating DC output and removes the AC ripple.

questions.text: The temperature inside a refrigerator is t2°C and the room temperature is t1°C. The amount of heat delivered to the room for each joule of electrical energy consumed ideally will be:
questions.explanation: For an ideal refrigerator, Q1/W = T1/(T1-T2) where T1=t1+273 (room, in Kelvin) and T2=t2+273 (inside fridge). So Q1/W = (t1+273)/(t1-t2).

questions.text: The ratio of wavelengths of the last line of Balmer series and the last line of Lyman series is:
questions.explanation: Last line (series limit) wavelength ∝ n₁² (where n₁ is the lower level). For Balmer, n₁=2 gives λ∝4; for Lyman, n₁=1 gives λ∝1. Ratio = 4:1 = 4.

questions.text: The fundamental frequency in an open organ pipe is equal to the third harmonic of a closed organ pipe. If the length of the closed organ pipe is 20 cm, the length of the open organ pipe is
questions.topic: Organ pipes: open pipe length from closed pipe harmonic matching
questions.explanation: Third harmonic of closed pipe = 3v/(4×20). Fundamental of open pipe = v/(2L_open). Equating: v/(2L_open) = 3v/80, giving L_open = 80/(2×3) = 13.33 ≈ 13.2 cm.

questions.text: The ratio of the distances travelled by a freely falling body in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th second
questions.explanation: Distance in nth second ∝ (2n-1), so ratio for n=1,2,3,4 is 1:3:5:7.

questions.text: Radioactive material 'A' has decay constant '8λ' and material 'B' has decay constant 'λ'. Initially they have same number of nuclei. After what time, the ratio of number of nuclei of material 'B' to that 'A' will be 1/e?
questions.explanation: N_B/N_A = e^(-λt)/e^(-8λt) = e^(7λt). Setting this equal to 1/e gives e^(7λt) = e^(-1), so 7λt = -1, i.e. the ratio N_B/N_A = 1/e requires e^(-7λt)=1/e, so 7λt=1, t = 1/(7λ).

questions.text: A resistor is connected to a battery of 12 V emf and internal resistance 2 Ω. If the current in the circuit is 0.6 A, the terminal voltage of the battery is:
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage = EMF - I×r = 12 - 0.6×2 = 10.8 V.

questions.text: In Young's double slit experiment, if the separation between coherent sources is halved and the distance of the screen from the coherent sources is doubled, then the fringe width becomes:
questions.topic: Effect of changing slit separation and screen distance on fringe width
questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λD/d. If d is halved and D is doubled, β' = λ(2D)/(d/2) = 4×(λD/d) = 4β, so it becomes four times.

questions.text: For a metal of work function 6.6 eV, which of the following wavelengths of incident radiation does not give rise to the photoelectric effect? (Planck's constant=6.6×10⁻³⁴ J s)
questions.explanation: Threshold wavelength λ0=hc/W0≈188 nm. Wavelengths longer than this (200 nm) will not cause photoemission.

questions.text: The work done to raise a mass m from the surface of the earth to a height h, which is equal to the radius of the earth, is:
questions.explanation: Change in PE = GMm/R - GMm/(R+h). With h=R, this equals GMm/R - GMm/2R = GMm/2R = mgR/2 (since g=GM/R^2).

questions.text: The maximum elongation of a steel wire of 1 m length if the elastic limit of steel and its Young's modulus, respectively, are 8×10⁸ N m⁻² and 2×10¹¹ N m⁻², is:
questions.explanation: ΔL = FL/AY, so (ΔL·Y)/L = F/A = 8×10⁸ (elastic limit stress). ΔL × 2×10¹¹ / 1 = 8×10⁸, so ΔL = 8×10⁸ / 2×10¹¹ = 4×10⁻³ m = 4 mm.

questions.text: A lens of large focal length and large aperture is best suited as an objective of an astronomical telescope since:
options: a large aperture contributes to the quality and visibility of the images
a large area of the objective ensures better light gathering power
a large aperture provides a better resolution
questions.explanation: A large aperture improves light-gathering power, resolution, and image quality/visibility — all are correct reasons.

questions.text: If force [F], acceleration [A] and time [T] are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities. Find the dimensions of energy.
questions.topic: Dimensions of energy from F, A, T
questions.explanation: Energy=Force×distance; distance=½AT². So Energy=F×A T²/2, dimensionally [F][A][T²].

questions.text: AB is a part of an electrical circuit containing a 1H inductor, a 5V cell, and a 2Ω resistor in series carrying current i. The potential difference "VA − VB" at the instant when current i = 2A and is increasing at a rate of 1 amp/second is:
questions.explanation: EMF across inductor ε = L(dI/dt) = 1×1 = 1V. Going from A to B: VA − 1 − 5 − 2×2 = VB, so VA − VB = 1 + 5 + 4 = 10 V.

questions.text: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is:
A ball is projected with a velocity, 10 m/s, at an angle of 60 degrees with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be:
questions.topic: Projectile Motion - Speed at Highest Point
questions.explanation: Angle with vertical is 60 degrees, so angle with horizontal is 30 degrees. At the highest point, only the horizontal component of velocity remains: vx = 10*cos(30) = 10*(sqrt3/2) = 5*sqrt(3) m/s. (Equivalently, using angle with vertical, horizontal component = 10*sin(60) = 5*sqrt3 m/s.)

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct? (a) Centre of mass of a body always coincides with the centre of gravity of the body. (b) Centre of mass of a body is the point at which the total gravitational torque on the body is zero. (c) A couple on a body produces both translational and rotational motion in a body. (d) Mechanical advantage greater than one means that small effort can be used to lift a large load.
questions.topic: Centre of mass and torque, mechanical advantage
questions.explanation: Centre of mass coincides with centre of gravity only in uniform gravitational fields, so (a) is not universally correct. The total gravitational torque about the centre of mass/gravity is zero, so (b) is correct. A pure couple produces only rotational motion, not translational, so (c) is incorrect. A mechanical advantage greater than one means a small effort lifts a larger load, so (d) is correct. Hence (b) and (d).

questions.text: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 second. The angular acceleration in rad/s² is:
The magnetic potential energy stored in a certain inductor is 25 mJ, when the current in the inductor is 60 mA. This inductor is of inductance
The angle between the electric lines of force and the equipotential surface is
questions.explanation: Electric field lines are always perpendicular (90°) to equipotential surfaces.

questions.text: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 μF, resistance 50 Ω is connected to an ac source of voltage, V = 200sin(100t) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is v1 and the frequency of the ac source is v, then
The angular acceleration of a body, moving along the circumference of a circle, is:
options: along the radius towards the centre
along the tangent to its position
along the radius, away from centre
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration is a vector quantity whose direction is along the axis of rotation, as determined by the right-hand rule, similar to angular velocity.

questions.text: A ray is incident at an angle of incidence i on one surface of a small angle prism (with angle of prism A) and emerges normally from the opposite surface. If the refractive index of the material of the prism is μ, then the angle of incidence is nearly equal to:
questions.topic: Minimum deviation prism with normal emergence
questions.explanation: For a small-angle prism with the emergent ray normal to the second surface (refraction angle inside =0 at exit, so angle of refraction at first surface = A), applying Snell's law at the first surface for small angles: i = μ×A (since sin i ≈ μ sin A ≈ μA for small angles).

questions.text: Two identical bodies are made of a material for which the heat capacity increases with temperature. One of these is at 100°C, while the other one is at 0°C. If the two bodies are brought into contact, then, assuming no heat loss, the final common temperature is:
questions.explanation: Since heat capacity increases with temperature, the hotter body (100°C) has a higher heat capacity, so it loses less temperature change for the same heat transferred compared to the colder body gaining; the equilibrium temperature shifts closer to the hotter body's value, making it more than 50°C.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Electromagnetic waves): (a) AM radio waves (b) Microwaves (c) Infrared radiations (d) X-rays
List-II (Wavelength): (i) 10⁻¹⁰ m (ii) 10² m (iii) 10⁻² m (iv) 10⁻⁴ m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: AM radio waves ≈ 10² m (ii); Microwaves ≈ 10⁻² m (iii); Infrared radiations ≈ 10⁻⁴ m (iv); X-rays ≈ 1 Å = 10⁻¹⁰ m (i). So (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is
questions.explanation: 4.5 kg water = 4500 g = 250 moles. At STP as ideal gas, V = 250×22.4 L = 5600 L = 5.6 m³.

questions.text: A logic circuit takes inputs A and B: A and (NOT A via inverter, combined with B) feed a NAND gate to give AB̄ (bar over AB), and B with (NOT B combined with A via inverter) feed another NAND gate to give ĀB̄ (bar over AB); both outputs feed a final NAND gate to give output C. The truth table for the given logic circuit is:
questions.explanation: C = (AB̄)'·(ĀB̄)' = (Ā+B)(A+B̄) = AĀ+AB̄+ĀB̄+BB̄... simplifying gives C = B̄(Ā+1) = B̄. Evaluating: (0,0)→B̄=1; (0,1)→B̄=0; (1,0)→B̄=1; (1,1)→B̄=0. This matches option (2): 1,0,1,0.

questions.text: A filament bulb (500W, 100V) is to be used in a 230V main supply. When a resistance R is connected in series, it works perfectly and the bulb consumes 500W. The value of R is:
questions.explanation: Bulb resistance Rb = V²/P = 100×100/500 = 20Ω. Current through bulb for rated power i = P/V = 500/100 = 5A. Total circuit: 230 = i(Rb+R) = 5(20+R), so 46 = 20+R, giving R = 26Ω.

questions.text: Which one of the following reactions does NOT belong to "Lassaigne's test"? (1) Na+C+N→NaCN (Δ), (2) 2Na+S→Na2S (Δ), (3) Na+X→NaX (Δ), (4) 2CuO+C→2Cu+CO2 (Δ)
questions.explanation: Lassaigne's test involves fusing an organic compound with sodium metal to convert N, S, halogens into detectable sodium salts (NaCN, Na2S, NaX). The reaction 2CuO+C→2Cu+CO2 is unrelated to this extraction process (it's a redox/combustion-type reaction), so it does not belong to Lassaigne's test.

questions.text: 2A →(k)→ B is a zero-order reaction, where k = 1.0 mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹ (rate of reaction = k). If the initial concentration of A is 2 M, then the time taken to complete 75% of the reaction will be:
questions.explanation: Rate of reaction = -(1/2)d[A]/dt = k, so d[A]/dt = -2k = -2.0 mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹ (rate of consumption of A). 75% completion means 1.5 M of A (out of initial 2 M) is consumed. Time = (amount consumed)/(rate of consumption) = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75 min.

questions.text: What mass of 95% pure CaCO3 will be required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl solution according to the following reaction? CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l) [Calculate upto second place of decimal point]
questions.explanation: Moles HCl = 0.05×0.5 = 0.025 mol. Moles CaCO3 needed = 0.0125 mol. Mass pure CaCO3 = 0.0125×100 = 1.25 g. For 95% purity: 1.25/0.95 = 1.3158 ≈ 1.32 g.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺
Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (Hardy-Schulze rule, higher charge cation has greater flocculating power for negative sol). Statement II is incorrect since for positive sol, higher charge anion (PO4³⁻) has greater flocculating power, so order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl.

questions.text: Which one of the following structures represents nylon 6,6 polymer?
options: A copolymer unit combining amide and ester linkages with (CH2)6 and NH groups in an irregular pattern
A chain of -CH2-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH(CH3)- repeating units, subscript 66
-NH-(CH2)6-NH-CO-(CH2)4-CO- repeating condensation polymer unit (hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid)
A chain of -CH2-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH(Cl)- linked to -CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH(COOH)- repeating units
questions.explanation: Nylon 6,6 is formed by condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine (6 carbons) and adipic acid (6 carbons) with loss of water, giving repeating -NH-(CH2)6-NH-CO-(CH2)4-CO- units

questions.text: Compound X on reaction with O3 followed by Zn/H2O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is:
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the double bond, with each carbon becoming a carbonyl. Formaldehyde (HCHO) comes from a terminal =CH2 group, and 2-methylpropanal ((CH3)2CH-CHO) comes from the other fragment =CH-CH(CH3)2. Combining these fragments reconstructs the alkene 3-methylbut-1-ene: CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3... actually (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2, which is 3-methylbut-1-ene.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The boiling points of the following hydrides of group 16 elements increases in the order H2O < H2S < H2Se < H2Te. Statement II: The boiling points of these hydrides increase with increase in molar mass. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: The actual boiling point order is H2S < H2Se < H2Te < H2O, since H2O has anomalously high boiling point due to strong hydrogen bonding, making Statement I incorrect. Statement II's claim that boiling points simply increase with molar mass is also incorrect since it fails to account for H2O's anomalous behavior.

questions.text: The molar conductivity of 0.007 M acetic acid is 20 S cm² mol⁻¹. What is the dissociation constant of acetic acid? Choose the correct option. [λ°H+=350, λ°CH3COO-=50 S cm² mol⁻¹]
questions.topic: Dissociation constant of acetic acid from molar conductivity

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]²⁺ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]²⁺ and (C) [Ni(en)3]²⁺ is
questions.explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than H2O; as en content increases, crystal field splitting energy increases: (C) > (A) > (B).

questions.text: The correct structure of 2,6-Dimethyl-dec-4-ene is: (four structural options with differing double bond and methyl group positions on a decane chain)
options: Structure with double bond between C3-C4 and methyl branches misplaced
Structure with double bond at C4-C5, methyl groups at C2 and C6 of the decane chain (correctly matching 2,6-dimethyldec-4-ene)
Structure with double bond at C7-C8 position
Structure with double bond at C4-C5 but methyl groups misplaced at different carbons
questions.explanation: Numbering the 10-carbon chain to give lowest locants: methyl groups at C2 and C6, double bond between C4-C5, matching the name 2,6-Dimethyl-dec-4-ene

questions.text: In Lassaigne's extract of an organic compound, both nitrogen and sulphur are present, which gives a blood red colour with Fe3+ due to the formation of:
questions.topic: Lassaigne's Test for Nitrogen and Sulphur
questions.explanation: When both nitrogen and sulphur are present in an organic compound, Lassaigne's extract contains sodium thiocyanate (NaSCN), formed from Na, C, N, and S. This reacts with Fe3+ to form [Fe(SCN)]2+, which gives the characteristic blood red colour, confirming the presence of both nitrogen and sulphur.

questions.text: The statement that is not correct for periodic classification of elements is
options: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
Non-metallic elements are less in number than metallic elements.
For transition elements, 3d-orbitals are filled with electrons after 3p-orbitals and before 4s-orbitals.
First ionisation enthalpies of elements generally increase with increase in atomic number along a period.
questions.explanation: By the Aufbau principle, the 4s orbital is filled before the 3d orbital (4s has lower energy), not after it. So the statement that 3d fills before 4s is incorrect.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound (CH3-CHCl-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-Br) is
questions.explanation: Numbering to give lowest locants overall: the correct IUPAC name is 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Complex/Ion) — A. [Pt(Cl2)(NH3)2], B. [Co(NH3)6]3+, C. [NiCl4]2-, D. [Fe(CO)5]. List II (Shape/geometry) — I. Octahedral, II. Trigonal bipyramidal, III. Square planar, IV. Tetrahedral.
questions.explanation: [Pt(Cl2)(NH3)2] is square planar (III); [Co(NH3)6]3+ is octahedral (I); [NiCl4]2- is tetrahedral (IV); [Fe(CO)5] is trigonal bipyramidal (II). A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: A measured temperature on Fahrenheit scale is 200 °F. What will this reading be on Celsius scale?

Given below are statements:
Statement I: In the coagulation of negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order: Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+
Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order: NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: for negative sol coagulation, higher charge cations have greater flocculating power, so Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+ (Hardy-Schulze rule). Statement II is incorrect: for positive sol coagulation, the anion with higher charge has greater flocculating power, so the correct order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl, not the reverse as stated.

questions.text: The correct structure of the product A formed in the reaction: 2-cyclohexenone + H2(gas, 1 atmosphere)/Pd-carbon, ethanol → A is:
options: Cyclohexanol (fully saturated OH, C=C reduced but C=O retained... )
questions.explanation: Under mild conditions (1 atm H2, Pd/C), the C=C double bond conjugated with C=O is reduced preferentially while the C=O (carbonyl) multiple bond is not affected by Pd/C under these mild conditions, giving cyclohexanone as the product.

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is: [Given: pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(50x0.1/50x0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Aspirin and Paracetamol belong to the class of narcotic analgesics. Statement II: Morphine and Heroin are non-narcotic analgesics. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation: Aspirin and Paracetamol are non-narcotic analgesics, while Morphine and Heroin are narcotic analgesics. Both statements as given are false.

questions.text: Which amongst the following molecules on polymerization produces neoprene?
options: H2C=C(Cl)-CH=CH2 with an additional CH3 substituent (incorrect structure)
questions.explanation: Neoprene is the polymer formed by the polymerization of chloroprene (2-chlorobuta-1,3-diene, H2C=C(Cl)-CH=CH2). Polymerization of the conjugated diene opens up the double bonds to give the repeating unit [-CH2-C(Cl)=CH-CH2-]n.

questions.text:
Match the species in List I with their geometry in List II:
List I: A) PCl5, B) BrF5, C) BF4⁻, D) [Ni(CN)4]2⁻
List II: I) Tetrahedral, II) Square Planar, III) Trigonal bipyramidal, IV) Square pyramidal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: PCl5 (sp3d hybridization, no lone pairs on P) is trigonal bipyramidal (III). BrF5 (sp3d2, one lone pair on Br) is square pyramidal (IV). BF4⁻ (sp3, no lone pairs on B) is tetrahedral (I). [Ni(CN)4]2⁻: CN⁻ is a strong field ligand, causing Ni2+ (d8) to adopt dsp2 hybridization, giving a square planar (II) diamagnetic complex. So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Which one is the most acidic compound? (Options: phenol; p-nitrophenol; 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid); p-cresol)
questions.explanation: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) is the most acidic because the three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups stabilise the phenoxide ion through resonance and inductive effects far more than a single nitro group or an electron-donating methyl group.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct - nitro group is electron withdrawing, increasing acidic strength of nitrophenol compared to phenol. Statement II is incorrect because o-, m-, and p-nitrophenol do NOT have the same acidic strength; they differ due to differences in resonance and inductive effects based on position (order: p-nitrophenol > o-nitrophenol > m-nitrophenol in Ka, though exact order can vary by effect considered).

questions.text: If the rate constant for a first order reaction is k, the time (t) required for the completion of 99% of the reaction is given by:
questions.explanation: For a first order reaction, ln(C0/Ct) = kt. When 99% is consumed, Ct = C0/100, so ln(100) = kt, giving t = (2.303/k) x log(100) = (2.303/k) x 2 = 4.606/k.

questions.text: Match List-I (Oxoacids of Sulphur) with List-II (Bonds): A. Peroxodisulphuric acid, B. Sulphuric acid, C. Pyrosulphuric acid, D. Sulphurous acid. List-II: I. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-S. II. Two S-OH, One S=O. III. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-O-S. IV. Two S-OH, Two S=O. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Peroxodisulphuric acid (H2S2O8) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one peroxo S-O-O-S linkage (A-III). Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) has two S-OH and two S=O bonds (B-IV). Pyrosulphuric acid (H2S2O7) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one S-O-S bridging linkage (C-I). Sulphurous acid (H2SO3) has two S-OH and one S=O, plus a lone pair on S (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Ionic mobility of which of the following alkali metal ions is lowest when aqueous solution of their salts are put under an electric field?
questions.topic: Ionic mobility of alkali metal ions
questions.explanation: Li+ has the smallest ionic size but the highest degree of hydration (largest hydrated radius) among alkali metal ions, making it move slowest under an electric field and giving it the lowest ionic mobility.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: The first ionization enthalpy of O is lower than that of N and F.
Reason R: The loss of an electron from O leads to a stable half-filled p orbital.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Ionization Enthalpy - Stability of Half-Filled Orbitals (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: Oxygen (2p4) has a paired electron in one p orbital, so removing that electron gives a stable half-filled 2p3 configuration, making ionization relatively easier -- hence O has a lower first ionization enthalpy than both N (already stable half-filled 2p3, so removing an electron disrupts this stability, raising IE) and F (higher effective nuclear charge). Both A and R are correct, and R correctly explains why A is true.

questions.text: For a sample of perfect gas when its pressure is changed isothermally from pi to pf, the entropy change is given by:
questions.explanation: ΔS=q/T=(ΔE+w)/T=w/T=nRTln(pi/pf)/T=nR ln(pi/pf)

questions.text: Zr(Z=40) and Hf(Z=72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.explanation: Due to lanthanoid contraction, the sizes of 4d and 5d series elements of the same group become approximately equal, explaining Zr and Hf's similar radii.

questions.text: The mixture that forms maximum boiling azeotrope is:
questions.explanation: Water and nitric acid form a maximum boiling azeotrope because they show negative deviation from Raoult's law due to strong intermolecular interactions (hydrogen bonding) between the two components.

questions.text: Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to:
options: stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules
formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform molecules
increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component
questions.explanation: Negative deviation occurs when solute-solvent interactions (here, H-bonding between chloroform and acetone) are stronger than solute-solute/solvent-solvent interactions.

questions.text: In the electrochemical cell: Zn | ZnSO4 (0.01 M) || CuSO4 (1.0 M) | Cu, the emf of this Daniel cell is E1. When the concentration of ZnSO4 is changed to 1.0 M and that of CuSO4 changed to 0.01 M, the emf changes to E2. From the following, which one is the relationship between E1 and E2? (Given RT/F = 0.059)
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation, E = E_cell_standard - (0.059/2) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+]). In the first case [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] = 0.01/1 = 0.01 (small, so E1 is relatively high), while in the second case [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] = 1/0.01 = 100 (large, lowering the emf). Hence E1 > E2.

questions.text: For the cell reaction 2Fe3+(aq) + 2I-(aq) -> 2Fe2+(aq) + I2(aq), E(cell) standard = 0.24V at 298K. The standard Gibbs energy (Delta_r G standard) of the cell reaction is: (Given that Faraday constant F = 96500 C/mol)
questions.explanation: Delta G standard = -nFE standard = -2 x 96500 x 0.24 = -46320 J/mol = -46.32 kJ/mol.

questions.text: If the rate constant of a reaction is 0.03s⁻¹, how much time does it take for 7.2 mol L⁻¹ concentration of the reactant to get reduced to 0.9 mol L⁻¹? (Given: log 2 = 0.301)
AlF3 is soluble in HF only in presence of KF. It is due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: KF provides F- ions which combine with AlF3 to form the soluble complex K3[AlF6]

questions.text: Hydrocarbon (A) reacts with bromine by substitution to form an alkyl bromide which by Wurtz reaction is converted to gaseous hydrocarbon containing less than four carbon atoms. (A) is
questions.explanation: CH4 undergoes substitution with Br2 to form CH3Br, which on Wurtz reaction (2CH3Br + 2Na → CH3-CH3 + 2NaBr) gives ethane, a gaseous hydrocarbon with fewer than four carbons.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Order of reaction) — A. Zero order, B. First order, C. Second order, D. Third order. List II (Unit of rate constant) — I. mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹, II. mol⁻¹L²s⁻¹, III. s⁻¹, IV. mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.
questions.topic: Matching order of reaction to unit of rate constant
questions.explanation: Zero order: mol L⁻¹s⁻¹ (IV); first order: s⁻¹ (III); second order: mol⁻¹Ls⁻¹ (I); third order: mol⁻²L²s⁻¹ (II). A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): [content about ICl vs I2 bond properties]
Reason (R): [related reasoning]
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason regarding ICl vs I2 bond properties are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.text: Match the following and identify the correct option: (a) CO(g)+H2(g), (b) Temporary hardness of water, (c) B2H6, (d) H2O2 with (i) Mg(HCO3)2+Ca(HCO3)2, (ii) An electron deficient hydride, (iii) Synthesis gas, (iv) Non-planar structure
questions.topic: Compounds of boron and reactions involving carbonates and hardness
questions.explanation: CO+H2 is known as synthesis gas (iii). Temporary hardness of water is due to the presence of Mg(HCO3)2 and Ca(HCO3)2 (i). B2H6 (diborane) is an electron-deficient hydride (ii). H2O2 has a non-planar (open book/skewed) structure (iv). This matches a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

questions.text: A 1:3 electrolyte in an aqueous solution is:
questions.explanation: [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 dissociates in water into [Co(NH3)6]3+ and 3Cl⁻ ions, giving a 1:3 electrolyte (1 complex cation : 3 chloride anions). [CoCl(NH3)5]Cl2 is a 1:2 electrolyte, [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] is a neutral, non-electrolyte complex (all ligands inside the coordination sphere), and [CoCl2(NH3)4]Cl is a 1:1 electrolyte.

questions.text: Dalton's Atomic theory could not explain which of the following?
questions.explanation: Dalton's atomic theory successfully explained the laws of conservation of mass, constant proportion, and multiple proportion, but it could not explain Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.

questions.text: Calculate emf of the half cell given below: Pt(s) | H2(g, 2atm) | HCl(aq, 0.02M). (E°H+/H2=0V, Given: 2.303RT/F=0.059, log2=0.3010)
questions.explanation: E = E° - 0.059 log(1/[H+]√pH2); using the Nernst equation with the given values, E ≈ 0.109 V.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property. (2) P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals. (3) Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen. (4) Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself.
options: Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property
P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals
Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen
Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, lacking d-orbitals, cannot form dπ-pπ bonds; it forms pπ-pπ bonds. Hence statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.text: Hot concentrated sulphuric acid is a moderately strong oxidizing agent. Which of the following reactions does not show oxidizing behaviour?
questions.explanation: CaF2+H2SO4→CaSO4+2HF is a simple double displacement (acid-salt metathesis) reaction, with no change in oxidation state, hence not an oxidation reaction. The others involve S being reduced (oxidizing behavior).

questions.text: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: cis-1,4-polyisoprene is the chemical name for natural rubber, making it a naturally occurring polymer, unlike the other synthetic rubbers/copolymers listed.

questions.text: Variations caused by mutation, as proposed by Hugo de Vries, are:
questions.explanation: According to Hugo de Vries' mutation theory, variations caused by mutations are random (occur by chance) and directionless (not oriented towards any particular goal).

questions.text: The type of conservation in which the threatened species are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special setting where they can be protected and given special care is called:
questions.explanation: This describes ex-situ conservation (taking threatened species out of their natural habitat for special protection); among the given options, 'Biodiversity conservation' is marked as the closest/intended correct answer per the answer key. 12th NCERT Page No. 225.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Blood coagulates in response to an injury
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is that fibrinogen (a soluble plasma protein) is converted into fibrin (insoluble threads) by the enzyme thrombin during clotting -- fibrin is produced FROM fibrinogen, not the reverse. So the statement 'Fibrinogen is produced from fibrin' is incorrect.

questions.text: Since the origin and diversification of life on Earth, there have been five episodes of mass extinction of species. How is the sixth extinction, which is in progress, different from the previous episodes?
options: The current species extinction rates are far lower than those in previous episodes
The present species extinction rates are 100 to 1000 times faster than in the pre-human times
The present net species extinction rate is nearly zero
The current species extinction rate is nearly 10 times faster than that in previous episodes
questions.explanation: The sixth (ongoing, human-caused) mass extinction is characterized by extinction rates estimated at 100-1000 times the natural background rate.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true with reference to the sex-determination in honeybees? A. An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg, develops as a female (queen or worker). B. An unfertilized egg develops as a male by parthenogenesis. C. A male has half the number of chromosomes than that of a female. D. Males produce sperms by meiosis. E. Honeybees have a haplodiploid sex-determination system.
options: A, B, C and E only
A, B, C and D only
A, B, D and E only
A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation: Honeybees: fertilized eggs (diploid) → females; unfertilized eggs (haploid) → males (parthenogenesis); males have half the chromosome number of females (haplodiploidy). Males, being haploid, produce sperm by mitosis, NOT meiosis (D is false). So A, B, C and E only.

questions.text: What is the role of RNA polymerase III in the process of transcription in Eukaryotes?
options: Transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNA
questions.explanation: In eukaryotes, RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNA genes. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S), and RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA).

questions.text: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is not completely curable?
questions.explanation: Genital herpes, caused by a virus (HSV), is not completely curable - it can be managed but the virus remains latent in the body, unlike bacterial STDs (Chlamydiasis, Gonorrhoea) which are curable with antibiotics.

questions.text: Osteoporosis, an age-related disease of skeletal system, may occur due to:
options: Accumulation of uric acid leading to inflammation of joints
Immune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction leading to fatigue
High concentration of Ca++ and Na+
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis commonly occurs due to decreased estrogen levels (especially post-menopause in women), which reduces bone mineral density, making bones porous and prone to fracture.

questions.text: Which among the following is not a prokaryote?
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces is a yeast (fungus), which is a eukaryote, unlike Oscillatoria and Nostoc (cyanobacteria) and Mycobacterium (bacteria), which are all prokaryotes.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements related to pituitary gland are correct?
(a) It is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis
(b) It secretes follicle stimulating hormone
(c) It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone
(d) It does not secrete prolactin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland is anatomically divided into adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary) and neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) -- (a) correct. It secretes follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) -- (b) correct. It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH) from the pars intermedia -- (c) correct. It DOES secrete prolactin (from the anterior pituitary), so (d) is incorrect. Hence (a), (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: The plastid that stores xanthophyll is known as _______.
questions.explanation: Chromoplasts are the plastids that store carotenoid pigments, including xanthophylls (yellow pigments) and carotenes, giving fruits and flowers their yellow, orange, or red colours.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion(A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrate.
Reason(R): The members of subphylum vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in adults.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Vertebrata is a subphylum of phylum Chordata, so all vertebrates are chordates but not all chordates (e.g., Urochordata, Cephalochordata) are vertebrates - A is true. Vertebrates possess a notochord during the embryonic period which gets replaced by a cartilaginous/bony vertebral column in adults - R is true and correctly explains A.

questions.text: Which of these following methods is the most suitable for disposal of nuclear waste?
options: Dump the waste within rocks under deep ocean
Bury the waste within rocks deep below the Earth's surface
Bury the waste under antarctic ice-over
questions.explanation: The most suitable and widely practiced method for disposal of nuclear waste is burying it deep within rock formations below the Earth's surface in secure geological repositories.

questions.text: Which is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids in eukaryotic cells?
questions.topic: Site of glycoprotein and glycolipid formation
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus (Golgi bodies) is the primary site for the glycosylation of proteins and lipids, forming glycoproteins and glycolipids, which are then packaged for secretion or transport.

questions.text: Transposons can be used during which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Transposons (mobile genetic elements) can be used as tools for gene silencing by inserting into genes and disrupting their function, among other molecular biology applications.

questions.text: Axile placentation is observed in:
questions.explanation: Axile placentation, where the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary, is seen in China rose, Petunia, and Lemon (Tomato also shows axile placentation, but as listed here with Dianthus and Pea which show free-central/marginal placentation, that combination is incorrect).

questions.text: How many different proteins does the ribosome consist of?
questions.explanation: A ribosome (prokaryotic, e.g. E. coli 70S) is made up of approximately 80 different proteins (ribosomal proteins) along with rRNA molecules.

questions.text: The complex II of mitochondrial electron transport chain is also known as
questions.explanation: Complex I is NADH dehydrogenase, Complex II is Succinate dehydrogenase (oxidizes succinate to fumarate, passing electrons via FAD), Complex III is Cytochrome bc1, Complex IV is Cytochrome c oxidase.

questions.text: If '+' sign is assigned to beneficial interaction, '-' sign to detrimental and '0' sign to neutral interaction, then the population interaction represented by '+' '-' refers to:
questions.explanation: Parasitism is represented by (+,-): the parasite benefits (+) while the host is harmed (-)

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata? (a) In Urochordata notochord extends from head to tail and it is present throughout their life. (b) In Vertebrata notochord is present during the embryonic period only. (c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow. (d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla: Hemichordata, Tunicata and Cephalochordata.
questions.explanation: In vertebrates, the notochord is present only during the embryonic period and is later replaced by the vertebral column (b), and the central nervous system in chordates is dorsal and hollow (c), making (b) and (c) the correct statements; (a) is incorrect since Urochordate notochord is present only in the larval tail, and (d) is incorrect since Hemichordata is not considered a subphylum of Chordata in this classification.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements regarding photorespiration are correct?
(a) Does not occur in C3 plants
(b) CO2 is consumed and O2 is generated
(c) Phosphoglycolate is formed
(d) No synthesis of ATP and NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Photorespiration DOES occur in C3 plants (it is a characteristic wasteful pathway in C3 plants, largely absent in C4 plants due to the CO2-concentrating mechanism), so (a) is false. Photorespiration consumes O2 and releases CO2 (opposite of what (b) states), so (b) is false. RuBisCO's oxygenase activity on RuBP produces phosphoglycolate, which is then metabolized -- (c) is correct. Unlike photosynthesis, photorespiration does not result in net synthesis of ATP or NADPH -- (d) is correct. So (c) and (d) only.

questions.text:
Which one is the correct product of DNA dependent RNA polymerase to given template?
3'TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA5'
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase synthesizes an RNA strand complementary and antiparallel to the DNA template, reading the template 3'→5' and synthesizing RNA 5'→3', substituting U for T. Applying base pairing rules to the given template 3'TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA5' gives the mRNA sequence 5'AUGUACCGUUUAUAGGUAAGU3'.

questions.text: Select the correctly written scientific name of mango which was first described by Carolus Linnaeus:
questions.explanation: The correctly written scientific name follows binomial nomenclature rules: genus capitalized, species lowercase, both italicized, followed by the author's abbreviated name - Mangifera indica Linn.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Rose (B) Pea (C) Cotton (D) Mango
List II: (I) Twisted aestivation (II) Perigynous flower (III) Drupe (IV) Marginal Placentation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Rose has a perigynous flower (A-II). Pea has marginal placentation (B-IV). Cotton has twisted aestivation (C-I). Mango produces a drupe fruit (D-III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III is correct.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. Iron, B. Zinc, C. Boron, D. Molybdenum. List II: I. Synthesis of auxin, II. Component of nitrate reductase, III. Activator of catalase, IV. Cell elongation and differentiation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Iron is an activator of catalase (A-III). Zinc is involved in the synthesis of auxin (tryptophan synthesis) (B-I). Boron is required for cell elongation and differentiation (C-IV). Molybdenum is a component of nitrate reductase (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Select the favourable conditions required for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin at the alveoli.
options: Low pO2, low pCO2, more H+, higher temperature
High pO2, low pCO2, less H+, lower temperature
Low pO2, high pCO2, more H+, higher temperature
High pO2, high pCO2, less H+, higher temperature
questions.explanation: Oxyhaemoglobin formation at alveoli is favoured by high pO2, low pCO2, less H+ concentration, and lower temperature — opposite conditions favour oxygen release at tissues (Bohr effect).

questions.text: Now a days it is possible to detect the mutated gene causing cancer by allowing radioactive probe to hybridise its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, followed by its detection using autoradiography because:
options: Mutated gene does not appear on photographic film as the probe has complementarity with it.
Mutated gene partially appears on a photographic film.
Mutated gene completely and clearly appears on a photographic film.
Mutated gene does not appear on a photographic film as the probe has no complementarity with it.
questions.explanation: The radioactive probe is designed to be complementary to the normal (non-mutated) gene sequence. Since it cannot hybridize with the mutated gene (no complementarity), the mutated gene does not appear (no signal) on the autoradiograph/photographic film.

questions.text: Movement and accumulation of ions across a membrane against their concentration gradient can be explained by:
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy (ATP) to move ions and molecules across a membrane against their concentration gradient, unlike passive transport, facilitated diffusion, or osmosis, which all move substances along their gradient.

questions.text: Bulliform cells are responsible for
options: Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
Protecting the plant from salt stress.
questions.topic: Bulliform Cells - Function in Leaf Curling
questions.explanation: Bulliform (motor) cells are large, empty cells present in the epidermis of grass (monocot) leaves. They help in inward curling of leaves during water stress to minimize water loss. 11th NCERT Page No. 77.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Lipase (B) Nuclease (C) Protease (D) Amylase
List II: (I) Peptide bond (II) Ester bond (III) Glycosidic bond (IV) Phosphodiester bond
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Lipase hydrolyzes ester bonds in lipids (A-II). Nuclease hydrolyzes phosphodiester bonds in nucleic acids (B-IV). Protease hydrolyzes peptide bonds in proteins (C-I). Amylase hydrolyzes glycosidic bonds in carbohydrates (D-III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III is correct.

questions.text: What is the name of the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart in a frog?
questions.explanation: Vena cava carries deoxygenated blood from body parts to the sinus venosus, which then passes this blood into the right atrium of the frog's heart.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement.
options: Split gene arrangement is characteristic of prokaryotes.
In capping, methyl guanosine triphosphate is added to the 3' end of hnRNA.
RNA polymerase binds with Rho factor to terminate the process of transcription in bacteria.
The coding strand in a transcription unit is copied to an mRNA.
questions.explanation: Rho factor is a protein that binds with RNA polymerase and assists in terminating transcription in bacteria (Rho-dependent termination). Split genes are characteristic of eukaryotes (not prokaryotes); capping adds methyl guanosine triphosphate to the 5' end (not 3'); and the template strand (not coding strand) is copied to make mRNA.

questions.text: Use of bioresources by multinational companies and organisations without authorisation from the concerned country and its people is called
questions.explanation: Biopiracy refers to the unauthorised use/exploitation of a country's bioresources (and associated traditional knowledge) by other nations or multinational companies without fair compensation or permission.

questions.text:
Which of the following are secondary lymphoid organs?
(a) Bone marrow (b) Tonsils (c) Spleen (d) Thymus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Bone marrow and thymus are PRIMARY lymphoid organs (where lymphocytes mature). Tonsils and spleen are SECONDARY lymphoid organs (where mature lymphocytes interact with antigens and undergo proliferation into effector cells), along with lymph nodes, Peyer's patches, and appendix. So (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: In which animal do haploid cells divide mitotically to produce gametes?
questions.topic: Animals where haploid cells divide mitotically to produce gametes
questions.explanation: In honeybees, males are haploid (from unfertilized eggs) and produce sperm via mitotic division of haploid cells, not meiosis.

questions.text: Under normal physiological conditions in human being every 100ml of oxygenated blood can deliver _____ ml of O₂ to the tissues.
questions.explanation: Under normal physiological conditions, every 100 ml of oxygenated blood delivers around 5 ml of O₂ to the tissues.

questions.text: Auxin is used by gardeners to prepare weed-free lawns. But no damage is caused to grass as auxin
options: Does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.
Can help in cell division in grasses, to produce growth
Promotes abscission of mature leaves only
questions.topic: Auxin Herbicide - Selective Action on Dicot Weeds
questions.explanation: Synthetic auxins like 2,4-D are used as selective herbicides because they do not affect mature monocotyledonous plants (grasses) but kill broad-leaved dicot weeds. 11th NCERT Page No. 176.

questions.text:
Match the hominids with their correct brain size.
(a) Homo habilis (b) Homo neanderthalensis (c) Homo erectus (d) Homo sapiens
(i) 900cc (ii) 1350cc (iii) 650-800 cc (iv) 1400 cc
Select the correct option.
questions.explanation: Homo habilis had a brain capacity of about 650-800 cc (iii); Homo erectus about 900 cc (i); Homo neanderthalensis about 1350 cc (ii); Homo sapiens about 1400 cc (iv).

questions.text: Use of an artificial kidney during hemodialysis may result in: (a) Nitrogenous waste build-up in the body (b) Non-elimination of excess potassium ions (c) Reduced absorption of calcium ions from gastro-intestinal tract (d) Reduced RBC production. Which of the following options is the most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Hemodialysis via artificial kidney does not correct the reduced absorption of calcium ions from the GI tract (normally regulated by erythropoietin and vitamin D activation functions of kidney) or the reduced RBC production (due to lack of erythropoietin secretion by diseased kidneys), since dialysis only removes wastes/excess ions but doesn't replace the kidney's hormonal functions.

questions.text: Tegmina in cockroach, arises from:
questions.explanation: The tegmina (forewings) of a cockroach arise from the mesothorax, while the hind wings arise from the metathorax.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the most abundant protein in the animals?
questions.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal kingdom, forming a major structural component of connective tissues, skin, bones and cartilage.

questions.text: Which one of the following symbols represents mating between relatives (consanguineous mating) in human pedigree analysis?
options: A double horizontal line connecting a square and a circle (indicating consanguineous mating)
A square and circle connected with a single line, with a filled square offspring below connected to another couple above
A filled square, filled circle, and filled diamond shown side by side
A square connected to a circle by a single horizontal line (normal mating symbol)
questions.explanation: In pedigree analysis, a double horizontal line connecting a square (male) and a circle (female) represents consanguineous mating (mating between relatives), as opposed to a single line which represents a normal (non-related) mating.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct? A. The Amazon rainforest being cut and cleared for cultivation of soyabeans is an example of habitat loss. B. Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon became extinct due to over-exploitation by humans. C. The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in East Africa helped in population growth of cichlid fish in the lake. D. Water hyacinth is an invasive species. E. When a species becomes extinct, the plant and animal species associated with it are not affected.
options: A, B, D and E only
questions.topic: Correct statements about habitat loss/extinction examples
questions.explanation: A is true (habitat loss example). B is true (over-exploitation led to their extinction). D is true (water hyacinth is invasive). C is false (Nile perch caused decline, not growth, of cichlid populations). E is false (co-extinction occurs). A, B and D only.

questions.text: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and calcium at a given time, is referred to as:
questions.topic: Term for nutrient amount in soil at a given time
questions.explanation: The amount of nutrients present in the soil at any given time is called the standing state (or standing state of nutrients).

questions.text: Diadelphous stamens are found in:
questions.explanation: Diadelphous stamens (filaments united into two bundles) are characteristic of pea (Fabaceae family) flowers.

questions.text: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system by the release of______.
questions.explanation: Muscle contraction is initiated when a motor neuron releases the neurotransmitter acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, which generates an action potential in the muscle fiber.

questions.text: Which of the following elements is responsible for maintaining turgor in cells?
questions.explanation: Potassium plays a key role in maintaining the turgor pressure of cells, regulating osmotic balance and stomatal movement.

questions.text: A non-proteinaceous enzyme is:
questions.explanation: Ribozymes are catalytic RNA molecules, making them non-proteinaceous enzymes, unlike the other options which are protein enzymes.

questions.text: Which of the following is present between the adjacent bones of the vertebral column?
questions.explanation: Cartilaginous intervertebral discs are present between adjacent vertebrae of the vertebral column, allowing flexibility and acting as shock absorbers.

questions.text: A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by the three regions in DNA and these are with respect to upstream and down stream end;
questions.topic: Transcription Unit - Promoter, Structural Gene, Terminator
questions.explanation: A transcription unit in DNA is defined by three regions: the promoter (upstream), the structural gene, and the terminator (downstream). 12th NCERT Page No. 92.

questions.text: Which of the following hormones released from the pituitary is actually synthesized in the hypothalamus?
questions.topic: Hypothalamic Hormones Released by Posterior Pituitary (ADH)
questions.explanation: ADH (vasopressin) and oxytocin are actually synthesized by the hypothalamus and are only stored and released from the posterior pituitary. LH, FSH and ACTH are synthesized and released by the anterior pituitary itself. 11th NCERT, Page No. - 242.

questions.text: Several hormones like hCG, hPL, estrogen, progesterone are produced by:
questions.explanation: The placenta acts as a temporary endocrine gland during pregnancy, producing hCG, human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogen, and progesterone.

questions.text: The posterior pituitary gland is not a 'true' endocrine gland because:
options: It is provided with a duct
It only stores and releases hormones
It is under the regulation of hypothalamus
questions.explanation: The posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) does not synthesize hormones itself; it only stores and releases hormones (oxytocin and vasopressin) that are synthesized by the hypothalamus, so it is not a 'true' endocrine gland.

questions.text: Choose the correct statement.
options: All Pisces have gills covered by an operculum.
All cyclostomes do not possess jaws and paired fins.
All reptiles have a three-chambered heart.
questions.explanation: All cyclostomes (like Petromyzon, Myxine) lack jaws and paired fins, which is correct. Not all Pisces have an operculum (e.g., cartilaginous fish have gill slits without an operculum), not all mammals are viviparous (e.g., Platypus, Echidna lay eggs), and crocodiles (reptiles) have a four-chambered heart.

questions.text: Match List I with List II related to muscular/skeletal system: List I — A. Tetany, B. Arthritis, C. Myasthenia gravis, D. Muscular dystrophy. List II — I. Inflammation of joints, II. Autoimmune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction, III. Wild contraction in muscle due to low Ca2+ in body fluid, IV. Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle.
questions.explanation: Tetany is caused by low Ca2+ causing wild contraction (III); Arthritis is inflammation of joints (I); Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of neuromuscular junction (II); Muscular dystrophy is progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle (IV). A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.text: The vascular cambium normally gives rise to:
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium, a lateral meristem, produces secondary xylem towards the inside and secondary phloem towards the outside during secondary growth in dicot stems and roots.

questions.text: Match the trophic levels with their correct species examples in grassland ecosystem: (a) Fourth trophic level, (b) Second trophic level, (c) First trophic level, (d) Third trophic level with (i) Crow, (ii) Vulture, (iii) Rabbit, (iv) Grass
questions.topic: Trophic levels and examples in grassland ecosystem
questions.explanation: In the grassland food chain (Grass→Rabbit→Snake/Crow→Vulture/Hawk type), grass is the first trophic level (iv), rabbit (herbivore) is the second (iii)... per official key, fourth trophic level is vulture (ii), second trophic level is rabbit (iii), first trophic level is grass (iv), third trophic level is crow (i). This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: AGGTATCGCAT is a sequence from the coding strand of a gene. What will be the corresponding sequence of the transcribed mRNA?
questions.explanation: Since the coding strand has the same sequence as the mRNA (except T is replaced by U), the mRNA sequence transcribed will be identical to the coding strand with U in place of T: AGGUAUCGCAU.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of chordates?
questions.explanation: Chordates are characterized by the presence of pharyngeal gill slits (not their absence), a dorsal hollow nerve cord, a notochord, and a post-anal tail at some stage of development. 'Absence of gills' is therefore NOT a characteristic of chordates -- the presence of gill slits is.

questions.text: Due to increasing air borne allergens and pollutants, many people in urban areas are suffering from respiratory disorder causing wheezing due to:
options: Proliferation of fibrous tissues and damage of the alveolar walls
reduction in the secretion of surfactants by pneumocytes
benign growth on mucous lining of nasal cavity
questions.explanation: Wheezing due to air borne allergens and pollutants in urban areas is caused by inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles, a characteristic feature of asthma.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. Taenia, B. Paramoecium, C. Periplaneta, D. Pheretima. List II: I. Nephridia, II. Contractile vacuole, III. Flame cells, IV. Urecose gland. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Taenia (tapeworm) excretes via flame cells (A-III). Paramoecium uses a contractile vacuole for osmoregulation/excretion (B-II). Periplaneta (cockroach) excretes via uricose glands (C-IV). Pheretima (earthworm) excretes via nephridia (D-I). So the correct match is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is not true about the universal rules of binomial nomenclature?
options: The first word in a biological name represents the specific epithet, while the second component denotes the genus
The specific epithet in the biological name starts with a small letter
Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined or printed in italics
Biological names are generally in Latin
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first word is the genus and the second is the specific epithet — the reverse of what statement 1 says, making it the incorrect statement.

questions.text: In gel electrophoresis, separated DNA fragments can be visualized with the help of:
questions.topic: Visualization of DNA in gel electrophoresis
questions.explanation: DNA fragments separated by gel electrophoresis are stained with ethidium bromide, which intercalates into the DNA and fluoresces under UV radiation, allowing the bands to be visualised.

questions.text: Alpha-helix is found in which level of protein structure?
questions.topic: Level of protein structure for alpha-helix
questions.explanation: The alpha-helix is a type of secondary structure of proteins, formed by hydrogen bonding within the polypeptide backbone.

questions.text: If a colour blind female marries a man whose mother was also colour blind, what are the chances of her progeny having colour blindness?
questions.explanation: A colour-blind man's mother being colour blind (XcXc) means the man himself must be XcY (colour blind, since he gets one Xc from his mother). Crossing a colour-blind woman (XcXc) with a colour-blind man (XcY) gives all daughters XcXc (colour blind) and all sons XcY (colour blind), so 100% of the progeny will be colour blind.

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage of inbreeding?
options: It exposes harmful recessive genes that are eliminated by selection.
Elimination of less desirable genes and accumulation of superior genes takes place due to it.
It decreases the productivity of inbred population, after continuous inbreeding.
questions.explanation: Decreased productivity of an inbred population after continuous inbreeding (inbreeding depression) is a disadvantage, not an advantage, of inbreeding. The other options describe genuine advantages of inbreeding — exposing and eliminating harmful recessive genes and accumulating superior genes (note: inbreeding actually increases, not decreases, homozygosity, but that aspect is treated as an advantage statement here).

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Protoplast fusion, (b) Plant tissue culture, (c) Meristem culture, (d) Micropropagation with (i) Totipotency, (ii) Pomato, (iii) Somaclones, (iv) Virus free plants.
questions.topic: Matching plant biotechnology term to application
questions.explanation: Protoplast fusion gives hybrids like Pomato (ii); Plant tissue culture is based on totipotency (i); Meristem culture gives virus-free plants (iv); Micropropagation produces somaclones (iii). (a)-(ii),(b)-(i),(c)-(iv),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: Good vision depends on adequate intake of carotene-rich food. Select the best option from the following statements: (a) Vitamin A derivatives are formed from carotene. (b) The photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the inner segment. (c) Retinal is a derivative of Vitamin A. (d) Retinal is a light absorbing part of all the visual photopigments.
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (c), and (d) are correct: Vitamin A derivatives form from carotene, retinal is a Vitamin A derivative, and retinal is the light-absorbing component of all visual photopigments. Statement (b) is incorrect because photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the outer segment, not the inner segment, of photoreceptor cells.

questions.text: By which method was a new breed 'Hisardale' of sheep formed by using Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams?
questions.explanation: Hisardale, a new sheep breed, was developed by cross-breeding Bikaneri ewes with Marino rams, combining desirable traits from both breeds.

questions.text: Cuboidal epithelium with brush border of microvilli is found in:
questions.topic: Location of cuboidal epithelium with brush border
questions.explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron is lined with cuboidal epithelium bearing a brush border of microvilli, which increases the surface area for reabsorption.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Exophthalmic goiter (B) Acromegaly (C) Cushing's syndrome (D) Cretinism
List II: (I) Excess secretion of cortisol, moon face & hyperglycemia (II) Hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone and stunted growth. (III) Hyper secretion of thyroid hormone & protruding eye balls. (IV) Excessive secretion of growth hormone.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Exophthalmic goiter involves hyper secretion of thyroid hormone and protruding eye balls (A-III). Acromegaly results from excessive secretion of growth hormone (B-IV). Cushing's syndrome involves excess cortisol, moon face, and hyperglycemia (C-I). Cretinism involves hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone and stunted growth (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Match the following columns and select the correct option: (a) Organ of Corti, (b) Cochlea, (c) Eustachian tube, (d) Stapes with (i) Connects middle ear and pharynx, (ii) Coiled part of the labyrinth, (iii) Attached to the oval window, (iv) Located on the basilar membrane.
questions.explanation: Organ of Corti is located on the basilar membrane (iv), Cochlea is the coiled part of the labyrinth (ii), Eustachian tube connects the middle ear and pharynx (i), and Stapes is attached to the oval window (iii). This matches a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification.
Reason (R): The ampicillin resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
