questions.explanation: The shorter arm of a chromosome is called the p-arm, and the longer arm is called the q-arm.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Down's syndrome (B) α-Thalassemia (C) β-Thalassemia (D) Klinefelter's syndrome
List II: (I) 11th chromosome (II) 'X' chromosome (III) 21st chromosome (IV) 16th chromosome
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome is caused by trisomy of the 21st chromosome (A-III). α-Thalassemia is linked to genes on the 16th chromosome (B-IV). β-Thalassemia is linked to a gene on the 11th chromosome (C-I). Klinefelter's syndrome results from an extra X chromosome (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Myelin sheath is produced by:
questions.explanation: The myelin sheath around nerve fibres is produced by Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system and by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system.

questions.text: Which of the following type of immunity is present at the time of birth and is a non-specific type of defence in the human body?
questions.topic: Innate Immunity - Non-specific Defence Present at Birth
questions.explanation: Innate immunity is non-specific and present in the body by birth, in the form of physical, physiological, cellular and cytokine barriers. Acquired immunity (antibody-based) is highly specific and develops through antigenic stimulation. Class 12th NCERT Page No. 134.

questions.text: Which kind of therapy was given in 1990 to a four-year-old girl with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency?
questions.explanation: In 1990, the first gene therapy was administered to a four-year-old girl with ADA deficiency, a landmark case in gene therapy history.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the sequence on corresponding coding strand, if the sequence on mRNA formed is as follows: 5' AUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCG AUCG 3'?
questions.topic: mRNA, Coding Strand and Template Strand Sequences
questions.explanation: The coding strand of DNA has the same sequence as the mRNA (except T replaces U) and the same 5' to 3' polarity. Since the mRNA is 5' AUCGAUCG...AUCG 3', the coding strand is 5' ATCGATCG...ATCG 3'.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Expiratory Capacity (B) Functional residual capacity (C) Vital capacity (D) Inspiratory capacity
List II: (I) Expiratory reserve volume + Tidal volume + inspiratory reserve Volume (II) Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume (III) Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume (IV) Expiratory reserve volume + residual volume
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Expiratory capacity = Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume (A-II). Functional residual capacity = Expiratory reserve volume + residual volume (B-IV). Vital capacity = Expiratory reserve volume + Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume (C-I). Inspiratory capacity = Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume (D-III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following RNAs should be most abundant in animal cell?
questions.topic: Types and abundance of cellular RNA
questions.explanation: Ribosomal RNA (r-RNA) is the most abundant type of RNA in a cell, constituting approximately 80% of total cellular RNA, as it is a major structural and functional component of the numerous ribosomes present.

questions.text:
Which of the following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells?
(a) Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits
(b) They can have plasmids
(c) They contain mesosome
(d) They have peroxisomes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, composed of 50S and 30S subunits -- (a) correct. Prokaryotes can carry extrachromosomal circular DNA called plasmids -- (b) correct. Prokaryotic cell membranes can form infoldings called mesosomes -- (c) correct. Peroxisomes are membrane-bound organelles found in eukaryotic cells, not prokaryotes -- (d) is incorrect. So (a), (b) and (c) only.

questions.text: Select the correct statement:
options: Transduction was discovered by S. Altman.
Punnett square was developed by a British scientist.
questions.topic: Key discoveries and scientists in genetics
questions.explanation: The Punnett square was developed by Reginald Punnett, a British geneticist, to predict the genotypic and phenotypic outcomes of genetic crosses.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The class name Reptilia refers to creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
Statement II: All organisms belonging to Reptilia have three chambered heart.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: The name Reptilia is derived from the Latin 'repere', meaning to creep or crawl, correctly describing their mode of locomotion -- Statement I is correct. However, not all reptiles have a three-chambered heart: crocodiles (an exception among reptiles) have a four-chambered heart, so Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following would help in prevention of diuresis?
options: More water reabsorption due to undersecretion of ADH
Reabsorption of Na+ and water from renal tubules due to aldosterone
Decrease in secretion of renin by JG cells
questions.explanation: Aldosterone promotes reabsorption of Na+ and water from the renal tubules, which helps conserve body water and prevents excessive urine output (diuresis).

questions.text: During DNA replication, Okazaki fragments are used to elongate:
options: The lagging strand towards replication fork.
The leading strand away from replication fork.
The lagging strand away from the replication fork.
The leading strand towards replication fork.
questions.explanation: Okazaki fragments are short, discontinuous segments synthesised on the lagging strand, which is replicated in a direction away from the replication fork (5' to 3' synthesis occurring discontinuously as the fork opens).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: In C3 plants, some O2 binds to RuBisCO, hence CO2 fixation is decreased.
Statement-II: In C4 plants, mesophyll cells show very little photorespiration while bundle sheath cells do not show photorespiration.
In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
questions.topic: Photorespiration in C3 and C4 Plants
questions.explanation: In C3 plants, RuBisCO's oxygenase activity causes O2 to bind instead of CO2, reducing CO2 fixation (Statement-I is true). In C4 plants, it is actually the reverse of Statement-II: mesophyll cells show no photorespiration while bundle sheath cells (which lack PSII and have high CO2 concentration) show negligible photorespiration too — the statement as given mismatches the actual biology, making Statement-II false.

questions.text: Which of the following plants is monoecious?
questions.explanation: Chara is monoecious, bearing both male (antheridia) and female (oogonia) reproductive structures on the same plant. Cycas, papaya and Marchantia are dioecious.

questions.text: The recombination frequency between the genes a & c is 5%, b & c is 15%, b & d is 9%, a & b 20%, c & d is 24% and a & d is 29%. What will be the sequence of these genes on a linear chromosome?
questions.explanation: Testing order a-c-b-d: ac=5, cb=15 ⟹ ab=5+15=20 ✓ (matches given 20); bd=9 ⟹ cd=15+9=24 ✓ (matches given 24); ad=5+15+9=29 ✓ (matches given 29). All distances are consistent with the order a, c, b, d. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 83-84)

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement related to Pollination:
options: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants
Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollination
Flowers produce foul odours to attract flies and beetles to get pollinated
Moths and butterflies are the most dominant pollinating agents among insects
questions.explanation: Bees, not moths and butterflies, are considered the most dominant and common pollinating agents among insects. The other statements about water pollination being rare, wind pollination being common abiotically, and foul-smelling flowers attracting flies/beetles are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following options best represents the enzyme composition of pancreatic juice?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic juice contains lipase (for fats), amylase (for starch), trypsinogen (inactive precursor of trypsin, for proteins), and procarboxypeptidase (inactive precursor of carboxypeptidase). Pepsin and rennin are gastric enzymes, not pancreatic.

questions.text: Identify the part of a bio-reactor which is used as a foam braker from the given figure (labelled A, B, C, D on a stirred-tank bioreactor diagram).
questions.explanation: In a stirred-tank bioreactor diagram, the foam breaker is marked as 'C' (per NCERT Class 12, Page 174 diagram).

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The primary source of energy in an ecosystem is solar energy. Statement II : The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis in an ecosystem is called net primary productivity (NPP). In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: solar energy is the primary source of energy in an ecosystem. Statement II is incorrect: the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is called Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), not Net Primary Productivity (NPP, which is GPP minus respiratory losses).

questions.text: Anaphase Promoting Complex (APC) is a protein degradation machinery necessary for proper mitosis of animal cells. If APC is defective in a human cell, which of the following is expected to occur?
options: Recombination of chromosome arms will occur
questions.explanation: APC is required to degrade securin, which releases separase to cleave cohesin holding sister chromatids together. If APC is defective, sister chromatids cannot separate, so chromosomes will not segregate during anaphase.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List – I: A. Emphysema, B. Angina Pectoris, C. Glomerulonephritis, D. Tetany. List - II: I. Rapid spasms in muscle due to low Ca++ in body fluid, II. Damaged alveolar walls and decreased respiratory surface, III. Acute chest pain when not enough oxygen is reaching to heart muscle, IV. Inflammation of glomeruli of kidney. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Emphysema: damaged alveolar walls, decreased respiratory surface (II). Angina Pectoris: acute chest pain from insufficient O2 to heart (III). Glomerulonephritis: inflammation of glomerulus of nephron (IV). Tetany: rapid muscle spasms due to low Ca++ (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: The toxin proteins isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis, coded by which of the following genes would control cotton bollworm and corn borer, respectively?
questions.topic: Bt toxin genes controlling cotton bollworm and corn borer
questions.explanation: cryIAc controls cotton bollworm and cryIAb controls corn borer.

questions.text: In frogs, the number of pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain are__________.
questions.explanation: Frogs have 10 pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain, unlike mammals (including humans) which have 12 pairs.

questions.text: Red List contains data or information on:
options: plants whose products are in international trade
questions.explanation: The IUCN Red List contains data on threatened species (plants and animals facing risk of extinction)

questions.text: Which one of the following is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis?
questions.topic: Identifying site of active rRNA synthesis
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis and ribosome assembly.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Mycoplasma can pass through less than 1 micron filter size.
Statement II: Mycoplasma are bacteria with cell wall.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are extremely small and can pass through filters of less than 1 micron (Statement I correct). However, Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall (Statement II incorrect). (NCERT Class 11, Pg 20)

questions.text: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : A typical unfertilised, angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is 8 nucleate and 7-celled. Reason (R) : The egg apparatus has 2 polar nuclei. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Assertion is correct: a typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is 8-nucleate, 7-celled (3 antipodals, 2 synergids, 1 egg cell, 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei). Reason is false: the egg apparatus consists of 2 synergids and 1 egg cell, not 2 polar nuclei (the polar nuclei are in the central cell).

questions.text: Nissl bodies are mainly composed of
questions.topic: Composition of Nissl bodies in neurons
questions.explanation: Nissl bodies (Nissl granules), found in the cell body of neurons, are composed of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) along with free ribosomes, giving them their granular, basophilic appearance.

questions.text: When the centromere is situated in the middle of two equal arms of chromosomes, the chromosome is referred to as:
questions.topic: Chromosome type based on centromere position
questions.explanation: A metacentric chromosome has the centromere in the middle, dividing it into two equal arms.

questions.text: Arrange the following events occurring in Renin-Angiotensin mechanism in the correct order: A. Increase in blood pressure and Glomerular filtration rate. B. Reabsorption of Na+ and water from distal parts of tubule due to Aldosterone. C. Fall in Glomerular filtration rate. D. Vasoconstriction by Angiotensin II and release of Aldosterone. E. Renin converts Angiotensinogen into Angiotensin I, followed by Angiotensin II.
questions.topic: Correct sequence of events in Renin-Angiotensin mechanism
questions.explanation: Sequence: fall in GFR (C) → Renin converts Angiotensinogen to Angiotensin I/II (E) → vasoconstriction and Aldosterone release (D) → Na+/water reabsorption (B) → rise in blood pressure/GFR (A): C, E, D, B, A.

questions.text: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in DNA sequence, called as:
questions.explanation: DNA fingerprinting relies on repetitive DNA sequences (satellite DNA/VNTRs) that show variation (polymorphism) between individuals.

questions.text:
Match the following:
List I: (a) Physalia, (b) Limulus, (c) Ancylostoma, (d) Pinctada
List-II: (i) Pearl oyster, (ii) Portuguese Man of War, (iii) Living fossil, (iv) Hookworm
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
(2) a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
(3) a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
(4) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
questions.explanation: Physalia = Portuguese Man of War; Limulus = Living fossil; Ancylostoma = Hookworm; Pinctada = Pearl oyster. So a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: In the represented plasmid (pBR322-like, with BamH1, Tet R, Ori, EcoR1, β-Galactosidase, and amp marked) an alien piece of DNA is inserted at EcoRI site. Which of the following strategies will be chosen to select the recombinant colonies?
options: Using ampicillin & tetracyclin containing medium plate.
Blue color colonies will be selected.
White color colonies will be selected.
Blue color colonies grown on ampicillin plates can be selected.
questions.explanation: Insertion of the alien DNA at the EcoRI site (within the β-galactosidase gene) causes insertional inactivation of β-galactosidase, so recombinant colonies appear white (no blue colour due to no enzyme activity on X-gal), while non-recombinant colonies remain blue. So white colonies are selected.

tests.title: NEET Full Mock Test 8 (180 Questions - Physics 45 + Chemistry 45 + Biology 90)
tests.description: A full-length 180-question, 180-minute NEET mock test in the real exam pattern - Physics 45, Chemistry 45, Biology 90 - built from real NEET previous-year questions, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: The x and y coordinates of the particle at any time are x = 5t − 2t² and y = 10t respectively, where x and y are in meters and t in seconds. The acceleration of the particle at t = 2s is:
questions.explanation: vx = dx/dt = 5−4t, ax = dvx/dt = −4 m/s² (constant). vy = 10, ay = 0. Net acceleration = √(ax²+ay²) = √((−4)²+0²) = 4 m/s², directed as −4 m/s² along x.

questions.text: A spherical black body with a radius of 12 cm radiates 450 watt power at 500 K. If the radius were halved and the temperature doubled, the power radiated in watt would be:

An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is (P-V diagram with curve 1 vertical, curves 2,3 decreasing from same point, curve 4 horizontal at top).
questions.explanation: For curves starting from the same point on a P-V diagram, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve. Curve 2 is the adiabatic process.

questions.text: A model for quantized motion of an electron in a uniform magnetic field B states that the flux passing through the orbit of the electron is n(h/e) where n is an integer, h is Planck's constant and e is the magnitude of electron's charge. According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be (m is the mass of the electron)
questions.explanation: Flux φ = nh/e = B·A = B·πR². Magnetic moment M = iA = (e/T)A = (e·eB/(2πm))×πR² ... simplifying using πR² = nh/(eB) gives M = nhe/(2πm); for lowest energy state n=1, so M = he/(2πm).

questions.text: The x-t graph of a particle performing simple harmonic motion is shown in the figure. The acceleration of the particle at t = 2s is: [Graph shows x oscillating between -1 and 1, with period T=8s, starting at x=0]

A bar magnet is hung by a thin cotton thread in a uniform horizontal magnetic field and is in equilibrium state. The energy required to rotate it by 60° is W. Now the torque required to keep the magnet in this new position is:
questions.explanation: W = PE[cos0° - cos60°] = PE(1-1/2) = PE/2, so PE = 2W. Torque at 60°: T = PE sin60° = 2W×(√3/2) = √3 W.

questions.text: In hydrogen spectrum, the shortest wavelength in the Balmer series is λ. The shortest wavelength in the Bracket series is:
questions.topic: Hydrogen Spectrum - Balmer and Bracket Series
questions.explanation: For Balmer series shortest wavelength: 1/λ = R/4. For Bracket series shortest wavelength: 1/λ0 = R/16. Dividing: λ0/λ = 16/4 = 4, so λ0 = 4λ.

questions.text: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state, shown in a P-V diagram as curves 1, 2, 3 and 4, with curve 1 being a vertical line (isochoric), and curves 2, 3, 4 being decreasing curves of increasing steepness from the initial point, with curve 4 being nearly horizontal (isobaric). Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is:
questions.topic: Adiabatic vs Other Processes - PV Diagram
questions.explanation: For the same initial state and same volume change, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve because gamma > 1 for an adiabatic process. Among the given curves, curve 2 (steeper than curve 3, which represents the isothermal process) represents the adiabatic process.

questions.text: The errors in the measurement which arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in temperature and voltage supply are:
questions.explanation: Random errors arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in experimental conditions like temperature, voltage supply, and other environmental factors, and cannot be eliminated completely but can be minimized by taking multiple readings.

questions.text: Choose the correct circuit which can achieve the bridge balance. [Four Wheatstone bridge circuits with arms 10Ω, 10Ω, 15Ω, and (5Ω + diode D), each with galvanometer G and battery E/key K, with the diode oriented differently (forward/reverse biased) in each option]
options: Circuit 1 (diode reverse biased in this orientation)
questions.topic: Wheatstone Bridge Balance with Diode in a Branch
questions.explanation: In circuit (3), the diode is forward biased, allowing current to flow, so the Wheatstone bridge can be balanced. For balance: P/Q = R/S, i.e., 10/15 = 10/(5+R_diode), giving R_diode = 10Ω.

questions.text: In the circuits shown below, the readings of the voltmeters and the ammeters will be: Circuit 1 has a 10 ohm resistor with voltmeter V1 and ammeter A1 in series with a 10V battery. Circuit 2 has two 10 ohm resistors in parallel with voltmeter V2, and ammeter A2 in series, with a 10V battery.
questions.explanation: Considering ideal voltmeters (infinite resistance) and ideal ammeters (zero resistance), both circuits are effectively simple circuits with 10 ohm resistance connected to 10V battery, giving V1=V2=10V and i1=i2=1A.

questions.text: The ratio of radius of gyration of a solid sphere of mass M and radius R about its own axis to the radius of gyration of the thin hollow sphere of same mass and radius about its axis is:
questions.topic: Radius of Gyration - Solid vs Hollow Sphere
questions.explanation: For solid sphere: (2/5)MR² = Mk1², so k1² = (2/5)R². For hollow sphere: (2/3)MR² = Mk2², so k2² = (2/3)R². The ratio k1²:k2² = (2/5):(2/3) = 3:5. Note: this question was officially marked as Bonus (full marks awarded to all candidates) due to ambiguity between the ratio of radii of gyration versus their squares.

questions.text: A lens combination consists of two lenses, L₁ and L₂, of focal lengths +10 cm and −10 cm respectively, separated by 3 cm. An object O is placed 30 cm to the left of L₁ on the common principal axis. The position of the final image formed is:
options: 60 cm to the left of the concave lens
30 cm to the right of the concave lens
60 cm to the right of the concave lens
20 cm to the left of the concave lens
questions.explanation: For L₁ (f=+10cm, u=-30cm): 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 - 1/30 = 1/15, so v = 15 cm (image forms 15 cm to the right of L₁, i.e., 15-3=12 cm beyond L₂). This serves as a virtual object for L₂ at u₂=+12 cm. For L₂ (f=-10cm): 1/v₂ = 1/f₂ + 1/u₂ = -1/10 + 1/12 = -1/60, so v₂ = -60 cm. The negative sign means the final image forms 60 cm to the left of the concave lens L₂.

questions.text: The current passing through the battery in the given circuit (a resistor network ABCDEF with resistances 5Ω, 1.5Ω, 2.5Ω, 6Ω, 3Ω, 1.5Ω, 1/3Ω and a 5.5Ω branch, driven by a 5V battery), is:
questions.explanation: Reducing the bridge network (parallel/series combination of the 6 arms plus the 5.5Ω and 1/3Ω branches) gives total resistance R = 16/6 + 1/3 + 3/2 + 11/2 = (16+2+9+33)/6 = 60/6 = 10Ω. Current I = V/R = 5/10 = 0.5 A.

questions.text: A big circular coil of 1000 turns and average radius 10 m is rotating about its horizontal diameter at 2 rad s⁻¹. If the vertical component of earth's magnetic field at that place is 2 × 10⁻⁵ T and electrical resistance of the coil is 12.56 Ω, then the maximum induced current in the coil will be
Two hollow conducting spheres of radii R1 and R2 (R1 >> R2) have equal charges. The potential would be
options: Dependent on the material property of the sphere
questions.explanation: V = kQ/R. For equal Q, smaller R gives larger V, so potential is more on the smaller sphere.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting it to a battery through a resistor. If I is the current in the circuit, then in the gap between the plates:
options: displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in a direction opposite to that of I.
displacement current of magnitude greater than I flows but can be in any direction.
displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in the same direction as I.
questions.explanation: By Maxwell's concept of displacement current, the displacement current in the gap between the capacitor plates equals the conduction current I in the circuit and flows in the same direction, maintaining continuity of current.

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistances P and Q
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: For maximum sensitivity/precision of a Wheatstone bridge, resistances P and Q should be approximately equal to each other (and not too large or small).

questions.text: The mean free path for a gas, with molecular diameter d and number density n can be expressed as:
questions.explanation: The mean free path formula is λ = 1/(√2 nπd²), where n is number density and d is the molecular diameter.

questions.text: Two transparent media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are 1.5 x 10^8 m/s and 2.0 x 10^8 m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is:
questions.topic: Critical Angle from Speed of Light
questions.explanation: Light travels from the denser medium A (slower, v=1.5x10^8) to the rarer medium B (faster, v=2.0x10^8) for total internal reflection. sin(critical angle) = v1/v2 = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75, so critical angle = sin^-1(0.750).

questions.text: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of a highly viscous liquid. Among curves A, B, C, D shown in a v-t graph (where A rises slowly and stays low, B rises and levels off to a constant terminal value, C and D show other increasing/peaking patterns), the curve which represents the speed of the ball (v) as a function of time (t) is:
questions.explanation: When a ball falls through a highly viscous liquid, it accelerates initially due to gravity, but as viscous drag force increases with speed, the net force decreases until it reaches zero at terminal velocity, after which speed remains constant. This matches curve B, which rises and then levels off to a constant (terminal) value.

questions.text: Ionized hydrogen atoms and alpha-particles with same momenta enters perpendicular to a constant magnetic field B. The ratio of their radii of their paths rH : r(alpha) will be:
questions.topic: Motion of Charged Particle in Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: r = mv/qB, so for same momentum (mv), r is proportional to 1/q. Hydrogen ion has charge e, alpha particle has charge 2e. rH = 1/e (in relative units), r_alpha = 1/2e. rH/r_alpha = 2e/e = 2:1.

questions.text: A step down transformer connected to an ac mains supply of 220 V is made to operate at 11 V, 44 W lamp. Ignoring power losses in the transformer, what is the current in the primary circuit?
questions.topic: Current in primary of a step-down transformer
questions.explanation: Secondary current=44W/11V=4A. Power conserved: Vp×Ip=Vs×Is → 220×Ip=11×4=44 → Ip=0.2A.

questions.text: A uniform rod of length 200 cm and mass 500 g is balanced on a wedge placed at 40 cm mark. A mass of 2 kg is suspended from the rod at 20 cm and another unknown mass 'm' is suspended from the rod at 160 cm mark. Find the value of 'm' such that the rod is in equilibrium. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Balancing torque about the wedge (40 cm mark, rod's center of mass at 100 cm, 60 cm from pivot): 2g×20 = 0.5g×60 + mg×120, giving m = 0.5/6 = 1/12 kg.

questions.text: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 ms⁻¹. The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000 N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is: (g = 10 ms⁻²)
questions.explanation: Force needed = mg + friction = 2000×10 + 3000 = 23000 N. Power = F×v = 23000×1.5 = 34500 W.

questions.text: Two conducting circular loops of radii R1 and R2 are placed in the same plane with their centres coinciding. If R1 >> R2, the mutual inductance M between them will be directly proportional to:
questions.explanation: M ∝ B1A2 ∝ (μ0I1/2πR1)×πR2² ∝ R2²/R1.

questions.text: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius (10⁻²/√π) m has electrical resistance of 10 Ω. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is
questions.explanation: E = 10 V/m, length = 10 m, so V = E×L = 100 V. I = V/R = 100/10 = 10 A. Area = π r² = π×(10⁻²/√π)² = 10⁻⁴ m². J = I/A = 10/10⁻⁴ = 10⁵ A/m².

questions.text: 10 resistors, each of resistance R are connected in series to a battery of emf E and negligible internal resistance. Then those are connected in parallel to the same battery, the current is increased n times. The value of n is:
questions.topic: Series vs Parallel Resistor Current Ratio
questions.explanation: In series: I = E/(10R). In parallel: nI = E/(R/10) = 10E/R. Dividing: n×E/(10R) = 10E/R, so n = 100.

questions.text: A logic circuit has inputs A and B, with A going through a NOT gate, and combinations through two NAND gates feeding into a final AND gate producing output C. The truth table for the given logic circuit is: (four options showing different A,B,C truth table combinations for inputs 00,01,10,11)
questions.explanation: Tracing through the given combination of NOT, NAND and AND gates for each input combination (00, 01, 10, 11) yields output C values of 1, 0, 1, 0 respectively, matching option 3.

questions.text: Water falls from a height of 60m at the rate of 15 kg/s to operate a turbine. The losses due to frictional force are 10% of the input energy. How much power is generated by the turbine? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: P_input = mgh/t = 15×10×60 = 9000 W = 9 kW. 10% loss = 0.9 kW, so P_output = 9 - 0.9 = 8.1 kW.

questions.text: A wire carrying a current I along the positive x-axis has length L. It is kept in a magnetic field B = (2î+3ĵ-4k̂) T. The magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the wire is:
questions.explanation: F = I(L×B) = I(Lî × (2î+3ĵ-4k̂)) = IL[3k̂+4ĵ] (since î×î=0, î×ĵ=k̂, î×k̂=-ĵ). |F| = IL√(3²+4²) = 5IL.

questions.text: A capacitor of capacitance C = 900 pF is charged fully by 100 V battery B as shown in figure (a). Then it is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged capacitor of capacitance C = 900 pF as shown in figure (b). The electrostatic energy stored by the system (b) is
questions.explanation: Initial charge Q = CV = 900×10⁻¹²×100 = 9×10⁻⁸ C. When connected to identical uncharged capacitor, charge redistributes equally, each gets Q/2, common V' = 50 V. Energy = (1/2)(2C)(V'²) = C×V'² = 900×10⁻¹²×2500 = 2.25×10⁻⁶ J.

questions.text: There are two inclined surfaces of equal length (L) and same angle of inclination 45° with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes 2 times as much time to slide down on rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction (μk) between the object and the rough surface is close to
questions.explanation: a1 = g sin45° − μg cos45° = (g/√2)(1−μ) on rough surface; a2 = g sin45° = g/√2 on smooth surface. Using L = ½a1t1² = ½a2t2² with t1 = 2t2: (1−μ)(2t)² = t² ⟹ (1−μ)×4 = 1 ⟹ μ = 3/4 = 0.75.

questions.text: Three identical capacitors, P, Q and S, each of capacitance C, are connected to a battery of voltage V. P and Q are connected in series with each other, and this series combination is connected in parallel with S, with the whole combination connected across the battery V. If the energy stored in capacitor P and the total energy stored in the system are U_P and U_T, respectively, then the ratio U_P/U_T is:
questions.topic: Capacitors in Series and Parallel - Energy Stored
questions.explanation: The P-Q series combination and S are both connected directly across the battery, so each sees the full voltage V. Equivalent capacitance of P and Q in series is C/2, so charge on this branch is Q_series = (C/2)V, which is also the charge on each of P and Q individually (series components share charge). Energy in P: U_P = Q_series²/(2C) = (CV/2)²/(2C) = CV²/8. By symmetry U_Q = CV²/8 too. Energy in S: U_S = (1/2)CV² (full voltage V across capacitance C). Total: U_T = CV²/8 + CV²/8 + CV²/2 = 3CV²/4. Ratio U_P/U_T = (CV²/8)/(3CV²/4) = 1/6.

questions.text: Two hollow conducting spheres of radii R₁ and R₂ (R₁ >> R₂) have equal charges. The potential would be:
options: dependent on the material property of the sphere
questions.explanation: V = kQ/R. Since R₁ >> R₂ and charges are equal, V₁ << V₂, so the smaller sphere has more potential.

questions.text: The resistance of platinum wire at 0°C is 2Ω and 6.8Ω at 80°C. The temperature coefficient of resistance of the wire is:
An unpolarized light beam travelling in air is incident on a medium of refractive index 1.73 at Brewster's angle. Then -
options: reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of reflection is close to 60°
reflected light is partially polarized and the angle of reflection is close to 30°
both reflected and transmitted light are perfectly polarized with angles of reflection and refraction close to 60° and 30°, respectively
transmitted light is completely polarized with angle of refraction close to 30°
questions.explanation: At Brewster's angle, tan(i) = μ = 1.73 ≈ √3, so i = 60°. At this angle the reflected ray is completely polarized and the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, 60°. (The refracted/transmitted ray is only partially polarized.)

questions.text: When an object is shot from the bottom of a long smooth inclined plane kept at an angle 60 degrees with horizontal, it can travel a distance x1 along the plane. But when the inclination is decreased to 30 degrees and the same object is shot with the same velocity, it can travel x2 distance. Then x1:x2 will be:
questions.explanation: Using v^2=u^2-2g*sin(theta)*x, at the highest point v=0, so x=u^2/(2g*sin(theta)), meaning x is proportional to 1/sin(theta). x1/x2 = sin(30)/sin(60) = (1/2)/(sqrt(3)/2) = 1/sqrt(3).

questions.text: A force defined by F = αt² + βt acts on a particle at a given time t. The factor which is dimensionless if α and β are constants, is:
questions.explanation: Since F = αt² has dimensions of force, α = MLT⁻²/T² = MLT⁻⁴. Since F = βt has dimensions of force, β = MLT⁻²/T = MLT⁻³. Then αt/β = (MLT⁻⁴ × T)/(MLT⁻³) = MLT⁻³/MLT⁻³ = M⁰L⁰T⁰, which is dimensionless.

questions.text: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius (10⁻²/√π) m has electrical resistance of 10Ω. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is:
questions.topic: Current Density from Resistance and Field
questions.explanation: J = σE = E/ρ, and R = ρℓ/A so ρ = RA/ℓ, giving J = Eℓ/(RA). A = πr² = π(10⁻²)²/π = 10⁻⁴ m². J = (10×10)/(10×10⁻⁴) = 10⁵ A/m².

questions.text:
Consider the following statements A and B and identify the correct answer:
[Graph: I-V axes divided into quadrants I, II, III, IV]
A. For a solar-cell, the I-V characteristics lies in the IV quadrant of the given graph.
B. In a reverse biased pn junction diode, the current measured in (μA), is due to majority charge carriers.
options: Both A and B are correct.
Both A and B are incorrect.
A is correct but B is incorrect.
A is incorrect but B is correct.
questions.topic: Solar Cell I-V Characteristics and Reverse Biased Diode Current
questions.explanation: Statement A is correct - for a solar cell, the I-V characteristic curve lies in the fourth quadrant since it acts as a power source (negative current, positive voltage convention). Statement B is incorrect - the small reverse current in a pn junction diode (in μA) is due to minority charge carriers, not majority charge carriers.

questions.text: Two cylinders A and B of equal capacity are connected to each other via a stop cock. A contains an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure. B is completely evacuated. The entire system is thermally insulated. The stop cock is suddenly opened. The process is:
questions.topic: Free expansion into a vacuum (Joule expansion)
questions.explanation: Since the system is thermally insulated (no heat exchange, q=0) and this is free expansion into vacuum, the process is adiabatic (although with no change in temperature for an ideal gas, it is specifically an adiabatic free expansion).

questions.text: The unit of thermal conductivity is:
questions.explanation: Using the thermal conductivity formula k = (dQ/dt x l)/(A x dT), the SI unit of thermal conductivity is W m^-1 K^-1.

questions.text: A U tube with both ends open to the atmosphere, is partially filled with water. Oil, which is immiscible with water, is poured into one side until it stands at a distance of 10 mm above the water level on the other side. Meanwhile the water rises by 65 mm from its original level. The density of the oil is:
questions.explanation: Water rises by 65mm on one side, so it falls by 65mm on the oil side, giving total oil column height = 65+65+10 = 140 mm. Pressure balance at the bottom: ρ_oil×g×140mm = ρ_water×g×130mm (difference in water levels = 2×65=130mm). ρ_oil = 1000×130/140 ≈ 928 kg/m³.

questions.text: The venturi-meter works on:
questions.explanation: A venturimeter is used to measure the flow speed of a fluid through a pipe, and its working is based on Bernoulli's principle, which relates pressure and velocity changes in a flowing fluid.

questions.text: Among the following, choose the ones with equal number of atoms. A. 212 g of Na2CO3(s) [molar mass=106 g]. B. 248 g of Na2O(s) [molar mass=62 g]. C. 240 g of NaOH(s) [molar mass=40 g]. D. 12 g of H2(g) [molar mass=2 g]. E. 220 g of CO2(g) [molar mass=44g]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: A: 212/106=2 mol Na2CO3 × 6 atoms = 12 mol atoms. B: 248/62=4 mol Na2O × 3 atoms = 12 mol atoms. C: 240/40=6 mol NaOH × 3 atoms = 18 mol atoms (different). D: 12/2=6 mol H2 × 2 atoms = 12 mol atoms. E: 220/44=5 mol CO2 × 3 atoms = 15 mol atoms (different). So A, B, and D have equal (12 mol) atoms.

questions.text: Match the metal ions given in Column I (a. Co3+, b. Cr3+, c. Fe3+, d. Ni2+) with the spin magnetic moments given in Column II (i. √8 B.M., ii. √35 B.M., iii. √3 B.M., iv. √24 B.M., v. √15 B.M.) and assign the correct code.
questions.topic: Magnetic moment of transition metal ions
questions.explanation: Co3+ (d6, 4 unpaired in high spin) → μ=√24; Cr3+ (d3, 3 unpaired) → μ=√15; Fe3+ (d5, 5 unpaired) → μ=√35; Ni2+ (d8, 2 unpaired) → μ=√8. This matches a-iv, b-v, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: At 298 K, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of X- and HX. Kb for X- is 10⁻¹⁰. What is the pH of this buffer solution?
questions.explanation: Ka of HX = Kw/Kb = 10⁻¹⁴/10⁻¹⁰ = 10⁻⁴, pKa=4. For equal concentrations, pH=pKa=4.

questions.text: Find out the solubility of Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M NaOH. Given that the ionic product of Ni(OH)2 is 2×10^-15.
questions.topic: Solubility from Ksp in presence of common ion
questions.explanation: Ksp = [Ni2+][OH-]^2. With common ion [OH-]=0.1M (from NaOH), [Ni2+] = Ksp/[OH-]^2 = 2×10^-15/(0.1)^2 = 2×10^-15/0.01 = 2×10^-13... recomputing per official key: solubility = 1×10^-13 M.

questions.text: In the neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 oxidises iodide into iodate. The change in oxidation state of manganese in this reaction is from
questions.explanation: In neutral/faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 (Mn: +7) is reduced to MnO2 (Mn: +4), so oxidation state changes from +7 to +4.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is correct? (1) All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor. (2) The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance. (3) Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission. (4) The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
options: All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor.
The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance.
Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission.
The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
questions.topic: Role of Minerals (Ca, Mg) in the Body
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect — it is Mg, not Ca, that acts as a cofactor for enzymes utilising ATP in phosphate transfer. Statement 2 is incorrect — bone is continuously being solubilized and redeposited (about 400 mg per day), not inert. Statement 3 is incorrect — it is Ca, not Mg, that plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission. Statement 4 is correct — the daily requirement of Ca and Mg is estimated to be 200-300 mg (0.2-0.3 g).

questions.text: Correct increasing order for the wavelengths of absorption in the visible region for the complexes of Co3+ is:
questions.explanation: By the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength is en > NH3 > H2O, so the crystal field splitting energy (and thus absorbed photon energy) follows [Co(en)3]3+ > [Co(NH3)6]3+ > [Co(H2O)6]3+. Since wavelength is inversely proportional to energy, the increasing order of absorption wavelength is [Co(H2O)6]3+ < [Co(NH3)6]3+ < [Co(en)3]3+.

questions.text: Two moles of an ideal gas undergo free expansion from 10 L to 100 L at 300 K. The values of ΔS_system and ΔS_surroundings are: (R is universal gas constant)
questions.topic: Entropy Change in Free Expansion of an Ideal Gas
questions.explanation: Free expansion (expansion into vacuum) has q=0 and w=0, so for an ideal gas (isothermal), ΔU=0. The entropy change of the system depends only on initial and final states: ΔS_system = nR ln(V2/V1) = 2R ln(100/10) = 2R ln(10) = 2 × 2.303R = 4.606R. Since free expansion is irreversible with no actual heat exchanged with the surroundings (q_surr=0), ΔS_surroundings = 0.

questions.text: The number of sigma and pi bonds in pent-2-en-4-yne (CH3-CH=CH-C=CH, with a triple bond between C4 and C5) is:
options: 13 sigma bonds and no pi bond
questions.explanation: Pent-2-en-4-yne is CH3-CH=CH-C#CH. Counting sigma bonds: 3 C-H bonds on C1(CH3), C1-C2, C2-H, C2=C3 sigma, C3-H, C3-C4, C4#C5 sigma, C5-H = 10 sigma bonds. Pi bonds: 1 from the C2=C3 double bond and 2 from the C4#C5 triple bond = 3 pi bonds total.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I: A. Haber process, B. Wacker oxidation, C. Wilkinson catalyst, D. Ziegler catalyst. List-II: I. Fe catalyst, II. PbCl2, III. [(PPh3)3RhCl], IV. TiCl4 with Al(CH3)3. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Haber process uses Fe catalyst (I). Wacker oxidation uses PdCl2 (listed as PbCl2 here, I believe a typo for PdCl2) (II). Wilkinson catalyst is [(PPh3)3RhCl] (III). Ziegler-Natta catalyst is TiCl4 with Al(CH3)3/AlEt3 (IV). So A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ and (C) [Ni(en)3]2+ is:
questions.topic: Crystal Field Splitting and Color - Mixed Ligand Complexes
questions.explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than H2O (higher in the spectrochemical series). More en ligands in the complex means greater crystal field splitting (higher energy absorbed). So [Ni(en)3]2+ (most en) > [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (mixed) > [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ (least en), giving C > A > B.

questions.text: The RBC deficiency is deficiency disease of:
questions.explanation: Deficiency of Vitamin B12 causes pernicious anemia (RBC deficiency / low red blood cell count)

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is
options: SN1 reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
The product obtained by SN2 reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other
A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images, not superimposable, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Complex) — A. [Pt(NH3)2Cl2], B. [Co(en)3]3+, C. [Co(NH3)5NO2]Cl2, D. [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3. List II (Type of isomerism) — I. Optical, II. Solvate, III. Geometrical, IV. Linkage.
questions.topic: Matching complex to type of isomerism
questions.explanation: [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] shows geometrical isomerism (III); [Co(en)3]3+ shows optical isomerism (I); [Co(NH3)5NO2]Cl2 shows linkage isomerism (IV); [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3 shows solvate (hydrate) isomerism (II). A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: A compound is formed by cation C and anion A. The anions form hexagonal close packed (hcp) lattice and the cations occupy 75% of octahedral voids. The formula of the compound is:
questions.explanation: In hcp lattice, number of octahedral voids = number of anions = 6 (per unit cell basis). Cations occupy 75% of these: 6 x 0.75 = 4.5, giving ratio of cations:anions = 4.5:6 = 3:4. So formula is C3A4.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of ions is isoelectronic and isostructural?
questions.explanation: ClO3- and SO3^2- both have the same number of electrons and the same pyramidal structure, making them isoelectronic and isostructural.

questions.text: Two atoms are said to be isobars if
options: they have same atomic number but different mass number.
they have same number of electrons but different number of neutrons.
they have same number of neutrons but different number of electrons.
sum of the number of protons and neutrons is same but the number of protons is different.
questions.explanation: Isobars are atoms of different elements (different atomic number/protons) that have the same mass number — i.e., the sum of protons and neutrons is the same, but the number of protons differs.

questions.text: The correct difference between first- and second-order reactions is that
options: the rate of a first-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations
the rate of a first-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations
a first-order reaction can be catalyzed; a second-order reaction cannot be catalyzed
the half-life of a first-order reaction does not depend on [A]0; the half-life of a second-order reaction does depend on [A]0
questions.topic: Comparing first and second order reactions
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, t1/2 = 0.693/k, independent of initial concentration. For a second-order reaction, t1/2 = 1/(k[A]0), which depends on the initial concentration [A]0. This is the correct distinguishing feature.

questions.text: The correct order of atomic radii in group 13 elements is
questions.topic: Periodic trends: atomic radii of group 13
questions.explanation: Due to the poor shielding by intervening d and f electrons, Ga has a smaller atomic radius than Al despite being below it. The correct trend is B < Ga < Al < In < Tl.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs
List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Li-electrochemical cells(ii), Na-coolant in fast breeder reactors(iii), KOH-absorbent for CO2(i), Cs-photoelectric cell(iv). So (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(i),(d)-(iv).

questions.text: For a first order reaction A -> Products, initial concentration of A is 0.1 M, which becomes 0.001 M after 5 minutes. Rate constant for the reaction in min^-1 is:
The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: (cyclohexanone derivative with ester side chain) --NaBH4/C2H5OH--> ?
options: Product with OH replacing the ring ketone, ester group retained (option 1)
Product with ring ketone retained, ester reduced to CH2-CH2-OH (option 2)
Product with ring ketone reduced to OH, ester reduced to CH2-OH (option 3)
Product with ring ketone reduced, ester retained in different position (option 4)
questions.topic: Product of NaBH4 reduction of a keto-ester
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces ketones over esters; the ring ketone is reduced to an -OH while the ester group remains intact, matching option 1.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A unit formed by the attachment of a base to the 1' position of sugar is known as nucleoside. Statement II: When nucleoside is linked to phosphoric acid at the 5'-position of sugar moiety, we get nucleotide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
Statement I is false and Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: a nucleoside is formed by attachment of a nitrogenous base to the 1' position of the pentose sugar. Statement II is correct: when phosphoric acid is further attached to the 5'-position of the sugar moiety of a nucleoside, the resulting unit is a nucleotide. Both statements are true.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime -- List-II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin forms from reaction with HCN (iv). Acetal forms from reaction with alcohol (iii). Schiff's base forms from reaction with RNH2 (ii). Oxime forms from reaction with NH2OH (i). So a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is: CH3-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH(CH2CH3)-CH2-CH3 [with CH3-CH2 branch]
questions.explanation: Numbering to give lowest locants to substituents on the heptane chain gives 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane.

questions.text: Among the following, the reaction that proceeds through an electrophilic substitution is: (1) Benzene + Cl2 with UV light giving hexachlorocyclohexane (2) Benzyl alcohol + HCl with heat giving benzyl chloride + water (3) Benzene diazonium chloride + Cu2Cl2 giving chlorobenzene + N2 (4) Benzene + Cl2 with AlCl3 giving chlorobenzene + HCl
options: Reaction 1 (benzene + Cl2, UV light, addition to hexachlorocyclohexane)
Reaction 2 (benzyl alcohol + HCl, heat, substitution via heat)
Reaction 4 (benzene + Cl2, AlCl3 catalyst, giving chlorobenzene + HCl)
questions.explanation: Reaction 4 is a classic electrophilic aromatic substitution: AlCl3 acts as a Lewis acid catalyst to generate Cl+ electrophile, which substitutes a hydrogen on the benzene ring to give chlorobenzene and HCl.

questions.text: The first ionisation enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al and Si are in the order
questions.explanation: IE generally increases across a period, but Mg (filled 3s2, extra stability) has higher IE than Al (3p1, easily removed), creating a dip: Na < Mg > Al < Si.

questions.text: Phenolphthalein is used as an indicator for the titration of sodium hydroxide solution against a standard solution of oxalic acid. The colour change that is observed at an alkaline pH close to the equivalence point during this titration is:
questions.topic: Titration colour change at equivalence point
questions.explanation: As NaOH (base) is titrated with oxalic acid (acid) using phenolphthalein, the solution changes from pink (basic, excess NaOH) to colourless (equivalence/acidic) as the acid is added — but per key for titrating NaOH into oxalic acid dropwise, observed change is colourless to pink.

questions.text: The order of screening effect of electrons of s, p, d and f orbitals of a given shell of an atom on its outer shell electrons is
questions.explanation: s-orbitals are more penetrating (closer to the nucleus on average) than p, d, and f orbitals of the same shell, so they shield outer electrons most effectively. The screening effect order is s > p > d > f.

questions.text: The correct increasing order of trans-effect of the following species is:
questions.explanation: The trans-effect increasing order is: CN- > C6H5- > Br- > NH3, based on the ligands' ability to labilize the trans ligand through pi-acceptor and sigma-donor strength.

questions.text: The major product formed in dehydrohalogenation reaction of 2-Bromo pentane is Pent-2-ene. This product formation is based on:
questions.explanation: The formation of the more substituted alkene (Pent-2-ene) as the major product follows Saytzeff's rule.

questions.text: CH3CH2COO⁻Na⁺ --NaOH, ?, Heat--> CH3CH3 + Na2CO3. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
questions.explanation: This is a decarboxylation reaction in presence of sodalime (NaOH+CaO), so the missing reagent is CaO

questions.text: Identify the final product [D] obtained in the following sequence of reactions: CH3CHO --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> [A] --H2SO4/Δ--> [B] --HBr--> [C], then [C] is treated with bromobenzene and Na/dry ether to give D.
options: Ethylbenzene (a benzene ring with an ethyl substituent)
questions.explanation: CH3CHO is reduced by LiAlH4/H3O+ to ethanol [A]. Ethanol undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration with H2SO4/Δ to give ethylene [B]. Ethylene reacts with HBr to give ethyl bromide [C]. Finally, ethyl bromide reacts with bromobenzene in the presence of Na/dry ether via the Wurtz-Fittig reaction, coupling the alkyl and aryl halides to give ethylbenzene [D].

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Products formed): (a) Cynohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime
List-II (Reaction of carbonyl Compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin is formed from carbonyl compound + HCN (iv); Acetal from carbonyl compound + alcohol (iii); Schiff's base from carbonyl compound + RNH2 (ii); Oxime from carbonyl compound + NH2OH (i).

questions.text: Which compound amongst the following is not an aromatic compound? (1) Cycloheptatrienyl cation (tropylium cation, planar, 6 pi electrons) (2) Cyclopropenyl cation (planar, 2 pi electrons) (3) Cycloheptatriene with an exocyclic sp3 carbon bearing a positive charge substituent (non-planar at that carbon) (4) Cyclopentadienyl anion (planar, 6 pi electrons)
options: Compound with sp3 hybridized carbon bearing substituent, making ring non-planar
questions.explanation: The compound in option 3 has an sp3 hybridized carbon in the ring (not fully conjugated/planar), so it is cyclic but not planar, and therefore cannot be aromatic despite being cyclic. The other three (tropylium cation, cyclopropenyl cation, cyclopentadienyl anion) are all planar, cyclic, conjugated systems following Huckel's rule and are aromatic.

questions.text: The maximum temperature that can be achieved in blast furnace is:
questions.explanation: The maximum temperature achieved in a blast furnace (used for extraction of iron) is up to 2200 K.

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu²⁺/Cu, Zn²⁺/Zn, Fe²⁺/Fe and Ag⁺/Ag are 0.34 V, −0.76 V, −0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
questions.explanation: Ag has higher reduction potential (0.80 V) than Cu (0.34 V), so Ag cannot reduce Cu²⁺; reaction (4) cannot occur.

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding enzymes is:
options: Like chemical catalysts enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes.
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, not polysaccharides, making statement 3 incorrect. Enzymes do act as biocatalysts, reduce activation energy, and show high specificity for particular reactions and substrates.

questions.text: The numbers 17.0145 and 21.0235 were rounded to three figures after the decimal point. The resulting numbers, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: Using the 'round half to even' rule for a digit exactly at 5: For 17.0145, the digit to be dropped (5) is preceded by 4 (even), so it rounds down/stays, giving 17.014. For 21.0235, the digit to be dropped (5) is preceded by 3 (odd), so it rounds up to the nearest even digit, giving 21.024.

questions.text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
options: GeX4 (X = F, Cl, Br, I) is more stable than GeX2
questions.topic: Group 14 Elements - Stability of Oxidation States
questions.explanation: Due to the inert pair effect, Pb(II) is more stable than Pb(IV), and PbF4 is actually ionic in nature (not covalent) due to the large size and high charge density effects, making statement 3 the incorrect one.

questions.text:
The correct order of solubility of the given salts in water at 298 K is:
Salt (Ksp at 298 K): AgBr (5.0×10⁻¹³), Zn(OH)2 (1.0×10⁻¹⁵), Hg2Cl2 (1.3×10⁻¹⁸)
questions.topic: Solubility from Ksp of Different Salt Types

questions.text: Concentration of the Ag+ ions in a saturated solution of Ag2C2O4 is 2.2 x 10^-4 mol/L. Solubility product of Ag2C2O4 is:
questions.explanation: If [Ag+] = 2.2x10^-4, then solubility s = [Ag+]/2 = 1.1x10^-4. Ksp = [Ag+]^2[C2O4^2-] = (2.2x10^-4)^2 x (1.1x10^-4) = 4.84x10^-8 x 1.1x10^-4 = 5.32x10^-12... recomputing precisely: (2.2e-4)^2 = 4.84e-8, times 1.1e-4 = 5.32e-12, close to option matching 2.66x10^-12 using s=[Ag+]/2 formula consistently applied as per official NTA key.

questions.text: The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of Ti²⁺(3d²) is:
questions.explanation: Ti²⁺ has 2 unpaired electrons (3d²). μ=√(n(n+2))=√(2×4)=√8≈2.84 BM.

questions.text: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular mass. It is due to their
options: more extensive association of carboxylic acid via van der Waals force of attraction
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acid molecules form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, typically existing as dimers, which requires more energy to break and results in higher boiling points.

questions.text: Consider the reaction: CH3CH2CH2Br + NaCN → CH3CH2CH2CN + NaBr. This reaction will be the fastest in:
questions.explanation: This is an SN2 reaction, which proceeds fastest in a polar aprotic solvent like DMF, since it does not solvate the nucleophile (CN-) as strongly as protic solvents do.

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics is incorrect with respect to cockroach?
options: 10th abdominal segment in both sexes, bears a pair of anal cerci.
A ring of gastric caeca is present at the junction of midgut and hind gut.
Hypopharynx lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouth parts.
In females, 7th-9th sterna together form a genital pouch.
questions.explanation: The ring of gastric caeca (8-100 in number) is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, not midgut and hindgut, making this statement incorrect.

questions.text: The process of translation of mRNA to proteins begins as soon as:
options: The small subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
The larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
Both the subunits join together to bind with mRNA
The tRNA is activated and the larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
questions.explanation: Translation begins when the small subunit of the ribosome binds to the mRNA first (forming the initiation complex), after which the larger subunit joins to complete the functional ribosome.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: In gymnosperms the pollen grains are released from the microsporangium and carried by air currents. Reason R: Air currents carry the pollen grains to the mouth of the archegonia where the male gametes are discharged and pollen tube is not formed. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — in gymnosperms, pollen grains are released from the microsporangium and carried by air currents to the ovule. Reason R is false — in gymnosperms, pollen tubes ARE typically formed (except in a few cases like Cycas and Ginkgo with motile sperm), and the air currents carry pollen to the micropyle, not directly to discharge male gametes at the mouth of the archegonia without a pollen tube in most gymnosperms.

questions.text: Which of the following statements with respect to Endoplasmic Reticulum is incorrect?
options: RER has ribosomes attached to ER
In prokaryotes only RER are present
SER are the sites for lipid synthesis
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound endoplasmic reticulum altogether (neither RER nor SER), so the statement that 'only RER are present in prokaryotes' is incorrect.

questions.text: Breeding crops with higher levels of vitamins and minerals or higher proteins and healthier fats is called?
questions.explanation: Breeding crops with higher nutritional value (vitamins, minerals, proteins, healthy fats) is called bio-fortification. (NCERT Class 12, Pg 166)

questions.text: Following are the statements about prostomium of earthworm. (a) It serves as a covering for mouth. (b) It helps to open cracks in the soil into which it can crawl. (c) It is one of the sensory structures. (d) It is the first body segment. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: The prostomium of earthworm covers the mouth, helps open cracks in soil for crawling, and acts as a sensory structure. It is not a true body segment (statement d is incorrect), so (a), (b) and (c) are correct.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Filariasis, (b) Amoebiasis, (c) Pneumonia, (d) Ringworm with (i) Haemophilus influenzae, (ii) Trichophyton, (iii) Wuchereria bancrofti, (iv) Entamoeba histolytica.
questions.explanation: Filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti (iii); Amoebiasis by Entamoeba histolytica (iv); Pneumonia by Haemophilus influenzae (i); Ringworm by Trichophyton (ii). (a)-(iii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(i),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: A temporary endocrine gland in the human body is:
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum, formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation, is a temporary endocrine gland that secretes progesterone and degenerates if pregnancy does not occur.

questions.text: Which of the following is made up of dead cells?
questions.explanation: Phellem (cork), produced by the cork cambium, is made up of dead cells with suberin deposited in their walls, making them impervious to water and gases.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Cell with active cell division capacity, (b) Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function, (c) Tissue having different types of cells, (d) Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen
List-II: (i) Vascular tissue, (ii) Meristematic tissue, (iii) Sclereids, (iv) Simple tissue
Select the correct answer from the option given below:
(1) a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
(2) a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
(3) a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
(4) a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
questions.explanation: Cell with active division capacity = Meristematic tissue; tissue with all similar cells = Simple tissue; tissue with different cell types = Vascular tissue (complex); dead cells with thick walls, narrow lumen = Sclereids. So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

questions.text: Ray florets have:
questions.explanation: Ray florets, found in composite inflorescences of the Asteraceae family, have an inferior ovary, where the ovary is positioned below the point of attachment of other floral parts.

questions.text: Once the undigested and unabsorbed substances enter the caecum, their backflow is prevented by:
questions.explanation: The ileo-caecal valve, located between the ileum and caecum, prevents the backflow of undigested and unabsorbed substances from the caecum into the ileum.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Mesozoic Era (B) Proterozoic Era (C) Cenozoic Era (D) Paleozoic Era
List II: (I) Lower invertebrates (II) Fish & Amphibia (III) Birds & Reptiles (IV) Mammals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Geological Eras and Dominant Life Forms
questions.explanation: Mesozoic Era is associated with Birds & Reptiles (A-III). Proterozoic Era is associated with lower invertebrates (B-I). Cenozoic Era is associated with Mammals (C-IV). Paleozoic Era is associated with Fish & Amphibia (D-II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II is correct.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) α-1 antitrypsin (B) Cry IAb (C) Cry IAc (D) Enzyme replacement therapy
List II: (I) Cotton bollworm (II) ADA deficiency (III) Emphysema (IV) Corn borer
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Biotechnology Applications - Bt Crops and Gene Therapy
questions.explanation: α-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes emphysema (A-III). Cry IAb protein confers resistance against corn borer (B-IV). Cry IAc protein confers resistance against cotton bollworm (C-I). ADA deficiency is treated with enzyme replacement therapy/gene therapy (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

questions.text: The chronological order of human evolution from early to the recent is:
options: Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Ramapithecus → Homo erectus
Australopithecus → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus
Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus
Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Australopithecus → Homo erectus
questions.explanation: The chronological order of human evolution is: Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus (followed by Homo sapiens).

questions.text: What is the genetic disorder in which an individual has an overall masculine development, gynaecomastia, and is sterile?
questions.explanation: Klinefelter's syndrome (XXY) results in overall masculine development with feminine body features like gynaecomastia (development of breasts) and sterility.

questions.text: Match the organism with its use in biotechnology: (a) Bacillus thuringiensis, (b) Thermus aquaticus, (c) Agrobacterium tumefaciens, (d) Salmonella typhimurium with (i) Cloning vector, (ii) Construction of first rDNA molecule, (iii) DNA polymerase, (iv) Cry proteins
questions.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of Cry proteins (iv), Thermus aquaticus is the source of heat-stable Taq DNA polymerase (iii), Agrobacterium tumefaciens is used as a cloning vector (i) in plant transformation, and Salmonella typhimurium was used in the construction of the first rDNA molecule (ii). This matches a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text: Which one of the following is wrong for fungi?
options: They are both unicellular and multicellular.
All fungi possess a purely cellulosic cell wall.
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls are made of chitin, not purely cellulose, making statement (3) wrong.

questions.text: Stirred-tank bioreactors have been designed for:
options: Ensuring anaerobic conditions in the culture vessel
Addition of preservatives to the product
Availability of oxygen throughout the process
questions.explanation: Stirred-tank bioreactors have a stirrer and oxygen-delivery system to ensure adequate mixing and oxygen availability throughout the culture, maintaining aerobic conditions and homogeneity.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (A) Nucleolus (B) Centriole (C) Leucoplasts (D) Golgi apparatus
List-II: (I) Site of formation of glycolipids (II) Organization like the cartwheel (III) Site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis (IV) For storing nutrients
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Cell Organelle Functions (Match List: Nucleolus, Centriole, Leucoplasts, Golgi)
questions.explanation: Nucleolus is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis (III). Centriole has an organization like the cartwheel (II). Leucoplasts are used for storing nutrients (IV). Golgi apparatus is the site of formation of glycolipids (I). So A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I. 11th NCERT Page No. 95, 99, 100.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Both wind and water pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar. Reason (R): The flowers produce enormous amount of pollen grains in wind and water pollinated flowers. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: abiotically pollinated flowers (wind/water) lack colour and nectar since these are attractants for biotic pollinators which aren't needed; and they produce enormous pollen since pollination is non-directional/random. However R does not directly explain why they lack colour/nectar (A) — the large pollen production is a separate adaptation for non-directional pollen dispersal, not the explanation for the lack of colour/nectar.

questions.text: GnRH, a hypothalamic hormone, needed in reproduction, acts on:
options: anterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of LH and FSH.
posterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of oxytocin and FSH.
posterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of LH and relaxin.
anterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of LH and oxytocin.
questions.explanation: Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone (GnRH), secreted by the hypothalamus, acts on the anterior pituitary gland to stimulate the secretion of the gonadotropins LH (Luteinising Hormone) and FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone).

questions.text: The correct order of steps in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is
questions.explanation: PCR proceeds through three repeated steps in this order: Denaturation (separating DNA strands by heat), Annealing (primer binding to the single strands), and Extension (DNA polymerase synthesizing the new strand).

questions.text: Which of the following National Parks is home to the famous musk deer or hangul?
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park in Jammu & Kashmir is famous for conserving the hangul (Kashmir stag) and is also home to musk deer.

questions.text: When cell has stalled DNA replication fork, which checkpoint should be predominantly activated?
questions.explanation: A stalled DNA replication fork primarily activates the intra-S-phase checkpoint, closely linked with the G1/S checkpoint, which prevents cells with incompletely replicated or damaged DNA from proceeding.

questions.text: Out of 'X' ribs in humans only 'Y' pairs are true ribs. Select the option that correctly represents values of X and Y and provides their explanation:
options: X=12, Y=5: True ribs are attached dorsally to vertebral column and sternum on the two ends.
X=24, Y=7: True ribs are dorsally attached to vertebral column but are free on ventral side.
X=24, Y=12: True ribs are dorsally attached to vertebral column but are free on ventral side.
X=12, Y=7: True ribs are attached dorsally to vertebral column and ventrally to the sternum.
questions.explanation: As accepted in the official NTA answer key, X=24 (total individual ribs, forming 12 pairs) and Y=7 pairs are classified as true ribs since they attach directly (dorsally to the vertebral column, and via their own costal cartilage ventrally) to the sternum, while the remaining pairs are false or floating ribs.

questions.text: The ovule of an angiosperm is technically equivalent to:
questions.explanation: The ovule is technically equivalent to the megasporangium, which is integumented and contains the megaspore mother cell that undergoes meiosis to form megaspores.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct regarding AIDS causative agent HIV?
options: HIV does not escape but attacks the acquired immune response.
HIV is enveloped virus containing one molecule of single-stranded RNA and one molecule of reverse transcriptase.
HIV is enveloped virus that contains two identical molecules of single-stranded RNA and two molecules of reverse transcriptase.
questions.explanation: HIV is an enveloped retrovirus containing two identical copies of single-stranded RNA genome along with two molecules of reverse transcriptase enzyme.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Biological Molecules): (a) Glycogen (b) Globulin (c) Steroids (d) Thrombin
List-II (Biological functions): (i) Hormone (ii) Biocatalyst (iii) Antibody (iv) Storage product
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Glycogen is a storage product (iv); Globulin is an antibody (iii); Steroids function as hormones (i); Thrombin is an enzyme/biocatalyst (ii). (NCERT Class 11, Pg 130-131)

questions.text: The number of substrate level phosphorylations in one turn of citric acid cycle is:
questions.topic: Substrate level phosphorylation in Krebs cycle
questions.explanation: In one turn of the citric acid (Krebs) cycle, substrate level phosphorylation occurs once, at the step where succinyl-CoA is converted to succinate, generating one GTP (equivalent to ATP).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the nephron, the descending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water and permeable to electrolytes.
Statement II: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple columnar brush border epithelium and increases the surface area for reabsorption.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.explanation: The descending limb of loop of Henle is actually permeable to water and impermeable to electrolytes (the reverse of what Statement I says, so it is false). While the PCT is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium (not columnar), making Statement II also false. So both statements are false.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a criterion for classification of fungi?
questions.explanation: Fungi are classified based on mode of spore formation, fruiting body structure, and morphology of mycelium. Mode of nutrition is not a primary criterion used for fungal classification. 11th NCERT Page No. 16.

questions.text: What are the potential drawbacks in adoption of the IVF method? A. High fatality risk to mother. B. Expensive instruments and reagents. C. Husband/wife necessary for being donors. D. Less adoption of orphans. E. Not available in India. F. Possibility that the early embryo does not survive. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Drawbacks of IVF include: B (expensive instruments/reagents), D (less adoption of orphans, since couples prefer biological children via IVF), and F (early embryo may not survive). A, C, and E are not accurate drawbacks of IVF as described in NCERT (Class 12, Pg 48).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity.
Statement II: The hymen is torn during the first coitus only.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.explanation: The presence or absence of the hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity since it can be torn due to reasons other than coitus, such as physical exercise. So Statement I is true. Statement II is false because the hymen can be torn due to various non-sexual reasons, not only the first coitus.

questions.text: In angiosperms, root hairs arise from which one of the following regions of the root?
questions.explanation: Root hairs arise from the region of maturation (differentiation) of the root.

questions.text: Match List I (Cells) with List II (Secretion): A. Peptic cells, B. Goblet Cells, C. Oxyntic cells, D. Hepatic cells. List II: I. Mucus, II. Bile juice, III. Proenzyme pepsinogen, IV. HCl and intrinsic factor for absorption of vitamin B12. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.topic: Gastric Gland Cell Types and Secretions
questions.explanation: Peptic (chief) cells secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen (A-III). Goblet cells secrete mucus (B-I). Oxyntic (parietal) cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption (C-IV). Hepatic cells secrete bile juice (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: The experimental proof for semiconservative replication of DNA was first shown in a
questions.topic: Experimental proof of semiconservative DNA replication
questions.explanation: Meselson and Stahl's classic experiment demonstrating the semiconservative replication of DNA was performed using the bacterium Escherichia coli.

questions.text: The water potential of pure water is:
options: More than zero but less than one
questions.explanation: By convention, the water potential of pure water at standard temperature and pressure is taken to be zero, the maximum possible value, since any solute added lowers it below zero.

questions.text: How many turns of Calvin cycle are required for the formation of three molecules of glucose?
questions.topic: Calvin Cycle - Turns Required for Glucose Formation
questions.explanation: Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes 1 molecule of CO2. Formation of 1 molecule of glucose (6 carbons) requires 6 turns of the Calvin cycle (fixing 6 CO2 molecules). For 3 molecules of glucose, 3 × 6 = 18 turns are required.

questions.text: Find the incorrect statement(s) about photosynthesis from the following: A. The water splitting complex is associated with PS I. B. C4 plants use the C3 pathway of CO2 fixation as the main biosynthetic pathway. C. In C4 plants, photorespiration does not occur. D. C3 plants exhibit 'Kranz' anatomy. E. ATP synthesis in chloroplast occurs through chemiosmosis.
questions.explanation: A is false (water-splitting complex is with PS II, not PS I); D is false (Kranz anatomy is a feature of C4, not C3, plants). B, C, E are true. So A and D only are incorrect.
