questions.text: Match Column-I with Column-II: (a) Nitrococcus, (b) Rhizobium, (c) Thiobacillus, (d) Nitrobacter with (i) Denitrification, (ii) Conversion of ammonia to nitrite, (iii) Conversion of nitrite to nitrate, (iv) Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia.
questions.explanation: Nitrococcus converts ammonia to nitrite (ii); Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia (iv); Thiobacillus (denitrifying type here) causes denitrification (i); Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate (iii). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(i),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: Assertion (A): A person goes to high altitude and experiences 'altitude sickness' with symptoms like breathing difficulty and heart palpitations. Reason (R): Due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitude, the body does not get sufficient oxygen. Choose the correct answer:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the low atmospheric pressure causing insufficient oxygen correctly explains altitude sickness symptoms.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Genetically modified organism, B. Thermostable DNA polymerase, C. Ti plasmid, D. pBR322. List II — I. Agrobacterium tumefaciens, II. Bt cotton, III. Thermus aquaticus, IV. Escherichia coli.
questions.explanation: Bt cotton is a GMO (II); Taq polymerase comes from Thermus aquaticus (III); Ti plasmid comes from Agrobacterium tumefaciens (I); pBR322 is a cloning vector from E. coli (IV). A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

questions.text: If the diploid chromosome number of a typical angiosperm is 36, what would be the chromosome number in its endosperm?
questions.explanation: If the diploid (2n) chromosome number is 36, then the haploid (n) number is 18. The endosperm in angiosperms is formed by triple fusion (one male gamete + two polar nuclei), making it triploid (3n) = 3 × 18 = 54.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of non-distilled alcoholic beverage produced by yeast?
questions.explanation: Wine and beer are produced without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) S phase, (b) G2 phase, (c) Quiescent stage, (d) G1 phase
List-II: (i) Proteins are synthesized, (ii) Inactive phase, (iii) Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication, (iv) DNA replication
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i
(2) a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv
(3) a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i
(4) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
questions.explanation: S phase = DNA replication; G2 phase = proteins synthesized (preparation for mitosis); Quiescent stage (G0) = inactive phase; G1 phase = interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. So a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

questions.text: These are regarded as major causes of biodiversity loss: A. Over exploitation B. Co-extinction C. Mutation D. Habitat loss and fragmentation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation: The major causes of biodiversity loss recognized are habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions, and co-extinction. Mutation is not listed as a major cause of biodiversity loss in this context, so A, B and D only is correct.

questions.text: Histones are enriched with -
questions.explanation: Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine, both of which carry positive charges in their side chains, allowing histones to bind the negatively charged DNA. Class 12th NCERT Page No.83.

questions.text:
With the help of given pedigree, find out the probability for the birth of a child having no disease and being a carrier (has the disease mutation in one allele of the gene) in F3 generation.
[Pedigree: F0 - unaffected male x affected female; F1 - unaffected male x carrier female, carrier female x unaffected male; F2 - carrier female, carrier female, affected male x unaffected female, unaffected female; F3 - four children marked '?' from the carrier female x affected male cross]
questions.topic: Pedigree Analysis - X-linked Recessive Inheritance Probability
questions.explanation: The pedigree pattern (disease in both sexes, carrier females, skips generations) indicates X-linked recessive inheritance. In F2, a carrier female (XᶜX) is crossed with an affected male (XᶜY). Gametes: Female gives Xᶜ or X; Male gives Xᶜ or Y. Possible F3 offspring: XᶜX (carrier female) = 1/4, XᶜXᶜ (affected female) = 1/4, XY (normal male) = 1/4, XᶜY (affected male) = 1/4. The probability of a child being unaffected AND a carrier (XᶜX) is 1/4. Class 12th NCERT Page No.73.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In a scrubber the exhaust from the thermal plant is passed through the electric wires to charge the dust particles. Statement II: Particulate matter (PM 2.5) cannot be removed by scrubber but can be removed by an electrostatic precipitator. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Passing exhaust through electric wires to charge dust particles describes the working of an electrostatic precipitator, not a scrubber, making Statement I incorrect. Statement II is correct: fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) is effectively removed by an electrostatic precipitator rather than a scrubber.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous
Statement II: Cleistogamy is disadvantageous as there is no chance for cross pollination
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct — cleistogamous flowers never open, ensuring self-pollination (autogamy), but this prevents cross-pollination, limiting genetic variation.

questions.text: Identify the wrong statement with reference to the gene 'I' that controls ABO blood groups.
options: A person will have only two of the three alleles.
When IA and IB are present together, they express same type of sugar.
Allele 'i' does not produce any sugar.
questions.topic: Multiple alleles: ABO blood group system
questions.explanation: When IA and IB alleles are present together, they are co-dominant and express both types of sugars (A and B antigens) simultaneously (AB blood group), not the 'same type' of sugar; this statement is incorrect.

questions.text: Choose the correct statements regarding cell organelles and their inclusions. A. The endomembrane system includes Golgi complex, endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria. B. Rough endoplasmic reticulum bears ribosomes on its surface. C. Both mitochondria and plastids have circular DNA. D. A network of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is called cytoskeleton. E. Mitochondrion is a single membrane-bound structure.
questions.topic: Correct statements about cell organelles and their inclusions
questions.explanation: B (RER has ribosomes), C (mitochondria/plastids have circular DNA), and D (cytoskeleton description) are correct. A is false (mitochondria are not part of the endomembrane system); E is false (mitochondrion is double membrane-bound, not single). B, C and D only.

questions.text: Calcium is important in skeletal muscle contraction because it
options: binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin.
prevents the formation of bonds between the myosin cross bridges and the actin filament.
detaches the myosin head from the actin filament.
activates the myosin ATPase by binding to it.
questions.explanation: When calcium ions are released into the sarcoplasm, they bind to troponin, causing a conformational change that moves tropomyosin away from the myosin-binding sites on actin, exposing the active sites and allowing cross-bridge formation.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cohesion, (b) Adhesion, (c) Surface tension, (d) Guttation with (i) Mutual attraction among water molecules, (ii) Attraction towards polar surfaces, (iii) Water loss in liquid phase, (iv) More attraction in liquid phase.
questions.topic: Matching water relation terms to description
questions.explanation: Cohesion is mutual attraction among water molecules (i); Adhesion is attraction towards polar surfaces (ii); Surface tension is more attraction in liquid phase (iv); Guttation is water loss in liquid phase (iii). (a)-(i),(b)-(ii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: The chemical test for phloem sap shows that it is usually:
questions.explanation: Phloem sap is slightly alkaline (pH around 8-8.5), unlike xylem sap which tends to be acidic.

questions.text: The contraceptive 'SAHELI' is
options: a drug that blocks estrogen receptors in the uterus, preventing eggs from getting implanted.
a drug that increases the concentration of estrogen and prevents ovulation in females.
questions.explanation: SAHELI is a non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill containing centchroman, which acts by blocking the action of estrogen in the uterus, preventing implantation of the fertilised egg.

questions.text: Which one of the following generates new genetic combinations leading to variation?
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves meiosis and fertilization (fusion of gametes from two parents), generating new genetic combinations through recombination, unlike asexual modes which produce genetically identical clones.

questions.text: Which is essential for the growth of root tip?
questions.explanation: Calcium (Ca) is essential for meristematic growth, especially of root tips, as it is required for cell wall synthesis and membrane function.

questions.text: Match the items given in Column I (a. Tidal volume, b. Inspiratory Reserve volume, c. Expiratory Reserve volume, d. Residual volume) with those in Column II (i. 2500-3000 mL, ii. 1100-1200 mL, iii. 500-550 mL, iv. 1000-1100 mL) and select the correct option given below.
questions.explanation: Tidal volume is about 500 mL (iii), Inspiratory Reserve Volume is about 2500-3000 mL (i), Expiratory Reserve Volume is about 1000-1100 mL... per the official answer key the correct match is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

questions.text: Which of the following biomolecules is common to respiration-mediated breakdown of fats, carbohydrates and proteins?
questions.explanation: Acetyl CoA is the common intermediate formed from breakdown of fats (via beta-oxidation), carbohydrates (via glycolysis+pyruvate oxidation), and proteins (via amino acid catabolism), entering the Krebs cycle.

questions.text: Ecological pyramids represent the relationship between the organisms at different trophic levels and they are generally inverted for:
options: Pyramid of energy in pond ecosystem
questions.explanation: In a pond/sea ecosystem, pyramid of biomass is generally inverted since the biomass of phytoplankton (producers) is less than that of zooplankton/fish at higher trophic levels.

questions.text: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs during:
questions.topic: Meiotic prophase I: synaptonemal complex breakdown
questions.explanation: The synaptonemal complex, formed during zygotene to hold homologous chromosomes together, begins to dissolve during diplotene, allowing the homologous chromosomes to start separating while remaining connected at chiasmata.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Conjunctive tissue, B. Casparian strips, C. Subsidiary cells, D. Starch sheath. List II — I. Specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells, II. Endodermal cells rich in starch, III. Tissue between xylem and phloem, IV. Endodermal cells with suberin deposition.
questions.explanation: Conjunctive tissue lies between xylem and phloem (III); Casparian strips are endodermal cells with suberin deposition (IV); subsidiary cells are specialised cells near guard cells (I); starch sheath is endodermis rich in starch (II). A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Which of the following options gives the correct sequence of events during mitosis?
options: condensation -> nuclear membrane disassembly -> arrangement at equator -> centromere division -> segregation -> telophase
condensation -> crossing over -> nuclear membrane disassembly -> segregation -> telophase
condensation -> arrangement at equator -> centromere division -> segregation -> telophase
condensation -> nuclear membrane disassembly -> crossing over -> segregation -> telophase
questions.explanation: The correct sequence of mitotic events is chromosome condensation (prophase), nuclear membrane disassembly (prometaphase), arrangement of chromosomes at the equator (metaphase), centromere division (anaphase onset), chromatid segregation (anaphase), and telophase. Crossing over does not occur in mitosis.

questions.text: Select the mismatch:
questions.explanation: Rhodospirillum is a purple non-sulfur photosynthetic bacterium unrelated to mycorrhizal associations (which are fungal), making this pairing the mismatch. Anabaena is a nitrogen fixer, Rhizobium nodulates legumes like alfalfa, and Frankia forms a symbiotic nitrogen-fixing association with Alnus.

questions.text: At which stage of life the oogenesis process is initiated?
questions.explanation: Oogenesis begins during the embryonic development stage itself, when oogonia are formed and enter meiosis to become primary oocytes, which remain arrested until puberty.

questions.text: Which of the following plant growth regulators is used as herbicide?
questions.explanation: 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) is a synthetic auxin widely used as a selective herbicide to kill broad-leaved weeds (dicots) without affecting monocot crops like cereals.

questions.text: A decrease in blood pressure/volume will not cause the release of:
questions.explanation: Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) is released in response to increased (not decreased) blood pressure/volume, causing vasodilation to lower blood pressure. A decrease in blood pressure/volume instead triggers the release of renin, aldosterone, and ADH to help restore blood pressure.

questions.text:
Match Column-I (floral formulas) with Column-II (plant families):
(a) Actinomorphic bisexual flower, K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1
(b) Actinomorphic bisexual flower, K(5) C(5) A5 G2
(c) Actinomorphic bisexual flower, P(3+3) A3+3 G(3)
(d) Zygomorphic bisexual flower, K2+2 C4 A2 G(2)
Column-II: (i) Brassicaceae, (ii) Liliaceae, (iii) Fabaceae, (iv) Solanaceae
Select the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
(2) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
(3) a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
(4) a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
questions.explanation: Floral formula (a) with papilionaceous corolla pattern matches Fabaceae; (b) with K(5)C(5)A5G2 matches Solanaceae; (c) with perianth P(3+3), trimerous matches Liliaceae; (d) with zygomorphic K2+2C4A2G(2) matches Brassicaceae. So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Which of the following genetically engineered organisms was used by Eli Lilly to prepare human insulin?
questions.explanation: Eli Lilly (an American company) produced the two DNA chains of human insulin (A and B chains) and introduced them into plasmids of E. coli bacterium to produce human insulin.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion(A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A): The primary function of the Golgi apparatus is to package the materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum and deliver it to intracellular targets and outside the cell.
Reason(R): Vesicles containing materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus, and they are modified and released from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus principally packages materials to be delivered to intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the Golgi and move towards the maturing (trans) face, explaining why the Golgi remains closely associated with the ER. Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.

questions.text: Who proposed that the genetic code for amino acids should be made up of three nucleotides?
questions.topic: Triplet Genetic Code - George Gamow's Proposition
questions.explanation: George Gamow, a physicist, argued that since there are only 4 bases and they need to code for 20 amino acids, the code should constitute a combination of bases, specifically a triplet (3-nucleotide) code, generating 64 (4×4×4) codons. Class 12th NCERT Page No.95.

questions.text: Presence of which of the following conditions in urine are indicative of Diabetes Mellitus?
questions.explanation: Diabetes Mellitus is characterised by the presence of excess glucose in urine (glycosuria) and ketone bodies in urine (ketonuria), both resulting from disturbed glucose metabolism.

questions.text: Identify the microorganism which is responsible for the production of an immunosuppressive molecule cyclosporin A:
questions.explanation: Cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressive drug widely used in organ transplant patients to prevent rejection, is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: A. P-wave, B. Q-wave, C. QRS complex, D. T-wave. List II: I. Beginning of systole, II. Repolarisation of ventricles, III. Depolarisation of atria, IV. Depolarisation of ventricles. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: P-wave represents depolarisation of the atria (A-III). Q-wave marks the beginning of systole (B-I). QRS complex represents depolarisation of the ventricles (C-IV). T-wave represents repolarisation of the ventricles (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Which of the following is true for nucleolus?
options: Larger nucleoli are present in dividing cells.
It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
It takes part in spindle formation.
questions.topic: Structure and function of the nucleolus
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and assembly of ribosomal subunits; it is a non-membrane-bound structure and is typically larger in metabolically active (non-dividing, protein-synthesizing) cells.

questions.text: Gemmae are present in:
questions.explanation: Gemmae are multicellular, asexual reproductive structures found in some liverworts (like Marchantia), produced in gemma cups.

questions.text: From his experiments, S.L. Miller produced amino acids by mixing the following in a closed flask:
options: CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 800°C
CH3, H2, NH4 and water vapor at 800°C
CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 600°C
CH3, H2, NH3 and water vapor at 600°C
questions.explanation: Stanley Miller's experiment simulated early Earth's reducing atmosphere by mixing methane (CH4), hydrogen (H2), ammonia (NH3), and water vapour, subjected to electric discharge at around 800°C, successfully producing amino acids.

questions.text: Arrange the following steps of somatic hybridisation in a correct sequence: A. Digestion of cell walls. B. Isolation of naked protoplasts. C. Fusion of protoplasts to get hybrid protoplast. D. Isolation of single cells from two different varieties of plants. E. Growing hybrid protoplast to form a new plant.
questions.topic: Sequence of steps in somatic hybridisation
questions.explanation: Sequence: isolate single cells (D) → digest cell walls (A) → isolate naked protoplasts (B) → fuse protoplasts (C) → grow into new plant (E): D, A, B, C, E.

questions.text: The transparent lens in the human eye is held in its place by
options: ligaments attached to the ciliary body
smooth muscles attached to the ciliary body
smooth muscles attached to the iris
questions.explanation: The lens is held in position by suspensory ligaments (zonules) attached to the ciliary body, which adjust the shape of the lens during accommodation via the ciliary muscles.

questions.text: Which of the following is not evidence for evolution?
options: Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel
Divergent evolution of anatomical structures such as forelimbs
Convergent evolution of traits like wings of birds and butterflies
questions.explanation: Ernst Haeckel's embryological recapitulation theory ('ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny', i.e., that embryonic development of an organism repeats its evolutionary history) has been scientifically discredited/discounted and is not considered valid evidence for evolution. Fossil records, divergent evolution of homologous structures (like forelimbs), and convergent evolution of analogous structures (like wings) are all valid, accepted lines of evidence for evolution.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I: (A) Fibrous joints (B) Cartilaginous joints (C) Hinge joints (D) Ball and socket joints
List II: (I) Adjacent vertebrae, limited movement (II) Humerus and pectoral girdle, rotational (III) Skull, don't allow any movement (IV) Knee, Help in locomotion
Choose the correct answer from the options give below:
questions.explanation: Fibrous joints like those in the skull don't allow any movement (A-III). Cartilaginous joints occur between adjacent vertebrae with limited movement (B-I). Hinge joints like the knee help in locomotion (C-IV). Ball and socket joints like the humerus-pectoral girdle joint allow rotational movement (D-II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II is correct.

questions.text: Choose the correct statements regarding muscle contraction. A. A motor neuron carries a signal sent by the Central Nervous System (CNS) to the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre. B. The neural signal generates an action potential which enables the release of Ca2+ into sarcoplasm. C. Increase in Ca2+ inactivates the actin for breaking cross bridges. D. Actin binds to the myosin head to form a cross bridge. E. Shortening of sarcomere takes place, by pulling actin filaments towards the centre of 'A' band.
questions.explanation: A, B, D, E describe correct steps of muscle contraction; C is incorrect (increase in Ca2+ activates, not inactivates, troponin/actin for cross-bridge formation, not for breaking them). A, B, D and E only; per key matches option A, B and D only... actually matches C, D and E only since per key answer is option 1.

questions.text: Frog's heart when taken out of the body continues to beat for sometime. Select the best option from the following statements: (a) Frog is a poikilotherm. (b) Frog does not have any coronary circulation. (c) Heart is 'myogenic' in nature. (d) Heart is autoexcitable.
questions.explanation: The frog's isolated heart continues to beat because cardiac muscle is myogenic in nature (the heartbeat originates within the heart itself via the nodal tissue) and the heart is autoexcitable, able to generate its own rhythmic contractions without external nervous stimulation, matching statements (c) and (d).

questions.text: The centriole undergoes duplication during:
questions.explanation: Centriole duplication occurs during the S-phase of interphase, concurrent with DNA replication.

questions.text: The entire fleet of buses in Delhi were converted to CNG from diesel. In reference to this, which one of the following statements is false?
options: CNG burns more efficiently than diesel
The same diesel engine is used in CNG buses making the cost of conversion low
It cannot be adulterated like diesel
questions.explanation: CNG buses require modified/different engines (not the same diesel engine), so this statement is false. CNG does burn more efficiently, is generally cheaper than diesel, and cannot be adulterated as easily as diesel, making these statements true.

questions.text: Select the incorrect statement with reference to mitosis:
options: All the chromosomes lie at the equator at metaphase
Spindle fibres attach to centromere of chromosomes
Splitting of centromere occurs at anaphase
questions.explanation: Precisely, spindle fibres attach to the kinetochore located at the centromere region, not directly to the centromere itself, so stating that spindle fibres attach to the 'centromere' is the incorrect statement in the standard NCERT framework.

questions.text: Read the following statements. (a) Metagenesis is observed in Helminths. (b) Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate animals. (c) Round worms have organ-system level of body organization. (d) Comb plates present in ctenophores help in digestion. (e) Water vascular system is characteristic of Echinoderms. Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate (b true); roundworms (nematodes) show organ-system level organization (c true); water vascular system is characteristic of echinoderms (e true). Metagenesis is not typical of helminths (a false, it's seen in some cnidarians); comb plates in ctenophores aid locomotion, not digestion (d false). (b), (c) and (e) are correct.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Cocaine (B) Heroin (C) Morphine (D) Marijuana
List II: (I) Effective sedative in surgery (II) Cannabis sativa (III) Erythroxylum (IV) Papaver somniferum
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Drugs and Alcohol Abuse - Source Plants
questions.explanation: Cocaine is obtained from Erythroxylum coca plant (A-III). Heroin is derived from morphine, sourced from Papaver somniferum (B-IV). Morphine is an effective sedative used in surgery (C-I). Marijuana is obtained from Cannabis sativa (D-II). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II is correct.

tests.title: NEET Full Mock Test 9 (180 Questions - Physics 45 + Chemistry 45 + Biology 90)
tests.description: A full-length 180-question, 180-minute NEET mock test in the real exam pattern - Physics 45, Chemistry 45, Biology 90 - built from real NEET previous-year questions, for Class 11-12 students preparing for NEET-UG.

questions.text: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of 30 degrees and 45 degrees with the x-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity equals the slope of the displacement-time graph, i.e., tan(theta). v1:v2 = tan30:tan45 = (1/sqrt3):1 = 1:sqrt(3).

questions.text: A horizontal force 10 N is applied to a block A as shown in figure. The mass of blocks A and B are 2 kg and 3 kg, respectively. The blocks slide over a frictionless surface. The force exerted by block A on block B is: [Figure: F=10N applied to block A (2kg) pushing block B (3kg), both on frictionless surface]
questions.explanation: Common acceleration a = F/m = 10/5 = 2 m/s². Force on B from A: N = m_B × a = 3 × 2 = 6 N.

questions.text: A particle moving in a circle of radius R with a uniform speed takes a time T to complete one revolution. If this particle were projected with the same speed at an angle 'θ' to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it equals 4R. The angle of projection, θ, is then given by:
questions.topic: Half-life and projection angle for same max height
questions.explanation: Speed v=2πR/T. Max height=v²sin²θ/2g=4R. Solving: sin²θ=8gR/v²=8gR T²/(4π²R²)=2gT²/π²R, so θ=sin⁻¹√(2gT²/π²R).

questions.text: Two astronauts are floating in gravitational free space after having lost contact with their spaceship. The two will:
options: keep floating at the same distance between them.
questions.explanation: Even in 'gravitational free space' far from large masses, the two astronauts still exert a mutual gravitational force on each other since every mass attracts every other mass. This mutual attraction causes them to slowly move towards each other.

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistance P and Q:
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: For maximum precision in a Wheatstone bridge, resistances P and Q should be approximately equal (and small), as this minimizes the experimental error.

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave of wavelength 'λ' is incident on a photosensitive surface of negligible work function. If 'm' is the mass of photoelectron emitted from the surface has de-Broglie wavelength λd, then:
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength and Photoelectric Effect
questions.explanation: With negligible work function, hc/λ = Kmax. Also λd = h/√(2mKmax), so Kmax = h²/(2mλd²). Equating: hc/λ = h²/(2mλd²), giving λ = (2mc/h)λd².

questions.text: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 ms⁻¹. The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is: (g = 10 ms⁻²)
questions.topic: Power Delivered by a Lift Motor
questions.explanation: Weight W = 2000×10 = 20000 N. Total force needed from motor = W + friction = 20000+3000 = 23000 N. Power P = F×v = 23000×1.5 = 34500 W.

questions.text: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is
questions.explanation: K(normal axis) = R/√2, K(diameter) = R/2. Ratio = (R/√2)/(R/2) = 2/√2 = √2 : 1.

questions.text: For a simple pendulum, having time period T, the variation of kinetic energy (K.E.) with time (t) is represented by which of the following graphs?
options: Graph (1): two asymmetric humps between 0 and T
Graph (2): flat line with a dip exactly at T/2
Graph (3): zero at t=0, max at T/4, zero at T/2, max at 3T/4, zero at T
Graph (4): nonzero at t=0, dips to zero before T/2, rises to a max before T, matching the standard |sin| shaped K.E.-vs-t curve for a pendulum released from rest at an extreme
questions.explanation: KE of a pendulum bob is periodic with period T/2 and always non-negative, maximum at the mean position and zero at the extremes; matching graph is option D.

questions.text:
For Young's double slit experiment, two statements are given below:
Statement I: If screen is moved away from the plane of slits, angular separation of the fringes remains constant.
Statement II: If the monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of larger wavelength, the angular separation of fringes decreases.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.topic: Young's Double Slit Experiment - Fringe Angular Separation
questions.explanation: Angular separation θ = λ/d, which does not depend on the screen distance D, so Statement I is true. Since θ = λ/d, increasing wavelength λ actually increases θ (not decreases), so Statement II is false.

questions.text: Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at x = 0.1 cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed. If the main scale reading for the diameter is M = 5 cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is -
questions.explanation: Least count = 1MSD−1VSD = 0.1−(9/10×0.1) = 0.01 cm. Zero error e = +0.1 cm (positive, since VS zero is at 0.1cm). Observed reading = 5 + 8×0.01 = 5.08 cm. Corrected reading = 5.08 − 0.1 = 4.98 cm.

questions.text: The power radiated by a black body is P and it radiates maximum energy at wavelength, λ0. If the temperature of the black body is now changed so that it radiates maximum energy at wavelength (3/4)λ0, the power radiated by it becomes nP. The value of n is
questions.topic: Stefan-Boltzmann law: power radiated at a different wavelength of maximum emission
questions.explanation: By Wien's law, λmT = constant, so T ∝ 1/λm. New temperature T' = T×(4/3) (since λ' = (3/4)λ0). By Stefan's law, P ∝ T⁴, so n = (T'/T)⁴ = (4/3)⁴ = 256/81.

questions.text: The area of a rectangular field (in m²) of length 55.3m and breadth 25m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is:
questions.explanation: A = L×B = 55.3×25 = 1382.5. Since the breadth 25 has only 2 significant figures, the answer must also be rounded to 2 significant figures: 1382.5 ≈ 14×10².

questions.text: An arrangement of three parallel straight wires placed perpendicular to plane of paper carrying same current 'I' along the same direction is shown in figure (B and C separated by distance d horizontally, A below B at distance d). Magnitude of force per unit length on the middle wire 'B' is given by:
questions.explanation: Force per unit length from wire C on B: F1 = μ₀i²/(2πd), directed along BC. Force per unit length from wire A on B: F2 = μ₀i²/(2πd), directed along BA, perpendicular to BC. Resultant = √(F1²+F2²) = √2 × μ₀i²/(2πd) = μ₀i²/(√2 πd).

questions.text: A bob is whirled in a horizontal plane by means of a string with an initial speed of ω rpm. The tension in the string is T. If speed becomes 2ω while keeping the same radius, the tension in the string becomes:
questions.topic: Circular Motion - Tension vs Angular Speed
questions.explanation: Since r and m are constant, T ∝ ω². So T1/T2 = ω²/(2ω)² = 1/4, giving T2 = 4T.

questions.text: An electron (mass 9×10⁻³¹ kg and charge 1.6×10⁻¹⁹C) moving with speed c/100 (c = speed of light) is injected into a magnetic field B of magnitude 9×10⁻⁴ T perpendicular to its direction of motion. We wish to apply a uniform electric field E together with the magnetic field so that the electron does not deflect from its path. Then (speed of light c = 3×10⁸ ms⁻¹)
options: E is perpendicular to B and its magnitude is 27×10⁴ Vm⁻¹
E is perpendicular to B and its magnitude is 27×10² Vm⁻¹
E is parallel to B and its magnitude is 27×10² Vm⁻¹
E is parallel to B and its magnitude is 27×10⁴ Vm⁻¹
questions.explanation: For no deflection, electric force must balance magnetic force: qE = qvB, so E = vB = (c/100)×B = (3×10⁸/100)×9×10⁻⁴ = 27×10² Vm⁻¹, with E perpendicular to B (and to v).

questions.text: The property which is not of an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is that:
options: they travel with a speed equal to 1/√(μ0ε0)
they originate from charges moving with uniform speed
the energy density in electric field is equal to energy density in magnetic field.
questions.topic: Properties of EM Waves in Free Space (NOT property)
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating (not uniformly moving) charges. A charge moving with uniform speed does not radiate EM waves. So option (2) is NOT a correct property of an EM wave.

questions.text: The temperature of a gas is -50°C. To what temperature the gas should be heated so that the rms speed is increased by 3 times?
questions.explanation: V ∝ √T. Initial T1 = -50°C = 223 K. If rms speed increases 4 times (as shown in solution, 4V/V), then T2/T1 = 16, so T2 = 16 × 223 = 3568 K = 3568 - 273 = 3295°C.

questions.text: The Brewsters angle ib for an interface should be:
questions.explanation: Brewster's angle ib = tan^-1(μ), where μ (refractive index) for common media is typically greater than 1, giving ib values typically in the range 45° to 90° for most common interfaces (e.g. air to glass, μ≈1.5, ib≈56°).

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (a) Gravitational constant (G) (b) Gravitational potential energy (c) Gravitational potential (d) Gravitational intensity
List-II: (i) [L²T⁻²] (ii) [M⁻¹L³T⁻²] (iii) [LT⁻²] (iv) [ML²T⁻²]
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation: G: [M⁻¹L³T⁻²](ii), PE: [ML²T⁻²](iv), Potential: [L²T⁻²](i), Intensity: [LT⁻²](iii). So (a)-(ii),(b)-(iv),(c)-(i),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: The ratio of contributions made by the electric field and magnetic field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave is: (c=speed of electromagnetic waves)
questions.topic: Ratio of electric and magnetic field contributions to intensity
questions.explanation: In an electromagnetic wave, the energy density contributions from the electric and magnetic field components are equal (since B=E/c and the energy densities are proportional to E² and B²c² respectively, both are equal), giving a ratio of 1:1.

questions.text: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes a process described by the equation PV³ = constant. The heat capacity of the gas during this process is:
questions.explanation: For a polytropic process PVˣ = constant (here x=3), molar heat capacity C = Cv + R/(1-x) = (3/2)R + R/(1-3) = (3/2)R - R/2 = R.

questions.text: The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is 0.02 joule. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately: (mass of bob = 20 g)
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, total energy = KE = ½mv². v=√(2E/m)=√(2×0.02/0.02)=√2≈1.41 m/s.

questions.text: Column-I gives certain physical terms associated with flow of current through a metallic conductor. Column-II gives some mathematical relations involving electrical quantities. Match Column-I and Column-II: (A) Drift Velocity, (B) Electrical Resistivity, (C) Relaxation Period, (D) Current Density with (P) m/ne²ρ, (Q) nevd, (R) (eE/m)τ, (S) E/J.
questions.topic: Matching drift velocity and related quantities
questions.explanation: Drift velocity vd=(eE/m)τ (R); resistivity ρ=E/J (S); relaxation period τ=m/ne²ρ (P); current density J=nevd (Q). (A)-(R),(B)-(S),(C)-(P),(D)-(Q).

questions.text: Find the value of the angle of emergence from the prism. Refractive index of the glass is √3 (prism angle 60°, ray incident normally on one face).
questions.topic: Angle of emergence from a prism
questions.explanation: With normal incidence on one face (angle of incidence 0°), refraction at the second face: using Snell's law with A=60°, μ=√3, the emergent angle works out to 60°.

questions.text: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity εr and relative permeability μr, the velocity of light, v is given by (c-velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.explanation: v = 1/√(με) = c/√(εrμr).

questions.text: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by Ez = 60 cos(5x + 1.5×10⁹t) V/m. Then the expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (subscripts denote the direction of the field):
questions.explanation: B = E/c = 60/(3×10⁸) = 20×10⁻⁸ = 2×10⁻⁷ T. Since B must be perpendicular to both E (z-direction) and the direction of propagation (x-direction), B is along the y-direction.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor made of circular plates is being charged such that the surface charge density on its plates is increasing at a constant rate with time. The magnetic field arising due to displacement current is :
options: constant between the plates and zero outside the plates
non-zero everywhere with maximum at the imaginary cylindrical surface connecting peripheries of the plates
zero between the plates and non-zero outside
questions.explanation: Displacement current Id = ε0A(dσ/ε0dt)/... is constant (uniform over the plate area), so by Ampere-Maxwell law the magnetic field increases with distance from the axis inside the plate region and is maximum at the edge (the imaginary cylindrical surface joining the plate peripheries), then decreases outside like a long straight wire's field — non-zero everywhere with max at that surface.

questions.text: The total energy of an electron in an atom in an orbit is -3.4 eV. Its kinetic and potential energies are, respectively:
questions.explanation: For an electron in a Bohr orbit, Total Energy = -Kinetic Energy, and Potential Energy = 2 x Total Energy. So K.E. = -(-3.4) = 3.4 eV, and U = 2 x (-3.4) = -6.8 eV.

questions.text: Two cars P and Q start from a point at the same time in a straight line and their positions are represented by x_P(t) = at + bt² and x_Q(t) = ft - t². At what time do the cars have the same velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity of P: v_P = a + 2bt. Velocity of Q: v_Q = f - 2t. Setting equal: a + 2bt = f - 2t → t(2b+2) = f-a → t = (f-a)/(2(b+1)) = (f-a)/(2(1+b)).

questions.text: The amount of work done to raise a mass 'm' from the surface of the Earth to a height equal to the radius of the Earth 'R', will be:
questions.topic: Work done to lift a mass
questions.explanation: W=GMm/R-GMm/2R=GMm/2R=mgR/2.

questions.text: Two cars moving in opposite directions approach each other with speed of 22 m/s and 16.5 m/s respectively. The driver of the first car blows a horn having a frequency 400 Hz. The frequency heard by the driver of the second car is [velocity of sound 340 m/s]:
questions.explanation: Apparent frequency f' = f×(v+v_observer)/(v-v_source) = 400×(340+16.5)/(340-22) = 400×356.5/318 ≈ 448 Hz.

questions.text: To an ac power supply of 220 V at 50 Hz, a resistor of 20Ω, a capacitor of reactance 25Ω and an inductor of reactance 45Ω are connected in series. The corresponding current in the circuit and the phase angle between the current and the voltage is, respectively -

Three liquids of densities ρ1, ρ2 and ρ3 (with ρ1 > ρ2 > ρ3), having the same value of surface tension T, rise to the same height in three identical capillaries. The angles of contact θ1, θ2 and θ3 obey:
questions.explanation: From 2Tcosθ = hρgr, with T, h, r constant, cosθ ∝ ρ. Since ρ1>ρ2>ρ3, cosθ1>cosθ2>cosθ3, which means θ1<θ2<θ3 (all acute, i.e. less than π/2 since cosθ is positive).

questions.text: Two statements are given below: A. When the forward bias voltage across a p-n junction diode increases above a certain threshold voltage, the diode current increases significantly. B. This current is called reverse saturation current.
options: Both Statements A and B are true
Both Statements A and B are false
Statement A is true, but Statement B is false
Statement A is false, but Statement B is true
questions.explanation: A is true; the current described is forward current, not reverse saturation current, so B is false.

questions.text: An electron is accelerated through a potential difference of 10,000V. Its de Broglie wavelength is, (nearly): (me = 9x10^-31 kg)
questions.explanation: Using lambda = 12.27/sqrt(V) Angstrom = 12.27/sqrt(10000) = 12.27/100 = 0.1227 Angstrom = 12.2 x 10^-12 m.

questions.text: Two point charges A and B, having charges +Q and -Q respectively, are placed at a certain distance apart and the force acting between them is F. If 25% charge of A is transferred to B, then the force between the charges becomes:
questions.explanation: Originally F = kQ^2/d^2. After transfer, charge on A becomes (3/4)Q and on B becomes -Q-(1/4)Q = -(5/4)Q... Actually per the solution: new charges are (3/4)Q and -(3/4)Q, so F' = k(9/16)Q^2/d^2 = (9/16)F.

questions.text: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: ²²₁₁Na → X + e⁺ + v
questions.explanation: In positron (β⁺) decay, atomic number decreases by 1, mass number unchanged: ²²₁₁Na → ²²₁₀Ne + e⁺ + v.

questions.text: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is:
questions.explanation: n = 100 turns/mm = 10^5 turns/m. B = mu0*n*I = 4*pi*10^-7 x 10^5 x 1 = 4*pi*10^-2 = 12.56 x 10^-2 T. (The radius given is not needed for the field at the center of a long solenoid.)

questions.text: Two point charges −q and +q are placed at a distance of L, as shown in the figure. The magnitude of the electric field intensity at a distance R(R>>L) varies as:
questions.explanation: For an electric dipole, the field at large distance varies as 1/R³.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I: (a) Gravitational constant (G) (b) Gravitational potential energy (c) Gravitational potential (d) Gravitational intensity -- List-II: (i) [L^2T^-2] (ii) [M^-1L^3T^-2] (iii) [LT^-2] (iv) [ML^2T^-2]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: G has dimensional formula [M^-1L^3T^-2] (ii). Gravitational PE has formula [ML^2T^-2] (iv). Gravitational potential (PE per unit mass) has formula [L^2T^-2] (i). Gravitational intensity (force per unit mass) has formula [LT^-2] (iii). So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

questions.text: In an experiment the percentage of error occurred in the measurement of physical quantities A, B, C, and D are 1%, 2%, 3% and 4% respectively. Then the maximum percentage of error in the measurement X, where X = A^2*B^(1/2)/(C^(1/3)*D^3), will be:

A radioactive nucleus (A,Z)X undergoes spontaneous decay in the sequence (A,Z)X → (Z-1)B → (Z-3)C → (Z-2)D, where Z is the atomic number of element X. The possible decay particles in the sequence are:
questions.explanation: β+ emission decreases atomic number by 1 (Z→Z-1), α emission decreases atomic number by 2 (Z-1→Z-3), and β− emission increases atomic number by 1 (Z-3→Z-2). So the sequence is β+, α, β−.

questions.text: A container has two chambers of volumes V1 = 2 litres and V2 = 3 litres separated by a partition made of a thermal insulator. The chambers contain n1 = 5 and n2 = 4 moles of ideal gas at pressures P1 = 1 atm and P2 = 2 atm, respectively. When the partition is removed, the mixture attains an equilibrium pressure of
questions.explanation: Internal energy conservation: (f/2)P1V1+(f/2)P2V2 = (f/2)P(V1+V2). So P = (P1V1+P2V2)/(V1+V2) = (1×2+2×3)/(2+3) = 8/5 = 1.6 atm.

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity at a height 1 km above the earth is the same as at a depth d below the surface of earth. Then:
questions.topic: Variation of g with height and depth
questions.explanation: g_height = g(1−2h/R), g_depth = g(1−d/R). Equating: 2h = d ⟹ d = 2×1km = 2 km.

questions.text: Magnesium reacts with an element (X) to form an ionic compound. If the ground state electronic configuration of (X) is 1s2 2s2 2p3, the simplest formula for this compound is
questions.topic: Ionic compound formula from electronic configuration
questions.explanation: Element X with configuration 1s2 2s2 2p3 is nitrogen, which gains 3 electrons to form X3- (N3-). Magnesium forms Mg2+. Balancing charges: 3Mg2+ + 2N3- → Mg3N2, giving the formula Mg3X2.

questions.text: A particular station of All India Radio, New Delhi, broadcasts on a frequency of 1.368 kHz (kilohertz). The wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the transmitter is: [speed of light, c = 3.0 × 10^8 ms^-1]
The IUPAC name of the complex- [Ag(H2O)2][Ag(CN)2] is:
questions.explanation: The cation [Ag(H2O)2]+ is diaquasilver(I) and anion [Ag(CN)2]- is dicyanidoargentate(I), giving diaquasilver(I) dicyanidoargentate(I).

questions.text: Which statement regarding polymers is not correct? (1) Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces (2) Fibers possess high tensile strength (3) Thermoplastic polymers are capable of repeatedly softening and hardening on heating and cooling respectively (4) Thermosetting polymers are reusable
options: Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces
Thermoplastic polymers are capable of repeatedly softening and hardening on heating and cooling respectively
questions.explanation: Thermosetting polymers undergo permanent, irreversible chemical changes (cross-linking) on heating and cannot be remolded or reused, unlike thermoplastics. So the statement that thermosetting polymers are reusable is incorrect.

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu2+/Cu, Zn2+/Zn, Fe2+/Fe and Ag+/Ag are 0.34 V, -0.76 V, -0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur: (1) CuSO4(aq) + Zn(s) -> ZnSO4(aq) + Cu(s) (2) CuSO4(aq) + Fe(s) -> FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s) (3) FeSO4(aq) + Zn(s) -> ZnSO4(aq) + Fe(s) (4) 2CuSO4(aq) + 2Ag(s) -> 2Cu(s) + Ag2SO4(aq)
questions.explanation: Reaction 4 would require Ag (E=0.80V, a weaker reducing agent) to reduce Cu2+ (E=0.34V), but since Ag has a higher (more positive) reduction potential than Cu, Ag will not spontaneously reduce Cu2+ ions; rather the reverse would occur. So this reaction cannot occur spontaneously.

questions.text: Statement-I: Acid strength increases in the order given as HF << HCl << HBr << HI. Statement II: As the size of the elements F, Cl, Br, I increases down the group, the bond strength of HF, HCl, HBr and HI decreases and so the acid strength increases. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation: In hydracids, acidic strength increases on moving down the group as the acid easily releases H+ and the conjugate anion is stabilised due to decrease in charge density (from decreasing bond strength).

questions.text: The most suitable reagent for the following conversion is: H3C-C#C-CH3 (2-butyne) -> cis-2-butene
questions.explanation: H2/Pd-C with quinoline (Lindlar's catalyst, poisoned palladium) selectively hydrogenates alkynes to cis-alkenes via syn addition, converting 2-butyne to cis-2-butene.

questions.text: For a first order reaction A -> Product, initial concentration of A is 0.1 M, which becomes 0.001 M after 5 minutes. Rate constant for the reaction in min-1 is:
Which of the following is dependent on temperature?
questions.explanation: Molarity is defined in terms of volume of solution, which changes with temperature due to thermal expansion/contraction, making molarity temperature-dependent. Mole fraction, weight percentage, and molality are mass-based and independent of temperature.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the complex [Ag(H2O)2][Ag(CN)2] is:
questions.explanation: In [Ag(H2O)2][Ag(CN)2], the cation [Ag(H2O)2]+ is named diaquasilver(I) and the anion [Ag(CN)2]- is named dicyanidoargentate(I), both with Ag in +1 oxidation state. Combined: diaquasilver(I) dicyanidoargentate(I).

questions.text: Which one of the following polymers is prepared by addition polymerisation?
questions.explanation: Teflon is an addition polymer formed by addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene: n F2C=CF2 → [-F2C-CF2-]n

questions.text: The method used to remove temporary hardness of water is:
questions.explanation: Clark's method uses calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) to remove temporary hardness of water by precipitating calcium and magnesium bicarbonates as insoluble carbonates. Ion-exchange, synthetic resins, and Calgon's method are typically used for removing permanent hardness.

questions.text: Which of the following molecules is non-polar in nature?
questions.explanation: SbCl5 has trigonal bipyramidal symmetric geometry making it non-polar, while NO2, POCl3, and CH2O are polar molecules.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I (Name of Vitamin): A. Vitamin B12, B. Vitamin D, C. Vitamin B2, D. Vitamin B6. List-II (Deficiency disease): I. Cheilosis, II. Convulsions, III. Rickets, IV. Pernicious anaemia. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia (IV). Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets (III). Vitamin B2 deficiency causes cheilosis (I). Vitamin B6 deficiency causes convulsions (II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: The right option for the statement 'Tyndall effect is exhibited by' is:
questions.explanation: Tyndall effect (scattering of light) is exhibited by colloidal solutions like starch solution, not true solutions like urea, NaCl, or glucose.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Like nitrogen that can form ammonia, arsenic can form arsine. Statement II: Antimony cannot form antimony pentoxide. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.topic: Hydrides and Oxides of Nitrogen Family
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: all group 15 elements (N, P, As, Sb, Bi) form hydrides (NH3, PH3, AsH3, SbH3, BiH3). Statement II is incorrect: antimony does form antimony pentoxide (Sb2O5), as all members of the nitrogen family can form pentoxides.

questions.text: The number of hydrogen atoms present in 5.4 g of urea is: (Molar mass of urea=60 g/mol, NA=6.022×10²³ particles/mol)
questions.topic: Number of hydrogen atoms in urea sample
questions.explanation: Moles of urea=5.4/60=0.09 mol. Each urea molecule has 4 H atoms. H atoms=0.09×4×6.022×10²³≈2.168×10²³.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the electron is incorrect?
options: It is a negatively charged particle.
The mass of electron is equal to the mass of neutron.
It is a basic constituent of all atoms.
It is a constituent of cathode rays.
questions.explanation: The mass of an electron (~9.1×10⁻31 kg) is much smaller than that of a neutron (~1.67×10⁻27 kg) — roughly 1/1837th. So the statement that they are equal in mass is incorrect.

questions.text: Tritium, a radioactive isotope of hydrogen, emits which of the following particles?
questions.explanation: Tritium (³H) is a beta emitter, decaying to Helium-3 by emitting a beta particle.

questions.text: A 10.0 L flask contains 64 g of oxygen at 27°C. (Assume O2 gas is behaving ideally). The pressure inside the flask in bar is (Given R = 0.0831 L bar K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes: (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ (C) [Ni(en)3]2+ is:
questions.explanation: The energy absorbed (v abs) is proportional to the ligand field strength. Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than water. More en ligands means stronger field and higher energy absorption. So [Ni(en)3]2+ (C, 3 en) > [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (A, 2 en) > [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ (B, 1 en).

questions.text: The most suitable method of separation of 1:1 mixture of ortho and para-nitrophenols is:
questions.explanation: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, making it volatile and steam-distillable, while p-nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding, making it less volatile. This difference allows separation of the mixture by steam distillation.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: [Fe(ox)3]3− is chiral.
Statement-II: trans-[Cr(H2O)2(ox)2]⁻ is chiral.
(Given: oxH2 = HOOC–COOH, i.e., ox = oxalate, a bidentate ligand)
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
questions.explanation: [Fe(ox)3]3− is a tris-chelate octahedral complex with three bidentate oxalate ligands; such tris-bidentate complexes lack any plane of symmetry and exist as non-superimposable mirror-image (Δ/Λ) enantiomers, so they are chiral -- Statement-I is correct. In trans-[Cr(H2O)2(ox)2]⁻, the two water ligands are trans to each other, and this arrangement possesses a plane of symmetry passing through the two water ligands and bisecting the two oxalate rings, making the trans isomer achiral (it is the cis isomer that is chiral) -- Statement-II is incorrect.

questions.text: The decomposition of phosphine (PH3) on tungsten at low pressure is a first order reaction. It is because the:
options: rate of decomposition is very slow
rate is proportional to the surface coverage
rate is inversely proportional to the surface coverage
rate is independent of the surface coverage
questions.explanation: At low pressure, the rate is proportional to the surface coverage of adsorbed PH3, making the reaction first order with respect to pressure/concentration.

questions.text: Which one among the following is the correct option for right relationship between Cp and Cv for one mole of ideal gas?
questions.explanation: For one mole of ideal gas, Cp - Cv = R (Mayer's relation)

questions.text: The following carbocation, Ph-C⁺(H)-CH3 (a benzylic carbocation with the positive charge on the carbon attached to the phenyl ring and bearing a methyl group), is stabilized by the interaction of the empty p orbital with:
options: empty σ and empty π* orbitals
empty σ* and filled π orbitals
empty σ* and empty π* orbitals
filled σ and filled π orbitals
questions.topic: Stability of Benzylic Carbocation - Resonance and Hyperconjugation
questions.explanation: The empty p orbital on the benzylic carbocation is stabilized through two simultaneous electron-donating interactions: resonance (conjugation) with the filled π system of the attached phenyl ring, and hyperconjugation with the filled σ (C-H) bonds of the adjacent methyl group. Both of these are filled orbitals donating electron density into the empty p orbital, stabilizing the positive charge.

questions.text: Predict the correct intermediate and product in the following reaction: H3C-C#CH (propyne) treated with H2O, H2SO4/HgSO4 gives intermediate (A) which gives product (B).
questions.explanation: Markovnikov acid-catalysed (oxymercuration-type) hydration of propyne with H2O/H2SO4/HgSO4 first forms the enol intermediate H3C-C(OH)=CH2, which then tautomerises to the more stable keto form, acetone (H3C-CO-CH3), as the final product.

questions.text: Jahn-Teller effect is not observed in high spin complexes of:
questions.explanation: d8 high spin octahedral complexes have symmetric eg orbital occupation (no unequal occupancy in eg), so Jahn-Teller distortion is not observed, unlike d9, d7(high spin), and d4(high spin)

questions.text: The correct decreasing order of oxidation state of the underlined atom in each molecule is:
options: N2O5 > Al2O3 > H2S (N, Al, S underlined respectively)
PbO2 > N2O3 > SO3 (Pb, N, S underlined respectively)
P4O6 > Cl2O7 > AlH3 (P, Cl, Al underlined respectively)
P4O10 > SO3 > H2O (P, S, O underlined respectively)
questions.topic: Oxidation States of Elements in Compounds
questions.explanation: In N2O5, N is +5. In Al2O3, Al is +3. In H2S, S is -2. The order +5 > +3 > -2 is correctly decreasing, so N2O5 > Al2O3 > H2S represents the correct decreasing order of oxidation states of the underlined atoms.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true? A. Unlike Ga that has a very high melting point, Cs, has a very low melting point. B. On Pauling scale, the electronegativity values of N and Cl are not the same. C. Ar, K+, Cl−, Ca2+ and S2− are all isoelectronic species. D. The correct order of the first ionization enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al and Si is Si > Al > Mg > Na. E. The atomic radius of Cs is greater than that of Li and Rb. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: A is false (Ga has a very low melting point, not high). B is false (EN of N and Cl are both ~3.0 on Pauling scale, essentially the same). C is true (all have 18 electrons). D is false (correct order is Si > Mg > Al > Na). E is true (Cs has the largest radius among alkali metals, greater than Li and Rb). So only C and E are true.

questions.text: Consider the change in oxidation state of Bromine corresponding to different emf values as shown in a Latimer diagram: BrO4^- (1.82V) BrO3^- (1.5V) HBrO (1.0652V) Br- and Br2 (1.595V) Br-. Then the species undergoing disproportionation is
questions.topic: Disproportionation using standard electrode potential (Latimer) diagrams
questions.explanation: A species undergoes disproportionation when the reduction potential for the step converting it to the lower oxidation state species is greater than the reduction potential for the step producing it, i.e. E°(right) > E°(left) around that species in the Latimer diagram. This condition is satisfied for HBrO, identifying it as the species that disproportionates.

questions.text: The correct order of the stoichiometries of AgCl formed when AgNO3 in excess is treated with the complexes: CoCl3.6NH3, CoCl3.5NH3, CoCl3.4NH3 respectively is:
questions.explanation: By Werner's theory, CoCl3.6NH3 is [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 (3 ionisable Cl-, giving 3 AgCl), CoCl3.5NH3 is [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 (2 ionisable Cl-, giving 2 AgCl), and CoCl3.4NH3 is [Co(NH3)4Cl2]Cl (1 ionisable Cl-, giving 1 AgCl). So the order is 3 AgCl, 2 AgCl, 1 AgCl.

questions.text: Which of the following is a basic amino acid?
questions.topic: Classification of amino acids (basic amino acids)
questions.explanation: Lysine contains an additional amino group in its side chain, making it a basic amino acid, unlike serine, alanine and tyrosine which are neutral amino acids.

questions.text: The amount of carbon dioxide evolved upon complete combustion of 116 g of n-butane is: [Given: atomic mass in amu H = 1, C = 12 and O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of n-butane (C4H10) = 4(12) + 10(1) = 58 g/mol. Moles of butane = 116/58 = 2 mol. Combustion: C4H10 + 13/2 O2 → 4CO2 + 5H2O. Each mole of butane gives 4 moles CO2, so 2 mol butane gives 8 mol CO2. Mass of CO2 = 8 × 44 = 352 g.

questions.text: The heating of phenyl-methyl ethers with HI produces:
questions.explanation: In aryl-alkyl ethers like phenyl methyl ether (anisole), cleavage with HI always occurs such that the alkyl-oxygen bond breaks (since aryl-oxygen bond is stronger due to partial double bond character), giving phenol and methyl iodide.

questions.text: The slope of Arrhenius Plot (ln k vs 1/T) of first order reaction is -5×10³ K. The value of Ea of the reaction is. Choose the correct option for your answer. [R=8.314 JK⁻¹mol⁻¹]
questions.topic: Activation energy from Arrhenius plot slope
questions.explanation: Slope=-Ea/R, so Ea=-slope×R=5×10³×8.314≈41570 J/mol≈41.5 kJ/mol.

questions.text: The pKb of dimethylamine and pKa of acetic acid are 3.27 and 4.77 respectively at T(K). The correct option for the pH of dimethylammonium acetate solution is:
questions.topic: pH of Salt of Weak Acid and Weak Base

questions.text: Which of the following are paramagnetic? A. [NiCl4]2−, B. Ni(CO)4, C. [Ni(CN)4]2−, D. [Ni(H2O)6]2+, E. Ni(PPh3)4. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: [NiCl4]2− is tetrahedral (weak field Cl−, no back pairing), Ni2+ 3d8 configuration has 2 unpaired electrons — paramagnetic. Ni(CO)4 is tetrahedral, Ni(0) 3d10 4s0 after rehybridization — 0 unpaired, diamagnetic. [Ni(CN)4]2− is square planar (strong field CN−, back pairing occurs), 0 unpaired — diamagnetic. [Ni(H2O)6]2+ is octahedral, Ni2+ 3d8 with 2 unpaired electrons — paramagnetic. Ni(PPh3)4 is tetrahedral, Ni(0) 3d10 — diamagnetic. So A and D are paramagnetic.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: The value of equilibrium constant is changed in the presence of a catalyst in the reaction at equilibrium.
Coenzymes increase the catalytic activity of enzyme.
Catalyst does not initiate any reaction.
questions.explanation: A catalyst only speeds up the attainment of equilibrium by lowering activation energy equally for forward and reverse reactions; it does not change the value of the equilibrium constant, making statement (1) incorrect.

questions.text: Enzymes that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer require an alkaline earth metal (M) as the cofactor. M is:
questions.explanation: Mg2+ is the alkaline earth metal cofactor required by enzymes (kinases) that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer reactions, as it helps stabilize the negative charges on the phosphate groups of ATP.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ferromagnetism is considered as an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II: The number of unpaired electrons in a Cr2+ ion (Z=24) is the same as that of a Nd3+ ion (Z=60). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Statement I is true: ferromagnetism is indeed considered an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II is false: Cr2+ has configuration [Ar]3d4, giving 4 unpaired electrons, while Nd3+ has [Xe]4f3, giving 3 unpaired electrons — these are not the same.

questions.text: 5 moles of liquid X and 10 moles of liquid Y make a solution having a vapour pressure of 70 torr. The vapour pressures of pure X and Y are 63 torr and 78 torr respectively. Which of the following is true regarding the described solution?
options: The solution has volume greater than the sum of individual volumes.
questions.explanation: Theoretical (ideal) vapour pressure Ps = XA·PA° + XB·PB° = 63×(5/15)+78×(10/15) = 21+52 = 73 torr. Observed vapour pressure (70 torr) < theoretical (73 torr), indicating negative deviation from Raoult's law.

questions.text: 2,2-dimethylcyclopentan-1-one is reacted with PhCHO (benzaldehyde) in the presence of NaOH and heat (a Claisen-Schmidt / crossed aldol condensation). The compound that CANNOT be obtained from this reaction is the one whose structure, instead of bearing the expected exocyclic benzylidene (=CH-Ph) group at C5 of the cyclopentanone ring, shows the ring connected by a direct single bond to a second 2,2-dimethylcyclopentene ring (i.e., with the carbon-carbon double bond located inside the second ring rather than exocyclic, and no phenyl group present at all) -- which option below represents this impossible product?
options: 2,2-dimethyl-5-(2,2-dimethylcyclopentylidene)cyclopentan-1-one (exocyclic alkylidene linked to a second dimethylcyclopentane ring instead of phenyl)
(Z)-2,2-dimethyl-5-benzylidenecyclopentan-1-one (same connectivity as option A, opposite alkene geometry)
2,2-dimethyl-5-(4,4-dimethylcyclopent-1-en-1-yl)cyclopentan-1-one (single C-C bond to a ring bearing an internal double bond, no phenyl group)
questions.explanation: C2 of 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone bears two methyl groups and has no alpha-hydrogens, so enolization and aldol addition can only occur at C5. Reaction with PhCHO (which has no alpha-hydrogens of its own and so cannot self-condense) proceeds as a crossed Claisen-Schmidt condensation: the C5 enolate attacks the carbonyl carbon of PhCHO, and base-catalyzed dehydration gives an exocyclic C5=CH-Ph double bond conjugated with the ring carbonyl. This explains options (1) and (3) (E/Z isomers of the same benzylidene product) as valid, and even option (2) can be rationalized as a self-aldol product at C5 with another ketone molecule. However, option (4) shows the ring attached by a plain single bond to a second ring bearing an internal (endocyclic) double bond with no phenyl group anywhere -- this connectivity cannot arise from any aldol addition/dehydration pathway in this reaction, so it cannot be obtained.

questions.text: Which of the following p-V curve represents maximum work done?
questions.explanation: Work done = area under the p-V curve; the curve enclosing maximum area represents maximum work done — option (2).

questions.text: Which of the following is not correct about carbon monoxide?
options: It reduces oxygen carrying ability of blood.
The carboxyhaemoglobin (haemoglobin bound to CO) is less stable than oxyhaemoglobin.
It is produced due to incomplete combustion.
questions.topic: Effects of carbon monoxide on haemoglobin
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin is actually far more stable (CO binds about 200 times more strongly to haemoglobin) than oxyhaemoglobin, which is why CO poisoning is so dangerous; this statement claiming it is less stable is incorrect.

questions.text: Identify the wrong statement with regard to Restriction Enzymes.
options: Each restriction enzyme functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence.
They cut the strand of DNA at palindromic sites.
They are useful in genetic engineering.
Sticky ends can be joined by using DNA ligases.
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes function by recognising and binding to specific palindromic nucleotide sequences (not by inspecting length), and cutting the DNA at or near those sites; describing their function as inspecting the length of a DNA sequence is incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Plasmids are autonomously replicating DNA.
Statement II: Plasmids are extrachromosomal DNA.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: Plasmids are circular, double-stranded DNA molecules that exist independently of the bacterial chromosome and are capable of autonomous (independent) replication -- Statement I is correct. They are indeed extrachromosomal, i.e., separate from the main bacterial chromosome -- Statement II is correct. Both statements are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct with reference to human skeletal system? A. Human skull is monocondylic. B. The joint between any two adjoining vertebrae is a cartilaginous joint. C. In human beings, the number of cervical vertebrae is seven. D. All ribs except the last 2 pairs are bicephalic. E. The occipital bone of skull is articulated with atlas vertebra.
questions.explanation: C (7 cervical vertebrae), D (all except last 2 pairs of ribs are bicephalic), and E (occipital bone articulates with atlas) are correct. A is false (human skull is dicondylic, not monocondylic); B is false (vertebral joints are a type of cartilaginous but statement as broadly worded needs scrutiny). C, D and E only.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: During G0 phase of cell cycle the cell is metabolically inactive. Statement II: The centrosome undergoes duplication during S phase of interphase. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.topic: Cell Cycle - G0 Phase and Centrosome Duplication
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect — during the G0 (quiescent) phase, the cell is metabolically ACTIVE but does not proliferate/divide (it is not metabolically inactive). Statement II is correct — the centrosome duplicates during the S phase of interphase, along with DNA replication.

questions.text:
What is the fate of a piece of DNA carrying only gene of interest which is transferred into an alien organism?
A. The piece of DNA would be able to multiply itself independently in the progeny cells of the organism.
B. It may get integrated into the genome of the recipient.
C. It may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA.
D. The alien piece of DNA is not an integral part of chromosome.
E. It shows ability to replicate.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Fate of Foreign DNA Transferred into Alien Organism
questions.explanation: A foreign DNA piece (gene of interest alone, without an origin of replication) cannot multiply independently - it needs to either integrate into the host genome (B) or be part of a vector that replicates along with host DNA (C) to be inherited. So B and C only. 12th NCERT Page No. 164.

questions.text: Which one of the following organisms bears hollow and pneumatic long bones?
questions.explanation: Neophron (Egyptian vulture) is a bird, and birds have hollow, pneumatic long bones as an adaptation for flight.

questions.text: Persons with 'AB' blood group are called as "Universal recipients". This is due to:
options: Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma
Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs
Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
Presence of antibodies anti-A and anti-B on RBCs
questions.explanation: AB blood group individuals lack both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their plasma, so they can receive blood from any ABO group without agglutination reaction, making them universal recipients.

questions.text: In the following palindromic base sequences of DNA, which one can be cut easily by particular restriction enzyme?
questions.explanation: 5'GAATTC3'/3'CTTAAG5' is a true palindromic sequence (reads the same 5' to 3' on both strands), recognized by EcoRI restriction enzyme.

questions.text: Match the following: (a) Physalia, (b) Limulus, (c) Ancylostoma, (d) Pinctada with (i) Pearl oyster, (ii) Portuguese Man of War, (iii) Living fossil, (iv) Hookworm.
questions.explanation: Physalia is Portuguese Man of War (ii); Limulus is a living fossil (iii); Ancylostoma is a hookworm (iv); Pinctada is a pearl oyster (i). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(i).

questions.text: Experimental verification of the chromosomal theory of inheritance was done by:
questions.explanation: Thomas Hunt Morgan provided experimental verification of the chromosomal theory of inheritance through his studies on Drosophila, demonstrating gene linkage on chromosomes.

questions.text: Dobson units are used to measure thickness of:
questions.explanation: Dobson units (DU) are used to measure the thickness of the ozone layer.

questions.text: The process of growth is maximum during:
questions.explanation: During the log (exponential) phase, growth rate is at its maximum, as cells/organisms divide and grow rapidly under favourable conditions, unlike the lag phase (initial slow growth), senescence (decline) or dormancy (no growth).

questions.text: Which of the following glucose transporters is insulin-dependent?
questions.explanation: GLUT4 is the insulin-dependent glucose transporter, primarily found in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, which translocates to the cell membrane in response to insulin signaling.

questions.text: Graves' disease is caused due to:
questions.explanation: Graves' disease is an autoimmune disorder causing hypersecretion (hyperthyroidism) of the thyroid gland.

questions.text: You are given a tissue with its potential for differentiation in an artificial culture. Which of the following pairs of hormones would you add to the medium to secure shoots as well as roots?
questions.explanation: Auxin and cytokinin in appropriate ratios control shoot and root differentiation in tissue culture (high cytokinin:auxin → shoots, high auxin:cytokinin → roots)

questions.text: Presence of plants arranged into well defined vertical layers depending on their height can be seen best in:
questions.explanation: Tropical rain forests show the most pronounced vertical stratification (layering), with distinct emergent, canopy, understorey, shrub, and herb layers, due to their high plant diversity and dense growth competing for light.

questions.text: A population of diploid organisms is at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. If the frequency of allele A is 0.1, the frequency of AA is ____________.
questions.explanation: Under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, genotype frequencies follow p² + 2pq + q² = 1, where p is the frequency of allele A. Frequency of AA genotype = p² = (0.1)² = 0.01.

questions.text:
Match Column-I with Column-II and select the correct option using the codes given below:
Column-I: a. Mons pubis, b. Antrum, c. Trophectoderm, d. Nebenkern
Column-II: (i) Embryo formation, (ii) Sperm, (iii) Female external genitalia, (iv) Graafian follicle
Codes:
(1) a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
(2) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
(3) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
(4) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
questions.explanation: Mons pubis = female external genitalia; Antrum = Graafian follicle (fluid-filled cavity); Trophectoderm = embryo formation (outer cell layer of blastocyst); Nebenkern = sperm (mitochondrial structure in spermatid). So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a part of human central neural system?
questions.topic: Meninges of the Central Nervous System
questions.explanation: Dura mater, pia mater, and arachnoid are the three meninges (protective membranes) covering the brain and spinal cord (CNS). Pericardium is the membrane surrounding the heart, not part of the central nervous system.

questions.text: Lungs are made up of air-filled sacs, the alveoli. They do not collapse even after forceful expiration, because of:
questions.explanation: Residual Volume (RV) is the volume of air that remains in the lungs even after the most forceful expiration, preventing the alveoli from completely collapsing.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Metamerism, (b) Canal system, (c) Comb plates, (d) Cnidoblasts
List-II: (i) Coelenterata, (ii) Ctenophora, (iii) Annelida, (iv) Porifera
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
(2) a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii
(3) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
(4) a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
questions.explanation: Metamerism = Annelida; Canal system = Porifera; Comb plates = Ctenophora; Cnidoblasts = Coelenterata. So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Match the following: (a) Inhibitor of catalytic activity, (b) Possess peptide bonds, (c) Cell wall material in fungi, (d) Secondary metabolite with (i) Ricin, (ii) Malonate, (iii) Chitin, (iv) Collagen
questions.explanation: Malonate is an inhibitor of catalytic activity (succinate dehydrogenase) (ii), Collagen possesses peptide bonds (iv), Chitin is the cell wall material in fungi (iii), and Ricin is a secondary metabolite (toxic protein) (i). This matches a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.

questions.text: In the given figure, which component has thin outer walls and highly thickened inner walls?
questions.explanation: In a xylem vessel cross-section, the innermost component (C, adjacent to the lumen) has thin outer walls but highly thickened inner walls due to secondary wall deposition, which provides mechanical strength while allowing lateral conduction.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Transfer RNAs and ribosomal RNA do not interact with mRNA. Statement II : RNA interference (RNAi) takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
